### Gotcha 136 — `device.setNetworkConditions()` requires Detox 20.49+ and is silently ignored on physical iOS devices [community]

**Root cause**: `device.setNetworkConditions()` was introduced in Detox 20.49 and is implemented via the iOS Simulator's Network Link Conditioner (`xcrun simctl status_bar`). On physical iOS devices the API call succeeds without error but has no effect. On Android emulators, the equivalent is the `emulator -netspeed` and `emulator -netdelay` flags set at boot time — `setNetworkConditions()` does not control Android emulator network after launch.

```ts
// BAD — assumes setNetworkConditions() works universally
await device.setNetworkConditions({ downloadBandwidth: 100, uploadBandwidth: 50 });
// Silently no-ops on physical iOS and Android emulators.

// GOOD — guard with platform and CI environment checks
async function throttleNetwork(kbps: number): Promise<void> {
  if (device.getPlatform() === 'ios' && process.env.CI === 'true') {
    // iOS Simulator in CI — setNetworkConditions is supported
    await device.setNetworkConditions({ downloadBandwidth: kbps, uploadBandwidth: kbps });
  } else if (device.getPlatform() === 'android') {
    // Android: use ADB to set network speed before test (must be done outside Detox)
    console.warn('[network] Android network throttling must be set via emulator boot flags');
  }
  // Physical device: skip silently
}

// Android emulator CI — set at launch time via avdArgs in .detoxrc.js:
// avdArgs: '-netspeed gprs -netdelay gprs'
// (100kbps down/up, 150ms latency — approximates GPRS)
```

### Gotcha 137 — `by.id()` matches hidden accessibility-only elements that are not visible on screen [community]

**Root cause**: React Native renders accessibility-only views (`accessible={true}` with zero-size or off-screen frames) that are invisible to the user but present in the accessibility tree. `by.id()` matches these if they share the same `testID`, causing Detox to interact with an invisible element and silently succeed without performing a visible UI change.

```ts
// Symptom: element(by.id('submit-btn')).tap() does not visually activate the button
// but Detox reports success.

// Diagnose with getAttributes():
const attrs = await element(by.id('submit-btn')).getAttributes() as Detox.ElementAttributes;
console.log('frame:', attrs.frame);
// If frame.width === 0 || frame.height === 0 → matched a zero-size accessibility view.

// FIX 1 — use waitFor toBeVisible() before tapping to ensure the element has a real frame:
await waitFor(element(by.id('submit-btn'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
await element(by.id('submit-btn')).tap();

// FIX 2 — use atIndex to prefer the visible duplicate:
// (Only acceptable when you know exactly how many duplicates exist)
await element(by.id('submit-btn')).atIndex(1).tap(); // Skip index 0 accessibility view

// BEST FIX — remove duplicate testID from accessibility-only views in the component:
// <View testID="submit-btn" accessible={false}> ← accessibility holder should NOT have testID
//   <TouchableOpacity testID="submit-btn" onPress={...}> ← only one element with this testID
```

### Gotcha 138 — `device.launchApp({ permissions: { notifications: 'YES' } })` silently grants in wrong alert timing on Android 13+ [community]

**Root cause**: Android 13 (API 33) introduced a runtime `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` permission. Detox's `permissions: { notifications: 'YES' }` shortcut grants `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` before app launch via `adb shell pm grant`. However, if the app calls `requestPermission()` at startup before Detox has finished the `pm grant` command, the permission check races with the grant and the app sees `PERMISSION_DENIED`. The grant succeeds, but the app already stored `denied` in local state for the current session.

```ts
// BAD — permission race condition on Android 13+
await device.launchApp({
  newInstance: true,
  permissions: { notifications: 'YES' }, // adb pm grant races with app startup
});
// App may start before pm grant completes → permission denied on first check

// GOOD — grant permission before cold-start, then confirm with a fresh launch
beforeAll(async () => {
  // Pre-grant via Detox's permissions mechanism before first launch
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true, permissions: { notifications: 'YES' } });
  await device.terminateApp();
  // Second launch: permission is already in the permission database → no race
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: false });
});

// OR: defer notification permission request to after app is fully initialised:
// In app code — delay requestPermission() call by 2 seconds post-startup
// to guarantee Detox has finished pm grant before the app checks the state.
```

### Gotcha 139 — `element(by.id('x')).swipe('up', 'fast')` on iOS dismisses a modal instead of scrolling the content inside it [community]

**Root cause**: iOS interprets a fast upward swipe on a `Modal` container as the system dismiss gesture (available since iOS 13 with `presentationStyle: 'pageSheet'`). When the modal's `ScrollView` and the modal dismiss gesture compete, iOS prioritises the dismiss gesture for fast swipes. Detox faithfully reproduces this behaviour — a fast swipe dismisses the modal rather than scrolling.

```ts
// BAD — fast swipe dismisses the modal sheet instead of scrolling
await element(by.id('bottom-sheet-scroll')).swipe('up', 'fast');
// Result: modal is dismissed, test fails on subsequent element lookup

// GOOD — use 'slow' speed to avoid triggering the dismiss gesture
await element(by.id('bottom-sheet-scroll')).swipe('up', 'slow');

// GOOD — use scroll() instead of swipe() for content inside modals:
await element(by.id('bottom-sheet-scroll')).scroll(300, 'down', 0.5, 0.5);

// GOOD — disable the interactive dismiss gesture in the component during testing:
// <Modal
//   visible={visible}
//   presentationStyle="pageSheet"
//   onRequestClose={onClose}
// >
//   ...
// </Modal>
// In test, launch with launchArgs: { DISABLE_MODAL_DISMISS_GESTURE: 'true' }
// In component: dismissable={launchArgs.DISABLE_MODAL_DISMISS_GESTURE !== 'true'}
```

### Gotcha 140 — `expect(element(by.id('x'))).toHaveValue('...')` fails on `<Switch>` — use `toHaveToggleValue()` instead [community]

**Root cause**: `toHaveValue()` reads the accessibility `value` property of an element. For a React Native `<Switch>`, the accessibility value is an empty string (`''`) on both platforms — the actual boolean state is stored in the `accessibilityState.checked` field. `toHaveToggleValue(true/false)` reads `accessibilityState.checked` and is the correct assertion for toggle state.

```ts
// BAD — toHaveValue('') always passes for <Switch> (empty string is the value)
await expect(element(by.id('dark-mode-switch'))).toHaveValue('true'); // FAILS — always ''
await expect(element(by.id('dark-mode-switch'))).toHaveValue('');    // PASSES but meaningless

// GOOD — toHaveToggleValue for <Switch>
await expect(element(by.id('dark-mode-switch'))).toHaveToggleValue(false); // off by default
await element(by.id('dark-mode-switch')).tap();
await expect(element(by.id('dark-mode-switch'))).toHaveToggleValue(true);  // now on

// GOOD — getAttributes() verification for multi-state toggle (3-state checkboxes):
const attrs = await element(by.id('tri-state-checkbox')).getAttributes() as Detox.ElementAttributes;
expect(attrs.value).toBe('mixed'); // Native <Checkbox> with indeterminate state
```

### Gotcha 141 — `device.shake()` triggers alert on iOS Simulator but `by.system()` cannot dismiss it if `ErrorBoundary` is not configured [community]

**Root cause**: On iOS Simulator, `device.shake()` sends a shake notification that triggers the "Erase All Content and Settings?" system alert if the app has not registered a custom shake handler. The alert is a native system dialog — it blocks all Detox interactions. If the test does not dismiss it via `by.system()`, subsequent element lookups time out and the alert persists for the remainder of the test session.

```ts
// Setup — always follow device.shake() with a system dialog guard:
it('shows undo popup on shake', async () => {
  await element(by.id('text-input')).replaceText('Hello world');
  await device.shake();

  // GUARD: dismiss system shake alert if it appears (iOS Simulator may show it)
  try {
    await waitFor(element(by.system.label('Undo Typing')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(1500);
    await element(by.system.label('Undo')).tap();
  } catch {
    // System undo alert did not appear — check for app-level shake popup instead
  }

  // In app code: register a shake handler to prevent the system alert:
  // useEffect(() => {
  //   const subscription = Shake.addListener(() => setShowUndoPopup(true));
  //   return () => subscription.remove();
  // }, []);
  await waitFor(element(by.id('undo-popup'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  await element(by.id('undo-btn')).tap();
});
```

### Gotcha 142 — `device.reloadReactNative()` does NOT reset `AsyncStorage` — use explicit clear or `newInstance: true` for storage tests [community]

**Root cause**: `device.reloadReactNative()` performs a JS bundle reload, which restarts the React Native JS runtime. It does NOT reset native storage: `AsyncStorage`, `MMKV`, `Realm`, SQLite, and Keychain data persist across `reloadReactNative()` calls. Tests that write to storage in one `it()` and expect a clean slate in the next will observe stale data.

```ts
// BAD — reloadReactNative() between tests does not clear AsyncStorage
describe('Onboarding flow', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative(); // Does NOT clear AsyncStorage
  });

  it('test 1 — sets HAS_SEEN_ONBOARDING=true', async () => {
    await element(by.id('skip-onboarding-btn')).tap();
    // AsyncStorage now has HAS_SEEN_ONBOARDING=true
  });

  it('test 2 — FAILS: skips to home because HAS_SEEN_ONBOARDING is still set', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('onboarding-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    // FAILS: the app skips onboarding because AsyncStorage wasn't cleared
  });
});

// GOOD option 1 — use newInstance: true (heavy, but always clean)
beforeEach(async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
});

// GOOD option 2 — clear via launchArgs gate in app code
beforeEach(async () => {
  await device.launchApp({
    newInstance: false,
    launchArgs: { CLEAR_ASYNC_STORAGE: 'true' },
  });
  // App reads CLEAR_ASYNC_STORAGE on startup and calls AsyncStorage.clear()
});

// GOOD option 3 — use device.resetContentAndSettings() for full simulator wipe
// (iOS Simulator only — Android: use device.launchApp({ delete: true }))
beforeAll(async () => {
  await device.resetContentAndSettings(); // Wipes all app storage + permissions
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
});
```

### Gotcha 143 — `element(by.id('x')).typeText()` appends to existing text on iOS when the cursor is not at the end [community]

**Root cause**: On iOS, `typeText()` inserts text at the current cursor position, not at the end. If the `TextInput` has a pre-filled value and the cursor is positioned mid-string (e.g., after a previous partial edit), `typeText()` inserts the new text at the cursor rather than appending it. The element appears to have unexpected text like `"Hello newText world"` instead of `"Hello world newText"`.

```ts
// BAD — typeText() inserts at cursor position, not end
await element(by.id('search-input')).typeText('React Native');
// If input had value "React " with cursor at index 6 → result: "React React NativeNative"

// GOOD — use replaceText() to set the full value atomically:
await element(by.id('search-input')).replaceText('React Native');

// GOOD — if you need to append text, tap to move cursor to end first:
await element(by.id('search-input')).tap(); // Moves cursor to end in most cases
await element(by.id('search-input')).typeText(' Native');

// BEST for forms — always use replaceText() for full field values:
async function fillInput(testID: string, value: string): Promise<void> {
  await element(by.id(testID)).tap();
  await element(by.id(testID)).replaceText(value);
  // Verify the value was set correctly:
  await expect(element(by.id(testID))).toHaveValue(value);
}
```

---

### Gotcha 144 — `waitFor()` with very short `withTimeout(500)` causes false failures on Android API 34+ due to window animation scale [community]

**Root cause**: Android 14 (API 34) increased the default window animation scale from 1.0× to 1.2× in the Developer Options. On CI emulators without the `--no-window-animation` flag, animated transitions (e.g., screen navigation, Dialog open) can take up to 600 ms. Any `withTimeout` below that threshold causes spurious timeouts on screen elements that are in the middle of animating in.

```ts
// BAD — 500 ms timeout is too short for animated navigation on Android 14+
await waitFor(element(by.id('cart-screen')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(500); // FAILS on Android API 34+ with default animation scale

// GOOD — use at least 3 000 ms for navigation transitions:
await waitFor(element(by.id('cart-screen')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(3000);

// CI FIX — disable window animations on Android emulator via ADB in CI:
// - name: Disable Android animations
//   run: |
//     adb shell settings put global window_animation_scale 0
//     adb shell settings put global transition_animation_scale 0
//     adb shell settings put global animator_duration_scale 0

// .detoxrc.js — for emulators launched by Detox, set avdArgs:
// avdArgs: '-no-window-animation'
// (equivalent to ADB settings above but applied at emulator boot)
```

---

### Gotcha 145 — `element(by.id('x')).pinch(1.5, 'fast')` has inverse semantics on Android vs iOS [community]

**Root cause**: Detox's `pinch(scale, speed, angle)` action maps to different native gesture APIs on each platform. On iOS (`XCUITest`), `scale > 1.0` means **zoom in** (fingers spreading apart), `scale < 1.0` means **zoom out** (fingers coming together). On Android (Espresso), Detox emulates pinch using pointer events — but the scale interpretation is **inverted**: `scale = 1.5` actually produces a zoom-out gesture on some Espresso versions.

```ts
// Symptom: map zoom test passes on iOS but zooms out on Android
await element(by.id('map-view')).pinch(2.0, 'slow'); // Zooms in on iOS, may zoom OUT on Android

// GOOD — use platform-specific scale values:
const zoomInScale = device.getPlatform() === 'ios' ? 2.0 : 0.5;
const zoomOutScale = device.getPlatform() === 'ios' ? 0.5 : 2.0;

await element(by.id('map-view')).pinch(zoomInScale, 'slow');
await waitFor(element(by.id('map-zoom-level-12'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

// Helper:
async function zoomIn(testID: string): Promise<void> {
  const scale = device.getPlatform() === 'ios' ? 2.0 : 0.5;
  await element(by.id(testID)).pinch(scale, 'slow');
}
async function zoomOut(testID: string): Promise<void> {
  const scale = device.getPlatform() === 'ios' ? 0.5 : 2.0;
  await element(by.id(testID)).pinch(scale, 'slow');
}
```

### Gotcha 146 — `by.text()` matching is case-sensitive and locale-dependent — use `testID` for i18n apps [community]

**Root cause**: `by.text()` performs a case-sensitive exact string match against the element's `text` property (iOS: `label`; Android: `text` attribute). In apps with runtime locale switching or i18n string substitution (e.g., `t('welcome', { name: 'Alice' })`), the text value varies between locales and test runs. Tests using `by.text()` that pass in English will fail in German or French CI runs because the translated string is different.

```ts
// BAD — text is locale-dependent and fragile
await element(by.text('Continue')).tap();       // Fails in French: 'Continuer'
await element(by.text('Welcome, Alice')).tap(); // Fails with different user names

// GOOD — use testID (locale-independent)
await element(by.id('continue-btn')).tap();
await element(by.id('welcome-message')).tap();

// ACCEPTABLE — use by.text() only in smoke tests that lock the locale:
// launchArgs: { DETOX_LOCALE: 'en-US' } + device.setLanguage('en') before test
// (Ensures text is always English for the test session)
await device.launchApp({
  newInstance: true,
  launchArgs: { DetoxLocale: 'en-US' },
});
await element(by.text('Continue')).tap(); // Safe when locale is locked

// CI — add locale to matrix for i18n regression:
// detox test -c ios.sim.release --device-name "iPhone 16" -- --locale fr-FR
// detox test -c ios.sim.release --device-name "iPhone 16" -- --locale de-DE
```

---

### Gotcha 147 — `device.captureViewHierarchy()` on Android returns `*.uihierarchy` format which is incompatible with iOS `*.viewhierarchy` parsers [community]

**Root cause**: iOS `captureViewHierarchy()` produces an Xcode `.viewhierarchy` archive (ZIP-based binary format). Android produces a JSON-like `.uihierarchy` text file. Any cross-platform tooling that parses these files must handle both formats explicitly — assuming one format silently fails on the other platform without an error, producing an empty or corrupt diff.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/parseHierarchy.ts
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

export function readHierarchyAsText(filePath: string): string {
  const ext = path.extname(filePath).toLowerCase();
  if (ext === '.uihierarchy') {
    // Android: plain text JSON-like format — read directly
    return fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf8');
  } else if (ext === '.viewhierarchy') {
    // iOS: binary ZIP archive — extract the embedded XML
    // Requires: npm install adm-zip
    // const AdmZip = require('adm-zip');
    // const zip = new AdmZip(filePath);
    // const entry = zip.getEntries().find(e => e.name.endsWith('.xml'));
    // return entry ? zip.readAsText(entry) : '';
    throw new Error(
      'iOS .viewhierarchy parsing requires adm-zip. ' +
        'Add it to your e2e devDependencies.',
    );
  }
  throw new Error(`Unknown hierarchy format: ${ext}`);
}

// In CI — use platform-conditional diffing:
const hierarchyPath = await device.captureViewHierarchy('checkout');
if (device.getPlatform() === 'android') {
  const text = readHierarchyAsText(hierarchyPath);
  expect(text).toContain('id/checkout_total_label');
}
// iOS: use Xcode's Accessibility Inspector or a dedicated view-hierarchy diff tool
```

### Gotcha 148 — Detox `--cleanup` flag terminates the emulator after each test file, causing extreme CI slowness when running many small spec files [community]

**Root cause**: When `--cleanup` is passed to `detox test`, Detox sends a `device.terminateApp()` + `device.shutdown()` after each test file. For a project with 50 spec files on Android, this means 50 emulator boot cycles (~2 min each on standard CI runners) — a total of over 100 minutes just for cold boots. The `--cleanup` flag exists for isolation, but it is almost never needed between test files in the same configuration run.

```ts
// BAD .detoxrc.js — cleanup at file level causes extreme CI slow-down
// (This is NOT in .detoxrc.js — --cleanup is a CLI flag)
// $ npx detox test -c android.emu.debug --cleanup
// ^ This shuts down the emulator after every spec file.

// GOOD CI workflow — omit --cleanup, rely on device.launchApp({ newInstance: true })
// in beforeAll for within-run isolation:
// $ npx detox test -c android.emu.debug
// No --cleanup → emulator stays alive across spec files → 80% CI time reduction.

// If you need full cleanup between matrix shards (different platforms), use
// the 'cleanup' lifecycle hook in globalTeardown instead:
// e2e/globalTeardown.ts:
// export default async () => {
//   await detox.cleanup();
// };

// .detoxrc.js jest config:
// jest: { globalTeardown: './e2e/globalTeardown.ts' }
// → cleanup runs once per shard, not once per spec file.
```

---

### Gotcha 149 — `element(by.id('x')).getAttributes()` returns `ElementAttributes[]` (array) when multiple elements match — always check the type before reading fields [community]

**Root cause**: If more than one element matches `by.id('x')` (e.g., a `testID` applied to both a wrapper `View` and an inner `Text`), `getAttributes()` returns an **array** of attribute objects (`ElementAttributes[]`) rather than a single `ElementAttributes`. Attempting to read `(result as Detox.ElementAttributes).text` on an array produces `undefined` — or crashes if you try `.frame.x` — making the assertion silently incorrect.

```ts
// BAD — assumes single match, crashes if there are duplicates
const attrs = await element(by.id('product-title')).getAttributes();
expect((attrs as Detox.ElementAttributes).text).toBe('Shoes'); // TypeError if attrs is an array

// GOOD — runtime type guard before reading attributes
type ElementAttrs = Detox.ElementAttributes;
type ElementAttrsArray = { elements: ElementAttrs[] };

function isSingle(attrs: ElementAttrs | ElementAttrsArray): attrs is ElementAttrs {
  return !('elements' in attrs);
}

const attrs = await element(by.id('product-title')).getAttributes();
if (isSingle(attrs)) {
  expect(attrs.text).toBe('Shoes');
} else {
  // Multiple matches — log a warning and use the first visible one
  console.warn(`[getAttributes] Multiple elements matched 'product-title': ${attrs.elements.length}`);
  const visible = attrs.elements.find(el => el.visible);
  expect(visible?.text).toBe('Shoes');
}

// BEST FIX — eliminate duplicate testIDs (see Gotcha 137)
// Only one element should carry testID="product-title".
// Verify in CI with a helper that asserts single-match before every getAttributes call:
async function getSingleAttributes(testID: string): Promise<Detox.ElementAttributes> {
  const attrs = await element(by.id(testID)).getAttributes();
  if ('elements' in attrs) {
    throw new Error(
      `Multiple elements matched testID="${testID}" (${attrs.elements.length}). ` +
        'Ensure only one element has this testID.',
    );
  }
  return attrs;
}
```

## Updated Anti-Patterns Checklist (Cycle 24 additions)

| Anti-Pattern | Fix |
|---|---|
| Using `waitFor().toBeVisible()` to detect fade-in elements in Fabric (RN 0.76+) | `opacity: 0` does not set `isHidden` in Fabric — use conditional rendering or `toHaveText()` / `frame.height > 0` guard instead (Gotcha 135) |
| Calling `device.setNetworkConditions()` on physical iOS or Android emulator | API is iOS Simulator-only (Detox 20.49+) and silently no-ops elsewhere — guard with platform + CI environment checks (Gotcha 136) |
| Having the same `testID` on a wrapper `View` and its inner child | Creates invisible duplicate matches in `by.id()` — only assign `testID` to the single interactive leaf element (Gotcha 137) |
| Relying on `permissions: { notifications: 'YES' }` for Android 13+ without a two-launch pattern | `pm grant` races with app startup — grant before cold-start, then do a second launch without `newInstance: true` (Gotcha 138) |
| Using `swipe('up', 'fast')` inside a `Modal` sheet | Fast swipe triggers iOS system dismiss gesture — use `scroll()` or `swipe('up', 'slow')` inside modal containers (Gotcha 139) |
| Using `toHaveValue()` to assert `<Switch>` state | `<Switch>` stores state in `accessibilityState.checked`, not `value` — use `toHaveToggleValue(true/false)` (Gotcha 140) |
| Calling `device.shake()` without a system dialog guard | Shake may trigger the iOS Simulator "Undo Typing" system alert — always wrap with a `try/catch` `by.system.label()` guard (Gotcha 141) |
| Relying on `reloadReactNative()` to clear `AsyncStorage` / `MMKV` | JS reload does not reset native storage — use `newInstance: true` or a `CLEAR_ASYNC_STORAGE` launchArgs gate (Gotcha 142) |
| Using `typeText()` without ensuring cursor position on iOS | `typeText()` inserts at cursor, not end — use `replaceText()` for setting full values atomically (Gotcha 143) |
| Using `withTimeout(500)` for screen navigation assertions on Android 14+ | Android 14 default animation scale is 1.2× — use minimum 3 000 ms for animated transitions; disable animations in CI via ADB settings (Gotcha 144) |
| Assuming `pinch(scale > 1.0)` means zoom-in on all platforms | Scale semantics are inverted between iOS and Android Espresso — use platform-conditional scale values (Gotcha 145) |
| Using `by.text()` in i18n apps without locking the locale | Text is locale-dependent — prefer `testID` selectors; lock locale via `launchArgs: { DetoxLocale: 'en-US' }` when `by.text()` is unavoidable (Gotcha 146) |
| Passing `--cleanup` to `detox test` in CI with many spec files | Shuts down the emulator after every spec file — omit `--cleanup` and use `globalTeardown` for shard-level cleanup instead (Gotcha 148) |
| Reading `getAttributes()` result without checking if it is an array | Returns `ElementAttributes[]` when multiple elements match — always use a runtime type guard before accessing fields (Gotcha 149) |

### Pattern 98 — `device.setSystemUI()` for Android emulator status-bar/keyboard/navigation-bar preset control (Detox 20.50+)

Detox 20.50 introduced `device.setSystemUI(preset)` on Android, allowing tests to configure the system UI chrome (status bar, navigation bar, keyboard visibility) to a named preset (`'genymotion'` or `'google'`). This replaces ad-hoc ADB commands in CI setup scripts and keeps system UI configuration inside the test process.

```ts
// .detoxrc.js — declare the systemUI preset per device configuration
module.exports = {
  devices: {
    'android.emu': {
      type: 'android.emulator',
      device: { avdName: 'Pixel_7_API_34' },
      systemUI: { preset: 'google' }, // 'google' | 'genymotion'
    },
  },
};

// In test — restore a specific UI state before checking navigation bar overlap:
it('content is not obscured by navigation bar', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });

  // Explicitly set the system UI preset mid-test (useful for context switches):
  await device.setSystemUI({ preset: 'google' });

  await waitFor(element(by.id('main-content'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);

  // Assert that the content frame does not overlap with the navigation bar:
  const attrs = await element(by.id('main-content')).getAttributes() as Detox.ElementAttributes;
  // Navigation bar on Pixel 7 with gesture navigation is 0 px tall — content fills screen.
  // With 3-button nav, the navigation bar is 48 dp — content must not go below that.
  expect(attrs.frame.y + attrs.frame.height).toBeLessThan(800); // approx usable height
});

// For Genymotion Cloud VMs:
// devices: { 'genymotion.emu': { systemUI: { preset: 'genymotion' } } }
// 'genymotion' preset hides the software navigation bar which is present by default.
```

### Pattern 99 — `by.web()` with `runScript()` for extracting computed DOM state in hybrid React Native WebViews

`by.web(webMatcher).runScript(fn)` evaluates a JavaScript function inside the WebView and returns the result to the Detox test process. This is the correct approach for asserting computed DOM state (e.g., CSS classes, `innerHTML`, form validation messages) that is not exposed through a native accessibility attribute.

```ts
// Verify that a dynamically injected CSS class is present after a user action
it('applies "active" class to the selected tab in WebView', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('webview-container'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);

  // Tap the "Reports" tab inside the WebView
  await element(by.web.id('tab-reports')).tap();

  // Use runScript to inspect the DOM class list — not available via native matchers
  const isActive: boolean = await element(by.web.id('tab-reports')).runScript(
    // Function receives the DOM element as the first argument
    (el: Element) => el.classList.contains('active'),
  );
  expect(isActive).toBe(true);
});

// Extract the full text content of a rich-text editor WebView:
it('rich text editor contains submitted content', async () => {
  await element(by.web.id('editor-submit-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('confirmation-banner'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

  const editorContent: string = await element(by.web.cssSelector('.ql-editor')).runScript(
    (el: Element) => (el as HTMLElement).innerText,
  );
  expect(editorContent).toContain('Hello from Detox');
});

// Wait for WebView URL navigation to complete before asserting:
it('navigates to checkout page in WebView', async () => {
  await element(by.web.id('proceed-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.web.cssSelector('h1')))
    .toHaveText('Checkout')
    .withTimeout(8000);
});
```

### Pattern 100 — `device.captureViewHierarchy()` triggered only on test failure via `afterEach` for zero-cost debugging artifacts

Capturing the view hierarchy on every test is slow (~300 ms on iOS, ~500 ms on Android). The production pattern is to capture it only when the test fails, using Detox's `jasmine`/`jest-circus` `currentTestInfo` API, avoiding artifact overhead on passing tests.

```ts
// e2e/jest.setup.ts — capture view hierarchy only on failure
import { device } from 'detox';
import * as path from 'path';

afterEach(async () => {
  const state = expect.getState();
  const testPassed = !state.assertionCalls || state.numPassingAsserts === state.assertionCalls;

  // Alternative: check jest-circus's currentTestInfo for failure status
  const testFailed = (global as any).__currentTestFailed === true;

  if (testFailed) {
    const safeName = (state.currentTestName ?? 'unknown')
      .replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '_')
      .slice(0, 60);
    const workerId = process.env.JEST_WORKER_ID ?? '0';

    try {
      const hierarchyPath = await device.captureViewHierarchy(`fail_${safeName}_w${workerId}`);
      console.log(`[hierarchy] Captured on failure: ${hierarchyPath}`);
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn(`[hierarchy] Capture failed: ${err}`);
    }
  }
});

// In jest.config.js — hook to set the __currentTestFailed global:
// setupFilesAfterFramework: ['./e2e/jest.failure-hook.ts']
// jest.failure-hook.ts:
// const originalFail = (global as any).fail;
// afterEach(() => {
//   (global as any).__currentTestFailed = expect.getState().assertionCalls > 0 &&
//     expect.getState().numPassingAsserts < expect.getState().assertionCalls;
// });
```

### Pattern 101 — Per-configuration `launchArgs` injection via environment variables for multi-environment CI pipelines

Large projects run Detox against multiple backend environments (dev, staging, prod-mirror). Rather than separate `.detoxrc.js` files, inject backend URL and auth token via environment variables resolved at test launch time. This keeps the test suite environment-agnostic and avoids duplicating configuration.

```ts
// .detoxrc.js — resolve backend URL from CI environment variable
const backendUrl = process.env.BACKEND_URL ?? 'https://dev.api.myapp.com';
const authToken  = process.env.E2E_AUTH_TOKEN ?? 'dev-token-insecure';

module.exports = {
  configurations: {
    'ios.sim.release': {
      device: { type: 'ios.simulator', device: { type: 'iPhone 16' } },
      app: { type: 'ios.app', binaryPath: 'ios/build/Release-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app' },
      launchArgs: {
        BACKEND_URL: backendUrl,
        AUTH_TOKEN: authToken,
      },
    },
    'android.emu.release': {
      device: { type: 'android.emulator', device: { avdName: 'Pixel_7_API_34' } },
      app: { type: 'android.apk', binaryPath: 'android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk' },
      launchArgs: {
        BACKEND_URL: backendUrl,
        AUTH_TOKEN: authToken,
      },
    },
  },
};

// In app code (React Native) — read via NativeModules.RNLaunchArgs or a bridge module:
// import { NativeModules } from 'react-native';
// const backendUrl = NativeModules.DetoxLaunchArgs?.BACKEND_URL ?? 'https://dev.api.myapp.com';

// In e2e test — read via device.reversePorts is not needed; launchArgs are passed to app.
// The test does NOT need to read the value — the app reads it from its own launch args.
// For assertions in tests: hard-code the expected environment label, not the full URL:
it('shows correct environment indicator in debug overlay', async () => {
  await waitFor(element(by.id('env-indicator'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  const env = process.env.BACKEND_URL?.includes('staging') ? 'staging' : 'dev';
  await expect(element(by.id('env-indicator'))).toHaveText(env);
});
```

### Pattern 102 — `element(by.id('x')).multiTap(count)` for double-tap and triple-tap gesture testing

`multiTap(count)` sends `count` rapid taps to an element. This is the correct API for double-tap (zoom in on maps/images), triple-tap (select all text in a `TextInput`), or custom double-tap event handlers — single `tap()` followed by another `tap()` with an async `await` between them is too slow to trigger double-tap recognition.

```ts
// BAD — two separate taps have too much delay for double-tap recognition
await element(by.id('map-view')).tap();
await element(by.id('map-view')).tap();
// Result: recognised as two single taps, not a double-tap

// GOOD — multiTap(2) fires two taps with minimal inter-tap delay
it('double-tap zooms in on the map', async () => {
  await waitFor(element(by.id('map-view'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  await element(by.id('map-view')).multiTap(2);

  await waitFor(element(by.id('map-zoom-level-12')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(3000);
});

// Triple-tap to select all text in a TextInput (iOS behaviour)
it('triple-tap selects all text', async () => {
  await element(by.id('text-input')).replaceText('Select me entirely');
  await element(by.id('text-input')).multiTap(3);

  // On iOS, triple-tap selects the word; then verify selection via accessibility
  const attrs = await element(by.id('text-input')).getAttributes() as Detox.ElementAttributes;
  // The value should still be the original text — selection does not clear value
  expect(attrs.text).toBe('Select me entirely');
});

// Custom double-tap handler:
it('activates quick-action menu on double-tap', async () => {
  await element(by.id('list-item-42')).multiTap(2);
  await waitFor(element(by.id('quick-action-menu'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
  await element(by.id('quick-action-delete')).tap();
});
```

---

### Pattern 103 — `device.setOrientation()` with pre/post-rotation `waitFor` guards for responsive layout tests

Testing responsive layouts requires rotating the device and asserting that the UI reflows correctly. `device.setOrientation('landscape')` / `device.setOrientation('portrait')` trigger the rotation, but the JS layout engine takes one or two render passes after the native rotation completes. Always add a `waitFor` after rotation before asserting layout-dependent elements.

```ts
// BAD — assertion fires before React Native re-layout after rotation
await device.setOrientation('landscape');
await expect(element(by.id('side-panel'))).toBeVisible(); // May fail — layout not done yet

// GOOD — wait for a layout-dependent element to appear after rotation
it('side panel appears in landscape mode', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

  // Rotate to landscape
  await device.setOrientation('landscape');

  // Wait for the layout to settle — the side panel only renders in landscape
  await waitFor(element(by.id('side-panel')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(4000);

  await expect(element(by.id('main-content'))).toBeVisible();
  await expect(element(by.id('side-panel'))).toBeVisible();

  // Rotate back — side panel should disappear
  await device.setOrientation('portrait');
  await waitFor(element(by.id('side-panel')))
    .not.toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(4000);
});

// Utility for cross-platform rotation guard:
async function rotateAndSettle(
  orientation: 'landscape' | 'portrait',
  anchorTestID: string,
): Promise<void> {
  await device.setOrientation(orientation);
  // Wait for any element to re-render as a proxy for layout completion
  await waitFor(element(by.id(anchorTestID))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
}
```

### Pattern 104 — Expo Go + Expo SDK 53 (`@expo/metro-config` v0.18+) Detox integration with `expo-modules-core` v2

Expo SDK 53 upgraded `expo-modules-core` to v2, which requires Detox 20.9+. The Metro config format also changed — Detox's `metro` preset must be applied via `withDetox()` from `@config-plugins/detox` rather than the legacy manual Metro config merge.

```ts
// metro.config.js — Expo SDK 53 + Detox 20.9+ (correct format)
const { getDefaultConfig } = require('expo/metro-config');
const { withDetox } = require('@config-plugins/detox');  // v0.5+ supports Expo SDK 53

const config = getDefaultConfig(__dirname);
module.exports = withDetox(config);

// .detoxrc.js — Expo managed workflow with EAS Build binary
module.exports = {
  configurations: {
    'ios.sim.debug': {
      device: { type: 'ios.simulator', device: { type: 'iPhone 16' } },
      app: {
        type: 'ios.app',
        // Point to the local build (run `npx expo run:ios --configuration Debug` first)
        binaryPath: 'ios/build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyExpoApp.app',
        build: 'npx expo run:ios --configuration Debug --no-build-cache',
      },
    },
    'android.emu.debug': {
      device: { type: 'android.emulator', device: { avdName: 'Pixel_7_API_34' } },
      app: {
        type: 'android.apk',
        binaryPath: 'android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk',
        build: 'npx expo run:android --configuration Debug',
      },
    },
  },
  testRunner: {
    args: { $0: 'jest', config: 'e2e/jest.config.ts' },
    jest: { setupTimeout: 300000 }, // 5 min for first expo prebuild
  },
};

// package.json — required peer deps for Expo SDK 53 + Detox 20.9+
// "detox": "^20.9.0"
// "expo-modules-core": "^2.0.0"    ← required by SDK 53
// "@config-plugins/detox": "^0.5.0"
```

### Pattern 105 — Detox `ignoreUnexpectedMessages` configuration to suppress spurious WS protocol warnings in CI logs

Detox communicates with the app under test via WebSocket. When the app emits unexpected or extra WS messages (common with some third-party analytics SDKs and React DevTools bridges), Detox logs a `[WARN] Unexpected message` line for each one. In busy CI environments this floods the logs and obscures real failures. `ignoreUnexpectedMessages: true` silences these warnings.

```ts
// .detoxrc.js — session configuration for suppressing spurious WS warnings
module.exports = {
  // ...
  session: {
    autoStart: true,
    debugSynchronization: 0,        // Disable verbose sync polling logs in CI
    ignoreUnexpectedMessages: true, // Suppress "Unexpected message" WS warnings (Detox 20.50+)
  },
  configurations: {
    'ios.sim.release': {
      // ...
    },
  },
};

// Note: ignoreUnexpectedMessages should be FALSE (default) during local debugging —
// unexpected messages can indicate the app is sending events out of order.
// Only enable in CI where the noise-to-signal ratio makes it impractical to leave enabled.

// Recommended CI vs local split:
const isCI = process.env.CI === 'true';
module.exports = {
  session: {
    autoStart: true,
    ignoreUnexpectedMessages: isCI, // true in CI, false locally
  },
};
```

---

### Pattern 106 — Jest `testRunner.jest.bail` + `testRunner.retries` combined strategy for CI cost control

Setting `bail: 1` in the Jest runner config stops all remaining tests after the first test suite (file) fails. Combined with `retries: 1`, Detox retries each failed test once before counting it as a failure. This combination minimises CI wallclock time: flaky tests get one retry, but a genuine product-breaking failure halts the run quickly.

```ts
// .detoxrc.js — bail + retries strategy
module.exports = {
  testRunner: {
    args: {
      $0: 'jest',
      config: 'e2e/jest.config.ts',
    },
    jest: {
      setupTimeout: 120000,
      bail: process.env.CI === 'true' ? 1 : 0, // halt after first suite failure in CI only
    },
    retries: process.env.CI === 'true' ? 1 : 0, // retry once in CI, no retries locally
  },
};

// GitHub Actions — capture exit code to distinguish bail from genuine failure:
// - name: Run Detox tests
//   id: detox
//   run: npx detox test -c ios.sim.release
//   continue-on-error: true
// - name: Check test result
//   run: |
//     if [ "${{ steps.detox.outcome }}" == "failure" ]; then
//       echo "Detox tests failed or bailed. Check artifacts for details."
//       exit 1
//     fi

// Recommended per-environment bail settings:
// Local dev:      bail: 0, retries: 0  → see all failures
// PR CI:          bail: 1, retries: 1  → fast feedback, absorb one flaky test
// Release CI:     bail: 0, retries: 2  → full run, aggressive flakiness tolerance
```

### Pattern 107 — React Native 0.83 + New Architecture: using `by.type()` with the updated Fabric component type names

React Native 0.83 (released with full New Architecture on by default) updated several internal Fabric component class names that Detox's `by.type()` matcher resolves against. Tests that previously matched `RCTScrollView` now need `RCTFabricScrollView` (Android) or the updated iOS XCUITest class identifier. Build a cross-version type name helper to avoid fragile hard-coded strings.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/rnTypeNames.ts — version-conditional type name resolution
import { device } from 'detox';

// RN 0.76+ New Architecture renames (Fabric renderer):
const FABRIC_TYPE_MAP = {
  ScrollView:    { ios: 'RCTScrollView',          android: 'com.facebook.react.views.scroll.ReactScrollView' },
  FlatList:      { ios: 'RCTScrollView',          android: 'com.facebook.react.views.scroll.ReactScrollView' },
  TextInput:     { ios: 'RCTTextInputView',        android: 'com.facebook.react.views.textinput.ReactEditText' },
  View:          { ios: 'RCTView',                android: 'com.facebook.react.views.view.ReactViewGroup' },
  Text:          { ios: 'RCTTextView',            android: 'com.facebook.react.views.text.ReactTextView' },
  TouchableOp:  { ios: 'RCTView',                android: 'com.facebook.react.views.view.ReactViewGroup' },
} as const;

type ComponentName = keyof typeof FABRIC_TYPE_MAP;

export function byComponentType(name: ComponentName): ReturnType<typeof by.type> {
  const platform = device.getPlatform() as 'ios' | 'android';
  const typeName = FABRIC_TYPE_MAP[name][platform];
  return by.type(typeName);
}

// Usage — matches the ScrollView regardless of RN architecture version:
it('scrolls through a FlatList using by.type()', async () => {
  await waitFor(element(byComponentType('FlatList')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(4000);

  await element(byComponentType('FlatList')).scroll(300, 'down');
  await waitFor(element(by.id('list-item-20'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
});

// REMINDER: prefer by.id() over by.type() — use by.type() only for
// third-party list components that do not expose testID.
```

---

### Gotcha 150 — `element.scroll()` with `whileElement().scroll()` accumulates scroll distance — do not combine with a hard-coded pixel count outside a loop [community]

**Root cause**: `waitFor(element(by.id('item'))).toBeVisible().whileElement(by.id('list')).scroll(200, 'down')` repeats the 200 px scroll until the target becomes visible (up to a Detox-internal limit of ~10 iterations). If the target element is already visible when the assertion runs, the scroll still fires once. Developers who also add a manual `element.scroll(1000)` before the `waitFor+whileElement` pattern double-scroll the list, overshoot the target, and then the `whileElement` scroll tries to scroll back (it does not — it only scrolls in one direction), leaving the element off-screen.

```ts
// BAD — manual pre-scroll + whileElement double-scroll
await element(by.id('product-list')).scroll(1000, 'down'); // Scrolls past the target
await waitFor(element(by.id('product-card-5')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .whileElement(by.id('product-list'))
  .scroll(200, 'down'); // Tries to scroll down again — target is already above viewport

// GOOD — use only whileElement scroll without manual pre-scroll
await waitFor(element(by.id('product-card-5')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .whileElement(by.id('product-list'))
  .scroll(200, 'down');

// GOOD — if you need directional awareness, reset scroll position first:
await element(by.id('product-list')).scroll(10000, 'up'); // Scroll to top
await waitFor(element(by.id('product-card-5')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .whileElement(by.id('product-list'))
  .scroll(200, 'down');
```

---

### Gotcha 151 — `device.openURL()` on Android requires the URL scheme to be declared in `AndroidManifest.xml` — missing `<data>` tag causes silent no-op [community]

**Root cause**: On Android, `device.openURL('myapp://order/42')` sends an `ACTION_VIEW` Intent. If the app's `AndroidManifest.xml` does not declare an `<intent-filter>` with the matching `<data android:scheme="myapp"/>` entry for the activity, the OS finds no matching handler. On Android 12+ (API 31+), an unresolvable explicit Intent throws `ActivityNotFoundException`, but Detox catches it and reports a warning rather than failing the test — so the navigation simply does not happen and subsequent element lookups time out silently.

```ts
// BAD — deep link to an order detail screen that is not declared in AndroidManifest.xml
await device.openURL('myapp://order/42');
await waitFor(element(by.id('order-detail-42'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
// Test times out: Intent was silently dropped

// CHECK — AndroidManifest.xml must include:
// <activity android:name=".MainActivity">
//   <intent-filter android:autoVerify="true">
//     <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW" />
//     <category android:name="android.intent.category.DEFAULT" />
//     <category android:name="android.intent.category.BROWSABLE" />
//     <data android:scheme="myapp" android:host="order" />
//   </intent-filter>
// </activity>

// GOOD — verify deep link registration before running deep link tests:
it('navigates to order detail via deep link', async () => {
  // Cold-start the app via deep link (tests that the link handler runs at startup)
  await device.launchApp({
    newInstance: true,
    url: 'myapp://order/42',
  });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('order-detail-42'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(6000);
});

// Warm-start deep link:
it('navigates to order detail via deep link from background', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  await device.sendToBackground();
  await device.openURL('myapp://order/42');
  await device.bringToForeground();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('order-detail-42'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(6000);
});
```

---

### Gotcha 152 — `device.setLocation()` requires calling `launchApp()` AFTER `setLocation()` on Android API 35 — calling it before launch sets a location that is immediately replaced by GPS cold-start [community]

**Root cause**: Android 35 (Android 15 QPR1) changed the mock location provider lifecycle. If `device.setLocation(lat, lon)` is called before `launchApp({ newInstance: true })`, the mock position is injected before the app's location provider initialises. On first startup, the Android Location Manager performs a GPS cold-start check that **replaces** the previously-set mock location with `null` until the next valid fix. The app receives `null` on the first location query, stores `null` in state, and tests that assert a displayed coordinate fail.

```ts
// BAD — setLocation before launch on Android API 35 is overridden by GPS cold-start
await device.setLocation(37.7749, -122.4194); // San Francisco
await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true }); // Mock location overridden by GPS cold-start

// GOOD — set location AFTER the app is fully launched and the location provider is initialised
it('displays user location on the map', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('map-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

  // Set location after launch — location provider is already initialised
  await device.setLocation(37.7749, -122.4194);

  // Wait for the map to update with the new location pin
  await waitFor(element(by.id('user-location-pin'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  await expect(element(by.id('location-label'))).toHaveText('San Francisco, CA');
});

// Cross-platform guard — 'always' permission required on iOS 17+:
// device.launchApp({ permissions: { location: 'always' } }) for iOS
// Android: grant ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION via permissions before launch
```

---

### Gotcha 153 — `element(by.id('x')).tapReturnKey()` on Android does NOT trigger `onSubmitEditing` when `returnKeyType` is not set [community]

**Root cause**: `tapReturnKey()` sends the keyboard return/enter key event to the focused `TextInput`. On iOS, this always fires `onSubmitEditing` regardless of `returnKeyType`. On Android (Espresso), `tapReturnKey()` dispatches a `KeyEvent.KEYCODE_ENTER` event. If the `TextInput` does not have `returnKeyType` set explicitly (which defaults to `'default'` — a new-line key on Android), Android interprets the Enter as a line break and does NOT fire `onSubmitEditing`. The submit handler is never called.

```ts
// BAD — no returnKeyType means Enter inserts a newline on Android, not submit
// Component: <TextInput testID="search-input" onSubmitEditing={handleSubmit} />
await element(by.id('search-input')).replaceText('React Native');
await element(by.id('search-input')).tapReturnKey();
// onSubmitEditing NEVER fires on Android — Enter inserts '\n' instead

// FIX — set returnKeyType in the component:
// <TextInput
//   testID="search-input"
//   returnKeyType="search"  // or "done", "go", "next", "send"
//   onSubmitEditing={handleSubmit}
// />

// In test — after fixing the component:
await element(by.id('search-input')).replaceText('React Native');
await element(by.id('search-input')).tapReturnKey();
await waitFor(element(by.id('search-results-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

// Cross-platform workaround when you cannot modify the component:
async function submitInput(testID: string): Promise<void> {
  if (device.getPlatform() === 'android') {
    // On Android, tap the search/submit button directly
    await element(by.id('search-submit-btn')).tap();
  } else {
    await element(by.id(testID)).tapReturnKey();
  }
}
```

---

### Gotcha 154 — `device.takeScreenshot()` on Android emulators in GitHub Actions produces black screenshots when hardware acceleration is disabled [community]

**Root cause**: The `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner` GitHub Action starts the emulator with `-gpu swiftshader_indirect` (software rendering). Some Android API levels (notably API 33+) have a known issue where `adb exec-out screencap` — which Detox uses internally for `takeScreenshot()` — returns a fully-black PNG when the GPU mode is `swiftshader_indirect`. The screenshot bytes are non-null (the file exists and has content) but every pixel is `#000000`.

```ts
// Symptom: screenshot files are created but are entirely black in CI
const screenshotPath = await device.takeScreenshot('cart-screen');
// File is created but all pixels are #000000 in GitHub Actions

// WORKAROUND 1 — use '-gpu guest' or '-gpu auto' in reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner:
// .github/workflows/detox.yml:
// - uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
//   with:
//     api-level: 33
//     arch: x86_64
//     gpu: 'swiftshader_indirect'   ← PROBLEM
//     emulator-options: '-no-snapshot -no-audio -no-window'
//     script: npx detox test -c android.emu.release

// Change to:
//     gpu: 'guest'                   ← WORKAROUND for API 33+ black screenshots
// Note: 'guest' requires KVM acceleration — only works on self-hosted runners or
//       GitHub's ubuntu-24.04 with nested virtualisation enabled.

// WORKAROUND 2 — skip screenshot assertions on Android CI, run locally or on macOS CI:
async function takeScreenshotGuarded(name: string): Promise<string | null> {
  if (device.getPlatform() === 'android' && process.env.CI === 'true') {
    console.warn(`[screenshot] Skipped on Android CI (black screenshot workaround)`);
    return null;
  }
  return device.takeScreenshot(name);
}

// WORKAROUND 3 — use Android API 30 (R) or below where the issue does not occur:
// android-emulator-runner api-level: 30 — swiftshader_indirect screenshots work correctly.
```

---

### Gotcha 155 — Detox server WebSocket port (`detoxServer.port`) must be unique per parallel CI shard — default port 8099 causes `EADDRINUSE` when multiple shards run on the same host [community]

**Root cause**: Detox starts an internal WebSocket server on port 8099 by default. When GitHub Actions matrix sharding runs N shards on the same macOS runner (common for iOS Simulator runs which cannot use `ubuntu` self-hosted runners with isolated VMs), all shards attempt to bind port 8099 simultaneously. The first shard succeeds; all others fail with `Error: listen EADDRINUSE 0.0.0.0:8099`.

```ts
// .detoxrc.js — derive unique Detox server port from JEST_WORKER_ID/shard index
const shardIndex = parseInt(process.env.SHARD_INDEX ?? process.env.JEST_WORKER_ID ?? '0', 10);
const detoxPort  = 8099 + shardIndex; // Shard 0→8099, 1→8100, 2→8101, ...

module.exports = {
  // ...
  session: {
    server: `ws://localhost:${detoxPort}`,
    sessionId: `MyApp-${shardIndex}`,
  },
  configurations: {
    'ios.sim.release': {
      // ...
    },
  },
};

// GitHub Actions matrix — pass SHARD_INDEX as env var per job:
// .github/workflows/detox-ios.yml:
// jobs:
//   detox:
//     strategy:
//       matrix:
//         shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
//     steps:
//       - name: Run Detox shard
//         env:
//           SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.shard }}
//         run: |
//           npx detox test -c ios.sim.release \
//             --shard-index ${{ matrix.shard }} \
//             --shard-count 4

// Alternative: use the DETOX_START_TIMESTAMP approach to avoid .detoxrc.js changes:
// Detox 20.x respects the DETOX_SERVER env var:
// export DETOX_SERVER="ws://localhost:$(( 8099 + SHARD_INDEX ))"
// npx detox test -c ios.sim.release
```

---

### Pattern 108 — Structured test artifact collection with `artifacts` config and `--record-logs` / `--take-screenshots` CLI flags for CI triage

Detox's artifact collection is controlled by the `artifacts` section in `.detoxrc.js` and overridden per-run via CLI flags. The recommended production pattern records logs and screenshots only on test failure to minimise CI storage, but enables full recording for dedicated "flakiness investigation" runs.

```ts
// .detoxrc.js — artifact collection configuration
module.exports = {
  artifacts: {
    rootDir: '.artifacts',                 // Base directory for all artifacts
    pathBuilder: './e2e/artifactPathBuilder.ts', // Custom path builder (see below)
    plugins: {
      // Record all app stdout/stderr logs
      log: process.env.CI ? { enabled: true, keepOnlyFailedTestsArtifacts: true } : { enabled: false },
      // Take a screenshot on test failure
      screenshot: {
        shouldTakeAutomaticScreenshot: process.env.CI === 'true',
        keepOnlyFailedTestsArtifacts: process.env.DETOX_FULL_ARTIFACTS !== 'true',
      },
      // Record video only in investigation runs (expensive)
      video: {
        enabled: process.env.DETOX_RECORD_VIDEO === 'true',
        keepOnlyFailedTestsArtifacts: true,
      },
      // Detox timeline (JSON performance trace)
      instruments: { enabled: false },
    },
  },
};

// e2e/artifactPathBuilder.ts — organise artifacts by shard and test name
import type { ArtifactPathBuilder, TestSummary } from 'detox';
import * as path from 'path';

export default class CustomPathBuilder implements ArtifactPathBuilder {
  buildPathForTestArtifact(artifactName: string, testSummary: TestSummary): string {
    const shardIndex = process.env.SHARD_INDEX ?? '0';
    const safeName = testSummary.fullName.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '_').slice(0, 60);
    return path.join('.artifacts', `shard-${shardIndex}`, safeName, artifactName);
  }
}

// CLI flags reference:
// --record-logs all        → record app stdout even on passing tests
// --record-logs failing    → record app stdout only on failing tests (default in CI)
// --take-screenshots all   → screenshot after every action
// --take-screenshots failing → screenshot on failure only (default in CI)
// --record-videos all      → video of every test (expensive)
// --record-performance all → instruments timeline (iOS only)
```

## Updated Anti-Patterns Checklist (Cycle 25 additions)

| Anti-Pattern | Fix |
|---|---|
| Relying on `by.type()` with pre-Fabric component names (e.g., `RCTScrollView`) after upgrading to RN 0.76+ New Architecture | Component type names changed in Fabric — use `byComponentType()` helper with platform-conditional type name map (Pattern 107) |
| Calling `device.setLocation()` before `launchApp()` on Android API 35 | GPS cold-start overwrites mock location — set location after app fully launches and location provider is initialised (Gotcha 152) |
| Using `tapReturnKey()` to trigger `onSubmitEditing` on Android with no `returnKeyType` on the TextInput | Missing `returnKeyType` causes Enter to insert newline not submit — set `returnKeyType="done"/"search"/"go"` in component (Gotcha 153) |
| Using `device.takeScreenshot()` for visual assertions on Android CI with `swiftshader_indirect` GPU mode | Returns all-black PNGs on API 33+ — switch to `gpu: 'guest'` on KVM runners or skip screenshot assertions on Android CI (Gotcha 154) |
| Running multiple Detox CI shards on the same host without unique `detoxServer.port` values | All shards collide on default port 8099 — derive port from `SHARD_INDEX` env var and set `session.server` accordingly (Gotcha 155) |
| Combining a manual `element.scroll()` before `waitFor.whileElement.scroll()` | Double-scroll overshoots the target — let `whileElement` scroll alone handle navigation to the target element (Gotcha 150) |
| Using two sequential `tap()` calls to simulate double-tap | Too much async delay between calls — use `multiTap(2)` instead (Pattern 102) |
| Asserting layout after `device.setOrientation()` without a `waitFor` wait | React Native needs 1-2 render passes after rotation — always `waitFor` a layout-dependent element before asserting dimensions (Pattern 103) |
