### Pattern 109 — `device.sendUserActivity()` for Handoff / Universal Links deep-link testing on iOS [official]

`device.sendUserActivity()` injects an `NSUserActivity` into a running iOS app, which is the mechanism underlying Handoff and Universal Links. Use it to test deep-link routing without relying on Safari or a companion app.

```ts
// e2e/deep-link.test.ts
import { device, expect, element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';

describe('Universal Links', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  });

  it('navigates to product detail via Handoff activity', async () => {
    // Simulate a Handoff / Universal Link open
    await device.sendUserActivity({
      activityType: 'NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb',
      userInfo: {},
      // The webpageURL maps to the Universal Link handler in AppDelegate
      webpageURL: 'https://myapp.example.com/products/42',
    });

    // Wait for the navigation stack to settle after activity injection
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(6000);

    await expect(element(by.id('product-title'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('product-id-label'))).toHaveText('42');
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Testing `NSUserActivityDelegate`-based flows, continuing activities from Apple Watch, or validating Universal Link routing without launching Safari. **Not suitable for** Android App Links — use `device.openURL()` with an `https://` scheme instead. **Alternative:** `device.openURL()` works for simple deep links but cannot inject `userInfo` payloads or `activityType`, making it insufficient for Handoff.

---

### Pattern 110 — `element(by.id('x')).adjustSliderToPosition(normalizedPosition)` for slider components [official]

Detox's `adjustSliderToPosition()` accepts a normalized float in `[0, 1]` representing the target position along the slider track. Use it to test range-based inputs — volume controls, budget sliders, seek bars.

```ts
// e2e/settings.test.ts
import { element, by, expect, waitFor } from 'detox';

it('sets notification volume to 80%', async () => {
  // Navigate to settings
  await element(by.id('settings-menu-item')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('notification-volume-slider')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(3000);

  // normalizedPosition: 0.0 = min, 1.0 = max, 0.8 = 80%
  await element(by.id('notification-volume-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.8);

  // Verify displayed percentage label reflects the new value
  await expect(element(by.id('volume-percentage-label'))).toHaveText('80%');
});

it('disables sound when slider is at 0', async () => {
  await element(by.id('settings-menu-item')).tap();
  await element(by.id('notification-volume-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.0);
  await expect(element(by.id('volume-percentage-label'))).toHaveText('0%');
  // Confirm the mute icon appears
  await expect(element(by.id('mute-icon'))).toBeVisible();
});
```

**When to use:** Any `<Slider>` component (React Native's built-in or `@react-native-community/slider`). **Gotcha:** `adjustSliderToPosition()` is iOS-only in Detox through v20.x — on Android it triggers an `UnsupportedOperationException`. On Android, use `swipe('right', 'slow', normalizedPercentage)` or set the value programmatically via a test mock bridge. **Alternative:** `element.scroll()` on the slider track, but it is far less reliable for precise percentage values.

---

### Pattern 111 — `device.bootSimulator()` / `device.shutdownSimulator()` for lifecycle testing and CI pre-warm scripts [official]

For advanced CI pipelines, programmatic simulator lifecycle management via `xcrun simctl` (invoked from Detox setup scripts) lets you pre-warm multiple simulators in parallel before distributing shards, or shut down simulators for memory management on shared runners.

```ts
// scripts/pre-warm-simulators.ts
// Run as a pre-step before the test matrix: ts-node scripts/pre-warm-simulators.ts
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

interface SimConfig {
  name: string;
  udid?: string; // runtime UDID, or use name for xcrun simctl
}

const SIMULATOR_CONFIGS: SimConfig[] = [
  { name: 'iPhone 16'     },
  { name: 'iPhone 16 Pro' },
];

async function preWarmAll(): Promise<void> {
  for (const cfg of SIMULATOR_CONFIGS) {
    console.log(`Booting simulator: ${cfg.name}...`);
    // xcrun simctl boot is idempotent — already-booted sims return error code but are fine
    execSync(`xcrun simctl boot "${cfg.name}" 2>/dev/null || true`, { stdio: 'inherit' });
  }

  // Give SpringBoard time to initialize (avoids "SpringBoard not ready" Detox error)
  console.log('Waiting 20s for SpringBoard to initialize across all simulators...');
  await new Promise<void>(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 20_000));
  console.log('Pre-warm complete.');
}

preWarmAll().catch(err => { console.error(err); process.exit(1); });

// In CI (GitHub Actions matrix job):
// jobs:
//   pre-warm:
//     runs-on: macos-15
//     steps:
//       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
//       - run: npx ts-node scripts/pre-warm-simulators.ts
//   detox-shard:
//     needs: pre-warm
//     strategy: { matrix: { shard: [0,1,2,3] } }
//     runs-on: macos-15
//     steps:
//       - run: npx detox test -c ios.sim.release --reuse ...
```

**When to use:** CI pipelines with 3+ parallel iOS shards where cold simulator boot costs 90–120 s per shard. Pre-warming in a setup job reduces total wall-clock time significantly. **Not suitable for** single-shard pipelines where the overhead of orchestrating pre-warm exceeds the savings. **Alternative:** `--reuse` flag on `detox test` reuses already-booted simulators within a single CI job but does not help with cross-job parallelism.

---

### Pattern 112 — `waitFor(element).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout()` as an absence guard after dismissal [official]

Asserting that an element is gone after an action (e.g., a modal closes, a toast disappears) prevents false-positive tests that pass before the dismissal animation completes.

```ts
// e2e/modal.test.ts
import { element, by, waitFor, expect, device } from 'detox';

it('dismisses the onboarding modal and does not show it again', async () => {
  await waitFor(element(by.id('onboarding-modal')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(4000);

  // Close the modal
  await element(by.id('onboarding-close-btn')).tap();

  // CORRECT: wait for element to disappear, not just check immediately after tap
  await waitFor(element(by.id('onboarding-modal')))
    .not.toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(3000);

  // Navigate away and return to confirm the modal does not re-appear
  await device.pressBack();
  await element(by.id('home-nav-item')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

  // Modal must not reappear — absence guard with short timeout
  await waitFor(element(by.id('onboarding-modal')))
    .not.toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(1500);
});
```

**When to use:** After dismissal, delete, or hide actions where the element should no longer be on screen. Prevents tests from incorrectly passing because the tap fires but the animation has not finished removing the element before the next assertion runs. **Gotcha:** The timeout on `.not.toBeVisible()` is a maximum wait — if the element is already invisible the assertion passes immediately. Set it long enough to cover the full animation duration.

---

### Pattern 113 — `element(by.id('x')).scrollTo('top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right')` for one-shot edge navigation [official]

`scrollTo()` jumps a scroll container directly to an edge without specifying a pixel distance. It is faster and more reliable than repeated `scroll()` calls when the target is always at the list edge.

```ts
// e2e/chat.test.ts
import { element, by, expect, waitFor } from 'detox';

it('scrolls to top to reveal the oldest message and back to bottom', async () => {
  // App opens at bottom of the list — scroll to top in one action
  await element(by.id('message-list')).scrollTo('top');

  await waitFor(element(by.id('message-item-0')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(3000);

  await expect(element(by.id('message-item-0'))).toHaveText('Welcome to the channel!');

  // Scroll back to bottom to confirm the "latest" indicator disappears
  await element(by.id('message-list')).scrollTo('bottom');

  await waitFor(element(by.id('new-messages-indicator')))
    .not.toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(2000);
});

it('loads more history via pull-to-refresh at the top', async () => {
  await element(by.id('message-list')).scrollTo('top');

  // Pull-to-refresh gesture at the scroll top
  await element(by.id('message-list')).swipe('down', 'slow', 0.5, 0.1, 0.1);

  await waitFor(element(by.id('history-loading-indicator')))
    .not.toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(6000);
});
```

**When to use:** FlatList, ScrollView, or SectionList tests where you need to reach a list edge quickly. Prefer over `scroll(NNN, 'pixels')` which requires knowing content height. **Limitation:** Does not work reliably on horizontal `ScrollView` on Android API below 31 — use `swipe('left'/'right')` instead for horizontal lists on older Android.

---

### Pattern 114 — `device.clearKeychain()` for resetting biometric and credential state between tests [official]

On iOS, `device.clearKeychain()` deletes all keychain items belonging to the test app, giving each test a clean credential state without reinstalling the app. Equivalent to a fresh install for auth-dependent tests.

```ts
// e2e/auth.test.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

describe('Authentication — credential persistence', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    // Ensure no residual credentials from previous test run
    await device.clearKeychain();
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    // Reset between tests so auth state does not leak to subsequent tests
    await device.clearKeychain();
    await device.reloadReactNative();
  });

  it('redirects to login when no stored credentials exist', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('login-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('stays logged in after reload when credentials are stored in keychain', async () => {
    // Log in first
    await element(by.id('email-input')).typeText('user@example.com');
    await element(by.id('password-input')).typeText('S3cur3P@ss!');
    await element(by.id('login-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

    // Reload — credentials should persist via Keychain Services
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('login-screen'))).not.toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Auth tests that rely on Keychain Services (e.g., `react-native-keychain`, Expo `SecureStore`). Prevents credential state leaking between test files when running in a shared simulator. **iOS only** — Android has no equivalent single API; use `device.launchApp({ newInstance: true })` or clear `SharedPreferences`/`EncryptedSharedPreferences` via a helper bridge. **Tradeoff:** Clearing the keychain is slower than `reloadReactNative()` alone — only use in auth-specific suites.

---

### Pattern 115 — Custom `DetoxCircusEnvironment` hook for per-test timing instrumentation [community]

By extending `DetoxCircusEnvironment`, you can inject timing probes around every test lifecycle event without modifying individual test files. Useful for detecting slow tests and building a performance budget dashboard.

```ts
// e2e/environment/TimingEnvironment.ts
import { DetoxCircusEnvironment } from 'detox/runners/jest';
import type { Circus } from '@jest/types';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

interface TestTiming { name: string; durationMs: number; suite: string; }

export default class TimingEnvironment extends DetoxCircusEnvironment {
  private timings: TestTiming[] = [];
  private testStart = 0;
  private currentSuite = '';

  async handleTestEvent(event: Circus.Event, state: Circus.State): Promise<void> {
    switch (event.name) {
      case 'describe_block_start':
        this.currentSuite = event.describeBlock.name;
        break;
      case 'test_start':
        this.testStart = Date.now();
        break;
      case 'test_done':
        this.timings.push({
          name: event.test.name,
          suite: this.currentSuite,
          durationMs: Date.now() - this.testStart,
        });
        break;
    }
    await super.handleTestEvent(event, state);
  }

  async teardown(): Promise<void> {
    const outDir = path.join(process.cwd(), '.artifacts', 'timings');
    fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(
      path.join(outDir, `shard-${process.env.SHARD_INDEX ?? '0'}.json`),
      JSON.stringify(this.timings, null, 2),
    );
    await super.teardown();
  }
}

// jest.config.js — point testEnvironment at the custom class:
// testEnvironment: './e2e/environment/TimingEnvironment.ts'
```

**When to use:** Teams with >50 E2E tests where slow tests are causing CI timeouts without clear culprits. The JSON artifacts are trivially merged across shards and fed into a CI dashboard. **Tradeoff:** Adds a class to maintain; Detox major version upgrades may require updating the `DetoxCircusEnvironment` import path. **Alternative:** Jest's `--verbose` flag shows per-test duration but not in machine-parseable form. [community]

---

### Pattern 116 — `device.installApp()` / `device.uninstallApp()` for multi-app interaction testing [official]

When testing flows that span two apps (e.g., a share extension, a companion widget app, or an auth redirect), install both apps before tests and coordinate teardown explicitly.

```ts
// e2e/share-extension.test.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';

const COMPANION_APP_ID     = 'com.example.CompanionApp';
const COMPANION_BINARY_PATH = process.env.COMPANION_APP_BINARY!;

describe('Share Extension', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    // Install the companion app that triggers the share extension
    await device.installApp(COMPANION_BINARY_PATH);
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    // Clean up the companion app so it does not affect other test suites
    await device.uninstallApp(COMPANION_APP_ID);
  });

  it('receives a shared URL from the companion app via share extension', async () => {
    // Companion app triggers share sheet via custom URL scheme
    await device.openURL({
      url: 'companion://share?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Farticle%2F1',
      sourceApp: COMPANION_APP_ID,
    });

    // Main app is invoked via the share extension handler
    await waitFor(element(by.id('shared-article-preview')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(8000);

    await element(by.id('save-article-btn')).tap();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('saved-confirmation-toast')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Apps with share extensions, Today widgets, notification content extensions, or SSO broker apps. **Limitation:** Android app-switching is fragile in emulators — prefer mocking the inter-app intent payload in unit tests for Android. **Tradeoff:** Multi-app E2E tests are significantly slower and harder to debug than single-app tests; reserve for critical user journeys involving external app handoff.

---

### Pattern 117 — `--inspect-brk` + VS Code remote debugger for stepping through E2E test code [community]

Running Detox with `--inspect-brk` starts the Jest process with the Node.js inspector, allowing you to set breakpoints in test code and step through assertions in VS Code — enormously useful when a test fails for an opaque reason.

```ts
// .vscode/launch.json — Detox debug launch configuration
// {
//   "name": "Detox E2E Debug",
//   "type": "node",
//   "request": "attach",
//   "port": 9229,
//   "restart": true,
//   "localRoot": "${workspaceFolder}",
//   "remoteRoot": "${workspaceFolder}"
// }

// package.json — add a debug script (--runInBand is REQUIRED for --inspect-brk)
// "scripts": {
//   "e2e:debug": "node --inspect-brk ./node_modules/.bin/jest --config e2e/jest.config.js --testNamePattern 'your test name' --runInBand"
// }

// e2e/login.test.ts — use debugger statement like in unit tests
import { element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

it('debug: login with valid credentials', async () => {
  await element(by.id('email-input')).typeText('admin@example.com');
  await element(by.id('password-input')).typeText('password123');

  debugger; // VS Code pauses here when attached to port 9229

  await element(by.id('login-btn')).tap();

  await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(5000);

  debugger; // Pause again after tap — inspect actual screen state in VS Code

  await expect(element(by.id('user-greeting'))).toBeVisible();
});

// Run: npm run e2e:debug
// Then in VS Code: Run → Start Debugging → "Detox E2E Debug"
// IMPORTANT: --runInBand is mandatory; parallel workers all attempt port 9229 and collide
```

**When to use:** Debugging intermittent failures or complex multi-step flows where `console.log` debugging is insufficient. **Not suitable for** CI — `--inspect-brk` pauses execution until a debugger attaches, so always exclude from pipeline scripts. **Community insight:** Always pair with `--testNamePattern` to run only the failing test; running all tests with `--inspect-brk` is impractical. [community]

---

### Pattern 118 — `element(by.id('x')).getAttributes()` with structured type narrowing for iOS vs Android attribute shapes [official]

`getAttributes()` returns different shapes on iOS (`ElementAttributes`) and Android (`AndroidElementAttributes`). Always narrow the type before reading platform-specific fields to avoid runtime errors on the opposite platform.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/getElementBounds.ts
import { element, by } from 'detox';

interface Bounds { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number; }

export async function getElementBounds(testID: string): Promise<Bounds> {
  const attrs = await element(by.id(testID)).getAttributes();

  // getAttributes() returns an array when multiple elements match — guard for that
  if (Array.isArray(attrs)) {
    throw new Error(`getElementBounds: multiple elements match testID="${testID}"`);
  }

  // Both iOS and Android share the 'frame' property in Detox 20.x
  const { frame } = attrs;
  if (!frame) {
    throw new Error(`getElementBounds: element "${testID}" has no frame — is it visible?`);
  }

  return { x: frame.x, y: frame.y, width: frame.width, height: frame.height };
}

// e2e/layout.test.ts — use the helper to assert pixel dimensions
it('product image fills at least 40% of screen width', async () => {
  const imageBounds  = await getElementBounds('product-hero-image');
  const screenBounds = await getElementBounds('root-screen-container');

  const ratio = imageBounds.width / screenBounds.width;
  expect(ratio).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0.4);
  expect(ratio).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1.0);
});
```

**When to use:** Layout regression tests, accessibility layout audits, and verifying responsive design breakpoints. **Tradeoff:** `getAttributes()` is a bridge call with ~50–100 ms overhead per call — do not call it inside tight loops. **Alternative:** `captureViewHierarchy()` gives all elements at once but requires parsing XML; `getAttributes()` is preferred for single-element checks.

---

### Pattern 119 — `by.id().withAncestor()` for scoped interaction within repeating list items [official]

When a FlatList renders many items that all have children with the same `testID` (e.g., each item has a `like-btn`), `by.id('like-btn')` is ambiguous. `withAncestor()` scopes the match to the item container, making interactions unambiguous without relying on `atIndex(N)`.

```ts
// e2e/feed.test.ts
import { element, by, expect } from 'detox';

// Component structure:
// <View testID={`feed-item-${post.id}`}>
//   <Text testID="post-title">{post.title}</Text>
//   <TouchableOpacity testID="like-btn" onPress={handleLike}>
//     <Text testID="like-count">{post.likes}</Text>
//   </TouchableOpacity>
// </View>

it('likes the second post without affecting the first', async () => {
  // Scoped matcher — only matches 'like-btn' that is a DESCENDANT of 'feed-item-post-2'
  const likeBtn = element(
    by.id('like-btn').withAncestor(by.id('feed-item-post-2'))
  );
  const likeCount = element(
    by.id('like-count').withAncestor(by.id('feed-item-post-2'))
  );

  await likeBtn.tap();

  // Confirm second post like count updated
  await expect(likeCount).toHaveText('1');

  // Confirm first post like count was NOT affected
  await expect(
    element(by.id('like-count').withAncestor(by.id('feed-item-post-1')))
  ).toHaveText('0');
});
```

**When to use:** Any list where multiple items share child `testID` values. Strongly preferred over `atIndex(N)` because it does not depend on list ordering, which changes when items are added or re-sorted. **Limitation:** `withAncestor()` traverses the entire ancestor chain — it can match elements nested deeply inside the ancestor, not only immediate children. Add an intermediate container with a unique `testID` if exact-parent matching is needed.

---

### Pattern 120 — Biometric prompt testing via `device.setBiometricEnrollment()` and `device.matchFace()` / `device.unmatchFace()` [official]

Detox exposes simulator-level biometric simulation APIs for testing Touch ID / Face ID flows without relying on real hardware.

```ts
// e2e/biometrics.test.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

describe('Biometric Authentication (iOS Simulator)', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    // Enroll Face ID on the simulator before the test suite starts
    await device.setBiometricEnrollment(true);
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      permissions: { faceid: 'YES' },
    });
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    // Dis-enroll so other test suites start with a known biometric state
    await device.setBiometricEnrollment(false);
  });

  it('unlocks the app with a successful Face ID match', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('biometric-prompt'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

    // Simulate a successful Face ID authentication
    await device.matchFace();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    await expect(element(by.id('biometric-prompt'))).not.toBeVisible();
  });

  it('shows an error after a failed Face ID attempt and falls back to PIN', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('biometric-prompt'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

    // Simulate a Face ID mismatch — biometric denial
    await device.unmatchFace();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('biometric-error-message'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('biometric-error-message'))).toHaveText('Face ID not recognized');

    // Verify the fallback to PIN prompt appears after failure
    await element(by.id('use-pin-instead-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('pin-entry-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Testing `react-native-biometrics`, `expo-local-authentication`, or any `LAContext`-based flow on iOS. **iOS Simulator only** — use `device.matchFinger()` / `device.unmatchFinger()` for Android fingerprint testing. **Tradeoff:** `setBiometricEnrollment(true)` persists across simulator boots — always dis-enroll in `afterAll` to avoid polluting unrelated test suites.

---

### Gotcha 156 — `element(by.id('x')).typeText()` on Android API 35 with autofill enabled inserts suggestion text before the typed string [community]

**Root cause**: Android 35 enhanced autofill suggestions are displayed inline (as a suffix of the current input value) rather than in a dropdown. When Detox calls `typeText()`, the Espresso text injection fires the `TextWatcher` which triggers autofill suggestion retrieval. On emulators with autofill services enabled, the suggestion text is concatenated with the typed value before assertions run. The result is a `TextInput` containing `"test@example.com (My Account)"` when only `"test@example.com"` was typed.

```ts
// BAD — autofill suggestion suffix corrupts typed value on Android API 35
await element(by.id('email-input')).typeText('test@example.com');
await expect(element(by.id('email-input'))).toHaveText('test@example.com');
// FAILS: actual text is 'test@example.com (My Account)' on Android 35

// FIX 1 — use replaceText() instead of typeText() for value-sensitive assertions
await element(by.id('email-input')).replaceText('test@example.com');
await expect(element(by.id('email-input'))).toHaveText('test@example.com');

// FIX 2 — configure the component to disable autofill in tests
// <TextInput autoComplete="off" autoCorrect={false} testID="email-input" />

// FIX 3 — cross-platform helper that uses replaceText on Android
async function safeTypeText(testID: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
  if (device.getPlatform() === 'android') {
    // replaceText bypasses the TextWatcher autofill trigger on Android 35
    await element(by.id(testID)).replaceText(text);
  } else {
    await element(by.id(testID)).typeText(text);
  }
}

// Usage:
await safeTypeText('email-input', 'test@example.com');
await safeTypeText('password-input', 'S3cur3P@ss!');
await element(by.id('login-btn')).tap();
await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
```

---

### Gotcha 157 — `waitFor(element).toBeVisible()` never resolves when the element is inside a `Modal` rendered via React Native's Portal API [community]

**Root cause**: Portal-based modals (from `react-native-paper`, `@rneui/themed`, and custom portal implementations) render content into a separate React root at the top of the view hierarchy. If the portal's animation driver runs outside the main React root, Detox's synchronization window can close before the portal content becomes visible, causing `waitFor` to time out even though the element is visually present.

```ts
// SYMPTOM — waitFor times out even though the Dialog is visually on screen
await element(by.id('open-dialog-btn')).tap();
await waitFor(element(by.id('dialog-content')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(5000); // Times out on Android with react-native-paper Dialog

// FIX 1 — add testID to the Portal host, wait for it before the portal content
// In the component: <Portal.Host testID="portal-host">
await element(by.id('open-dialog-btn')).tap();
await waitFor(element(by.id('portal-host'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
await waitFor(element(by.id('dialog-content'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

// FIX 2 — disable Detox synchronization during the tap, then re-enable
await device.disableSynchronization();
await element(by.id('open-dialog-btn')).tap();
await new Promise<void>(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 600)); // let portal render
await device.enableSynchronization();
await waitFor(element(by.id('dialog-content'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

// FIX 3 — iOS only: wait for RCTModalHostView to appear (no testID needed)
// await waitFor(element(by.type('RCTModalHostView'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
// Then wait for the specific content:
await waitFor(element(by.id('dialog-content'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
```

---

### Gotcha 158 — `device.reloadReactNative()` on Expo SDK 53 retriggers the splash screen, blocking all element visibility [community]

**Root cause**: Expo SDK 53 changed `expo-splash-screen` internals so that the splash screen guard (`SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync()`) is re-evaluated on every React root mount — including the one triggered by Detox's `reloadReactNative()`. In previous SDK versions, reloading the JS bundle did not re-run the native splash screen logic. After the reload, all UI elements are behind the splash guard until `SplashScreen.hideAsync()` is called in the app's boot sequence.

```ts
// BAD — after reloadReactNative() on Expo SDK 53, elements are behind the splash screen
await device.reloadReactNative();
await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000); // FAILS

// FIX 1 — wait for the splash screen to disappear before asserting UI
await device.reloadReactNative();
// Expo SDK 53: splash screen container uses testID 'expo-splash-screen-container'
await waitFor(element(by.id('expo-splash-screen-container')))
  .not.toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(8000);
await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

// FIX 2 — disable preventAutoHideAsync in E2E builds via a launch argument
// In app code (app.tsx or App.tsx entry):
// if (!process.env.E2E) { await SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync(); }
// In .detoxrc.js:
// configurations: { 'ios.sim.release': { app: { launchArgs: { E2E: 'true' } } } }

// FIX 3 — prefer launchApp({ newInstance: true }) over reloadReactNative() for Expo SDK 53+
beforeEach(async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true, launchArgs: { E2E: 'true' } });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
});
```

### Gotcha 159 — `element(by.text()).tap()` on a `Text` inside a `Pressable` fires the wrong touch target on iOS 18+ [community]

**Root cause**: iOS 18 changed hit-test priority so that `Pressable`'s touch handler frame no longer automatically receives taps sent to a descendant `Text` node. When `by.text()` matches a `Text` element inside a `Pressable`, Detox's XCTest injection sends the tap to the `Text` node's frame. On iOS 17 and below, this propagated up to the `Pressable`; on iOS 18+, the `Text` consumes the tap in layouts where `hitSlop` is used or where `Pressable` has a custom `onPress` without pointer events set.

```ts
// BAD — taps the Text node directly, Pressable.onPress not fired on iOS 18+
await element(by.text('Add to Cart')).tap();
await waitFor(element(by.id('cart-count-badge'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
// FAILS on iOS 18+ — Pressable.onPress is never invoked

// FIX 1 — add testID to the Pressable and use by.id()
// Component: <Pressable testID="add-to-cart-btn" onPress={handleAdd}><Text>Add to Cart</Text></Pressable>
await element(by.id('add-to-cart-btn')).tap();

// FIX 2 — scope with withAncestor when testID cannot be added to the Pressable
await element(by.text('Add to Cart').withAncestor(by.id('product-card-42'))).tap();

// Defensive helper: prefers testID, falls back to scoped text match
async function tapByIdOrText(
  testID: string,
  fallbackText: string,
  ancestorID?: string,
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await element(by.id(testID)).tap();
  } catch {
    const matcher = ancestorID
      ? by.text(fallbackText).withAncestor(by.id(ancestorID))
      : by.text(fallbackText);
    await element(matcher).tap();
  }
}

// Usage:
await tapByIdOrText('add-to-cart-btn', 'Add to Cart', 'product-card-42');
await waitFor(element(by.id('cart-count-badge'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
```

---

### Gotcha 160 — `forceExit: true` in `jest.config.js` skips Detox `globalTeardown`, producing 0-byte screenshots and leaked simulator sessions [community]

**Root cause**: `forceExit: true` calls `process.exit()` after tests complete, bypassing Jest's `afterAll`/`globalTeardown` lifecycle. Detox uses `globalTeardown` to call `detox.cleanup()`, which flushes pending artifact writes, closes the WebSocket session, and stops the simulator (when `--cleanup` is set). With `forceExit: true`, cleanup is skipped: screenshots are 0-byte files, the WebSocket session leaks, and on the next run Detox may attach to the stale session and see unexpected state.

```ts
// BAD — jest.config.js
// module.exports = {
//   testEnvironment: './e2e/environment.ts',
//   forceExit: true,      // ← NEVER use with Detox — bypasses globalTeardown
//   globalSetup: 'detox/runners/jest/globalSetup',
//   globalTeardown: 'detox/runners/jest/globalTeardown',
// };

// CORRECT — increase testTimeout instead of using forceExit
// jest.config.js:
module.exports = {
  testEnvironment: './e2e/environment.ts',
  globalSetup:    'detox/runners/jest/globalSetup',
  globalTeardown: 'detox/runners/jest/globalTeardown',
  testTimeout: 120_000, // 2-minute per-test timeout — prevents individual test hangs
  // Do NOT set forceExit: true
};

// If tests are hanging and you need to diagnose open handles:
// npx jest --config e2e/jest.config.js --detectOpenHandles
// This prints the stack trace of the open handle without skipping cleanup.

// Common causes of Detox test hangs (that tempt people to use forceExit):
// 1. Uncleared setInterval in a mock module — fix: clearInterval in afterAll
// 2. Unresolved Promise from a mock server — fix: await server.close() in afterAll
// 3. WS session from a previous test left open — fix: remove forceExit, fix the root cause

afterAll(async () => {
  // Always clean up mock servers and polling intervals
  clearInterval(globalPollingInterval);
  await mockWebSocketServer.close();
});
```

## Updated Anti-Patterns Checklist (Cycle 26 additions)

| Anti-Pattern | Fix |
|---|---|
| Using `by.text()` to tap a `Text` inside a `Pressable` on iOS 18+ | iOS 18 hit-test change means the Text node consumes the tap — add `testID` to the `Pressable` and use `by.id()` (Gotcha 159) |
| Using `forceExit: true` in `jest.config.js` with Detox | Force-exit skips `globalTeardown` → Detox cleanup never runs → 0-byte screenshots, leaked WebSocket sessions — use `testTimeout` instead (Gotcha 160) |
| Calling `typeText()` on Android API 35 email inputs with autofill enabled | Autofill suggestion is appended to the typed value — use `replaceText()` on Android or set `autoComplete="off"` in the component (Gotcha 156) |
| Using `waitFor(modal-content).toBeVisible()` when modal is rendered via a Portal | Portal runs in a separate React root — Detox sync exits before portal renders — wait for portal host first or disable sync around the tap (Gotcha 157) |
| Using `device.reloadReactNative()` in Expo SDK 53 without a splash guard | Reload re-triggers splash screen, blocking all element visibility — wait for splash dismissal testID or pass `E2E` launch arg to skip `preventAutoHideAsync` (Gotcha 158) |
| Using `adjustSliderToPosition()` on Android | iOS-only API in Detox 20.x — throws `UnsupportedOperationException` on Android — use `swipe()` with a normalized speed value on Android (Pattern 110) |
| Reading `getAttributes()` result without checking for array return | Multiple matching elements return `ElementAttributes[]` not a single object — always check `Array.isArray()` before accessing `frame` (Pattern 118) |
| Using `atIndex(N)` for list items instead of `withAncestor()` | Index-based selection breaks when list order changes — scope by parent container `testID` using `withAncestor()` instead (Pattern 119) |

### Pattern 121 — `element(by.id('x')).pinch(scale, speed, angle)` for multi-touch zoom gestures [official]

Detox exposes `pinch()` to simulate a two-finger pinch-in or pinch-out on a map, image, or custom gesture surface. The `scale` parameter is normalized: values > 1 expand (zoom in), values < 1 contract (zoom out). `speed` accepts `'slow'` or `'fast'`. `angle` (0–360 degrees) controls the rotation of the two-finger axis.

```ts
// e2e/map.test.ts
import { element, by, expect, waitFor, device } from 'detox';

describe('Map Zoom gestures', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('map-view'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(6000);
  });

  it('zooms into the map to reveal street-level detail', async () => {
    // Pinch-out: scale > 1 = zoom in (expand two fingers apart)
    await element(by.id('map-view')).pinch(2.0, 'slow', 0);
    // Verify the zoom label / detail layer appears
    await expect(element(by.id('street-label-layer'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('zooms out to the city overview', async () => {
    // Pinch-in: scale < 1 = zoom out (bring two fingers together)
    await element(by.id('map-view')).pinch(0.5, 'slow', 0);
    await expect(element(by.id('city-boundary-outline'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('rotates the map 45 degrees using angled pinch', async () => {
    // angle parameter rotates the gesture axis — useful for MapKit rotation
    await element(by.id('map-view')).pinch(1.0, 'slow', 45);
    await expect(element(by.id('rotation-compass-indicator'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Maps (`react-native-maps`), PDF viewers, image galleries, canvas drawing apps. **Not suitable for** Android — `pinch()` is an iOS Simulator-only API in Detox 20.x. On Android use `element.scroll()` or a two-pointer swipe helper. **Tradeoff:** `scale` semantics are inverted between iOS and Android (iOS: 2.0 = zoom in; Android custom: depends on implementation) — wrap in a `platformPinch()` helper if you share tests across platforms. [official]

---

### Pattern 122 — `device.launchApp({ permissions: { camera: 'NO' } })` + `device.openURL('app-settings:')` for permission-recovery flow testing [community]

Testing the "go to Settings" permission recovery flow requires launching with a denied permission state, triggering the in-app recovery CTA, then re-launching with permission granted to simulate the user toggling it in Settings.

```ts
// e2e/camera-permission-recovery.test.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

describe('Camera permission recovery flow', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    // Launch with camera permission explicitly denied to simulate cold state
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      permissions: { camera: 'NO' },
    });
  });

  it('shows the permission-denied banner after attempting to open camera', async () => {
    await element(by.id('open-camera-btn')).tap();

    // The app shows a "Grant camera access" CTA after denial
    await waitFor(element(by.id('camera-denied-banner')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(4000);
    await expect(element(by.id('go-to-settings-btn'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('recovers after returning from Settings with permission granted', async () => {
    // Simulate the user toggling the permission in iOS Settings and returning
    // Re-launch with permission now granted — closest approximation available in Detox
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: false,
      permissions: { camera: 'YES' },
    });
    await element(by.id('open-camera-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('camera-preview')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Testing the "permission denied → go to Settings → return" recovery UX present in camera, microphone, contacts, and location flows. **Tradeoff:** Detox cannot automate interactions inside Settings.app — use a second `launchApp({ permissions: { camera: 'YES' } })` to simulate "user returned and granted". `newInstance: false` preserves the app's navigation stack so the camera screen reloads in place. **Not suitable for** verifying the Settings.app UI itself. [community]

---

### Pattern 123 — Structured `describe` + `beforeAll` hierarchy for test suite speed — lazy `newInstance` vs. `reloadReactNative()` tiering [community]

Using `newInstance: true` for every test is the safest but slowest approach (~6–12 s per cold boot). Structuring tests in a three-tier hierarchy allows maximum isolation only where needed and fast JS reloads for the majority of tests.

```ts
// e2e/checkout.test.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';
import { loginAs } from './helpers/auth';

/**
 * Tier 1 — Cold boot once per suite (newInstance: true)
 *   → covers tests that mutate Keychain, push notification state, or crash recovery
 * Tier 2 — JS reload per describe block (reloadReactNative())
 *   → covers feature areas; native state persists across the block
 * Tier 3 — No reset between tests inside a describe block
 *   → covers sequential user flows where state is intentionally carried forward
 */
describe('Checkout Suite', () => {
  // Tier 1: cold boot once for the entire suite
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await loginAs('checkout-user@example.com');
  });

  // Tier 2: JS reload isolates each feature area
  describe('Cart', () => {
    beforeAll(async () => {
      await device.reloadReactNative();
    });

    it('adds item to cart', async () => {
      await element(by.id('product-add-btn')).tap();
      await waitFor(element(by.id('cart-badge'))).toHaveText('1').withTimeout(3000);
    });

    // Tier 3: no reset — test intentionally builds on prior cart state
    it('shows item in cart drawer', async () => {
      await element(by.id('cart-icon')).tap();
      await waitFor(element(by.id('cart-item-0'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    });
  });

  describe('Payment', () => {
    beforeAll(async () => {
      await device.reloadReactNative();
    });

    it('renders the payment form', async () => {
      await element(by.id('proceed-to-payment-btn')).tap();
      await waitFor(element(by.id('payment-form'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    });
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Any medium-to-large Detox suite (>20 tests). **Tradeoff:** Tier 3 (stateful) tests fail in isolation when run with `--testNamePattern`. Keep the sequential dependency explicit with a comment. **Community lesson [community]:** Teams at Shopify and Airbnb have reported 30–50% suite-time reduction by moving from per-test `newInstance` to this three-tier model — the key insight is that native storage is almost never dirtied by feature-area tests, only by explicit Keychain/permissions operations.

---

### Pattern 124 — `device.setNetworkConditions()` with `try/finally` reset guard for offline/slow-network simulation on iOS Simulator [official]

`device.setNetworkConditions()` (Detox 20.49+, iOS Simulator only) lets tests simulate bandwidth throttling, packet loss, and offline conditions. Wrap network degradation tests with `try/finally` to ensure conditions are reset regardless of test outcome.

```ts
// e2e/network-resilience.test.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

const OFFLINE = {
  wifi: { downSpeed: 0, upSpeed: 0, packetLoss: 100 }, // fully offline
};
const SLOW_3G = {
  wifi: { downSpeed: 400_000, upSpeed: 150_000, packetLoss: 5 }, // ~400 kbps
};

describe('Offline resilience', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    // Always reset — failure to reset bleeds conditions into subsequent tests
    await device.resetNetworkConditions();
  });

  it('shows an offline banner within 3 s of losing connectivity', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-feed'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
    try {
      await device.setNetworkConditions(OFFLINE);
      await element(by.id('refresh-btn')).tap();
      await waitFor(element(by.id('offline-banner')))
        .toBeVisible()
        .withTimeout(6000);
    } finally {
      await device.resetNetworkConditions();
    }
  });

  it('shows a degraded-quality indicator on slow 3G', async () => {
    try {
      await device.setNetworkConditions(SLOW_3G);
      await element(by.id('load-hd-video-btn')).tap();
      await waitFor(element(by.id('low-quality-indicator')))
        .toBeVisible()
        .withTimeout(10000);
    } finally {
      await device.resetNetworkConditions();
    }
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Testing offline banners, retry logic, degraded-quality indicators, and request timeout flows on iOS Simulator. **Tradeoff:** Only works on iOS Simulator — `setNetworkConditions()` is a silent no-op on physical iOS devices and all Android targets (Gotcha 136). **Alternative:** Use a lightweight mock server with `launchArgs` to inject pre-canned error responses — works cross-platform and is more reproducible in CI. [official]

---

### Pattern 125 — `element(by.id('x')).tapAtPoint({ x, y })` for precise coordinate taps on canvas or custom drawing views [official]

`tapAtPoint()` sends a tap to an absolute coordinate within the element's bounds. Use it when the target is a custom canvas, chart, or drawing surface where there are no child accessibility elements to target.

```ts
// e2e/canvas-drawing.test.ts
import { element, by, expect, waitFor, device } from 'detox';

describe('Canvas Drawing Tool', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('drawing-canvas'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('draws a stroke at the center of the canvas', async () => {
    // Get canvas dimensions to compute center point
    const attrs = await element(by.id('drawing-canvas')).getAttributes();
    if (Array.isArray(attrs)) throw new Error('Expected single element');

    const { width, height } = attrs.frame;
    const center = { x: Math.round(width / 2), y: Math.round(height / 2) };

    await element(by.id('drawing-canvas')).tapAtPoint(center);
    await expect(element(by.id('stroke-count'))).toHaveText('1');
  });

  it('taps the top-left corner to place a dot', async () => {
    await element(by.id('drawing-canvas')).tapAtPoint({ x: 10, y: 10 });
    await expect(element(by.id('stroke-count'))).toHaveText('1');
  });

  it('taps a chart data point by computed position', async () => {
    // For a bar chart: each bar is at equal intervals
    const barWidth = 60;  // known from chart config
    const barIndex = 2;   // 3rd bar
    const x = barWidth * barIndex + barWidth / 2;
    await element(by.id('bar-chart')).tapAtPoint({ x, y: 50 });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('tooltip-bar-2'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Charts (`react-native-charts-wrapper`, `victory-native`), canvas/SVG drawing surfaces, map overlays with no accessible child elements. **Tradeoff:** Coordinates are in element-relative pixels and change with device screen size — compute them from `getAttributes().frame` rather than hard-coding. **Not suitable for** elements that have proper `testID` props — use `by.id()` for anything addressable by accessibility identifier. [official]

---

### Pattern 126 — `jest.retryTimes()` per describe block + `.detoxrc.js` `testRunner.retries` for quarantined flaky tests [community]

Rather than silently retrying every test, use a fine-grained `jest.retryTimes()` per describe block to quarantine known-flaky interactions while you track them down. Pair with `.detoxrc.js` `testRunner.retries` for framework-level retries on crash recovery.

```ts
// e2e/flaky-animation.test.ts — quarantine approach
import { device, element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';

describe('Shared element transition (flaky on iOS 26)', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
  });

  // Quarantine: retry up to 2 times while root cause is investigated
  // MUST be removed once the underlying race condition is fixed
  // Tracked in: https://github.com/myorg/myapp/issues/1234
  jest.retryTimes(2, { logErrorsBeforeRetry: true });

  it('navigates to detail screen via hero animation', async () => {
    await element(by.id('product-card-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(8000);
    await expect(element(by.id('product-hero-image'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});

// .detoxrc.js — framework-level retries for crash/session-loss recovery
// testRunner: {
//   jest: {
//     retries: 1,   // retry a test once if the Detox session crashes
//     bail: 3,      // stop the suite after 3 non-retriable failures
//   }
// }
```

**When to use:** Known flaky tests under active investigation — quarantine prevents CI red while the root cause is tracked. **Tradeoff:** Retries mask real failures and inflate CI time. Every `jest.retryTimes()` call should be paired with a tracking issue link and a removal date. **Community lesson [community]:** Teams that allow unlimited retries without tracking end up with 20–30% of their suite silently broken for months — enforce a policy: max 2 retries, must have a linked issue.

---

### Pattern 127 — `element(by.id('x')).swipe()` with `normalizedStartX/Y` for swipeable card decks (Tinder-style) [official]

Swipeable card decks use horizontal fling gestures. Providing `normalizedStartX` keeps the gesture anchor in the correct part of the card so the velocity threshold is met and the dismiss animation triggers.

```ts
// e2e/card-deck.test.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

// Helper: swipe a card left (reject) or right (accept)
async function swipeCard(
  cardTestID: string,
  direction: 'left' | 'right',
  speed: 'fast' | 'slow' = 'fast',
): Promise<void> {
  // Start from the center of the card (normalizedStartX: 0.5, normalizedStartY: 0.5)
  // to avoid triggering a parent scroll — the 6th parameter is normalizedStartX
  await element(by.id(cardTestID)).swipe(direction, speed, 0.7, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5);
}

describe('Card Deck', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('card-deck-container')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('accepts the first card and shows the next', async () => {
    await swipeCard('card-deck-item-0', 'right');
    await waitFor(element(by.id('card-deck-item-0')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('card-deck-item-1'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('rejects the first card and increments counter', async () => {
    await swipeCard('card-deck-item-0', 'left');
    await waitFor(element(by.id('rejected-count-label')))
      .toHaveText('1')
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('shows empty-state after swiping all cards', async () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
      await swipeCard(`card-deck-item-${i}`, 'right');
      await waitFor(element(by.id(`card-deck-item-${i}`)))
        .not.toBeVisible()
        .withTimeout(2000);
    }
    await waitFor(element(by.id('empty-deck-message')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Card decks, swipe-to-delete list rows, onboarding carousels. **Tradeoff:** `swipe()` sends a single continuous gesture; if the card doesn't dismiss, increase `normalizedOffset` (4th param) or use `'fast'` speed. **Alternative:** `longPressAndDrag()` is more reliable for drag-to-reorder but `swipe()` is correct for fling-dismissal gestures. [official]

---

### Pattern 128 — Custom `DetoxCircusEnvironment` subclass with `onTestStart` / `onTestComplete` for Datadog / Sentry E2E telemetry [community]

Detox uses a custom Jest environment (`DetoxCircusEnvironment`). Subclassing it allows emitting test lifecycle events to observability platforms, correlating test pass/fail with Sentry error IDs or Datadog trace IDs from the same CI run.

```ts
// e2e/environment/DetoxObservabilityEnvironment.ts
import { DetoxCircusEnvironment } from 'detox/runners/jest';

interface TestEventPayload {
  ddsource: string;
  service: string;
  message: string;
  level: 'info' | 'error';
  duration_ms: number;
  commit_sha: string;
}

export default class DetoxObservabilityEnvironment extends DetoxCircusEnvironment {
  private testStartTime = 0;

  async handleTestStart(event: { test: { fullName: string } }): Promise<void> {
    await super.handleTestStart(event);
    this.testStartTime = Date.now();
  }

  async handleTestComplete(event: {
    test: { fullName: string; errors: Error[] };
  }): Promise<void> {
    await super.handleTestComplete(event);
    const duration = Date.now() - this.testStartTime;
    const passed = event.test.errors.length === 0;

    const payload: TestEventPayload = {
      ddsource:    'detox',
      service:     'e2e-tests',
      message:     `${passed ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'}: ${event.test.fullName}`,
      level:       passed ? 'info' : 'error',
      duration_ms: duration,
      commit_sha:  process.env.GITHUB_SHA ?? 'local',
    };

    if (process.env.DD_API_KEY) {
      // Fire-and-forget — do NOT await; must not block test teardown
      fetch('https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input', {
        method:  'POST',
        headers: { 'DD-API-KEY': process.env.DD_API_KEY, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body:    JSON.stringify([payload]),
      }).catch(console.warn);
    }
  }
}

// jest.config.js:
// testEnvironment: './e2e/environment/DetoxObservabilityEnvironment.ts'
```

**When to use:** Large teams running 100+ E2E tests where test-level flakiness tracking is needed. **Tradeoff:** Custom environment must call `super.*` methods for every override or Detox setup/teardown breaks silently. `DD_API_KEY` must be a CI secret — never hard-code. **Alternative:** `jest-circus`'s `testResultsProcessor` is simpler but fires once per suite, not per test. [community]

---

### Pattern 129 — `device.setOrientation()` + layout-settled guard for responsive breakpoint testing [official]

Testing responsive layouts across portrait/landscape requires a stable assertion target after the rotation animation completes. Use a `layout-settled-indicator` testID driven by a post-layout effect, or wait for a layout-specific element to appear.

```ts
// e2e/responsive.test.ts
import { device, element, by, expect, waitFor } from 'detox';

async function rotateAndSettle(orientation: 'portrait' | 'landscape'): Promise<void> {
  await device.setOrientation(orientation);
  // Wait for the post-rotation layout to stabilize
  // The app drives 'layout-settled-indicator' via a useEffect on Dimensions.get()
  await waitFor(element(by.id('layout-settled-indicator')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(3000);
}

describe('Responsive layout', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('dashboard-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(6000);
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    // Always return to portrait to avoid bleeding into subsequent suites
    await device.setOrientation('portrait');
  });

  it('shows sidebar navigation in landscape mode', async () => {
    await rotateAndSettle('landscape');
    await expect(element(by.id('sidebar-nav'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('bottom-tab-bar'))).not.toBeVisible();
  });

  it('shows bottom tab bar in portrait mode', async () => {
    await rotateAndSettle('portrait');
    await expect(element(by.id('bottom-tab-bar'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('sidebar-nav'))).not.toBeVisible();
  });

  it('renders two-column grid layout in landscape', async () => {
    await rotateAndSettle('landscape');
    await element(by.id('products-tab')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('product-grid-col-left'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('product-grid-col-right'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Apps with adaptive layouts for tablets, large-screen Android, and landscape mode. **Tradeoff:** `device.setOrientation()` is a no-op on Android Emulator API 34+ without hardware rendering (`-gpu swiftshader_indirect` flag) — see Gotcha 57. Always reset orientation in `afterAll` to avoid polluting subsequent test files. [official]

### Gotcha 161 — `element(by.id('x')).longPress()` fires as a tap when the element is inside a `ScrollView` with `scrollEventThrottle` < 16 ms on iOS [community]

**Root cause**: When a `ScrollView` is configured with `scrollEventThrottle={16}` or lower, iOS's pan gesture recognizer competes with the long-press recognizer on touch-down. The `longPress()` gesture's initial pan threshold is crossed before the minimum hold duration elapses, causing UIKit to interpret the touch as a scroll pan and cancel the long press. Detox's XCTest injection falls back to a zero-duration tap.

```ts
// SYMPTOM — longPress() in a fast-scrolling ScrollView fires as a tap
await element(by.id('message-item-5')).longPress(800); // fires as tap on iOS

// DIAGNOSIS — parent ScrollView has a very low scrollEventThrottle:
// <ScrollView scrollEventThrottle={16} testID="message-list">
//   <MessageItem testID="message-item-5" ... />
// </ScrollView>

// FIX 1 — increase hold duration so it fires before the competing gesture
await element(by.id('message-item-5')).longPress(1200);

// FIX 2 — raise scrollEventThrottle in E2E builds to reduce pan competition
// scrollEventThrottle={IS_E2E_BUILD ? 200 : 16}

// FIX 3 — disable ScrollView momentum via launchArgs
await device.launchApp({ launchArgs: { DISABLE_SCROLL_MOMENTUM: 'true' } });
await element(by.id('message-item-5')).longPress(800);
await waitFor(element(by.id('context-menu'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

// WHY this matters: context menus in chat apps and notes apps depend on longPress
// and are almost always inside scroll views — this is one of the most common
// unexplained "longPress does nothing" failure modes in iOS Detox testing
```

---

### Gotcha 162 — `toHaveText()` on a `Text` with `numberOfLines` truncation returns the FULL untruncated string, not the visually displayed text [community]

**Root cause**: Detox's `toHaveText()` reads the element's text content from the React Native accessibility tree, not the visually rendered string. `Text numberOfLines={2}` visually truncates with an ellipsis but the accessibility value remains the full untruncated string, making assertions on truncated text pass with the full value.

```ts
// Component:
// <Text numberOfLines={2} testID="description-text">
//   This is a very long description that will be truncated after two lines
// </Text>

// MISLEADING PASS — passes even though only 2 lines are shown
await expect(element(by.id('description-text')))
  .toHaveText('This is a very long description that will be truncated after two lines');

// CORRECT approach 1 — use getAttributes().frame.height to verify truncation
const attrs = await element(by.id('description-text')).getAttributes();
if (Array.isArray(attrs)) throw new Error('Expected single element');
// Full-text height would exceed 2 lines at ~22px/line; truncated = < 60px
const isTruncated = attrs.frame.height < 60;
expect(isTruncated).toBe(true);

// CORRECT approach 2 — expose a "show more" button testID that only renders
// when the text is actually truncated (driven by onTextLayout)
await expect(element(by.id('show-more-btn'))).toBeVisible();

// WHY this matters: product cards, notifications, and feed items commonly use
// numberOfLines — asserting the full text value does NOT validate truncation UX
```

---

### Gotcha 163 — `device.launchApp({ url: '...' })` cold-start deep link races with RN Metro bundle load on Android API 35+ New Architecture [community]

**Root cause**: On Android API 35+ with the New Architecture enabled, the Metro JS bundle and module registry initialise on a background thread. The deep link intent fires before `NavigationContainer` mounts, silently dropping the navigation action. The user lands on the home screen instead of the linked route. This race does not occur on iOS because the URL is delivered via `application(_:continue:restorationHandler:)` which is called after the JS bundle has loaded.

```ts
// BAD — deep link fires before NavigationContainer mounts on Android API 35+
await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true, url: 'myapp://products/42' });
await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(5000); // FAILS — lands on home screen instead

// FIX 1 — two-phase: launch first, wait for mount, then open the URL
await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
await device.openURL({ url: 'myapp://products/42' });
await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(5000);

// FIX 2 — abstract into a reusable helper with an app-root-ready guard
async function launchWithDeepLink(url: string): Promise<void> {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('app-root-ready')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(10000);
  await device.openURL({ url });
}

await launchWithDeepLink('myapp://products/42');
await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(5000);

// WHY: app-root-ready is a hidden testID set by the app only after
// NavigationContainer reports onReady — this provides a reliable sync point
```

---

### Gotcha 164 — `element(by.id('x')).typeText()` produces duplicate characters on Android API 36 when gesture (swipe) keyboard is enabled by default [community]

**Root cause**: Android API 36 enables gesture keyboard (Gboard swipe) by default in the emulator image. Detox's `typeText()` injects characters via UIAutomator events, but with gesture typing enabled, the IME's autocorrect engine treats each character injection as a separate gesture candidate and may insert the character twice before the IME buffer flushes.

```ts
// SYMPTOM — typeText() produces doubled characters on Android API 36
await element(by.id('search-input')).tap();
await element(by.id('search-input')).typeText('hello'); // produces 'hheelloo'

// FIX 1 — use replaceText() which sets the value atomically via accessibility API
await element(by.id('search-input')).replaceText('hello'); // safe on all APIs

// FIX 2 — disable autocorrect on the input component
// <TextInput
//   testID="search-input"
//   autoCorrect={false}
//   autoComplete="off"
//   autoCapitalize="none"
// />

// FIX 3 — switch to a non-gesture IME via adb in CI setup
// adb shell ime set com.android.inputmethod.latin/.LatinIME

// Rule of thumb: use replaceText() for setting any value;
// reserve typeText() ONLY for testing key-press-sensitive interactions
// like autocomplete triggers or submit-on-keystroke behaviors
await element(by.id('search-input')).replaceText('hello');
await expect(element(by.id('search-input'))).toHaveValue('hello');

// WHY this matters: typeText() is the first method most Detox tutorials show,
// making this a trap for teams upgrading Android emulators to API 36
```

---

### Gotcha 165 — `waitFor(element(by.id('android-toast'))).not.toBeVisible()` resolves before the toast animation begins, leaving a visible toast during the next assertion [community]

**Root cause**: Android toast animations run on a separate `WindowManager` layer outside the React Native view hierarchy. Detox's synchronization tracks the RN JS thread and the main looper but does not wait for `WindowManager` toast entrance animations. A negative `not.toBeVisible()` check resolves in the brief window before the toast window is attached, then the toast appears and is visible for the subsequent check.

```ts
// SYMPTOM — continue-btn tap fails because the toast is still showing
await element(by.id('save-btn')).tap();
await waitFor(element(by.id('success-toast'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(500);
await element(by.id('continue-btn')).tap(); // FAILS — toast is now visible, covering button

// FIX 1 — wait for the toast to APPEAR first, then wait for dismissal
await element(by.id('save-btn')).tap();
await waitFor(element(by.id('success-toast')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(4000);
await waitFor(element(by.id('success-toast')))
  .not.toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(5000);
await element(by.id('continue-btn')).tap();

// FIX 2 — implement toasts as RN components instead of native android.widget.Toast
// RN-based toasts are tracked by the React Native synchronization layer

// FIX 3 — if toast state is irrelevant, just wait for the next target element
await element(by.id('save-btn')).tap();
await waitFor(element(by.id('continue-btn'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
await element(by.id('continue-btn')).tap();

// WHY this matters: ToastAndroid.show() is used in many RN apps and creates a
// WindowManager overlay that Detox cannot synchronize with natively
```

---

### Gotcha 166 — `device.takeScreenshot()` throws `ENAMETOOLONG` / `ENOENT` on Windows CI when the test name contains `:`, `|`, `?`, or `\n` [community]

**Root cause**: Detox derives the screenshot filename from the test's full name (including `describe` nesting). On Windows CI runners (GitHub Actions `windows-latest`), test names containing characters illegal in NTFS (`:`  `?` `|` `<` `>` `"` `\n`) cause Node.js `fs.writeFile()` to throw `ENAMETOOLONG` or `ENOENT`. This does not occur on macOS/Linux because those filesystems allow most special characters.

```ts
// SYMPTOM — throws ENAMETOOLONG on Windows CI
// Test: 'Checkout: payment flow > credit card > Visa: 4242 | success'
await device.takeScreenshot('checkout-payment-step'); // throws on Windows

// FIX — sanitise filenames before passing to takeScreenshot()
function sanitiseFilename(name: string): string {
  return name
    .replace(/[/:?|<>"\\]/g, '-')  // replace illegal Windows path chars
    .replace(/\s+/g, '_')           // spaces → underscores
    .replace(/-{2,}/g, '-')         // collapse double dashes
    .substring(0, 100);             // cap length to prevent ENAMETOOLONG
}

// Usage in tests:
const testName = expect.getState().currentTestName ?? 'screenshot';
await device.takeScreenshot(sanitiseFilename(testName));

// CI env config to keep artifact path short on Windows:
// env:
//   DETOX_ARTIFACTS_PATH: C:\a\artifacts
// .detoxrc.js:
// artifacts: { rootDir: process.env.DETOX_ARTIFACTS_PATH ?? '.detox/artifacts' }

// WHY this matters: cross-platform CI (macOS for iOS, Windows for Android emulators)
// is increasingly common; filename sanitisation should be in every shared test helper
```

---

### Gotcha 167 — `element(by.id('x')).scroll()` while keyboard is open in `KeyboardAwareScrollView` dismisses the keyboard instead of scrolling [community]

**Root cause**: `KeyboardAwareScrollView` (from `react-native-keyboard-aware-scroll-view`) wraps a `ScrollView` and intercepts scroll events to offset content for the keyboard. When Detox calls `element.scroll()`, `KeyboardAwareScrollView`'s responder chain intercepts the gesture and triggers a keyboard-dismiss animation, collapsing the keyboard. After dismissal, the scroll gesture is already complete with 0 net offset, leaving the content at the top.

```ts
// SYMPTOM — scroll() dismisses keyboard and resets scroll position to top
await element(by.id('email-input')).tap(); // opens keyboard
await element(by.id('keyboard-aware-scroll')).scroll(300, 'down'); // dismisses keyboard, doesn't scroll

// FIX 1 — dismiss keyboard explicitly BEFORE scrolling
await element(by.id('email-input')).tapReturnKey(); // close keyboard
await waitFor(element(by.id('keyboard-aware-scroll'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
await element(by.id('keyboard-aware-scroll')).scroll(300, 'down');

// FIX 2 — use scrollTo('bottom') for edge-of-form navigation
await element(by.id('keyboard-aware-scroll')).scrollTo('bottom');
await element(by.id('submit-btn')).tap();

// FIX 3 — set keyboardShouldPersistTaps='handled' on the scroll container
// <KeyboardAwareScrollView
//   keyboardShouldPersistTaps="handled"
//   testID="keyboard-aware-scroll"
// >

// Reusable helper: dismiss keyboard then scroll
async function scrollFormField(scrollViewID: string, pixels: number): Promise<void> {
  // Attempt keyboard dismissal via a neutral tap if keyboard may be open
  try {
    await element(by.id('keyboard-dismiss-overlay')).tap();
  } catch { /* keyboard was not open — safe to ignore */ }
  await element(by.id(scrollViewID)).scroll(pixels, 'down');
}

// WHY this matters: virtually all multi-field forms use either KeyboardAwareScrollView
// or KeyboardAvoidingView, making this scroll-with-keyboard issue the #1 reported
// Detox form-filling gotcha on Stack Overflow (2024–2026)
```

## Updated Anti-Patterns Checklist (Cycle 27 additions)

| Anti-Pattern | Fix |
|---|---|
| Using `longPress()` inside a `ScrollView` with `scrollEventThrottle` < 16 ms without increasing hold duration | Competing pan gesture cancels the long press on iOS — increase duration to 1200+ ms or raise `scrollEventThrottle` in E2E builds (Gotcha 161) |
| Using `toHaveText()` to assert truncation on a `Text` with `numberOfLines` | Returns the FULL untruncated string from the accessibility tree — use `getAttributes().frame.height` or a testID-gated "show more" button (Gotcha 162) |
| Using `device.launchApp({ url: '...' })` cold-start deep link on Android API 35+ New Architecture | Deep link fires before `NavigationContainer` mounts — use two-phase launch: `launchApp()` then `openURL()` after `app-root-ready` is visible (Gotcha 163) |
| Using `typeText()` to set values on Android API 36 with gesture keyboard enabled | Duplicate characters from IME gesture engine — use `replaceText()` for all value-setting; `typeText()` only for key-press sequence testing (Gotcha 164) |
| Asserting `waitFor(toast).not.toBeVisible()` before an action that shows a native Android toast | Resolves before the `WindowManager` layer attaches — wait for the toast to appear first, then wait for dismissal (Gotcha 165) |
| Passing test names with `:` or `|` characters to `device.takeScreenshot()` on Windows CI runners | Illegal NTFS path characters cause `ENAMETOOLONG` — sanitise filenames with a helper before calling `takeScreenshot()` (Gotcha 166) |
| Calling `element.scroll()` while keyboard is open inside `KeyboardAwareScrollView` | Keyboard intercepts the gesture and dismisses itself — dismiss keyboard first via `tapReturnKey()` then scroll (Gotcha 167) |

### Pattern 98 — Fabric concurrent-mode render guard using `useIsReady` sentinel testID [official]

React Native 0.76+ with the New Architecture (Fabric) renders some subtrees concurrently. A component may mount, execute one render pass, then suspend while data loads, leaving a partial UI visible. Tapping into that partial state causes test failures that are non-reproducible locally (where the JS bundle is warm) but consistent in CI (cold-start).

```ts
// In the app: a sentinel that only becomes visible after all async data resolves
// src/components/AppReady.tsx
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { View } from 'react-native';

export function AppReadySentinel(): JSX.Element | null {
  const [ready, setReady] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    // resolves after NavigationContainer.onReady fires (app passes this via context)
    // You wire this to your actual readiness signal (e.g., data hydration complete)
    const t = setTimeout(() => setReady(true), 0); // microtask flush
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, []);
  if (!ready) return null;
  return <View testID="app-fabric-ready" style={{ width: 0, height: 0 }} />;
}

// e2e/helpers/waitForReady.ts
export async function waitForAppReady(timeoutMs = 12000): Promise<void> {
  await waitFor(element(by.id('app-fabric-ready')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(timeoutMs);
}

// e2e/login.test.ts — use in beforeAll after launchApp
beforeAll(async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  await waitForAppReady(); // blocks until Fabric concurrent passes settle
});
```

**When to use:** Any test suite running against RN 0.76+ Fabric builds where the first few assertions flake intermittently in CI. **When NOT to use:** Old architecture / paper builds — the sentinel adds ~50ms overhead per suite. **Alternative:** `waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible()` works if the home screen is never conditionally suspended, but the sentinel is more precise. [official]

---

### Pattern 99 — `device.setLocation()` + geofence-triggered feature testing [official]

Location-gated features (store finders, regional pricing, delivery radius) require simulating GPS sequences. Use `device.setLocation()` calls in sequence to simulate movement into and out of a geofence.

```ts
// e2e/geofence.test.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';

const STORE_LAT = 37.7749;
const STORE_LNG = -122.4194;
const OUTSIDE_LAT = 37.7849;   // ~1.1 km north — outside 500 m geofence
const OUTSIDE_LNG = -122.4194;

describe('Nearby Store Banner', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      permissions: { location: 'always' },
    });
  });

  it('shows the nearby-store banner when user enters the geofence', async () => {
    // Start outside the geofence
    await device.setLocation(OUTSIDE_LAT, OUTSIDE_LNG);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('nearby-store-banner')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);

    // Move inside the geofence — triggers region-enter callback
    await device.setLocation(STORE_LAT, STORE_LNG);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('nearby-store-banner')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(8000);
    await expect(element(by.id('nearby-store-name'))).toHaveText('Mission St Store');
  });

  it('hides the banner when user leaves the geofence', async () => {
    await device.setLocation(OUTSIDE_LAT, OUTSIDE_LNG);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('nearby-store-banner')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(8000);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Location-permission flows, geofence triggers, map-pin visible-region tests. **When NOT to use:** Physical device testing — `device.setLocation()` is a simulator/emulator-only API and throws on real hardware. **Alternative:** Inject a mock location provider via `launchArgs` (`MOCK_LOCATION=...`) if your app already has a location abstraction layer. [official]

---

### Pattern 100 — `skipIf` conditional-skip helper for Android API-level and iOS version guards [community]

Some features are only available on specific OS versions. Rather than wrapping every assertion in an `if`, create a `skipIf` helper that skips the entire `it` block with a clear message when the precondition is not met.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/skipIf.ts
type SkipPredicate = () => Promise<boolean>;

export function skipIf(
  predicate: SkipPredicate,
  reason: string,
  name: string,
  fn: () => Promise<void>,
): void {
  it(name, async () => {
    if (await predicate()) {
      console.log(`[SKIP] ${reason}`);
      return; // jest marks this as passed — no pending/skip API in jest-circus
    }
    await fn();
  });
}

// Reusable predicates
export const belowAndroidAPI = (level: number) => async (): Promise<boolean> =>
  device.getPlatform() === 'android' && (await device.getAPILevel()) < level;

export const belowiOSVersion = (major: number) => async (): Promise<boolean> =>
  device.getPlatform() === 'ios' &&
  parseInt((await (device as any).getRuntimeEnvironment?.()?.osVersion ?? '0'), 10) < major;

// e2e/notifications.test.ts — skip Notification Permission Rationale on Android < 33
import { skipIf, belowAndroidAPI } from './helpers/skipIf';

describe('Notification Permission', () => {
  skipIf(
    belowAndroidAPI(33),
    'POST_NOTIFICATIONS rationale only shown on Android 13+ (API 33+)',
    'shows rationale dialog before requesting notification permission',
    async () => {
      await element(by.id('enable-notifications-btn')).tap();
      await waitFor(element(by.id('notification-rationale-dialog')))
        .toBeVisible()
        .withTimeout(3000);
    },
  );
});
```

**When to use:** Conditional platform features, OS-version-gated APIs, biometric types that differ across iOS/Android versions. **When NOT to use:** When the feature should work everywhere — `skipIf` is for unavailable OS capabilities, not for ignoring failures on a version you haven't fixed yet. **Alternative:** jest's `test.skip` / `xit` — but those are unconditional compile-time decisions; `skipIf` is runtime-conditional and prints a clear reason. [community]

---

### Pattern 101 — `element.multiTap()` for double-tap and triple-tap gesture interactions [official]

Some interactions require rapid successive taps: photo zoom-to-fit (double-tap), text select-all (triple-tap), custom gesture recognizers. `element.multiTap(count)` fires the correct number of taps with the platform's system inter-tap interval, ensuring recognizers fire reliably without manual timing.

```ts
// e2e/gallery.test.ts
describe('Photo Viewer', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('photo-thumb-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('photo-full-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('zooms to fit on double-tap', async () => {
    // Assert default scale — app exposes scale via testID on an overlay label
    await expect(element(by.id('zoom-scale-label'))).toHaveText('1.0x');

    // Double-tap to zoom in (photo viewer zoom-to-fit gesture)
    await element(by.id('photo-full-screen')).multiTap(2);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('zoom-scale-label')))
      .not.toHaveText('1.0x')
      .withTimeout(2000);

    // Double-tap again to zoom back out to fit
    await element(by.id('photo-full-screen')).multiTap(2);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('zoom-scale-label')))
      .toHaveText('1.0x')
      .withTimeout(2000);
  });

  it('selects all text on triple-tap in caption edit field', async () => {
    await element(by.id('edit-caption-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('caption-input'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await element(by.id('caption-input')).multiTap(3); // select-all gesture
    // After select-all, typeText replaces the entire value
    await element(by.id('caption-input')).typeText('New caption');
    await expect(element(by.id('caption-input'))).toHaveValue('New caption');
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Double-tap-to-zoom, triple-tap-to-select, custom multi-tap gesture recognizers. **When NOT to use:** Rapid UI stress testing — `multiTap` uses the system inter-tap delay and is not a performance/load testing tool. **Alternative:** Multiple sequential `tap()` calls work but may miss the recognizer's timing window on iOS; `multiTap` is the correct API for recognized gesture counts. [official]
