### Pattern 102 — Detox → Maestro migration safety net via parallel-run parity comparison [community]

When migrating from Detox to Maestro (or vice versa), run both frameworks against the same scenario in CI to confirm behavioral parity before decommissioning the old suite.

```ts
// e2e/parity/compareResults.ts — run after both Detox and Maestro CI jobs complete
// Both suites output JUnit XML which this script parses and diffs

import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

interface TestResult {
  name:     string;
  status:   'pass' | 'fail';
}

function parseJUnit(xmlPath: string): TestResult[] {
  const xml = fs.readFileSync(xmlPath, 'utf8');
  const matches = [...xml.matchAll(
    /<testcase[^>]+name="([^"]+)"[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/testcase>/g,
  )];
  return matches.map(m => ({
    name:   m[1],
    status: m[2].includes('<failure') || m[2].includes('<error') ? 'fail' : 'pass',
  }));
}

const detoxResults  = parseJUnit('./artifacts/detox-junit.xml');
const maestroResults = parseJUnit('./artifacts/maestro-junit.xml');

const discrepancies = detoxResults.filter(d => {
  const m = maestroResults.find(r => r.name === d.name);
  return m !== undefined && m.status !== d.status;
});

const missingInMaestro = detoxResults.filter(
  d => !maestroResults.find(r => r.name === d.name),
);

if (discrepancies.length > 0 || missingInMaestro.length > 0) {
  console.error('PARITY FAILURES:', { discrepancies, missingInMaestro });
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log(`Parity check passed — ${detoxResults.length} tests matched`);
```

**When to use:** Incremental framework migrations where you cannot afford regressions during the transition period. **When NOT to use:** Steady-state — once parity is confirmed for a test group, remove the Detox version; running both permanently doubles CI time. **Alternative:** Manual code-review of ported tests; but automated parity detection catches subtle behavioral differences (e.g., timing, gesture velocity) that review misses. [community]

### Pattern 103 — `by.web()` multi-WebView frame selection in hybrid apps [official]

Apps embedding multiple `WebView` components (e.g., a content renderer and an ad frame) require scoping `by.web()` matchers to the correct frame using `element(by.id('webview-testid')).web(by.web.cssSelector(...))`. The page-level `web(by...)` shorthand hits the first WebView in hierarchy order, which may be the ad frame.

```ts
// e2e/hybridApp.test.ts
import { element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

describe('Hybrid app with article WebView and ad WebView', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('article-webview'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
  });

  it('interacts with the article WebView, not the ad frame', async () => {
    // Scope to the specific WebView by its native testID
    const articleWeb = element(by.id('article-webview')).web;

    // Wait for a heading element inside the article WebView specifically
    await waitFor(articleWeb(by.web.cssSelector('h1')))
      .toExist()
      .withTimeout(5000);

    const heading = await articleWeb(by.web.cssSelector('h1')).getInnerText();
    expect(heading).toBeTruthy();

    // Tap a link inside the article frame only
    await articleWeb(by.web.cssSelector('a.read-more')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('full-article-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('verifies ad WebView exists without interacting with it', async () => {
    const adWeb = element(by.id('ad-webview')).web;
    await waitFor(adWeb(by.web.cssSelector('div.ad-container')))
      .toExist()
      .withTimeout(3000);
    // Never tap ad content in E2E tests — side effects are unpredictable
    await expect(element(by.id('article-webview'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Any hybrid app with multiple co-existing WebViews, or RN apps embedding an ad SDK that renders its own WebView. **When NOT to use:** Single-WebView apps — the top-level `web(by...)` shorthand is sufficient and more readable. **Alternative:** Use native bridge injection via `launchArgs` to mock ad frames entirely, removing the need to work around ad-frame selector interference. [official]

---

### Pattern 104 — `withVideoSync` helper: `disableSynchronization` scoped to video-player screens [official]

Video player screens (RN Video, Expo AV) emit continuous `onProgress` callbacks that keep the JS event loop busy. Detox never detects the app as idle and `waitFor` times out. The fix is disabling synchronization only for the video interaction scope, then unconditionally re-enabling via `try/finally`.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/withVideoSync.ts
export async function withVideoSync<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  await device.disableSynchronization();
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    // Always re-enable — even if fn() throws — to prevent sync leaking into next test
    await device.enableSynchronization();
  }
}

// e2e/videoPlayer.test.ts
import { withVideoSync } from './helpers/withVideoSync';

it('plays and pauses a video', async () => {
  await element(by.id('video-thumbnail-0')).tap();

  await withVideoSync(async () => {
    // waitFor inside no-sync zone — use explicit timeouts
    await waitFor(element(by.id('video-player-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(8000);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('play-pause-btn')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);

    await element(by.id('play-pause-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('pause-icon')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);

    await element(by.id('play-pause-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('play-icon')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });
  // Synchronization is re-enabled here — normal idle detection resumes
});
```

**When to use:** Video players, audio players, real-time data streams (WebSocket ticker feeds, animated live maps). **When NOT to use:** Navigation, form flows, or any screen where Detox synchronization is working correctly — disabling it removes the idle-detection safety net. **Alternative:** Use `launchArgs` to swap in a mock player that fires a single `onLoad` event and goes quiet; this keeps sync enabled but requires app-side mocking infrastructure. [official]

---

### Pattern 105 — Artifact-on-failure: `device.takeScreenshot()` only when a test fails [community]

Capturing screenshots for every test inflates CI artifact storage. A `afterEach` hook that only captures on failure provides actionable debug evidence without noise.

```ts
// e2e/setup/screenshotOnFailure.ts
import * as path from 'path';

function sanitizeName(name: string): string {
  return name
    .replace(/[/:?|<>"\\]/g, '-')
    .replace(/\s+/g, '_')
    .substring(0, 80);
}

afterEach(async () => {
  // jest-circus exposes failure state via expect.getState()
  const jestState   = expect.getState() as any;
  const testFailed  = jestState.currentTestName && jestState.numFailingTests > 0;
  const testName    = jestState.currentTestName as string | undefined;
  const testPath    = jestState.testPath as string | undefined;

  if (testFailed && testName) {
    const suiteName = sanitizeName(path.basename(testPath ?? 'unknown', '.test.ts'));
    const caseName  = sanitizeName(testName);
    const ts        = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-');
    await device.takeScreenshot(`FAIL_${suiteName}_${caseName}_${ts}`);
  }
});

// Alternative: use .detoxrc.js built-in config (zero custom code):
// artifacts: {
//   screenshots: {
//     shouldTakeAutomaticSnapshots: true,
//     keepOnlyFailedTestsArtifacts: true,
//   }
// }
```

**When to use:** CI pipelines where artifact storage is limited; projects wanting focused debug artifacts. **When NOT to use:** Visual regression pipelines that require a screenshot per test as a baseline. **Alternative:** Detox's built-in `artifacts.screenshots.keepOnlyFailedTestsArtifacts: true` in `.detoxrc.js` achieves the same with zero custom code — prefer the config option over the manual hook. [community]

---

### Pattern 106 — React Native Skia canvas testing via `testID` state-mirror overlay [community]

`@shopify/react-native-skia` renders to a GPU canvas with no accessibility tree. `by.id()` cannot match drawn content. The correct pattern is a hidden testID-instrumented overlay element that reflects computed canvas state as a JSON string, readable via `getAttributes()`.

```ts
// In the app component — expose computed canvas state via a hidden text element
// <Canvas testID="chart-canvas" style={styles.canvas}>
//   <Path ... />
// </Canvas>
// {/* Hidden accessibility mirror for Detox — zero visual size */}
// <Text
//   testID="chart-state-mirror"
//   accessible={false}
//   style={{ position: 'absolute', opacity: 0, width: 0, height: 0 }}
// >
//   {JSON.stringify({ bars: barCount, maxValue, highlightIndex })}
// </Text>

// e2e/charts.test.ts
it('renders the correct number of bars after data loads', async () => {
  await waitFor(element(by.id('chart-state-mirror')))
    .toExist()
    .withTimeout(8000);

  const attrs = await element(by.id('chart-state-mirror')).getAttributes();
  const state = JSON.parse((attrs as any).text ?? '{}') as {
    bars: number; maxValue: number; highlightIndex: number;
  };

  expect(state.bars).toBe(12);
  expect(state.maxValue).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(state.highlightIndex).toBe(-1); // no bar highlighted initially
});

it('highlights the tapped bar and updates the state mirror', async () => {
  await element(by.id('chart-canvas')).tap(); // taps center bar by default
  await waitFor(element(by.id('chart-state-mirror'))).toExist().withTimeout(2000);
  const attrs = await element(by.id('chart-state-mirror')).getAttributes();
  const state = JSON.parse((attrs as any).text ?? '{}');
  expect(state.highlightIndex).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
});
```

**When to use:** Any `@shopify/react-native-skia`, `react-native-svg`, or `react-native-canvas` component where drawn state must be asserted structurally. **When NOT to use:** Standard RN components — the state-mirror pattern adds maintenance overhead; use normal matchers there. **Alternative:** Screenshot + `pixelmatch`/`odiff` visual diffing catches visual regressions without state mirrors but gives binary pass/fail without semantic reason for the diff. [community]

---

### Pattern 107 — Per-test retry budget with idempotency guard in jest-circus [community]

Network-dependent E2E tests in CI environments with variable latency can flake on transient timeouts. Configuring `testRunner.retries` in Detox 20.x is safe only when tests are idempotent. A `runOnce` guard prevents side-effect duplication on retries for non-idempotent actions.

```ts
// .detoxrc.js — enable retries (Detox 20.x)
// testRunner: {
//   jest: { retries: 2, bail: 0 }
// }

// e2e/helpers/runOnce.ts
const _ran = new Map<string, boolean>();

export function runOnce<T>(
  key: string,
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
): () => Promise<T | undefined> {
  return async () => {
    if (_ran.get(key)) {
      console.log(`[runOnce] skipping duplicate run for key: ${key}`);
      return undefined;
    }
    _ran.set(key, true);
    return fn();
  };
}

// e2e/checkout.test.ts — place order is NOT idempotent; guard it with runOnce
import { runOnce } from './helpers/runOnce';

const placeOrder = runOnce('checkout-place-order', async () => {
  await element(by.id('place-order-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('order-confirmation-screen')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(10000);
});

it('places an order and shows confirmation', async () => {
  await element(by.id('checkout-summary-screen')).scrollTo('bottom');
  await placeOrder(); // safe to call on retry — only fires once
  await expect(element(by.id('order-id-label'))).toBeVisible();
});
```

**When to use:** CI environments with inconsistent network/emulator latency; idempotent API calls (read-only assertions, search queries). **When NOT to use:** State-mutating actions that cannot be made idempotent (payment processing, irreversible deletes) — fix the underlying flake instead of retrying. **Alternative:** `testRunner.retries` with `device.reloadReactNative()` in `beforeEach` is simpler but slower; `runOnce` avoids the reload cost when flakes are caused purely by timeout variance. [community]

---

### Pattern 108 — `device.pressBack()` + predictive back gesture testing on Android 14+ [official]

Android 14 (API 34) introduced predictive back: the system shows a destination-screen preview before the user completes the back swipe. `device.pressBack()` commits the back navigation (equivalent to completing the swipe), making it the correct API for back-stack assertions.

```ts
// e2e/backNavigation.test.ts
describe('Android Back Navigation', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
  });

  it('navigates back from detail screen via pressBack()', async () => {
    await element(by.id('product-list-item-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(4000);

    await device.pressBack(); // commits predictive back gesture

    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(4000);
    await expect(element(by.id('product-detail-screen'))).not.toBeVisible();
  });

  it('back stack depth: three levels return to root in two presses', async () => {
    await element(by.id('product-list-item-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await element(by.id('add-review-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('review-form-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    await device.pressBack();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await device.pressBack();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Android back-navigation flows, testing Android predictive back on API 34+, verifying `BackHandler` intercepts, confirming back-stack depth. **When NOT to use:** iOS — `device.pressBack()` is Android-only; use a UI back button tap for cross-platform back tests. **Alternative:** `device.pressBack()` is preferred over tapping a toolbar back button when the goal is testing *system* back gesture behavior rather than the app's back button UI. [official]

---

### Pattern 109 — `getAttributes().frame.y` ordering check for sorted-list validation [community]

Validating that a visible list is sorted (by price, date, name) normally requires reading each cell value. For short above-the-fold lists, comparing `frame.y` across items is faster: lower `frame.y` means higher on screen, confirming visual sort order without reading every cell value.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/assertSortedByY.ts
export async function assertElementsOrderedTopToBottom(
  testIDs: string[],
): Promise<void> {
  const yPositions: number[] = [];
  for (const id of testIDs) {
    const attrs = await element(by.id(id)).getAttributes();
    yPositions.push((attrs as any).frame.y as number);
  }
  for (let i = 1; i < yPositions.length; i++) {
    expect(yPositions[i]).toBeGreaterThan(yPositions[i - 1]);
  }
}

// e2e/productList.test.ts
it('displays products sorted by price ascending after applying filter', async () => {
  await element(by.id('sort-btn')).tap();
  await element(by.id('sort-price-asc-option')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('product-list-item-0'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

  // Assert first 4 visible items are ordered top-to-bottom (ascending price order)
  await assertElementsOrderedTopToBottom([
    'product-list-item-0',
    'product-list-item-1',
    'product-list-item-2',
    'product-list-item-3',
  ]);

  // Also assert actual price labels for semantic correctness
  await expect(element(by.id('product-price-0'))).toHaveText('$9.99');
  await expect(element(by.id('product-price-1'))).toHaveText('$14.99');
});
```

**When to use:** Sort-order validation for visible above-the-fold items; layout regression checks for absolutely-positioned elements. **When NOT to use:** Lists longer than the viewport — items below the fold return `frame.y = 0` or out-of-bounds coordinates; scroll to each item first. **Alternative:** Reading each price/date label and comparing numerically is more semantically correct but slower (multiple `getAttributes` IPC round-trips vs a simple position comparison). [community]

---

### Pattern 110 — Multi-app (detach) testing with `bundleId` switching [official]

Some RN apps have companion apps sharing an App Group container (admin tool, share extension, notification extension). `device.launchApp({ bundleId })` switches between installed apps within a single test to assert cross-app data consistency.

```ts
// .detoxrc.js — register both apps under separate app keys
// apps: {
//   'ios.main':  { type: 'ios.app', bundleId: 'com.example.MainApp',  binaryPath: 'ios/build/MainApp.app' },
//   'ios.admin': { type: 'ios.app', bundleId: 'com.example.AdminApp', binaryPath: 'ios/build/AdminApp.app' },
// }

// e2e/multiApp.test.ts
const MAIN_BUNDLE  = 'com.example.MainApp';
const ADMIN_BUNDLE = 'com.example.AdminApp';

describe('Admin App → Main App promo code sync', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true, bundleId: MAIN_BUNDLE });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
  });

  it('promo created in admin app is redeemable in main app', async () => {
    // Switch to admin app and create a promo code
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true, bundleId: ADMIN_BUNDLE });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('admin-dashboard'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    await element(by.id('create-promo-btn')).tap();
    await element(by.id('promo-code-input')).replaceText('TESTCODE50');
    await element(by.id('save-promo-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('promo-saved-toast'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Switch back to main app — shared App Group / API sync
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: false, bundleId: MAIN_BUNDLE });
    await element(by.id('promo-entry-input')).replaceText('TESTCODE50');
    await element(by.id('apply-promo-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('discount-applied-label')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Main + admin app pairs sharing an App Group; notification service extension testing; companion watch app data sync verification. **When NOT to use:** Apps that share no data — cross-app launch overhead (~3s per switch) is unjustified. **Alternative:** Mock the shared data store via `launchArgs` to avoid launching the second app when the sync mechanism itself is not under test. [official]

---

### Pattern 111 — `globalSetup` + `globalTeardown` for emulator lifecycle management [official]

Booting and killing the emulator per spec file is the single largest CI time sink in large E2E suites. `globalSetup` / `globalTeardown` boot the emulator once and keep it warm for the entire test run.

```ts
// e2e/setup/globalSetup.ts
import { execSync, spawnSync } from 'child_process';

export default async function globalSetup(): Promise<void> {
  if (!process.env.CI || process.platform !== 'linux') return;

  const avdName = process.env.AVD_NAME ?? 'Pixel_7_API_34';
  console.log(`[globalSetup] booting AVD: ${avdName}`);

  spawnSync(
    `${process.env.ANDROID_HOME}/emulator/emulator`,
    ['-avd', avdName, '-no-window', '-no-audio', '-no-boot-anim', '-gpu', 'swiftshader_indirect'],
    { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' },
  );

  // Poll for boot completion (max 3 minutes)
  const deadline = Date.now() + 180_000;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    try {
      const out = execSync('adb shell getprop sys.boot_completed', { timeout: 5000 }).toString();
      if (out.trim() === '1') { console.log('[globalSetup] emulator ready'); return; }
    } catch { /* not ready yet — keep polling */ }
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 3000));
  }
  throw new Error('[globalSetup] emulator failed to boot within 3 minutes');
}

// e2e/setup/globalTeardown.ts
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

export default async function globalTeardown(): Promise<void> {
  if (process.env.CI && process.platform === 'linux') {
    execSync('adb emu kill', { stdio: 'inherit' });
    console.log('[globalTeardown] emulator shut down');
  }
}

// jest.config.js
// globalSetup:    './e2e/setup/globalSetup.ts',
// globalTeardown: './e2e/setup/globalTeardown.ts',
```

**When to use:** CI jobs with 10+ spec files where emulator boot time is a meaningful fraction of total CI time. **When NOT to use:** Local development — the emulator is already running; the `process.env.CI` guard makes the `globalSetup` a no-op locally. **Alternative:** Detox's `--keepAliveBoot` flag (where available) achieves the same with less boilerplate; `globalSetup` gives more control over AVD selection, boot diagnostics, and custom pre-boot configuration. [official]

---

### Pattern 112 — `element.swipe()` with `startNormalizedX/Y` for momentum-scroll / infinite-feed validation [official]

Testing infinite-scroll feeds requires a fast swipe that releases with momentum, causing the list to coast past the initial swipe endpoint. `element.swipe()` with `'fast'` speed and controlled `startNormalizedX/Y` anchors the gesture away from navigation zones and accurately exercises the load-more trigger.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/flingFeedDown.ts
export async function flingFeedDown(
  listTestID: string,
  passes = 3,
): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < passes; i++) {
    await element(by.id(listTestID)).swipe(
      'up',    // direction — up moves content downward (scrolls list forward)
      'fast',  // speed — releases with momentum to trigger load-more
      0.85,    // normalizedOffset — travel 85% of element height per fling
      0.5,     // startNormalizedX — center horizontally
      0.8,     // startNormalizedY — start 80% from top, avoiding sticky header
    );
    // Wait for any in-flight page load to settle before the next fling
    await waitFor(element(by.id('feed-loading-indicator')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  }
}

// e2e/feed.test.ts
import { flingFeedDown } from './helpers/flingFeedDown';

it('loads a second page of items via infinite scroll', async () => {
  await waitFor(element(by.id('feed-list-item-0'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

  await flingFeedDown('feed-list', 2);

  // After 2 fast flings, a second page (10 items) should have loaded
  await waitFor(element(by.id('feed-list-item-10')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(8000);
});

it('shows end-of-feed sentinel after exhausting all pages', async () => {
  let endVisible = false;
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 12 && !endVisible; attempt++) {
    await flingFeedDown('feed-list', 1);
    try {
      await waitFor(element(by.id('end-of-feed-label')))
        .toBeVisible()
        .withTimeout(1000);
      endVisible = true;
    } catch { /* sentinel not yet visible — keep flinging */ }
  }
  expect(endVisible).toBe(true);
});
```

**When to use:** Infinite-scroll feeds, paginated lists, pull-to-load-more patterns. **When NOT to use:** Precision navigation to a specific list item — use `scrollTo()` + `waitFor` for deterministic item targeting. **Alternative:** `element.scrollTo('bottom')` works for simple static lists but does not exercise the momentum/pagination trigger; `flingFeedDown` specifically validates that scroll velocity crosses the load-more threshold. [official]

---

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 28

### Gotcha 168 — `waitFor(element(by.id('x'))).toExist()` passes for elements inside a hidden `Modal` on iOS 17+ [community]

**Root cause**: iOS 17 changed how UIKit reports off-screen modal contents. A `Modal` with `visible={false}` previously removed child views from the accessibility tree. In iOS 17+, the modal subtree is retained in a detached window and its elements remain reachable by the Detox query engine. `toExist()` therefore resolves even when the modal is not presented, causing false-positive assertions.

```ts
// BAD — passes even when the modal is NOT presented on iOS 17+
await waitFor(element(by.id('modal-confirm-btn'))).toExist().withTimeout(3000);

// GOOD — use toBeVisible() which checks the rendered frame, not just tree existence
await waitFor(element(by.id('modal-confirm-btn'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

// ALSO GOOD — assert the modal container is visible before asserting its contents
await expect(element(by.id('confirmation-modal'))).toBeVisible();
await expect(element(by.id('modal-confirm-btn'))).toBeVisible();

// WHY this matters: many test suites use toExist() as a "lighter" alternative to
// toBeVisible(), but on iOS 17+ this no longer implies the element is presented
// to the user — toBeVisible() is the only safe assertion for modal content
```

---

### Gotcha 169 — `device.launchApp({ permissions: { camera: 'YES' } })` has no effect on Android 14+ without `newInstance: true` [community]

**Root cause**: On Android 14+, Detox grants permissions by resetting the app's runtime permission state via `pm grant`. This requires the app to restart for the permission flag to propagate to the app's `PackageManager` cache. Calling `launchApp({ permissions })` on a running instance silently succeeds but the app process still reads the stale permission state from its cached `ContextImpl`.

```ts
// BAD — permission appears granted but app reads PERMISSION_DENIED at runtime
await device.launchApp({ permissions: { camera: 'YES' } }); // no newInstance
await element(by.id('open-camera-btn')).tap();
// → "Camera permission denied" toast — app cached the old permission state

// GOOD — always pair permissions with newInstance: true on Android 14+
await device.launchApp({
  newInstance: true,           // kills and restarts the process so PM cache flushes
  permissions: { camera: 'YES' },
});
await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
await element(by.id('open-camera-btn')).tap();
await waitFor(element(by.id('camera-preview-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

// WHY this matters: permission tests that passed reliably on Android 13 silently
// break on Android 14+ without newInstance — the call succeeds with no error,
// making this one of the hardest regressions to diagnose on an Android version bump
```

---

### Gotcha 170 — `element.swipe('left', 'fast')` on a `ViewPager`/`PagerView` with `overScrollMode='never'` silently no-ops on Android API 35+ [community]

**Root cause**: Android API 35 tightened gesture conflict resolution in `ViewPager2`. When `overScrollMode='never'` is set (common in onboarding carousels to suppress the overscroll glow), the gesture recognizer rejects fast-fling events that fall below a tightened velocity threshold, treating them as accidental touches. Detox's `swipe('left', 'fast')` produces a gesture inside the tightened rejection zone.

```ts
// SYMPTOM — onboarding carousel stays on page 1, no error thrown
await element(by.id('onboarding-pager')).swipe('left', 'fast');
await expect(element(by.id('onboarding-page-2'))).toBeVisible(); // FAILS silently

// FIX 1 — use 'slow' speed with a large normalizedOffset
await element(by.id('onboarding-pager')).swipe('left', 'slow', 0.7);
await waitFor(element(by.id('onboarding-page-2'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);

// FIX 2 — tap a page-indicator dot if the carousel exposes them
await element(by.id('page-indicator-dot-1')).tap();
await waitFor(element(by.id('onboarding-page-2'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);

// FIX 3 — set overScrollMode='always' in E2E flavor builds via launchArgs gate:
// if (process.env.DETOX_BUILD) { overScrollMode = 'always'; }

// WHY this matters: onboarding carousels are typically the first screens new
// engineers test — silent no-ops without thrown errors make this particularly
// confusing for teams upgrading their Android emulator image to API 35
```

---

### Gotcha 171 — `getAttributes().frame.y` returns post-animation destination coordinates while a `LayoutAnimation` is still in flight on iOS [community]

**Root cause**: `LayoutAnimation` on iOS (Classic Architecture) schedules position updates on the Core Animation display link. When Detox calls `getAttributes()` after `LayoutAnimation.configureNext()` triggers but before the animation completes, the iOS accessibility system returns the *destination* frame (where the element will end up) while the visual position is still mid-animation. Tap coordinates computed from these attributes land in the wrong place.

```ts
// SYMPTOM — tap lands in wrong location because element is still animating
await element(by.id('expand-section-btn')).tap(); // triggers LayoutAnimation
const attrs = await element(by.id('first-expanded-item')).getAttributes();
// attrs.frame.y is the post-animation value — element is still visually moving
await element(by.id('first-expanded-item')).tap(); // MISSES the moving element

// FIX — wait for a layout-animation-settled sentinel before reading attributes
// The app sets this testID visible in an onAnimationDidEnd callback:
// LayoutAnimation.configureNext(config, () => setLayoutSettled(true));
await element(by.id('expand-section-btn')).tap();
await waitFor(element(by.id('layout-animation-settled')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(2000);
const safeAttrs = await element(by.id('first-expanded-item')).getAttributes();
await element(by.id('first-expanded-item')).tap(); // correct static position

// WHY this matters: LayoutAnimation is extremely common in React Native (accordion
// sections, expandable list items, animated cart badges) — stale getAttributes()
// is the root cause of a significant class of "intermittently mis-tapped element"
// reports filed against Detox on GitHub (2024–2026)
```

---

### Gotcha 172 — `device.reloadReactNative()` called inside a test does NOT re-run `beforeAll` — subsequent tests in the same `describe` block start from a blank slate [community]

**Root cause**: jest-circus records `beforeAll` completion as a flag on the describe scope. When `device.reloadReactNative()` is called inside a test, the JS bundle reloads but jest-circus does not re-execute `beforeAll`. Tests that follow assume the navigation state and mock data established in `beforeAll` are still in place, but the newly loaded bundle has none of that state.

```ts
// BAD — reloadReactNative() inside a test invalidates beforeAll navigation state
describe('Settings Flow', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await loginAsTestUser(); // navigates to settings after login
  });

  it('changes notification preference', async () => {
    await element(by.id('notifications-toggle')).tap();
  });

  it('clears cache and verifies reload', async () => {
    await element(by.id('clear-cache-btn')).tap();
    await device.reloadReactNative(); // ← invalidates beforeAll navigation state
  });

  it('shows updated preference after reload', async () => {
    // FAILS — app is on login screen; beforeAll loginAsTestUser() never re-ran
    await expect(element(by.id('notifications-toggle'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});

// GOOD — if reload is required mid-suite, restore navigation state in the same test
it('clears cache, reloads, and verifies updated preference', async () => {
  await element(by.id('clear-cache-btn')).tap();
  await device.reloadReactNative();
  await loginAsTestUser(); // explicitly restore beforeAll navigation state
  await expect(element(by.id('notifications-toggle'))).toBeVisible();
});

// WHY this matters: developers intuitively expect reloadReactNative() to "just
// refresh the app" with setup intact — the jest-circus scope model means it does
// not, and the resulting failure is test-order-dependent and hard to bisect
```

---

## Updated Anti-Patterns Checklist (Cycle 28 additions)

| Anti-Pattern | Fix |
|---|---|
| Using `toExist()` to assert modal content is presented on iOS 17+ | iOS 17+ retains modal subtree in detached window — use `toBeVisible()` which checks rendered frame (Gotcha 168) |
| Calling `launchApp({ permissions })` on Android 14+ without `newInstance: true` | App process caches stale permission state — always pair permissions with `newInstance: true` on Android 14+ (Gotcha 169) |
| Using `swipe('left', 'fast')` on `ViewPager`/`PagerView` with `overScrollMode='never'` on Android API 35+ | Fast fling falls below tightened velocity threshold — use `'slow'` speed with large `normalizedOffset` or tap indicator dot (Gotcha 170) |
| Reading `getAttributes().frame.y` immediately after a `LayoutAnimation.configureNext()` trigger on iOS | Accessibility reports post-animation destination while element is still mid-flight — wait for `layout-animation-settled` sentinel (Gotcha 171) |

## Cycle 29 — 2026-05-14

### Pattern 113 — `by.ancestor()` and `by.descendant()` scoped selectors for repeated testIDs in lists [official]

When multiple list items share child elements with the same `testID` (e.g., every row has a `testID="row-action-btn"`), `by.id()` alone is ambiguous. Scoping with `by.ancestor()` or `by.descendant()` uniquely resolves the target without requiring globally unique testIDs on every leaf element.

```ts
// In the component — testID on container, shared testID on action buttons
// <View testID={`order-item-${order.id}`}>
//   <Text testID="order-item-title">{order.title}</Text>
//   <TouchableOpacity testID="order-action-btn">...</TouchableOpacity>
// </View>

// e2e/orderList.test.ts
it('taps the action button on a specific order row', async () => {
  // Scope the tap to the second order's container using by.ancestor()
  await element(
    by.id('order-action-btn').withAncestor(by.id('order-item-order-002')),
  ).tap();

  await waitFor(element(by.id('order-detail-screen')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(4000);
});

it('verifies the title inside a known ancestor container', async () => {
  // by.descendant() used on the container side: find container that has this child
  const targetRow = element(
    by.id('order-item-order-002').withDescendant(by.id('order-item-title')),
  );
  await expect(targetRow).toBeVisible();

  // Scoped child access via ancestor chain
  const titleEl = element(
    by.id('order-item-title').withAncestor(by.id('order-item-order-002')),
  );
  await expect(titleEl).toHaveText('Office Supplies Order');
});
```

**When to use:** Repeated testIDs inside homogeneous list rows; any scenario where globally unique leaf testIDs are impractical to maintain. **When NOT to use:** When the list is virtualized (FlatList/FlashList) and the target row is off-screen — scroll to the row first, then use the ancestor scope. **Alternative:** `by.id('order-action-btn').atIndex(1)` is simpler but fragile if row order changes; ancestor scoping is render-order-independent. [official]

---

### Pattern 114 — `device.setLocation()` for geofence and location-aware feature testing [official]

Location-gated features (store locators, geofence notifications, delivery radius checks) require injecting precise GPS coordinates at test time. `device.setLocation()` drives the platform location simulator without a physical device.

```ts
// e2e/storeLocator.test.ts
const STORE_LAT  = 37.7749;
const STORE_LNG  = -122.4194; // San Francisco — inside delivery zone
const REMOTE_LAT = 34.0522;
const REMOTE_LNG = -118.2437; // Los Angeles — outside delivery zone

describe('Delivery zone enforcement', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      permissions: { location: 'always' },
    });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
  });

  it('shows delivery available when inside zone', async () => {
    await device.setLocation(STORE_LAT, STORE_LNG);
    await element(by.id('refresh-location-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('delivery-available-banner')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('delivery-available-banner')))
      .toHaveText('Delivery available in your area');
  });

  it('shows out-of-zone message when outside delivery radius', async () => {
    await device.setLocation(REMOTE_LAT, REMOTE_LNG);
    await element(by.id('refresh-location-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('delivery-unavailable-banner')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    // Reset to a neutral coordinate to avoid polluting later tests
    await device.setLocation(0, 0);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Geofence triggers, store locators, delivery radius checks, location-gated feature flags, map center assertions. **When NOT to use:** Physical Android devices (silent no-op on real hardware without GPS mock providers); always gate with `if (device.getPlatform() === 'ios' || isEmulator())`. **Alternative:** Mock the JS location module via `launchArgs` + a custom `Location.getCurrentPosition` stub when testing UI rendering only — avoids the simulated location race condition between `setLocation()` and the app's location listener. [official]

---

### Pattern 115 — `waitFor().toHaveText()` with dynamic content polling [official]

Asserting text that changes asynchronously (countdown timers, live scores, processing status labels) requires `waitFor` with a text matcher. This is more reliable than a fixed-timeout `expect` because Detox's synchronization engine idles until the text update settles.

```ts
// e2e/paymentProcessing.test.ts
it('shows processing → success state transition on payment screen', async () => {
  await element(by.id('pay-now-btn')).tap();

  // First state: processing banner appears immediately
  await waitFor(element(by.id('payment-status-label')))
    .toHaveText('Processing…')
    .withTimeout(3000);

  // Second state: success after async API response
  // withTimeout covers variable network latency in CI
  await waitFor(element(by.id('payment-status-label')))
    .toHaveText('Payment successful!')
    .withTimeout(15000);

  // Confirm the confirm button activates after success
  await waitFor(element(by.id('done-btn')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(2000);
  await element(by.id('done-btn')).tap();

  await waitFor(element(by.id('receipt-screen')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(4000);
});
```

**When to use:** Async status labels, countdown/progress text, streaming responses, polling indicators. **When NOT to use:** Text that requires locale-aware comparison — `toHaveText()` is an exact string match; use `toHaveLabel()` with a localized accessibility label or read via `getAttributes().text` and assert with Jest matchers. **Alternative:** `waitFor().toBeVisible()` on a success-state container element avoids text brittle matching when the exact wording may vary. [official]

---

### Pattern 116 — `element.adjustSliderToPosition()` for `Slider` component testing [official]

React Native's `<Slider>` (and `@react-native-community/slider`) component requires `adjustSliderToPosition()` for deterministic value setting. Direct `tap()` or `swipe()` on a slider track produces non-deterministic values due to touch target imprecision.

```ts
// e2e/settingsVolume.test.ts
describe('Volume slider', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('nav-settings-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('settings-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('sets volume to 50% using adjustSliderToPosition', async () => {
    // normalizedPosition: 0.0 = min, 1.0 = max, 0.5 = 50%
    await element(by.id('volume-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.5);

    // Read the current value via accessibility value attribute
    const attrs = await element(by.id('volume-slider')).getAttributes();
    const value = parseFloat((attrs as any).value ?? '0');
    // Sliders may land within ±5% of target due to discrete steps
    expect(value).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0.45);
    expect(value).toBeLessThanOrEqual(0.55);
  });

  it('sets volume to maximum and confirms display label', async () => {
    await element(by.id('volume-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(1.0);
    await expect(element(by.id('volume-value-label'))).toHaveText('100%');
  });

  it('sets volume to minimum', async () => {
    await element(by.id('volume-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.0);
    await expect(element(by.id('volume-value-label'))).toHaveText('0%');
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Any `Slider` or range-input component where a specific normalized value must be set deterministically. **When NOT to use:** Custom gesture-based sliders implemented with `PanResponder` or RNGH — they do not use the native Slider accessibility action and `adjustSliderToPosition()` will no-op silently; use `longPressAndDrag()` instead. **Alternative:** Expose a `setValueForTest(n)` JS function via `launchArgs` bridge for discrete-step sliders where `adjustSliderToPosition()` can land between steps. [official]

---

### Pattern 117 — `by.label()` with `accessibilityLabel` for icon-only buttons [official]

Icon-only buttons (hamburger menus, close buttons, toolbar icons) have no visible text. Setting `accessibilityLabel` and targeting with `by.label()` is the canonical approach — it mirrors how screen readers and accessibility audits identify these elements.

```ts
// In the component
// <TouchableOpacity
//   accessibilityLabel="Open navigation menu"
//   accessibilityRole="button"
//   testID="nav-menu-btn"
//   onPress={openMenu}
// >
//   <HamburgerIcon />
// </TouchableOpacity>

// e2e/navigation.test.ts
it('opens the navigation drawer via the hamburger icon', async () => {
  // Primary: testID selector (fastest, unambiguous)
  await element(by.id('nav-menu-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('nav-drawer'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

  // Close and verify via accessibilityLabel as fallback selector validation
  await element(by.id('nav-drawer-close-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('nav-drawer'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);

  // Also confirm by.label() can locate the button (a11y audit sanity check)
  const btnByLabel = element(by.label('Open navigation menu'));
  await expect(btnByLabel).toBeVisible();
  await btnByLabel.tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('nav-drawer'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
});

it('accessibility audit — all icon buttons have accessibilityLabel', async () => {
  const toolbarButtons = ['nav-menu-btn', 'search-btn', 'cart-btn', 'profile-btn'];
  for (const id of toolbarButtons) {
    const attrs = await element(by.id(id)).getAttributes();
    expect((attrs as any).label).toBeTruthy();
  }
});
```

**When to use:** Icon-only interactive elements; cross-validation that `accessibilityLabel` is correctly wired; accessibility audit tests. **When NOT to use:** Elements that already have stable `testID` props — `by.label()` is slower due to accessibility tree traversal and locale-sensitive. **Alternative:** `by.id()` is always preferred for non-a11y test purposes; use `by.label()` specifically when the test intent is to verify accessibility labeling. [official]

### Pattern 118 — `device.shake()` with dev-menu guard for shake-triggered app flows [official]

In development builds, device shake opens the React Native dev menu. In production builds, some apps implement shake-to-report-bug flows. Testing shake-triggered UI requires gating on build type and wrapping with a `by.system()` guard for the dev menu case.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/shakeDevice.ts
export async function shakeDevice(): Promise<void> {
  // device.shake() is a no-op on physical devices and Android emulators
  // without hardware shake simulation — only reliable on iOS Simulator
  if (device.getPlatform() === 'ios') {
    await device.shake();
  } else {
    // Android: no cross-platform shake API — skip on Android CI gracefully
    console.warn('[shakeDevice] Android shake not supported — test skipped');
  }
}

// e2e/bugReport.test.ts
it('opens the bug report sheet on device shake in release build', async () => {
  if (device.getPlatform() !== 'ios') {
    console.log('Skipping — shake only reliable on iOS Simulator');
    return;
  }

  await device.shake();

  // If running debug build, dev menu may appear — dismiss it first
  try {
    await waitFor(element(by.label('Stop Profiling')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(1000);
    // Dev menu is open — dismiss and skip; this is a debug build
    await device.pressBack();
    return;
  } catch { /* expected on release build — continue */ }

  // Release build: custom bug report sheet should appear
  await waitFor(element(by.id('bug-report-sheet')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(3000);
  await element(by.id('bug-report-cancel-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('bug-report-sheet'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
});
```

**When to use:** Apps with shake-to-report-bug flows in production builds; verifying the dev menu does not appear in release builds. **When NOT to use:** Android CI — `device.shake()` is a no-op on Android emulators and physical devices. **Alternative:** Expose a `__TRIGGER_BUG_REPORT__` `launchArgs` flag that programmatically opens the sheet; removes the platform limitation and makes the test cross-platform. [official]

---

### Pattern 119 — Jest `moduleNameMapper` generated from `tsconfig.json` path aliases to prevent E2E import resolution drift [community]

Large TypeScript RN codebases use `tsconfig` path aliases (`@components/*`, `@utils/*`). These aliases break Detox's Jest runner unless the `moduleNameMapper` in `jest.config.js` mirrors `tsconfig.json`. A one-source-of-truth generator prevents drift between TS compilation and Detox test resolution.

```ts
// scripts/generateJestAliases.ts
// Run via: npx ts-node scripts/generateJestAliases.ts
import * as fs   from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

interface TsConfig {
  compilerOptions?: { paths?: Record<string, string[]> };
}

const tsconfig: TsConfig = JSON.parse(
  fs.readFileSync(path.resolve(__dirname, '../tsconfig.json'), 'utf-8'),
);

const paths = tsconfig.compilerOptions?.paths ?? {};
const moduleNameMapper: Record<string, string> = {};

for (const [alias, targets] of Object.entries(paths)) {
  // Convert "@components/*" → "^@components/(.*)$": "<rootDir>/src/components/$1"
  const key   = `^${alias.replace('*', '(.*)')}$`;
  const value = `<rootDir>/${targets[0]!.replace('*', '$1')}`;
  moduleNameMapper[key] = value;
}

const output = [
  '// AUTO-GENERATED — do not edit manually',
  '// Run: npx ts-node scripts/generateJestAliases.ts',
  `module.exports = { moduleNameMapper: ${JSON.stringify(moduleNameMapper, null, 2)} };`,
].join('\n');

fs.writeFileSync(
  path.resolve(__dirname, '../e2e/generatedAliases.js'),
  output,
);
console.log('[generateJestAliases] written', Object.keys(moduleNameMapper).length, 'aliases');

// jest.e2e.config.js — consume the generated mapper
// const { moduleNameMapper } = require('./e2e/generatedAliases');
// module.exports = { preset: 'ts-jest', testEnvironment: 'node', moduleNameMapper };
```

**When to use:** Monorepos or large projects with `tsconfig` path aliases in E2E test files; any setup where `import { foo } from '@utils/foo'` fails in Detox tests. **When NOT to use:** Projects using Metro's `resolver.alias` config instead of `tsconfig paths` — in that case configure Metro's Detox-specific resolver. **Alternative:** `babel-plugin-module-resolver` resolves aliases at Babel transpile time without `moduleNameMapper`, but adds Babel as a dependency if the project is already on SWC. [community]

---

### Pattern 120 — `toHaveToggleValue()` for Switch component state assertions [official]

`<Switch>` components in React Native report their state as an accessibility toggle value, not a text value. `toHaveValue()` always returns `''` for Switch elements. `toHaveToggleValue(true/false)` is the correct matcher added in Detox 20.x.

```ts
// e2e/settings.test.ts
describe('Notification toggle', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('nav-settings-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('settings-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('is OFF by default', async () => {
    // WRONG — toHaveValue always returns '' for Switch elements
    // await expect(element(by.id('notifications-switch'))).toHaveValue('false');

    // CORRECT — toHaveToggleValue reads the accessibility toggle state
    await expect(element(by.id('notifications-switch'))).toHaveToggleValue(false);
  });

  it('turns ON when tapped', async () => {
    await element(by.id('notifications-switch')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('notifications-switch'))).toHaveToggleValue(true);
  });

  it('persists toggle state across reloadReactNative', async () => {
    await expect(element(by.id('notifications-switch'))).toHaveToggleValue(true);
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('nav-settings-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('settings-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    await expect(element(by.id('notifications-switch'))).toHaveToggleValue(true);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Any `<Switch>` or toggle component implementing the native accessibility toggle role. **When NOT to use:** Custom toggle buttons implemented as `Pressable` with two visual states — those don't implement the native accessibility toggle role and `toHaveToggleValue()` will throw; use `getAttributes().value` or a visual testID swap instead. **Alternative:** Read `(await element(by.id('x')).getAttributes()).value` and compare to `'1'`/`'0'` (platform-specific string) — but `toHaveToggleValue` is cleaner and cross-platform. [official]

---

### Pattern 121 — MSW v2 + `device.reverseTcp()` for zero-app-change network stubbing [community]

MSW v2 runs in a Node.js environment. Pairing it with a lightweight HTTP intercept server alongside `device.reverseTcp()` lets Detox tests mock all API calls without modifying app source code, keeping the test boundary at the HTTP layer.

```ts
// e2e/setup/mswServer.ts
import { setupServer }   from 'msw/node';
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';

const MOCK_PORT = 9999;

export const server = setupServer(
  http.get(`http://localhost:${MOCK_PORT}/api/products`, () =>
    HttpResponse.json([
      { id: '1', name: 'Widget A', price: 9.99 },
      { id: '2', name: 'Widget B', price: 14.99 },
    ]),
  ),
  http.post(`http://localhost:${MOCK_PORT}/api/checkout`, async ({ request }) => {
    const body = await request.json() as Record<string, unknown>;
    return HttpResponse.json(
      { orderId: `ORDER-${Date.now()}`, ...body },
      { status: 201 },
    );
  }),
);

export async function startMswServer(): Promise<void> {
  server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'warn' });
  if (device.getPlatform() === 'android') {
    // Route Android emulator traffic back to the host machine's mock server
    await device.reverseTcp(MOCK_PORT, MOCK_PORT);
  }
}

export async function stopMswServer(): Promise<void> {
  server.close();
}

// e2e/products.test.ts
import { startMswServer, stopMswServer } from './setup/mswServer';

beforeAll(async () => { await startMswServer(); });
afterAll(async () => { await stopMswServer(); });

it('displays mocked product list from MSW', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({
    newInstance: true,
    launchArgs: { API_BASE: `http://localhost:${9999}` },
  });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('product-list-item-0'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(6000);
  await expect(element(by.id('product-name-0'))).toHaveText('Widget A');
  await expect(element(by.id('product-name-1'))).toHaveText('Widget B');
});
```

**When to use:** Full E2E tests that need deterministic API responses without a running backend; testing error/edge-case API states (500s, network timeouts, malformed responses). **When NOT to use:** Tests specifically validating real API integration — MSW stubs bypass actual network behavior. **Alternative:** Detox's `launchArgs`-based mock server pattern (Pattern 51) is lighter weight but requires app-side instrumentation; MSW gives zero app-side changes at the cost of a proxy process. [community]

---

### Pattern 122 — `device.getLaunchArgs()` for conditional test behavior per environment configuration [official]

Tests that run in multiple environments (dev, staging, production) need to vary assertions based on backend capabilities. `device.getLaunchArgs()` reads the `launchArgs` passed at app start, enabling environment-specific assertion branching within a single test file.

```ts
// .detoxrc.js — define per-configuration launchArgs
// configurations: {
//   'ios.staging':    { ..., launchArgs: { ENV: 'staging',    FEATURE_PAYMENTS: 'true'  } },
//   'ios.production': { ..., launchArgs: { ENV: 'production', FEATURE_PAYMENTS: 'false' } },
// }

// e2e/helpers/envFlags.ts
export async function getEnvFlag(key: string): Promise<string | undefined> {
  const args = await device.getLaunchArgs();
  return (args as Record<string, string>)[key];
}

export async function featureEnabled(flag: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const val = await getEnvFlag(flag);
  return val === 'true' || val === '1';
}

// e2e/checkout.test.ts
import { featureEnabled } from './helpers/envFlags';

it('checkout respects the FEATURE_PAYMENTS flag per configuration', async () => {
  const paymentsEnabled = await featureEnabled('FEATURE_PAYMENTS');

  await element(by.id('cart-checkout-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('checkout-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);

  if (paymentsEnabled) {
    await expect(element(by.id('payment-form'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('payment-disabled-banner'))).not.toBeVisible();
  } else {
    await expect(element(by.id('payment-disabled-banner'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('payment-form'))).not.toBeVisible();
  }
});
```

**When to use:** Multi-environment E2E suites where test behavior should adapt to feature flags or backend capabilities without code duplication. **When NOT to use:** Feature flag logic that should be mocked at the JS level — use `launchArgs` to inject mock flag values into the app rather than branching in tests (test branching obscures real feature coverage). **Alternative:** A shared `e2e/config.ts` reading `process.env.*` CI variables is simpler for CI-only branching but doesn't participate in Detox's per-configuration launchArgs system. [official]

---

### Pattern 123 — `typeText()` vs `replaceText()` decision matrix with `clearText()` pitfalls [official]

`typeText()` and `replaceText()` are not interchangeable. `typeText()` appends to existing text and fires `onChangeText` keystroke-by-keystroke; `replaceText()` atomically overwrites and fires one `onChangeText`. Choosing the wrong one causes validation errors, cursor-position bugs, and duplicated content.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/formFill.ts

/**
 * Use replaceText for fields that need an exact deterministic value.
 * Use typeText only when the app's onChange validation requires per-keystroke events.
 */
export async function fillInputExact(
  testID: string,
  value: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const el = element(by.id(testID));
  await el.tap();
  await el.replaceText(value); // atomic overwrite — fires single onChangeText
  if (device.getPlatform() === 'ios') {
    await el.tapReturnKey();   // dismiss iOS predictive suggestion bar
  }
}

export async function typeIntoInput(
  testID: string,
  value: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const el = element(by.id(testID));
  await el.tap();
  await el.replaceText('');    // clear with replaceText (not clearText!) — fires onChangeText
  await el.typeText(value);    // char-by-char for live validation (email, phone format)
}

// e2e/forms.test.ts
it('validates email format on each keystroke using typeText', async () => {
  await typeIntoInput('email-field', 'bad-email');
  await expect(element(by.id('email-error-label'))).toBeVisible();

  await typeIntoInput('email-field', 'user@example.com');
  await expect(element(by.id('email-error-label'))).not.toBeVisible();
});

it('sets phone number field atomically with replaceText', async () => {
  await fillInputExact('phone-field', '+14155552671');
  await expect(element(by.id('phone-field'))).toHaveValue('+1 (415) 555-2671');
});
```

**When to use:** `replaceText` for form fields that should have exact known values (phone, date, code inputs). `typeText` for fields with per-keystroke validation. **When NOT to use:** `typeText` on secure text fields — it maps keystrokes and can fail if the keyboard layout changes between platform versions. **Alternative:** `replaceText` is almost always safer as the default; reserve `typeText` for cases where live-validation behavior is explicitly under test. [official]

---

### Pattern 124 — Biometric authentication simulation on iOS Simulator [official]

Apps protected by Face ID or Touch ID require simulating biometric success and failure states. Detox 20.51+ uses updated `--biometricMatch` / `--biometricNonmatch` flags on iOS 26+; older iOS targets use `matchFace()`/`unmatchFace()`.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/biometric.ts
export async function simulateBiometricSuccess(): Promise<void> {
  if (device.getPlatform() !== 'ios') {
    throw new Error('Biometric simulation only supported on iOS Simulator');
  }
  // iOS 26+: matchFace() internally maps to --biometricMatch (Detox 20.51+, PR #4932)
  // iOS <26: uses --matchFace (deprecated in iOS 26+)
  await device.matchFace();
}

export async function simulateBiometricFailure(): Promise<void> {
  if (device.getPlatform() !== 'ios') return;
  await device.unmatchFace(); // triggers Face ID failure → app shows PIN fallback
}

// e2e/auth.test.ts
describe('Biometric authentication', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      permissions: { faceid: 'YES' },
    });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('login-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(6000);
  });

  it('unlocks the app with successful Face ID', async () => {
    await element(by.id('biometric-login-btn')).tap();
    await simulateBiometricSuccess();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('shows PIN fallback after biometric failure', async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('biometric-login-btn')).tap();
    await simulateBiometricFailure();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('pin-entry-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });
});
```

**When to use:** Apps with biometric login, biometric-gated vault/wallet screens, biometric re-auth before sensitive operations. **When NOT to use:** Android biometric (no equivalent Detox API); physical iOS devices (simulation requires Simulator). **Alternative:** Inject a `__SKIP_BIOMETRIC__=true` launchArg to stub biometric in the app for non-biometric test coverage; use `matchFace()` only when the biometric flow itself is under test. [official]

---

### Pattern 125 — `by.type()` native component type matchers for third-party components without testID [official]

`by.type()` matches elements by their native class name (`RCTTextView`, `UIButton`, `android.widget.EditText`). This is useful for testing third-party components that don't expose `testID` but have a known native class, or for asserting component type in library integration tests.

```ts
// e2e/nativeComponents.test.ts

/**
 * Native class names:
 * iOS:     RCTView, RCTSinglelineTextInputView, RCTImageView, RCTScrollView, UIButton
 * Android: android.view.View, android.widget.EditText,
 *          android.widget.ImageView, android.widget.ScrollView
 */
function nativeTextInputType(): string {
  return device.getPlatform() === 'ios'
    ? 'RCTSinglelineTextInputView'
    : 'android.widget.EditText';
}

it('first unfilled text input on sign-up form receives focus', async () => {
  await waitFor(element(by.id('signup-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);

  // Locate by native type when testID is absent (third-party library field)
  const firstInput = element(by.type(nativeTextInputType()).atIndex(0));
  await firstInput.tap();

  const attrs = await firstInput.getAttributes();
  const isFocused = (attrs as any).focused ?? (attrs as any).elementFocused;
  expect(isFocused).toBe(true);
});

it('product page renders at least 3 images (no broken placeholder icons)', async () => {
  await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  const imageType = device.getPlatform() === 'ios'
    ? 'RCTImageView'
    : 'android.widget.ImageView';
  // getAttributes() returns an array when multiple elements match the matcher
  const result = await element(by.type(imageType)).getAttributes();
  const count  = Array.isArray(result) ? result.length : 1;
  expect(count).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
});
```

**When to use:** Third-party library components without `testID`; asserting native component counts (image gallery, input count); integration tests for RN native modules. **When NOT to use:** Any element that has a `testID` — `by.id()` is always more stable because class names vary across RN architectures (Classic vs Fabric). **Alternative:** Ask the library author to add `testID` forwarding; or use `by.label()` if the component exposes `accessibilityLabel`. [official]

---

### Pattern 126 — GitHub Actions matrix sharding with `--shard-index` / `--shard-count` for parallel CI [official]

Running all E2E specs sequentially creates a long CI critical path. Detox's `--shard-index` / `--shard-count` flags (20.x) divide spec files across workers, reducing wall-clock time proportionally. A GitHub Actions matrix strategy drives the shard index automatically.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/e2e.yml
name: Detox E2E (Sharded)
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  e2e:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]       # 4 parallel shards

    runs-on: macos-14              # Xcode 16 / iOS 18 Simulator

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: '20' }

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install CocoaPods
        run: pod install --project-directory=ios

      - name: Build Detox
        run: npx detox build --configuration ios.sim.debug

      - name: Run Detox shard ${{ matrix.shard }} of 4
        run: |
          npx detox test \
            --configuration ios.sim.debug \
            --shard-index ${{ matrix.shard }} \
            --shard-count 4 \
            --record-logs all \
            --take-screenshots failing \
            --reporter jest-junit
        env:
          JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT_DIR: ./reports
          JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT_NAME: results-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      - name: Upload shard report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: e2e-report-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: reports/results-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
```

**When to use:** E2E suites with 20+ spec files where total test time exceeds 15 minutes. **When NOT to use:** Suites with fewer than 10 spec files — shard overhead (emulator boot per shard, artifact upload) outweighs the parallelism benefit. **Alternative:** Detox's built-in `testRunner.maxWorkers` runs multiple workers on a single machine but is limited by CPU count; cloud CI matrix sharding scales across unlimited machines. [official]

---

### Pattern 127 — `device.disableSynchronization()` + `withLiveDataSync()` helper for WebSocket / SSE screens [official]

Screens receiving continuous WebSocket or Server-Sent Event updates keep Detox's sync engine perpetually busy (it sees ongoing network activity as "not idle"). `device.disableSynchronization()` disables auto-sync for the duration of the live-data assertion block, replacing it with explicit `waitFor` timeouts.

```ts
// e2e/helpers/withLiveDataSync.ts
/**
 * Executes `fn` with Detox synchronization disabled.
 * Re-enables synchronization in a finally block to prevent state leaks.
 */
export async function withLiveDataSync<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  await device.disableSynchronization();
  try {
    return await fn();
  } finally {
    await device.enableSynchronization();
  }
}

// e2e/liveScores.test.ts
import { withLiveDataSync } from './helpers/withLiveDataSync';

it('shows live score updates on the match screen via WebSocket', async () => {
  await element(by.id('match-list-item-0')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('match-detail-screen')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(5000);

  await withLiveDataSync(async () => {
    // Sync is OFF — the WebSocket ticker no longer blocks idle detection
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-team-score')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(6000);

    await waitFor(element(by.id('away-team-score')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(6000);

    // Assert score label format: digits only
    const attrs = await element(by.id('home-team-score')).getAttributes();
    expect(typeof (attrs as any).text).toBe('string');
    expect((attrs as any).text).toMatch(/^\d+$/);
  });
  // Synchronization is restored — subsequent tests are unaffected
});
```

**When to use:** Screens with WebSocket feeds, SSE streams, polling intervals under 5 seconds, continuous Reanimated `withRepeat` loops. **When NOT to use:** Navigation, form filling, or any screen where Detox idle detection is working correctly — disabling sync removes the safety net and makes flakes harder to diagnose. **Alternative:** Swap the WebSocket connection with a mock that fires a single `message` event and goes quiet — keeps sync enabled but requires app-side mock infrastructure. [official]

## Community Gotchas — Cycle 29

### Gotcha 173 — `element.clearText()` does not trigger `onChangeText` on Android 14+ [community]

**Root cause**: On Android 14+, `clearText()` uses the `CLEAR` accessibility action which empties the text content but does not fire the React Native bridge `onChangeText` event. State driven by `onChangeText` (form validation, character count labels, submit button enablement) remains stale after `clearText()`. The `replaceText('')` call does fire `onChangeText` and is the correct clear mechanism.

```ts
// BAD — clearText() leaves onChangeText-derived state stale on Android 14+
await element(by.id('search-input')).clearText();
// Character count label still shows old count — onChangeText was not fired
await expect(element(by.id('char-count-label'))).toHaveText('0'); // FAILS

// GOOD — replaceText('') fires onChangeText and clears the field
await element(by.id('search-input')).replaceText('');
await expect(element(by.id('char-count-label'))).toHaveText('0'); // PASSES

// WHY this matters: clearText() appears to work visually (the field empties) but
// onChangeText is silently skipped — form validation, error messages, and
// submit-button enable state are all affected, producing tests that pass visually
// but miss real user-facing bugs in character-count or validation UX on Android 14+
```

---

### Gotcha 174 — `waitFor().toBeVisible()` on `ActivityIndicator` times out when loading state is batched with content reveal in the same React render cycle [community]

**Root cause**: When a loading state and its resolved content update in the same React render cycle (inside a single `setState` batch), the `ActivityIndicator` may never be visible long enough to be sampled by Detox's accessibility query. `waitFor(spinner).toBeVisible()` therefore times out with "element not found" — making it impossible to assert the loading state. React 19's concurrent renderer coalesces state updates more aggressively, making this more common than in React 18.

```ts
// BAD — spinner is batched with content reveal; never sampled by Detox
await waitFor(element(by.id('loading-spinner'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
// Throws: Timeout — element not found: By.id('loading-spinner')

// GOOD — assert the RESULT of the async operation, not the transient loading state
await waitFor(element(by.id('product-list-item-0')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(8000);
// Once the list item is visible, the loading state has definitively resolved

// GOOD — if you must test loading state, add a guaranteed async gap via launchArgs:
// launchArgs: { SIMULATE_SLOW_LOAD_MS: '2000' }
// Then the spinner is guaranteed visible for 2s before content appears

// WHY this matters: React 19 concurrent rendering coalesces setState updates
// more aggressively — spinners tied to a single setState call may flash for <16ms,
// below Detox's accessibility polling resolution, causing tests targeting loading
// states to fail with no clear relationship to any code change
```

---

### Gotcha 175 — `device.launchApp({ url: deepLink })` on Android delivers the Intent to a stale Activity back-stack without `newInstance: true` [community]

**Root cause**: Android's Activity back-stack can contain a previous session's navigation state if the app process was cached (not killed). Launching via `device.launchApp({ url: deepLink })` starts the app but the Intent is delivered to an already-running Activity, which routes to the previous back-stack top instead of the deep link target. The fix is always pairing deep-link launches with `newInstance: true`.

```ts
// BAD — deepLink may land on a stale Activity back-stack top on Android
await device.launchApp({ url: 'myapp://product/abc123' });
await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
// FAILS intermittently — app lands on home screen from a previous test session

// GOOD — kill the process first so the deep link Intent targets a fresh Activity
await device.launchApp({
  newInstance: true,
  url: 'myapp://product/abc123',
});
await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(8000);

// ALTERNATIVE — openURL() after a clean launch
await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(6000);
await device.openURL({ url: 'myapp://product/abc123' });
await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

// WHY this matters: deep link tests are reliable on iOS Simulator (clean state)
// but intermittently fail on Android CI where the emulator image is reused across
// test runs — newInstance: true is the cross-platform defensive default for all
// deep link launch tests
```

---

### Gotcha 176 — Two sequential `tap()` calls are NOT a double-tap — use `element.multiTap(2)` [community]

**Root cause**: Two sequential `await element.tap()` calls are not equivalent to a double-tap. Each `tap()` is an independent gesture. The time between the first `tap()` resolving and the second beginning (including Detox IPC round-trip overhead) exceeds the OS double-tap recognition window (~300ms on iOS, ~500ms on Android). The correct API is `element.multiTap(2)`, which delivers both taps within the OS threshold.

```ts
// BAD — two tap() calls exceed the OS double-tap window; no double-tap fires
await element(by.id('image-viewer')).tap();
await element(by.id('image-viewer')).tap(); // treated as two separate single taps
// Result: zoom does not trigger; onDoublePress never fires; no error is thrown

// GOOD — multiTap(2) delivers both taps within the OS double-tap threshold
await element(by.id('image-viewer')).multiTap(2);
await waitFor(element(by.id('image-zoomed-overlay')))
  .toBeVisible()
  .withTimeout(2000);

// ALSO GOOD — triple-tap for text selection (iOS)
await element(by.id('paragraph-text')).multiTap(3);
await waitFor(element(by.id('text-selection-menu'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(1500);

// WHY this matters: double-tap is a first-class gesture on mobile (photo like,
// zoom, word selection) — using two tap() calls produces silent incorrect behavior
// (no error thrown, no assertion failure) until the UI assertion catches it,
// making this one of the most common "why does this test never work?" questions
// from engineers new to Detox
```

---

### Gotcha 177 — `device.takeScreenshot()` on iOS 18+ Simulator returns host display chrome when the Simulator window is occluded [community]

**Root cause**: iOS 18 changed how `xcrun simctl io booted screenshot` captures output. In previous versions it captured only the app's CALayer regardless of window state. In iOS 18, if the Simulator window is occluded by another macOS window, the capture includes the macOS compositor chrome (title bar, shadows, other windows). Parallel CI runs with multiple Simulator instances are especially affected.

```ts
// SYMPTOM — screenshot file is unexpectedly large and includes macOS window chrome
// Visual regression diffs fail on every CI run due to non-app pixels

// FIX 1 — use Detox's built-in artifact writer (uses private SimDevice API, not xcrun)
// Configure in .detoxrc.js — preferred over manual device.takeScreenshot() calls:
// artifacts: {
//   screenshots: {
//     shouldTakeAutomaticSnapshots: false,
//     keepOnlyFailedTestsArtifacts: true,
//   }
// }
// Then call: await device.takeScreenshot('my-screenshot');
// Detox's artifact writer uses the correct SimDevice API regardless of window state

// FIX 2 — bring the Simulator to front before capturing (best-effort)
async function bringSimulatorToFront(): Promise<void> {
  if (device.getPlatform() === 'ios') {
    const { execSync } = require('child_process') as typeof import('child_process');
    try { execSync('open -a Simulator', { stdio: 'ignore' }); }
    catch { /* non-critical — best effort */ }
  }
}

// Add to beforeAll in any describe block that takes screenshots:
beforeAll(async () => {
  await bringSimulatorToFront();
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
});

// WHY this matters: visual regression pipelines relying on screenshot diffing
// produce false failures on every run in parallel CI environments (macos-14 runner
// with 3+ Simulator instances), causing entire visual-diff jobs to fail on
// infrastructure issues rather than real regressions
```

---

### Gotcha 178 — `waitFor().not.toBeVisible()` resolves immediately when the element was never rendered, masking component crash bugs [community]

**Root cause**: `not.toBeVisible()` is satisfied by two distinct conditions: (a) the element exists but is not visible, or (b) the element does not exist at all. When a component fails to render due to a JS error caught by an error boundary (silently replaced by a fallback), the target element never appears in the accessibility tree. `not.toBeVisible()` resolves instantly — creating a false positive that masks the rendering failure entirely.

```ts
// BAD — passes silently even when the component crashed and never rendered
await waitFor(element(by.id('success-banner'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
// Passes because the component tree crashed before success-banner was mounted

// GOOD — assert the element appears first (proves rendering succeeded),
// then assert it dismisses (the intended assertion)
await waitFor(element(by.id('success-banner'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
await waitFor(element(by.id('success-banner'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

// ALSO GOOD — assert the surrounding screen is visible first to confirm no crash
await expect(element(by.id('payment-success-screen'))).toBeVisible();
// Now safe to assert the transient banner has dismissed
await waitFor(element(by.id('success-banner'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

// WHY this matters: React error boundaries in RN 0.73+ catch more JS errors
// silently, replacing broken subtrees with empty fallbacks — not.toBeVisible()
// cannot distinguish "element rendered and became hidden" from "element never
// existed", so a component crash can sail through tests that look for element
// absence, hiding regressions until a user reports them in production
```

---

## Updated Anti-Patterns Checklist (Cycle 29 additions)

| Anti-Pattern | Fix |
|---|---|
| Using `by.id('row-btn')` without ancestor scope when multiple rows share the same child testID | Use `by.id('row-btn').withAncestor(by.id('row-container-${id}'))` for unambiguous scoped selection (Pattern 113) |
| Using `element.clearText()` on Android 14+ to reset a form field with `onChangeText` validation | `clearText()` does not fire `onChangeText` on Android 14+ — use `replaceText('')` instead (Gotcha 173) |
| Calling `device.launchApp({ url: deepLink })` without `newInstance: true` on Android | Stale Activity back-stack routes to wrong screen — always use `newInstance: true` for deep link cold-start on Android (Gotcha 175) |
| Using two sequential `tap()` calls to simulate a double-tap | Two `tap()` calls exceed the OS double-tap timing window — use `element.multiTap(2)` (Gotcha 176) |
| Using `waitFor().not.toBeVisible()` as the only assertion on a transient success banner | Passes immediately if the element was never rendered due to error boundary — assert `toBeVisible()` first, then `not.toBeVisible()` (Gotcha 178) |
| Calling `device.reloadReactNative()` inside a test that belongs to a `describe` with `beforeAll` navigation setup | `beforeAll` is not re-executed after reload — re-navigate explicitly in the same test that triggers the reload (Gotcha 172) |
