**Pattern 502** — `device.setLocation()` GPS Coordinate Testing for Location-Aware Features

```typescript
// helpers/locationHelper.ts
import { device } from 'detox';

export interface LatLng { lat: number; lon: number }

export const LOCATIONS = {
  newYork:    { lat: 40.7128, lon: -74.0060 },
  london:     { lat: 51.5074, lon: -0.1278  },
  sydney:     { lat: -33.8688, lon: 151.2093 },
  nullIsland: { lat: 0,       lon: 0         },
} as const;

export async function setDeviceLocation(loc: LatLng): Promise<void> {
  await device.setLocation(loc.lat, loc.lon);
}

// e2e/nearby.test.ts
it('shows nearby restaurants for New York', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({
    newInstance: true,
    permissions: { location: 'always' },
  });
  await setDeviceLocation(LOCATIONS.newYork);
  await element(by.id('find-nearby-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('results-list')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(5000);
  const attrs = await element(by.id('results-list')).getAttributes();
  expect((attrs as { elements: unknown[] }).elements.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});

it('shows empty state outside service area', async () => {
  await setDeviceLocation(LOCATIONS.nullIsland);
  await element(by.id('find-nearby-btn')).tap();
  await expect(element(by.id('empty-state-label'))).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.setLocation()` works on iOS Simulator and Android Emulator but is silently ignored on physical devices — use a CI-only gate (`if (device.getPlatform() === 'ios' && isSimulator())`) to skip these tests on real-device farm jobs. On Android Emulator API 35+, `setLocation()` requires the cold-start permission grant pattern (two `launchApp()` calls — see Gotcha G114). Avoid asserting on rendered map tile content; always assert on app-layer UI elements (list counts, labels) that depend on the coordinate, not on map rendering itself which varies by network and tile cache state.

**Pattern 503** — `waitFor().toBeVisible().whileElement().scroll()` with Dynamic Section Header Skip

```typescript
// helpers/listHelper.ts
import { element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';

/**
 * Scrolls a SectionList until a target item is visible, skipping sticky headers.
 * Android RecyclerView with sticky headers can cause scroll to land on a header
 * rather than the item — re-scroll by one item height if a header is detected.
 */
export async function scrollSectionListToItem(
  listTestID: string,
  itemTestID: string,
  maxScrolls = 20,
): Promise<void> {
  await waitFor(element(by.id(itemTestID)))
    .toBeVisible()
    .whileElement(by.id(listTestID))
    .scroll(200, 'down');
  // Confirm item is actually in view (not a header that matched a similar testID)
  const attrs = await element(by.id(itemTestID)).getAttributes();
  const frame = (attrs as { frame: { y: number; height: number } }).frame;
  if (frame.y < 0 || frame.height === 0) {
    // Item is clipped — scroll one more step
    await element(by.id(listTestID)).scroll(80, 'down');
  }
}

// e2e/contacts.test.ts
it('scrolls to contact "Zara Wilson" in alphabetical list', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  await scrollSectionListToItem('contacts-section-list', 'contact-zara-wilson');
  await element(by.id('contact-zara-wilson')).tap();
  await expect(element(by.id('contact-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `whileElement().scroll()` uses the element itself as the scroll container, which means the scroll origin must be the list's `testID`, not a parent wrapper. Sticky section headers on Android (`SectionList` with `stickySectionHeadersEnabled={true}`) can intercept the `waitFor` check — the header has a different `testID` convention but shares the letter prefix, causing the scroll to stop one row early. Always validate the target item's `frame.y` against a threshold (> 0 and < viewport height) after the scroll loop to confirm the item is genuinely visible and not occluded.

**Pattern 504** — Deep Link Testing with `device.openURL()` and Universal Link Fallback Verification

```typescript
// e2e/deepLinks.test.ts
import { device, element, by, expect, waitFor } from 'detox';

const SCHEME = 'myapp';
const UNIVERSAL = 'https://example.com';

async function openDeepLink(path: string, useUniversal = false): Promise<void> {
  const url = useUniversal
    ? `${UNIVERSAL}/${path}`
    : `${SCHEME}://${path}`;
  // Ensure app is running before sending the URL (warm-start pattern)
  await device.openURL({ url });
}

describe('Deep Link Routing', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    // Cold-start: app must already be running for openURL to route correctly
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  });

  it('routes myapp://products/42 to ProductDetailScreen', async () => {
    await openDeepLink('products/42');
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(4000);
    await expect(element(by.id('product-id-label'))).toHaveText('42');
  });

  it('falls back to Universal Link https://example.com/products/42', async () => {
    await openDeepLink('products/42', true);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('shows 404 screen for unknown route', async () => {
    await openDeepLink('unknown/route/that/does/not/exist');
    await waitFor(element(by.id('not-found-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.openURL()` requires the app to be in the foreground or recently backgrounded — calling it before `launchApp()` results in the URL being dropped silently. For cold-start deep link scenarios, pass the URL via `launchApp({ url })` instead. Universal Links on iOS require the AASA file to be reachable at `https://example.com/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` even in Simulator — use `launchArgs: { BYPASS_AASA: '1' }` in a debug build variant to skip AASA validation during tests.

**Pattern 505** — `element.longPress()` with Duration and Position for Custom Context Menu Testing

```typescript
// e2e/contextMenu.test.ts
import { device, element, by, expect, waitFor } from 'detox';

async function longPressElement(
  testID: string,
  durationMs = 800,
  x?: number,
  y?: number,
): Promise<void> {
  if (x !== undefined && y !== undefined) {
    await element(by.id(testID)).longPress(durationMs, x, y);
  } else {
    await element(by.id(testID)).longPress(durationMs);
  }
}

describe('Context Menu', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('message-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('shows context menu on long press of a message bubble', async () => {
    await longPressElement('message-bubble-0', 800);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('context-menu-overlay')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);
    await expect(element(by.id('context-menu-copy-btn'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('context-menu-delete-btn'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('copies message text via context menu', async () => {
    await longPressElement('message-bubble-0', 800);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('context-menu-overlay'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await element(by.id('context-menu-copy-btn')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('copy-success-toast'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('dismisses context menu on backdrop tap', async () => {
    await longPressElement('message-bubble-0', 800);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('context-menu-overlay'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await element(by.id('context-menu-backdrop')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('context-menu-overlay'))).not.toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `element.longPress(durationMs)` triggers the native `onLongPress` handler, but the minimum effective duration differs by platform: iOS UIGestureRecognizer fires at ~500 ms while Android's `LongPressGestureHandler` default threshold is 300 ms. Always use ≥800 ms to ensure cross-platform reliability. The x/y position overload places the press at absolute pixel offsets from the element's top-left corner — misuse can trigger an adjacent element if the offset falls outside the bounds, particularly on small list-item cells.

**Pattern 506** — `device.disableSynchronization()` / `device.enableSynchronization()` Scoped Wrapper for Animation-Heavy Screens

```typescript
// helpers/syncHelper.ts
import { device } from 'detox';

/**
 * Temporarily disables Detox synchronisation for the duration of the callback.
 * Use ONLY for screens that drive continuous animations (video players, maps,
 * canvas-based charts) where Detox would wait forever for idle.
 * Always re-enable in finally to avoid leaving sync off for subsequent tests.
 */
export async function withSyncDisabled<T>(
  action: () => Promise<T>,
): Promise<T> {
  await device.disableSynchronization();
  try {
    return await action();
  } finally {
    await device.enableSynchronization();
  }
}

// e2e/videoPlayer.test.ts
it('shows playback controls while video is playing', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  await element(by.id('video-card-0')).tap();
  await withSyncDisabled(async () => {
    // Video renders at 60 fps — sync would never resolve idle
    await element(by.id('play-pause-btn')).tap();
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1500)); // deliberate wait inside sync-off zone
    await expect(element(by.id('playback-progress-bar'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('current-time-label'))).toBeVisible();
  });
  // Sync is restored here — subsequent actions use full synchronisation
  await element(by.id('back-btn')).tap();
});
```
Tradeoff: `disableSynchronization()` is a global state toggle — if the callback throws and `enableSynchronization()` is not called in `finally`, ALL subsequent tests in the worker run without synchronisation, causing cascading non-deterministic failures. Always use the `withSyncDisabled` wrapper (try/finally) rather than raw paired calls. Avoid nesting `withSyncDisabled` calls; if the inner action completes, the outer `finally` re-enables sync before the outer action is done, causing unexpected idle waits.

**Pattern 507** — `by.label()` + `by.value()` Combined Matcher for Accessible List Items

```typescript
// e2e/accessibleList.test.ts
import { device, element, by, expect, waitFor } from 'detox';

/**
 * Finds a list item by its accessibilityLabel AND accessibilityValue combination.
 * This is more precise than label alone when multiple items share a label prefix
 * (e.g., "Product" with value "In stock" vs "Product" with value "Out of stock").
 */
async function tapAccessibleListItem(label: string, value: string): Promise<void> {
  await element(by.label(label).and(by.value(value))).tap();
}

describe('Accessible Product List', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('taps an in-stock product row', async () => {
    await tapAccessibleListItem('Widget Pro', 'In stock');
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('stock-badge'))).toHaveText('In stock');
  });

  it('taps an out-of-stock product and sees disabled checkout', async () => {
    await tapAccessibleListItem('Widget Lite', 'Out of stock');
    await expect(element(by.id('add-to-cart-btn'))).not.toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('notify-me-btn'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `by.label().and(by.value())` applies both matchers simultaneously — both must be set on the same element, not on different nodes in the subtree. On Android, `accessibilityLabel` maps to `contentDescription` and `accessibilityValue` maps to `stateDescription` (API 30+) or is silently ignored below API 30. Always provide a `testID` fallback on Android and gate `by.value()` assertions with `device.getAPILevel() >= 30`. The combined matcher is significantly more readable in accessibility-first test strategies than index-based `atIndex()` selectors.

**Pattern 508** — Screenshot-Gated Visual Regression with `device.takeScreenshot()` and `jest-image-snapshot`

```typescript
// e2e/visualRegression.test.ts
import { device, element, by, expect } from 'detox';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import { toMatchImageSnapshot } from 'jest-image-snapshot';

expect.extend({ toMatchImageSnapshot });

async function captureAndCompare(
  screenshotName: string,
  maskTestIDs: string[] = [],
): Promise<void> {
  const screenshotPath = await device.takeScreenshot(screenshotName);
  const imageBuffer = fs.readFileSync(screenshotPath);
  (expect(imageBuffer) as unknown as { toMatchImageSnapshot: Function }).toMatchImageSnapshot({
    customSnapshotIdentifier: `${screenshotName}-${device.getPlatform()}`,
    failureThreshold: 0.03,
    failureThresholdType: 'percent',
  });
}

it('product list matches visual baseline', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  // Freeze dynamic content before screenshotting
  await device.setStatusBar({
    time: '9:41',
    batteryLevel: 100,
    batteryState: 'charged',
    wifiMode: 'active',
    wifiBars: 3,
  });
  await element(by.id('product-list')).waitFor;
  await captureAndCompare('product-list-screen');
  await device.resetStatusBar();
});
```
Tradeoff: Visual regression screenshots are inherently fragile on CI if font rendering, DPI, or OS-version differs from the baseline machine. Gate baselines per platform-OS-version tuple (e.g., `ios-18.3`, `android-35`) using a `customSnapshotIdentifier` that embeds `device.getPlatform()` and the OS version from `device.getUIDevice()`. Retina scaling (2×/3×) means pixel dimensions differ from logical point frames — always normalise screenshots to logical-point resolution (divide by `displayScale`) before comparing with element `frame` coordinates (see Pattern 499 related note).

**Pattern 509** — `element.scroll()` with `startPositionX`/`startPositionY` for Nested Horizontal-in-Vertical Scroll Containers

```typescript
// helpers/scrollHelper.ts
import { element, by } from 'detox';

/**
 * Scrolls a horizontal carousel nested inside a vertical ScrollView.
 * Uses startPositionY close to the carousel's centre to avoid triggering
 * the outer vertical scroll (which captures gestures at the edges).
 */
export async function scrollCarouselRight(
  carouselTestID: string,
  pixels = 300,
): Promise<void> {
  await element(by.id(carouselTestID)).scroll(pixels, 'right', 0.5, 0.5);
}

export async function scrollCarouselLeft(
  carouselTestID: string,
  pixels = 300,
): Promise<void> {
  await element(by.id(carouselTestID)).scroll(pixels, 'left', 0.5, 0.5);
}

// e2e/homeFeed.test.ts
it('reveals the 5th card in the featured carousel', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('featured-carousel'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  // Scroll right to reveal item not initially visible
  await scrollCarouselRight('featured-carousel', 350);
  await scrollCarouselRight('featured-carousel', 350);
  await expect(element(by.id('carousel-card-4'))).toBeVisible();
  await element(by.id('carousel-card-4')).tap();
  await expect(element(by.id('article-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: The `startPositionX`/`startPositionY` arguments to `element.scroll()` are normalised (0.0–1.0) offsets within the element's bounding box — a value of `0.5, 0.5` starts the gesture from the element centre, which is reliable for carousels. Setting `startPositionY` close to `0.0` or `1.0` in a nested scroll setup risks the outer vertical scroll container intercepting the gesture on iOS (UIScrollView gesture conflict) or Android (`NestedScrollingChild` consuming the event). When the carousel is partially off-screen, `waitFor().toBeVisible()` first to bring it into the viewport before attempting to scroll it.

**Pattern 510** — `device.getUIDevice()` for Runtime Device Metadata Guards in Shared Spec Files

```typescript
// helpers/deviceMetadata.ts
import { device } from 'detox';

interface DetoxDeviceMetadata {
  os: {
    name: string;
    version: string;
  };
}

let cachedMetadata: DetoxDeviceMetadata | null = null;

export async function getDeviceMetadata(): Promise<DetoxDeviceMetadata> {
  if (cachedMetadata) return cachedMetadata;
  // device.getUIDevice() returns the UIDevice object on iOS or UiDevice on Android
  // We infer OS version from it; shape depends on platform
  const platform = device.getPlatform();
  const apiLevel = platform === 'android' ? await device.getAPILevel() : null;
  cachedMetadata = {
    os: {
      name: platform,
      version: apiLevel ? `${apiLevel}` : 'unknown',
    },
  };
  return cachedMetadata;
}

export async function skipOnAndroidBelow(minApiLevel: number): Promise<boolean> {
  if (device.getPlatform() !== 'android') return false;
  const level = await device.getAPILevel();
  return level < minApiLevel;
}

// e2e/permissions.test.ts
it('shows precise location prompt (Android API 31+)', async () => {
  if (await skipOnAndroidBelow(31)) {
    return; // Precise location introduced in API 31
  }
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true, permissions: { location: 'inuse' } });
  await element(by.id('request-precise-location-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.system.label('Precise'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  await element(by.system.label('Precise')).tap();
});
```
Tradeoff: Caching `getAPILevel()` at the suite level (rather than per-test) is important — the call involves a native bridge round-trip and adds ~50 ms on each invocation. However, the cache must be scoped to `beforeAll`/module level, not a module constant, because `device` is not available at module import time. Prefer explicit version guards (`if (await skipOnAndroidBelow(31)) return`) over Jest `test.skip()` because `test.skip()` still shows in CI reports as skipped (confusing), while an early `return` makes the test vacuously pass (which is the correct intent for "not applicable").

---

**Pattern 511** — `device.appLaunchArgs` Static Injection for Feature Flag Testing Without Native Relaunch

```typescript
// e2e/featureFlags.test.ts
import { device, element, by, expect, waitFor } from 'detox';

/**
 * Launches the app with a specific feature flag set via launchArgs.
 * The app reads FEATURE_FLAGS from NativeModules.RNConfig or launchArgs
 * at startup and gates components accordingly.
 */
async function launchWithFlags(flags: Record<string, string>): Promise<void> {
  await device.launchApp({
    newInstance: true,
    launchArgs: { FEATURE_FLAGS: JSON.stringify(flags) },
  });
}

describe('Feature Flag: New Checkout Flow', () => {
  it('shows legacy checkout when flag is off', async () => {
    await launchWithFlags({ newCheckout: 'false' });
    await element(by.id('cart-checkout-btn')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('legacy-checkout-screen'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('shows new checkout flow when flag is on', async () => {
    await launchWithFlags({ newCheckout: 'true' });
    await element(by.id('cart-checkout-btn')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('new-checkout-screen'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('express-pay-section'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('new checkout flow completes order successfully', async () => {
    await launchWithFlags({ newCheckout: 'true', expressPayEnabled: 'true' });
    await element(by.id('cart-checkout-btn')).tap();
    await element(by.id('express-pay-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('order-confirmation-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(6000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `launchArgs` are passed as a flat string map — complex flag structures must be JSON-serialised and parsed in the app. `JSON.stringify()` in test code and `JSON.parse()` in app code introduces a serialisation boundary; boolean strings like `'true'`/`'false'` are not JavaScript booleans after `JSON.stringify` unless wrapped in an object. Always parse `FEATURE_FLAGS` with `JSON.parse(launchArgs.FEATURE_FLAGS ?? '{}')` in the app and default every flag to its production-safe value to prevent test-only launchArgs from corrupting prod builds.

---

**Pattern 512** — `element.multiTap()` for Double-Tap and Triple-Tap Gesture Testing

```typescript
// e2e/gestures.test.ts
import { device, element, by, expect, waitFor } from 'detox';

describe('Multi-Tap Gestures', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('photo-viewer-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('double-taps a photo to toggle zoom', async () => {
    await element(by.id('photo-image')).multiTap(2);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('photo-zoomed-indicator')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);
    await expect(element(by.id('zoom-level-label'))).toHaveText('2×');
  });

  it('double-taps again to zoom out', async () => {
    await element(by.id('photo-image')).multiTap(2);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('photo-zoomed-indicator'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await element(by.id('photo-image')).multiTap(2);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('photo-zoomed-indicator'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
  });

  it('triple-taps a text node to select all', async () => {
    await element(by.id('editable-note')).tap();
    await element(by.id('editable-note')).multiTap(3);
    // iOS text selection toolbar appears; assert on a selection-only action
    await expect(element(by.id('text-selection-copy-btn'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `element.multiTap(count)` fires `count` taps at the default inter-tap interval, which Detox derives from the platform's double-tap threshold (~300 ms on iOS, ~500 ms on Android). This means a `multiTap(2)` on Android may exceed the gesture system's double-tap recognition window on CI with animation scale 1.2×. If the double-tap is not recognised, the app receives two independent single taps — add a `waitFor` after `multiTap` with a fallback to `tap()` twice with a manual 200 ms gap. On Android, double-tap zoom in `react-native-zoom-toolkit` uses a custom `GestureDetector` with a configurable delay — always co-ordinate test timing with the configured threshold.

---

**Pattern 513** — `device.reverseTcp()` + `device.reversePorts()` for Android Emulator ↔ Host Mock Server Communication

```typescript
// e2e/setup/androidNetworkSetup.ts
import { device } from 'detox';

const MOCK_SERVER_PORT = 3001;

/**
 * Forwards Android emulator port to host machine mock server.
 * Required when a Node.js mock server runs on the CI host and the Android
 * emulator needs to reach it via localhost inside the emulator.
 * iOS Simulator shares the host network namespace — no setup needed.
 */
export async function setupAndroidPortForwarding(): Promise<void> {
  if (device.getPlatform() !== 'android') return;
  await device.reverseTcp(MOCK_SERVER_PORT, MOCK_SERVER_PORT);
}

export async function teardownAndroidPortForwarding(): Promise<void> {
  if (device.getPlatform() !== 'android') return;
  // reverseTcp cleanup: no explicit removal API in Detox 20.x
  // adb reverse is automatically cleaned up when the emulator process exits
}

// e2e/api.test.ts
beforeAll(async () => {
  await setupAndroidPortForwarding();
  await device.launchApp({
    newInstance: true,
    launchArgs: { API_BASE_URL: `http://localhost:${MOCK_SERVER_PORT}` },
  });
});

it('loads user profile from mock API', async () => {
  await element(by.id('profile-tab')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('user-name-label')))
    .toHaveText('Jane Doe')
    .withTimeout(4000);
});

it('handles 500 error from mock API gracefully', async () => {
  // Instruct mock server to return 500 for next request
  await fetch(`http://localhost:${MOCK_SERVER_PORT}/__configure`, {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ nextResponse: { status: 500 } }),
  });
  await element(by.id('refresh-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('error-banner'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.reverseTcp(remotePort, localPort)` wraps `adb reverse tcp:PORT tcp:PORT` — it is per-emulator-instance and must be called after `launchApp()` since the `adb` serial is only assigned once the emulator boots. In parallel CI with multiple workers, each worker gets a different `JEST_WORKER_ID` — assign unique mock server ports via `const port = 3000 + parseInt(process.env.JEST_WORKER_ID || '1', 10)` and pass that port to both `reverseTcp()` and `launchArgs.API_BASE_URL` to avoid port collisions between workers.

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha G310: `element.adjustSliderToPosition()` silently clamps positions outside 0.0–1.0 rather than throwing — out-of-range positions resolve to 0 or 1**
When `adjustSliderToPosition()` is called with a value below `0.0` or above `1.0` (e.g., `1.1` or `-0.05`), Detox silently clamps the position to the valid range rather than throwing an error. This means a test that passes `1.1` (intending to overshoot and verify clamping) will instead set the slider to its maximum value without any indication that the input was invalid.
Why this matters: TypeScript types for `adjustSliderToPosition()` accept `number`, not `number between 0 and 1`, so a calculation error in the normalisation formula (e.g., `value / max` where `max` is accidentally 0) passes `Infinity`, which clamps to `1.0` — the slider jumps to maximum and the test passes incorrectly. CI pipelines do not catch this because the slider ends up in a valid state.
Fix: Add an assertion guard before calling `adjustSliderToPosition()`: `if (pos < 0 || pos > 1) throw new Error(...)`. Then verify the resulting `getAttributes().value` matches the expected value within tolerance (see Pattern 499 helper). In TypeScript, use a branded type `type NormalizedPosition = number & { __brand: 'NormalizedPosition' }` and a factory function `toNormalized(n: number)` that throws on out-of-range input to prevent the issue at the call site.

---

**Gotcha G311: `device.openURL()` on Android requires the app to be foregrounded via `device.launchApp()` first — calling it on a cold-start background process silently drops the intent**
On Android, `device.openURL()` sends an `Intent.ACTION_VIEW` to the app process. If the app is not yet running (cold start) or is in a stopped state (e.g., after `device.terminateApp()`), the intent may be delivered to a new process before the React Native bridge has initialised, and the `Linking.getInitialURL()` call in the JS thread returns `null`. The app mounts its root navigator without the deep link path, landing on the home screen instead of the target route.
Why this matters: Deep link tests that follow the pattern `terminateApp() → openURL()` reliably fail on Android but pass on iOS (which uses `UIApplication.open(_:options:)` and properly queues the URL until the app finishes launching). The intermittency is higher on physical Android devices where launch time varies.
Fix: Use `device.launchApp({ url: 'myapp://path' })` for cold-start deep links on Android — this bundles the URL with the initial intent and Detox ensures it is available via `Linking.getInitialURL()` before React renders. Reserve `device.openURL()` for warm-start scenarios where the app is already running in the foreground or background.

---

**Gotcha G312: `waitFor(element).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout()` does not poll — it evaluates once immediately and resolves, causing false passes when an element is animating out**
`waitFor().not.toBeVisible()` uses Detox's synchronisation to wait for the app to be idle, then evaluates the visibility condition once. If an element is in the middle of a fade-out animation (opacity transitioning from 1 to 0), Detox considers the app "not idle" and waits for the animation to finish before checking visibility. However, with `disableSynchronization()` active or when using `withTimeout(0)`, the check fires immediately — if the element is still partially visible at opacity > 0.1 (Detox's visibility threshold), the assertion fails; if it is at opacity < 0.1 but not yet removed from the tree, it passes prematurely.
Why this matters: Modal dismissal tests and toast hide tests frequently use `not.toBeVisible()` to confirm the overlay is gone. When the dismiss animation is 300 ms and Detox checks at the ~150 ms midpoint (because something else caused an idle-check), the toast may be at opacity 0.5, which is above the visibility threshold — the assertion fails with "element is still visible" even though it will be gone in 150 ms.
Fix: Prefer `waitFor(element).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000)` with a generous timeout over no-timeout assertions. If the element is conditionally rendered (not just hidden), assert `not.toExist()` instead — this waits for the element to be unmounted from the tree, which is a more reliable terminal state than opacity-based visibility.

---

**Gotcha G313: `device.launchApp({ permissions: { camera: 'YES' } })` on Android 13+ does not pre-grant the `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` permission — media access requires a separate permissions key**
Android 13 replaced `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` with granular media permissions (`READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`, `READ_MEDIA_VIDEO`, `READ_MEDIA_AUDIO`). Detox's `permissions` map in `launchApp()` pre-grants permissions by their Detox alias: `camera` maps to `android.permission.CAMERA`, but `photos` maps to `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` (the pre-API-33 permission). On Android 13+ (API 33+), passing `permissions: { photos: 'YES' }` grants `READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, which is ignored by the runtime — the new media picker still prompts for `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES`.
Why this matters: Photo picker tests that worked on Android 12 emulators break on Android 13 CI jobs because the pre-granted permission is the wrong one. The picker dialog appears unexpectedly mid-test, causing the `tap()` on the gallery button to hit the permission dialog overlay instead of the intended UI.
Fix: For Android 13+ (API 33+), add an `afterEach` `device.launchApp({ newInstance: true, permissions: { camera: 'YES', medialibrary: 'YES' } })` pattern — `medialibrary` is the Detox alias that maps to `READ_MEDIA_IMAGES` on API 33+. Wrap with `if (await device.getAPILevel() >= 33)` to maintain compatibility with older emulator jobs.

---

**Gotcha G314: `element.typeText()` with multi-line strings containing `\n` inserts a literal newline character on iOS but submits the form on Android (triggers `onSubmitEditing`)**
When `typeText('\n')` or `typeText('line1\nline2')` is called on a `TextInput` with `multiline={false}`, iOS inserts a newline character into the field value (because the iOS keyboard returns character directly). Android interprets `\n` as the Return key action, which triggers `onSubmitEditing` — if the input is a search field or a login form, this submits the form mid-fill with incomplete data.
Why this matters: Tests that simulate multi-step form fill using a single `typeText('username\n')` to fill and submit a field will pass on iOS (newline in the value, no submit) but cause the form to submit prematurely on Android, landing on an error screen. The failure is systematic (every Android run) but looks like a "wrong navigation" error rather than an input problem.
Fix: Replace `typeText('username\n')` with `typeText('username')` followed by `element(by.id('input')).tapReturnKey()` on platforms where you want submit-on-return, or simply use two separate `typeText()` calls without `\n`. For `multiline={true}` fields where newlines are intentional, use `typeText('line1\nline2')` — this is safe on both platforms for multiline inputs.

## Cycle 59 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 514** — `element.tap()` with `x`/`y` offset for Tapping Inside a Complex Canvas or Map View

When a component renders a non-interactive wrapper with a single `testID` (e.g., a map tile, a custom canvas, or an SVG chart), `element.tap()` hits the centre of the bounding box by default. For charts and maps, the desired interaction is almost always at a specific coordinate offset from the element's origin. Use `element.tap({ x, y })` with offsets derived from the element's `frame` to target sub-regions deterministically.

```typescript
// helpers/tapAtNormalizedPoint.ts
import { element as detoxElement, by, element } from 'detox';

/**
 * Taps at a normalised position (0–1 each axis) within a named element.
 * Uses getAttributes().frame to convert to absolute pixel offsets.
 */
export async function tapAtNormalizedPoint(
  testID: string,
  nx: number,
  ny: number,
): Promise<void> {
  const el = element(by.id(testID));
  const attrs = await el.getAttributes();
  if ('frame' in attrs) {
    const { width, height } = attrs.frame;
    await el.tap({ x: Math.round(width * nx), y: Math.round(height * ny) });
  } else {
    throw new Error(`getAttributes() returned array for testID="${testID}". Ensure testID is unique.`);
  }
}

// e2e/map.test.ts
describe('Map interaction', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  });

  it('taps the south-east quadrant of the map canvas', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('map-canvas')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
    // Tap 75% across, 75% down — south-east quadrant
    await tapAtNormalizedPoint('map-canvas', 0.75, 0.75);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('location-detail-panel')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `getAttributes()` adds a round-trip to the Detox server (~30–80 ms on a warm simulator). For tight performance budgets, hard-code pixel offsets in a constant file keyed by device resolution and update them when screen layouts change. The frame-derived approach is more resilient across device sizes but slower. On Android, `frame` values are in logical pixels (dp), not physical pixels — do NOT multiply by `devicePixelRatio`.

---

**Pattern 515** — `device.shake()` with System-Alert Guard for Feedback/Debug Overlay Testing

`device.shake()` is the canonical way to trigger shake-gesture handlers on iOS Simulator (e.g., open an in-app debug menu, undo-text dialog, or feedback reporter). On iOS 18.4+ simulators the system "Report Feedback" sheet intercepts the shake intermittently. Wrap the shake call with a system-alert guard that dismisses the sheet if it appears before proceeding.

```typescript
// helpers/shakeWithGuard.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';

const FEEDBACK_SHEET_LABEL_IOS = 'Report Feedback';
const SHAKE_SETTLE_MS = 600;

export async function shakeWithGuard(): Promise<void> {
  await device.shake();
  // Allow system sheet to appear within 800 ms
  try {
    await waitFor(element(by.label(FEEDBACK_SHEET_LABEL_IOS)))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(800);
    // Dismiss the system feedback sheet by tapping Cancel
    await element(by.label('Cancel')).tap();
  } catch {
    // No system sheet appeared — normal path, continue
  }
}

// e2e/debugMenu.test.ts
import { shakeWithGuard } from '../helpers/shakeWithGuard';

describe('Debug menu (iOS Simulator)', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('opens the in-app debug menu on shake', async () => {
    await shakeWithGuard();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('debug-menu-overlay')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);
    await expect(element(by.id('debug-menu-version-label'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The 800 ms guard adds latency to every shake call that does NOT encounter the feedback sheet. Reduce it to 400 ms on fast M-series Mac runners and increase to 1200 ms on slow Linux CI machines. Alternatively, pre-dismiss the feedback sheet in `globalSetup` by programmatically resetting Simulator feedback preferences via `xcrun simctl` before the test suite starts — this avoids per-test overhead.

---

**Pattern 516** — `element.getAttributes()` Runtime Type Guard for Single vs Multi-Element Results

`element.getAttributes()` returns `ElementAttributes` when a single element matches the selector, but returns `ElementAttributes[]` (an array) when multiple elements match. Calling `.frame` directly on an array throws at runtime with an obscure "cannot read property of undefined" message. Add a runtime type guard before every `getAttributes()` call in shared helpers.

```typescript
// helpers/getSingleAttributes.ts
import { element, by, NativeElement } from 'detox';

interface SingleElementAttributes {
  frame: { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number };
  text?: string;
  label?: string;
  value?: string | boolean;
  enabled?: boolean;
  visible?: boolean;
}

type DetoxAttributes = SingleElementAttributes | SingleElementAttributes[];

function isSingleAttributes(
  attrs: DetoxAttributes,
): attrs is SingleElementAttributes {
  return !Array.isArray(attrs);
}

export async function getSingleAttributes(
  testID: string,
): Promise<SingleElementAttributes> {
  const el = element(by.id(testID));
  const attrs = (await el.getAttributes()) as DetoxAttributes;
  if (!isSingleAttributes(attrs)) {
    throw new Error(
      `getSingleAttributes(): testID="${testID}" matched ${(attrs as SingleElementAttributes[]).length} elements. ` +
        `Ensure testID is unique in the current view hierarchy.`,
    );
  }
  return attrs;
}

// Usage in a test
it('asserts the card frame width is at least 300 dp', async () => {
  const attrs = await getSingleAttributes('product-card');
  expect(attrs.frame.width).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(300);
});
```
Tradeoff: The helper throws on multi-match, which is the correct failure mode — a non-unique `testID` is a product bug, not a test bug. If the intent is to check ALL matching elements (e.g., verifying every list item's `enabled` state), iterate over the array form explicitly and do not use this helper. Keep the raw `getAttributes()` call for array scenarios so the intent is clear at the call site.

---

**Pattern 517** — `device.appLaunchArgs.modify()` for In-Suite Feature Flag Mutation Without Relaunch

`device.appLaunchArgs.modify(patch)` (Detox 20.9+) merges a patch object into the current launch args without triggering a full app relaunch. Combined with a JS-thread reload via `device.reloadReactNative()`, this allows flipping feature flags between `it` blocks in a single describe suite — avoiding the 3–6 s cold-start cost of `newInstance: true`.

```typescript
// e2e/featureFlags.test.ts
describe('New checkout flow behind CHECKOUT_V2 flag', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      launchArgs: { CHECKOUT_V2: '0' },
    });
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    await device.terminateApp();
  });

  it('shows legacy checkout when flag is OFF', async () => {
    await element(by.id('cart-checkout-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('legacy-checkout-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('shows new checkout when flag is ON', async () => {
    // Flip the flag — no full relaunch needed
    device.appLaunchArgs.modify({ CHECKOUT_V2: '1' });
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

    await element(by.id('cart-checkout-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('checkout-v2-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('restores legacy checkout after flag is reset', async () => {
    device.appLaunchArgs.modify({ CHECKOUT_V2: '0' });
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

    await element(by.id('cart-checkout-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('legacy-checkout-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `appLaunchArgs.modify()` patches the args in-memory on the Detox side but the app must actively read the new value — it must call `NativeModules.RNConfig.get('CHECKOUT_V2')` or equivalent on each JS-reload (not once at module level). Apps that cache launch args at module scope during initialisation will not see the change after `reloadReactNative()`. For those apps, `newInstance: true` with the updated args remains the only correct approach.

---

**Pattern 518** — `by.web()` with `webElement.selectAllText()` for WebView Input Field Clearing

When filling a form inside a `WebView`, Detox's `by.web()` API provides `webElement.clearText()` but it is unreliable on certain Android WebView versions — it clears the DOM `value` but does not trigger React's synthetic `onChange`, leaving controlled inputs stale. A more robust approach is `selectAllText()` followed by `typeText()` which replaces selected content and fires all input events.

```typescript
// helpers/fillWebInput.ts
import { web, by } from 'detox';

/**
 * Clears and fills a WebView text input using selectAllText + typeText strategy.
 * More reliable than clearText() for React-controlled inputs inside WebViews.
 */
export async function fillWebInput(
  webViewTestID: string,
  inputSelector: string,
  value: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const webEl = web(by.id(webViewTestID))
    .element(by.web.cssSelector(inputSelector));

  await webEl.tap();
  await webEl.selectAllText();
  await webEl.typeText(value, true); // replaceSelectedText = true
}

// e2e/webviewForm.test.ts
describe('WebView embedded payment form', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('open-payment-webview-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('payment-webview')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(6000);
  });

  it('fills and submits the card number field', async () => {
    await fillWebInput('payment-webview', '#card-number', '4111111111111111');
    await fillWebInput('payment-webview', '#expiry', '12/28');
    await fillWebInput('payment-webview', '#cvv', '123');

    await web(by.id('payment-webview'))
      .element(by.web.cssSelector('#submit-btn'))
      .tap();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('payment-success-banner')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `selectAllText()` is an iOS-only WebView API in Detox — on Android, fall back to `longPress()` on the field followed by a "Select All" context-menu tap, or use `replaceText()` via the native `by.id()` selector if the WebView input is accessible to the native accessibility tree (requires `importantForAccessibility="yes"` in the HTML). Check `device.getPlatform()` and branch accordingly in `fillWebInput`.

---

**Pattern 519** — `detox test --reuse` Flag for Iterative Local Test Development

When iterating on a single test file locally, the default `detox test` flow boots the emulator from scratch each run. Passing `--reuse` skips `device.launchApp()` on subsequent runs and reuses the already-running simulator/emulator, cutting per-run startup from ~20 s down to ~3 s. Combine with `--testPathPattern` to scope to a single spec file.

```typescript
// package.json scripts
// "scripts": {
//   "e2e:dev": "detox test --reuse --testPathPattern=login --loglevel=debug"
// }

// .detoxrc.ts — mark the debug configuration for reuse-compatible behaviour
import type { Detox } from 'detox';
const config: Detox.DetoxConfig = {
  testRunner: {
    args: { $0: 'jest', config: 'e2e/jest.config.ts' },
    jest: { setupTimeout: 120000 },
  },
  apps: {
    'ios.debug': {
      type: 'ios.app',
      binaryPath: 'ios/build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app',
    },
  },
  devices: {
    simulator: {
      type: 'ios.simulator',
      device: { type: 'iPhone 16' },
    },
  },
  configurations: {
    'ios.debug': {
      device: 'simulator',
      app: 'ios.debug',
    },
  },
};
export default config;

// e2e/login.test.ts — guard against stale state when reusing
describe('Login flow', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    // Always reset JS state even when --reuse skips cold boot
    await device.reloadReactNative();
  });

  it('rejects invalid credentials', async () => {
    await element(by.id('email-input')).replaceText('bad@email.com');
    await element(by.id('password-input')).replaceText('wrong');
    await element(by.id('login-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('error-message')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('error-message'))).toHaveText('Invalid credentials');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `--reuse` skips the `beforeAll` launch sequence, so any test that relies on cold-start state (cleared keychain, fresh permissions, specific deep-link URL on startup) will produce incorrect results. Keep `--reuse` strictly for local development iteration. CI pipelines must never use `--reuse` — each CI job must start from a clean emulator state. Add a CI check in your Makefile/workflow: `if [[ "$REUSE" == "1" && "$CI" == "true" ]]; then echo "ERROR: --reuse forbidden in CI" && exit 1; fi`.

---

**Pattern 520** — `element.swipe()` with `speed: 'slow'` for Drawer/Side-Menu Open Without Triggering System Gestures

iOS system navigation gestures (back swipe from the left edge, Control Center from the top edge) compete with `element.swipe()` when the start position is close to the screen edge. Using `speed: 'slow'` with an `startNormalizedX` offset of 0.15–0.20 (rather than 0.0–0.05) avoids triggering the system edge-swipe and reliably opens side drawers.

```typescript
// helpers/openDrawer.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';

interface DrawerConfig {
  drawerTestID: string;
  /** Normalised X start for the swipe — keep >= 0.15 to avoid iOS edge gesture */
  startNX?: number;
  /** Normalised Y mid-point to swipe from — 0.5 = vertical centre */
  startNY?: number;
}

export async function openLeftDrawer({
  drawerTestID,
  startNX = 0.15,
  startNY = 0.5,
}: DrawerConfig): Promise<void> {
  // Swipe right from the left region of the screen content area
  await element(by.id('app-root')).swipe('right', 'slow', 0.6, startNX, startNY);
  await waitFor(element(by.id(drawerTestID)))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(2000);
}

export async function closeLeftDrawer({
  drawerTestID,
}: Pick<DrawerConfig, 'drawerTestID'>): Promise<void> {
  await element(by.id(drawerTestID)).swipe('left', 'slow', 0.6, 0.8, 0.5);
  await waitFor(element(by.id(drawerTestID)))
    .not.toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(2000);
}

// e2e/drawer.test.ts
describe('Navigation drawer', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('opens and closes the navigation drawer', async () => {
    await openLeftDrawer({ drawerTestID: 'nav-drawer' });
    await expect(element(by.id('drawer-profile-link'))).toBeVisible();
    await closeLeftDrawer({ drawerTestID: 'nav-drawer' });
    await expect(element(by.id('nav-drawer'))).not.toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `speed: 'slow'` adds ~200 ms to each swipe gesture. On Android there is no equivalent system-edge gesture conflict, but slow speed still reduces false-positive failures caused by the gesture being classified as a scroll rather than a swipe on low-end emulators. The `0.6` normalised velocity parameter (third argument) controls how far the swipe travels — increase it to 0.8 for drawers that require a longer drag to latch open.

---

**Pattern 521** — `device.clearKeychain()` Between Authentication Test Suites to Prevent Token Bleed

On iOS, the Simulator keychain persists across app launches within the same Simulator instance unless explicitly cleared. Stored authentication tokens, biometric keys, and refresh tokens from one test suite can cause subsequent suites to skip the login flow entirely, making tests that assume a logged-out state produce false passes. Call `device.clearKeychain()` in `beforeAll` of any suite that tests authentication or onboarding.

```typescript
// e2e/auth/onboarding.test.ts
describe('Onboarding flow (unauthenticated)', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    // Purge all keychain items so the app treats this as a first install
    await device.clearKeychain();
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      delete: true, // also wipe user defaults / SQLite on first run
    });
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    await device.terminateApp();
  });

  it('shows the onboarding carousel on first launch', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('onboarding-step-1')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('onboarding-progress-dot-0'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('navigates through all onboarding steps', async () => {
    for (let step = 1; step <= 3; step++) {
      await element(by.id('onboarding-next-btn')).tap();
      await waitFor(element(by.id(`onboarding-step-${step + 1 <= 3 ? step + 1 : 'done'}`)))
        .toBeVisible()
        .withTimeout(3000);
    }
  });

  it('lands on the signup screen after completing onboarding', async () => {
    await element(by.id('onboarding-get-started-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('signup-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.clearKeychain()` is an iOS-only API — on Android, secure storage is scoped to the app's UID and is erased automatically by `launchApp({ delete: true })` (which reinstalls the APK). Wrap keychain-clearing logic in `if (device.getPlatform() === 'ios')` to keep the helper cross-platform. Note that `clearKeychain()` clears ALL keychain items for ALL apps on the Simulator, not just your app — this is safe for CI but should be avoided in shared Simulator environments where other apps' keychain data matters.

---

**Pattern 522** — `waitFor().toHaveText()` with a Locale-Resolved Text Helper for i18n Suites

Hard-coding expected strings in `toHaveText('Sign in')` couples tests to the current locale. When the same suite is run against a French locale build, the assertion fails with `toHaveText('Se connecter')`. Centralise all display-text expectations behind an `i18n(key)` helper that reads from the same translation JSON the app ships, so the test suite is locale-agnostic.

```typescript
// helpers/i18n.ts
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

// Reads from the same locales directory the React Native app bundles
const LOCALE = process.env.DETOX_LOCALE ?? 'en';
const translationsPath = path.resolve(
  __dirname,
  `../../src/locales/${LOCALE}.json`,
);
const translations: Record<string, string> = JSON.parse(
  fs.readFileSync(translationsPath, 'utf-8'),
);

export function i18n(key: string): string {
  const value = translations[key];
  if (!value) {
    throw new Error(`i18n key "${key}" not found in locale "${LOCALE}"`);
  }
  return value;
}

// e2e/login.test.ts
import { i18n } from '../helpers/i18n';

describe('Login screen', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      launchArgs: { RN_LOCALE: process.env.DETOX_LOCALE ?? 'en' },
    });
  });

  it('shows the correct headline text for the current locale', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('login-headline')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('login-headline'))).toHaveText(
      i18n('login.headline'),
    );
  });

  it('shows the correct CTA button label', async () => {
    await expect(element(by.id('login-submit-btn'))).toHaveText(
      i18n('login.submitLabel'),
    );
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `i18n` helper loads the JSON file synchronously at import time. In a large monorepo where translation files live far from the `e2e/` directory, the `path.resolve` call can silently succeed but read the wrong file if the working directory is not the project root. Pin the path to `__dirname` relative to the helper's own file location (as shown), not to `process.cwd()`. The helper also fails fast if a key is missing — treat that as a required side-effect: missing translation keys in tests mean the app ships without that string, which is a real bug.

---

**Pattern 523** — `element.scrollTo('top')` Before Asserting First-List-Item Visibility to Prevent Stale Scroll State

When a test suite runs multiple scroll-heavy scenarios in sequence and `reloadReactNative()` is used between tests (rather than `newInstance: true`), scroll position can persist in the JS state if the component does not reset its `ScrollView`/`FlatList` `contentOffset` on unmount. A defensive `scrollTo('top')` at the start of any test that asserts the first list item is visible prevents false negatives.

```typescript
// helpers/resetScroll.ts
import { element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';

/**
 * Scrolls a list to the top and waits for the first item to be visible.
 * Use in beforeEach for any test that asserts list-top content.
 */
export async function resetListToTop(
  listTestID: string,
  firstItemTestID: string,
  timeoutMs = 3000,
): Promise<void> {
  await element(by.id(listTestID)).scrollTo('top');
  await waitFor(element(by.id(firstItemTestID)))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(timeoutMs);
}

// e2e/feed.test.ts
import { resetListToTop } from '../helpers/resetScroll';

describe('News feed', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('feed-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('feed-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    await resetListToTop('feed-list', 'feed-item-0');
  });

  it('shows the first article headline', async () => {
    await expect(element(by.id('feed-item-0-title'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('feed-item-0-title'))).toHaveText('Breaking News');
  });

  it('shows the pull-to-refresh spinner on drag', async () => {
    await element(by.id('feed-list')).scroll(150, 'down');
    await waitFor(element(by.id('refresh-indicator'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    // Release and wait for refresh to complete
    await waitFor(element(by.id('refresh-indicator')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(6000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `scrollTo('top')` on a `FlatList` fires a native scroll-to-offset call, which completes synchronously on iOS but may trigger a layout recalculation on Android that is detected as "not idle" by Detox's synchroniser, adding 50–200 ms before the subsequent `waitFor` resolves. On very large lists (10 000+ items) with `initialNumToRender` tuned down, scrolling back to the top from a deeply scrolled position forces a full re-render window, which can take 500–1000 ms. In those cases, prefer `device.reloadReactNative()` over `scrollTo('top')` if cold-start cost is acceptable.

---

**Pattern 524** — Structured Test Artifact Collection with `afterEach` Screenshot + Log Bundle

CI failures are most actionable when they include a screenshot, a device log, and the view hierarchy at the moment of failure. Implement an `afterEach` artifact bundle in a custom `testEnvironment` or a shared `afterEach` helper that fires only when the test has failed, keeping the artifact directory lean for passing runs.

```typescript
// e2e/setup/artifactCollector.ts
import { device } from 'detox';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

const ARTIFACTS_DIR = process.env.DETOX_ARTIFACTS_PATH ?? path.resolve(__dirname, '../../e2e-artifacts');

function sanitize(name: string): string {
  return name.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, '_').slice(0, 120);
}

/**
 * Call inside afterEach to save screenshot + view hierarchy on failure.
 * Access `expect.getState().currentTestName` to get the failing test name.
 */
export async function collectArtifactsOnFailure(): Promise<void> {
  const state = (expect as any).getState?.();
  const failed = state?.assertionCalls > 0 && state?.numPassingAsserts < state?.assertionCalls;
  // Jest sets `currentTestName` on the global expect state
  const testName = state?.currentTestName ?? 'unknown-test';

  // Alternative: use jasmine/jest global currentTest info
  if (process.env.JEST_CURRENT_TEST_FAILED !== 'true' && !failed) return;

  const safeName = sanitize(testName);
  const timestamp = Date.now();
  const dir = path.join(ARTIFACTS_DIR, `${safeName}-${timestamp}`);
  fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });

  try {
    await device.takeScreenshot(path.join(dir, 'failure-screenshot'));
  } catch { /* ignore if device is unavailable */ }

  try {
    await device.captureViewHierarchy(path.join(dir, 'view-hierarchy'));
  } catch { /* ignore — not available on all platforms */ }
}

// e2e/jest.setup.ts
import { collectArtifactsOnFailure } from './setup/artifactCollector';

afterEach(async () => {
  await collectArtifactsOnFailure();
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.captureViewHierarchy()` adds 200–800 ms per failed test. On large test suites with many failures (e.g., first run against a newly broken build), this can significantly inflate total suite time. Gate `captureViewHierarchy` behind a `DETOX_CAPTURE_HIERARCHY=1` env variable so it is opt-in in CI and defaults off for local development. Screenshots via `device.takeScreenshot()` are fast (~30 ms) and should always be enabled for failing tests.

---

**Pattern 525** — `by.id()` with `atIndex(n)` for Asserting Specific Notification Cells in Notification Center Lists

When a list renders multiple items with the same structural `testID` pattern (e.g., `notification-cell`), `by.id('notification-cell')` matches all of them and `atIndex(n)` selects by render order in the accessibility tree. Use this for notification lists, search results, and activity feeds where items share a testID stem and an index suffix is either absent or dynamic.

```typescript
// helpers/notificationHelpers.ts
import { element, by, waitFor, expect as detoxExpect } from 'detox';

/**
 * Asserts text of the nth notification cell (0-indexed).
 * Assumes cells have testID="notification-cell" and inner text via testID="notification-cell-title".
 */
export async function assertNotificationAt(
  index: number,
  expectedTitle: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const cell = element(by.id('notification-cell')).atIndex(index);
  await detoxExpect(cell).toBeVisible();
  // Assert the title inside the nth cell using withAncestor
  const title = element(
    by.id('notification-cell-title').withAncestor(by.id('notification-cell').atIndex(index)),
  );
  await detoxExpect(title).toHaveText(expectedTitle);
}

export async function tapNotificationAt(index: number): Promise<void> {
  await element(by.id('notification-cell')).atIndex(index).tap();
}

// e2e/notifications.test.ts
describe('Notifications list', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      launchArgs: { SEED_NOTIFICATIONS: '3' },
    });
    await element(by.id('notifications-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('notification-cell')).atIndex(0))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('shows seeded notifications in correct order', async () => {
    await assertNotificationAt(0, 'Welcome to the app');
    await assertNotificationAt(1, 'Your profile is complete');
    await assertNotificationAt(2, 'New feature available');
  });

  it('navigates to notification detail on tap', async () => {
    await tapNotificationAt(0);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('notification-detail-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `atIndex(n)` is positional — it depends on the DOM/accessibility-tree order, which can change if the list re-renders with a different sort order, inserts an ad/promoted item at a fixed position, or re-orders items based on unread-first logic. Prefer unique per-item `testID`s derived from item IDs (e.g., `notification-cell-${id}`) whenever the backend returns stable IDs. Reserve `atIndex` for cases where item-level IDs are genuinely unavailable (paginated cursors, ephemeral toasts).

---

**Pattern 526** — `device.sendUserNotification()` Payload Testing for Rich Notification Rendering

Rich push notifications (those with images, action buttons, and custom UI extensions) must be tested end-to-end including the notification banner, the expanded view, and the action button taps. Use `device.sendUserNotification()` with a fully-formed APNS-style payload to trigger the notification while the app is in the foreground or background, then assert the rendered notification UI via Detox's system-element selectors.

```typescript
// helpers/pushNotification.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';

interface RichNotificationPayload {
  trigger?: { type: 'push' };
  title: string;
  subtitle?: string;
  body: string;
  badge?: number;
  payload?: Record<string, unknown>;
  /** iOS notification category for action buttons */
  category?: string;
}

export async function sendRichNotification(
  notif: RichNotificationPayload,
): Promise<void> {
  await device.sendUserNotification({
    trigger: notif.trigger ?? { type: 'push' },
    title: notif.title,
    subtitle: notif.subtitle,
    body: notif.body,
    badge: notif.badge ?? 1,
    payload: { aps: { 'content-available': 1 }, ...(notif.payload ?? {}) },
    category: notif.category,
  });
}

// e2e/pushNotifications.test.ts
describe('Rich push notification rendering', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      permissions: { notifications: 'YES' },
    });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('renders a rich notification banner with action buttons', async () => {
    await device.sendToHome();

    await sendRichNotification({
      title: 'New Order',
      body: 'Your order #1234 has shipped',
      category: 'ORDER_UPDATE',
    });

    // Assert the banner appears in the system notification area
    await waitFor(element(by.label('New Order')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
    await waitFor(element(by.label('Your order #1234 has shipped')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);
  });

  it('taps the "Track" action button on the notification', async () => {
    await element(by.label('Track')).tap();
    // App is foregrounded by the action and navigates to tracking screen
    await waitFor(element(by.id('order-tracking-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(4000);
    await expect(element(by.id('order-id-label'))).toHaveText('#1234');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.sendUserNotification()` is iOS-only. For Android, the equivalent is to send a broadcast intent via `device.reverseTcp()` + a local test server that triggers FCM through the app's `BroadcastReceiver`. Action button testing on the notification shade requires the Simulator to be in background/foreground-inactive state — tests that run entirely in the foreground will see the in-app notification handler fire instead of the system banner, meaning `by.label('Track')` will not find the system notification UI element. Always call `device.sendToHome()` before sending notifications that need system-banner rendering.

---

**Pattern 527** — `jest.retryTimes()` with `--forceExit` Guard to Prevent Hanging Retry Suites

`jest.retryTimes(n)` re-runs failing tests up to `n` times within the same Jest worker. Without pairing this with `device.reloadReactNative()` or `device.launchApp()` in the `beforeEach`, retried tests start from whatever dirty state the failing test left — often repeating the same failure. Additionally, when retries are enabled and a `device.terminateApp()` call in `afterAll` is skipped due to an unhandled promise rejection, the Jest worker hangs. Use `--forceExit` in CI detox test commands when `retryTimes` is active.

```typescript
// e2e/jest.config.ts
import type { Config } from 'jest';

const config: Config = {
  preset: 'ts-jest',
  testEnvironment: 'detox/runners/jest/testEnvironment',
  testTimeout: 120000,
  // forceExit is critical when using retryTimes — prevents hang on dirty teardown
  forceExit: true,
  globalSetup: 'detox/runners/jest/globalSetup',
  globalTeardown: 'detox/runners/jest/globalTeardown',
  testSequencer: './e2e/setup/testSequencer.ts',
};
export default config;

// e2e/flaky/animatedTransition.test.ts
// Retry up to 2 times for known-flaky animation timing tests
jest.retryTimes(2, { logErrorsBeforeRetry: true });

describe('Animated screen transition', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    // CRITICAL: reset state before EACH attempt, including retries
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    // Wrap in try/catch so a retry-induced dirty state doesn't block teardown
    try {
      await device.terminateApp();
    } catch {
      // swallow — forceExit will clean up the worker process
    }
  });

  it('completes the hero transition within 600 ms', async () => {
    const start = Date.now();
    await element(by.id('hero-card')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('detail-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(600);
    expect(Date.now() - start).toBeLessThan(600);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `logErrorsBeforeRetry: true` logs the failure reason before re-running, which is invaluable for diagnosing intermittent failures but adds noise to CI logs. Limit `retryTimes` to 2 — beyond 2 retries, the test is either genuinely broken or the app has a real flakiness issue that should be fixed at the source. Never use `retryTimes` for tests that mutate server-side state (e.g., purchases, account creation) — the retry will execute the mutation again, potentially creating duplicate records.

---

**Pattern 528** — Cross-Platform `accessibilityRole` Assertion via `by.traits()` (iOS) and `by.type()` (Android)

Asserting that a button is semantically a `button` (not just a `View` with an `onPress`) requires different APIs on iOS and Android. On iOS use `by.traits(['button'])` to verify the `UIAccessibilityTraitButton` trait. On Android use `by.type('android.widget.Button')` or assert `accessibilityRole` via `getAttributes().accessibilityRole`. Wrap in a cross-platform helper for consistent coverage.

```typescript
// helpers/assertAccessibilityRole.ts
import { device, element, by } from 'detox';

type CommonRole = 'button' | 'link' | 'image' | 'text' | 'header' | 'search';

const IOS_TRAIT_MAP: Record<CommonRole, string[]> = {
  button: ['button'],
  link: ['link'],
  image: ['image'],
  text: ['staticText'],
  header: ['header'],
  search: ['searchField'],
};

const ANDROID_TYPE_MAP: Record<CommonRole, string> = {
  button: 'android.widget.Button',
  link: 'android.widget.TextView',
  image: 'android.widget.ImageView',
  text: 'android.widget.TextView',
  header: 'android.widget.TextView',
  search: 'android.widget.EditText',
};

export async function assertAccessibilityRole(
  testID: string,
  role: CommonRole,
): Promise<void> {
  const platform = device.getPlatform();
  if (platform === 'ios') {
    const traits = IOS_TRAIT_MAP[role];
    if (!traits) throw new Error(`No iOS trait mapping for role "${role}"`);
    await expect(element(by.id(testID).and(by.traits(traits)))).toBeVisible();
  } else {
    // Android: assert via getAttributes().accessibilityRole (RN accessibility bridge)
    const attrs = await element(by.id(testID)).getAttributes();
    if (Array.isArray(attrs)) {
      throw new Error(`assertAccessibilityRole: testID="${testID}" matched multiple elements`);
    }
    const actualRole = (attrs as any).accessibilityRole as string | undefined;
    if (actualRole !== role) {
      throw new Error(
        `Expected accessibilityRole "${role}" but got "${actualRole}" for testID="${testID}"`,
      );
    }
  }
}

// e2e/a11y.test.ts
describe('Accessibility role assertions', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('confirms the search bar has the search role', async () => {
    await assertAccessibilityRole('global-search-bar', 'search');
  });

  it('confirms the hero CTA is a button', async () => {
    await assertAccessibilityRole('hero-cta-btn', 'button');
  });

  it('confirms the logo image has the image role', async () => {
    await assertAccessibilityRole('app-logo', 'image');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `getAttributes().accessibilityRole` on Android reflects the React Native `accessibilityRole` prop propagated through the native bridge, not the raw Android `AccessibilityNodeInfo` class. If a developer uses a bare `View` with `onPress` but does not set `accessibilityRole="button"`, the helper will report `undefined`, catching the a11y bug. By contrast, `by.traits(['button'])` on iOS matches the native `UIAccessibilityTraitButton` trait, which RN sets automatically for `TouchableOpacity` even without an explicit `accessibilityRole` prop — so iOS may pass where Android correctly fails. Document this asymmetry in your test suite and enforce `accessibilityRole` on all interactive elements in your component library lint rules.

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha G315: `element.scrollTo('bottom')` on Android `FlatList` with `onEndReached` pagination triggers the end-reached callback before `waitFor` resolves — next-page items appear mid-assertion**
When `scrollTo('bottom')` is used to scroll to the end of a paginated `FlatList`, it fires the native scroll event that triggers `onEndReached`. If the `onEndReached` callback fetches the next page and appends items, the list height increases after `scrollTo` returns, causing the "bottom" to move further down. Detox's synchroniser waits for the list to be idle, but the newly appended items trigger another re-render cycle, which can cause `waitFor(element(by.id('last-item'))).toBeVisible()` to evaluate before the final batch of items is rendered.
Why this matters: Tests that paginate through a list by calling `scrollTo('bottom')` repeatedly will intermittently skip the assertion on the true final item because the list is still loading page N+1 when the assertion fires. This produces false passes on fast simulators (page loads quickly, list settles before assertion evaluates) and false negatives on slow CI runners (list still loading when assertion fires).
Fix: After `scrollTo('bottom')`, add `await waitFor(element(by.id('loading-spinner'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000)` to ensure the pagination request is complete before asserting. If no loading indicator is present, use a `waitFor(element(by.id('end-of-list-marker'))).toBeVisible()` with an explicit end-of-list sentinel element rendered by the app when `hasNextPage` becomes false.

---

**Gotcha G316: `device.reloadReactNative()` after `device.disableSynchronization()` leaves synchronization permanently disabled — all subsequent `waitFor()` calls time out immediately**
If a test calls `device.disableSynchronization()` (e.g., to skip animation idle detection) and then calls `device.reloadReactNative()` without first calling `device.enableSynchronization()`, the JS bundle reloads but the Detox bridge retains the disabled-synchronization flag. Subsequent `waitFor()` assertions check the condition once (finding the app not yet idle) and resolve or reject immediately rather than polling, causing a cascade of failures in any test that runs after the offending one.
Why this matters: This failure mode is particularly insidious because the failing tests are in entirely unrelated files — the test that calls `disableSynchronization()` passes, and everything afterwards fails with cryptic "element not visible" errors. The root cause is far removed from the symptom. It is also not caught by `--runInBand` single-worker runs because the state only bleed when `reloadReactNative()` is used; a full `newInstance: true` relaunch resets the flag.
Fix: Always pair `disableSynchronization()` with `enableSynchronization()` in a `try/finally` block (see Pattern 476 `withSyncDisabled()` helper). If `reloadReactNative()` must be called while sync is disabled, call `enableSynchronization()` first, then `reloadReactNative()`. In `beforeEach`, defensively call `device.enableSynchronization()` at the top if your suite uses any `disableSynchronization()` calls, regardless of whether the previous test completed cleanly.

---

**Gotcha G317: `element(by.id('x')).atIndex(0)` and `element(by.id('x')).atIndex(1)` may resolve to the same native view on iOS when the view hierarchy has been partially recycled by UICollectionView**
On iOS, `UICollectionView` (which backs `FlatList`) recycles cells aggressively. When two cells share the same `testID` (which is propagated to the cell's `accessibilityIdentifier`), the accessibility tree can contain stale recycled cells whose `accessibilityIdentifier` has not yet been updated to reflect new data. As a result, `atIndex(0)` and `atIndex(1)` both resolve to the most-recently-rendered cell, which may be the same physical view instance with two different logical positions.
Why this matters: Tests that use `atIndex(n)` to assert on multiple list cells — e.g., verifying that items are in the correct sort order — will silently compare the same cell against itself, producing false passes. This is especially common after rapid programmatic scrolling (`scrollTo('bottom')` then `scrollTo('top')`) which causes heavy recycling before the accessibility tree stabilises.
Fix: After any scroll operation, call `waitFor(element(by.id('first-cell-unique-id'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000)` to ensure the list has settled before using `atIndex`. Better long-term fix: assign unique `testID` values per item (`cell-${item.id}`) so `atIndex` is never needed. When unique IDs are unavailable, add a 500 ms `waitFor` pause after scrolling in CI configurations by increasing `withTimeout` — do not use `sleep()`.

---

**Gotcha G318: `device.takeScreenshot()` on Android Emulator API 36 returns a black frame when hardware acceleration is disabled**
Android Emulator API 36 (Android 16) defaults to hardware-accelerated rendering for edge-to-edge display support. When the emulator is run in CI with the `-gpu swiftshader_indirect` or `-gpu off` flag (common in Linux-based CI environments without a GPU), `device.takeScreenshot()` returns a valid PNG file but the content is a solid black image because the framebuffer compositor cannot capture software-rendered frames.
Why this matters: Visual regression pipelines that compare screenshots fail with 100% pixel differences, causing all screenshot-gated tests to fail in CI while passing locally (where the developer has a GPU). The PNG file is created with the correct dimensions, so file-existence checks pass — the black content is only caught when the image is actually inspected.
Fix: In GitHub Actions / Linux CI, use `-gpu host` with KVM acceleration enabled (`enable-kvm: true` in the `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner` action) to enable hardware rendering. If KVM is unavailable (nested virtualisation not supported), fall back to `-gpu swiftshader_indirect` and disable screenshot-based visual regression for that CI configuration via a `SKIP_VISUAL_REGRESSION=1` env variable, running visual tests only on macOS runners with hardware GPU access.

---

**Gotcha G319: `waitFor(element(by.id('modal'))).toBeVisible()` resolves before the modal's enter animation is complete, causing subsequent `element.tap()` inside the modal to hit the element underneath**
Detox's `toBeVisible()` resolves when the element's `visibility` attribute in the accessibility tree changes to `true` — this happens when the element is added to the tree and has a non-zero frame. For modals and bottom sheets with an enter animation (sliding up, fading in), the frame is set immediately when the component mounts even though the animation places it off-screen at opacity 0 or translateY 100%. The accessibility tree reports it as visible (non-zero frame, not clipped) before it reaches its final on-screen position.
Why this matters: `await waitFor(element(by.id('modal'))).toBeVisible()` followed immediately by `await element(by.id('modal-confirm-btn')).tap()` will often tap the button behind the modal (the one at the same screen coordinates the button will eventually occupy) if the enter animation has not completed. This produces unexpected navigation or state changes — the wrong action fires silently.
Fix: After `toBeVisible()`, add a second assertion on a text element inside the modal that is only rendered after the animation completes (e.g., `await waitFor(element(by.id('modal-title'))).toHaveText('Confirm').withTimeout(2000)`). If no such sentinel exists, use `waitFor(element(by.id('modal-confirm-btn'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(1500)` — the button's own visibility resolves correctly because it is a descendant that is only composited after the parent animation finishes. Avoid `sleep()` even though a fixed 300 ms delay "works" — the correct fix is to assert a stable terminal state.

## Cycle 60 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 529** — `element.pinch()` for Map and Image Zoom-In / Zoom-Out Gesture Testing

```typescript
// helpers/pinchHelper.ts
import { element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';

/**
 * Performs a pinch gesture on an element.
 * @param testID  - testID of the pinchable element
 * @param scale   - >1 to zoom in, <1 to zoom out (e.g. 2.0 or 0.5)
 * @param speed   - 'fast' | 'slow' — use 'slow' for reactive gesture handlers
 * @param angle   - radians; 0 = horizontal, Math.PI/2 = vertical
 */
export async function pinchElement(
  testID: string,
  scale: number,
  speed: 'fast' | 'slow' = 'slow',
  angle = 0,
): Promise<void> {
  await element(by.id(testID)).pinch(scale, speed, angle);
}

// e2e/mapView.test.ts
describe('Map Pinch-to-Zoom', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      permissions: { location: 'inuse' },
    });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('map-view'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('zooms in to street level with a 2× pinch', async () => {
    await pinchElement('map-view', 2.0, 'slow');
    const attrs = await element(by.id('zoom-level-label')).getAttributes();
    const zoom = parseFloat((attrs as { text: string }).text);
    expect(zoom).toBeGreaterThan(14); // street-level zoom
  });

  it('zooms out to city level with a 0.4× pinch', async () => {
    await pinchElement('map-view', 0.4, 'slow');
    const attrs = await element(by.id('zoom-level-label')).getAttributes();
    const zoom = parseFloat((attrs as { text: string }).text);
    expect(zoom).toBeLessThan(10);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `element.pinch()` is an iOS-only API in Detox — Android does not expose a `pinch()` action because Android's `UiAutomator2` pinch gesture requires two separate pointer IDs that the Detox driver does not bridge. On Android, simulate pinch-to-zoom with `element.scroll(pixels, 'up')` on a `ScaleGestureDetector`-backed view only if the component exposes a zoom-level `testID`; otherwise assert indirectly on rendered content changes (tile label text, marker count) rather than the gesture itself. Always prefer `speed: 'slow'` for map and photo viewer components that use `PanResponder` — fast pinches miss the gesture recogniser's minimum velocity threshold.
