**Pattern 562** — `element.multiTap()` for Double-Tap and Triple-Tap Gesture Testing on Media and Editor Components
```typescript
// multi-tap-gestures.e2e.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

describe('Multi-tap gesture handlers', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('nav-media-viewer')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('media-viewer-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('double-tap on the image toggles zoom between 1× and 2×', async () => {
    const img = element(by.id('fullscreen-image'));

    // Confirm the initial zoom state via a testID on the zoom label overlay
    await expect(element(by.id('zoom-level-label'))).toHaveText('1×');

    await img.multiTap(2); // two rapid taps in the same location

    await waitFor(element(by.id('zoom-level-label')))
      .toHaveText('2×')
      .withTimeout(1500);

    // Double-tap again to zoom back out
    await img.multiTap(2);

    await waitFor(element(by.id('zoom-level-label')))
      .toHaveText('1×')
      .withTimeout(1500);
  });

  it('triple-tap in a rich-text editor selects the current paragraph', async () => {
    await element(by.id('nav-editor')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('rich-text-editor'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    await element(by.id('rich-text-editor')).tap(); // focus
    await element(by.id('rich-text-editor')).typeText('First paragraph text here.');

    await element(by.id('rich-text-editor')).multiTap(3); // select paragraph

    // The selection toolbar should appear
    await waitFor(element(by.id('selection-toolbar'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(1500);
    await expect(element(by.id('toolbar-bold-btn'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `element.multiTap(count)` issues `count` rapid synthesized taps with the system-defined inter-tap interval (~120 ms on iOS Simulator); on Android the synthesized inter-tap interval may exceed the OS double-tap threshold on slower emulators (API 28 and below), causing the gesture to be interpreted as two separate single taps rather than a double-tap — if this occurs, reduce the emulator animation scale to 0 via `adb shell settings put global transition_animation_scale 0` in CI setup scripts, which tightens the tap-recognition window.

**Pattern 563** — `element.adjustSliderToPosition()` for Range-Slider and Volume-Control Assertion
```typescript
// slider-controls.e2e.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

// adjustSliderToPosition(normalizedPosition) accepts a value 0–1 and maps it
// to the slider's full range. The assertion verifies the app's label reflects
// the correct value after the gesture.

describe('Volume and price-range sliders', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('nav-settings')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('settings-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('sets the volume slider to 50% and confirms the label reads 50', async () => {
    const slider = element(by.id('volume-slider'));
    await slider.adjustSliderToPosition(0.5); // 0 = min, 1 = max

    // App renders the current value as text in a sibling label
    await expect(element(by.id('volume-value-label'))).toHaveText('50');
  });

  it('sets the volume to maximum (1.0) and confirms the mute-off icon is hidden', async () => {
    await element(by.id('volume-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(1.0);
    await expect(element(by.id('mute-icon'))).not.toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('volume-value-label'))).toHaveText('100');
  });

  it('sets the price-range max slider to 75% and filters the product list', async () => {
    await element(by.id('nav-shop')).tap();
    await element(by.id('filter-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('price-range-panel'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    const maxSlider = element(by.id('price-max-slider'));
    await maxSlider.adjustSliderToPosition(0.75);

    await element(by.id('apply-filters-btn')).tap();

    // Product list should now show at most $750 items (max = $1000, 75% = $750)
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    const priceLabels = await element(by.id('product-price-0')).getAttributes();
    const price = parseFloat(((priceLabels as any).text as string).replace('$', ''));
    expect(price).toBeLessThanOrEqual(750);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `adjustSliderToPosition()` is iOS only in Detox's standard implementation; on Android you must use `element.scroll()` with a calculated pixel offset derived from the slider's `frame.width` and the target value, or use Detox's `element.setColumnToValue()` if the slider is backed by a `UIPickerView`; always test slider actions at the boundaries (0 and 1) separately from midpoints because OS-level clamping can cause off-by-one rounding that breaks `toHaveText` assertions.

**Pattern 564** — `by.web().element(by.web.id())` Multi-Step WebView Form Fill and Submission Testing
```typescript
// webview-form.e2e.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect, web } from 'detox';

// Detox 20+ ships a dedicated web() driver that interacts with WKWebView / WebView
// elements via the WebDriver protocol without needing a separate Appium server.

describe('WebView embedded checkout form', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('nav-checkout')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('checkout-webview'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('fills in the shipping address and submits the form', async () => {
    const webviewEl = web(by.id('checkout-webview'));

    // Type into the name field identified by its HTML id attribute
    await webviewEl.element(by.web.id('shipping-name')).typeText('Jane Doe');
    await webviewEl.element(by.web.id('shipping-address')).typeText('123 Main St');
    await webviewEl.element(by.web.id('shipping-city')).typeText('San Francisco');

    // Select a dropdown option by its visible text
    await webviewEl.element(by.web.id('shipping-state')).tap();
    await webviewEl.element(by.web.cssSelector('option[value="CA"]')).tap();

    await webviewEl.element(by.web.id('shipping-zip')).typeText('94105');

    // Submit
    await webviewEl.element(by.web.id('submit-btn')).tap();

    // After submission the WebView navigates to a confirmation page
    await waitFor(webviewEl.element(by.web.id('confirmation-heading')))
      .toExist()
      .withTimeout(8000);

    const headingText = await webviewEl.element(by.web.id('confirmation-heading')).getText();
    expect(headingText).toBe('Order confirmed!');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `web()` driver uses JavaScript injection under the hood (`window.__detox__.query(...)`) and requires the WebView's `javaScriptEnabled` prop to be `true` and `allowsInlineMediaPlayback` to not interfere with focus events; on Android, `WebChromeClient.onConsoleMessage` logging must be enabled in the debug build for Detox to receive JS execution results — if the WebView is in a `SameDocument` navigation the driver loses its context and all subsequent `web()` calls time out; call `webviewEl.runScript('window.__detox__.reset()')` in `afterEach` to reinitialise the bridge after any full-page navigation.

**Pattern 565** — `device.installApp()` / `device.uninstallApp()` for OTA Update and Fresh-Install State Verification
```typescript
// fresh-install-flow.e2e.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';
import * as path from 'path';

// Tests that require a truly clean install state (no prior shared preferences,
// no sandboxed caches, no residual keychain) cannot rely on launchApp({ delete: true }).
// device.uninstallApp() + device.installApp() performs a genuine reinstall.

describe('Fresh-install onboarding flow', () => {
  const appPath = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../build/MyApp.app'); // iOS Simulator

  beforeAll(async () => {
    // Uninstall removes the sandbox, keychain items, and app data entirely
    await device.uninstallApp();
    await device.installApp(); // reinstalls the .app bundle built by CI
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    // Restore the app for subsequent test suites without the overhead of reinstall
    // (already installed; launchApp will just bring it back)
  });

  it('shows the permissions request modal on the very first launch', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('onboarding-step-1')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(6000);

    await expect(element(by.id('request-notifications-btn'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('skip-permissions-btn'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('stores the onboarding-complete flag after finishing the flow', async () => {
    await element(by.id('request-notifications-btn')).tap();
    // Grant system alert
    await waitFor(element(by.label('Allow')).withAncestor(by.type('_UIAlertControllerActionView')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
    await element(by.label('Allow')).withAncestor(by.type('_UIAlertControllerActionView')).tap();

    await element(by.id('continue-btn')).tap();
    await element(by.id('continue-btn')).tap(); // step 2, step 3

    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

    // On a real reinstall the flag must have been written; verify by restarting
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    // Should go straight to home screen, not onboarding
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('onboarding-step-1'))).not.toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.uninstallApp()` + `device.installApp()` adds 15–45 seconds per test suite on a CI runner (app signing verification, sandbox creation, data-container allocation), making it prohibitively slow as a `beforeEach` hook; use it only in a dedicated `fresh-install.e2e.ts` suite that runs in its own CI job and gate it behind a `FRESH_INSTALL=true` environment variable so the majority of the test run skips reinstall and uses `launchApp({ delete: true })` instead.

**Pattern 566** — `device.takeScreenshot()` + Jest Snapshot Comparison for Visual Regression Gating
```typescript
// visual-regression.e2e.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

// Detox's built-in device.takeScreenshot() saves a PNG to the artifacts directory.
// This pattern uses pixel-diff comparison with a stored baseline to gate visual regressions.
// Requires: `npm install pixelmatch pngjs`

const BASELINE_DIR = path.resolve(__dirname, '__visual_baselines__');
const THRESHOLD = 0.01; // 1% pixel difference allowed

async function assertVisualMatch(snapshotName: string): Promise<void> {
  const screenshotPath = await device.takeScreenshot(snapshotName);
  const baselinePath = path.join(BASELINE_DIR, `${snapshotName}.png`);

  if (!fs.existsSync(baselinePath)) {
    // First run: write the baseline
    fs.mkdirSync(BASELINE_DIR, { recursive: true });
    fs.copyFileSync(screenshotPath, baselinePath);
    console.log(`[visual] Baseline written for "${snapshotName}"`);
    return;
  }

  const { PNG } = require('pngjs');
  const pixelmatch = require('pixelmatch');
  const img1 = PNG.sync.read(fs.readFileSync(baselinePath));
  const img2 = PNG.sync.read(fs.readFileSync(screenshotPath));
  const { width, height } = img1;
  const diff = new PNG({ width, height });
  const mismatchedPixels = pixelmatch(img1.data, img2.data, diff.data, width, height, { threshold: 0.1 });
  const ratio = mismatchedPixels / (width * height);

  if (ratio > THRESHOLD) {
    const diffPath = path.join(BASELINE_DIR, `${snapshotName}.diff.png`);
    fs.writeFileSync(diffPath, PNG.sync.write(diff));
    throw new Error(
      `Visual regression detected for "${snapshotName}": ${(ratio * 100).toFixed(2)}% pixels differ. Diff saved to ${diffPath}`,
    );
  }
}

describe('Visual regression: product detail screen', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true, launchArgs: { E2E_DISABLE_ANIMATIONS: '1' } });
    await element(by.id('nav-shop')).tap();
    await element(by.id('product-item-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('product detail hero section matches baseline', async () => {
    await assertVisualMatch('product-detail-hero');
  });

  it('product reviews section matches baseline', async () => {
    await element(by.id('product-detail-screen')).scroll(400, 'down');
    await assertVisualMatch('product-detail-reviews');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.takeScreenshot()` captures the entire device screen including the status bar — use `device.setStatusBar({ time: '9:41', batteryLevel: 100, batteryState: 'charged' })` before every screenshot to freeze the status bar to a deterministic state, otherwise the clock digits change between runs causing spurious pixel-diff failures; also disable all animations via `UIView.setAnimationsEnabled(false)` in an `E2E_DISABLE_ANIMATIONS` launch-arg branch, since a partially-animated element at screenshot time produces inconsistent baselines even on the same device.

---

**Pattern 567** — `element.setColumnToValue()` for `UIPickerView` / `Picker` Date and Category Selection
```typescript
// picker-selection.e2e.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

// React Native's <Picker> and date-picker dialogs are backed by UIPickerView (iOS)
// and Spinner / NumberPicker (Android). Detox's setColumnToValue() addresses a
// named column and an exact value string, avoiding brittle scroll-then-assert loops.

describe('Date of birth picker on profile setup', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('nav-profile')).tap();
    await element(by.id('edit-profile-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('dob-field'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('sets the date of birth to 15 March 1990 and saves', async () => {
    await element(by.id('dob-field')).tap(); // opens inline picker

    await waitFor(element(by.id('dob-picker'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);

    // iOS UIPickerView columns: [0] = month, [1] = day, [2] = year
    await element(by.id('dob-picker')).setColumnToValue(0, 'March');
    await element(by.id('dob-picker')).setColumnToValue(1, '15');
    await element(by.id('dob-picker')).setColumnToValue(2, '1990');

    await element(by.id('picker-done-btn')).tap();

    await expect(element(by.id('dob-field'))).toHaveText('March 15, 1990');
  });

  it('sets the category picker to "Electronics" in the product filter', async () => {
    await element(by.id('nav-shop')).tap();
    await element(by.id('filter-btn')).tap();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('category-picker'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Single-column picker
    await element(by.id('category-picker')).setColumnToValue(0, 'Electronics');
    await element(by.id('apply-filters-btn')).tap();

    await expect(element(by.id('active-filter-chip'))).toHaveText('Electronics');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `setColumnToValue()` matches by visible text (display label), not by the underlying `Picker.Item` value prop — if the app formats dates differently based on device locale (`März` in German, `marzo` in Spanish), the string literal in the test must match the current device locale; set the simulator locale explicitly in `detox.config.js` using `device.type = 'ios.simulator'` with a `bootArgs` entry of `-AppleLanguages "(en-US)" -AppleLocale "en_US"` to ensure locale-invariant picker text across CI regions.

**Pattern 568** — `waitFor(element).toHaveText().withTimeout()` Polling for Server-Driven UI Updates and Real-Time Data
```typescript
// real-time-data.e2e.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

// waitFor().toHaveText() polls the element's text every ~100 ms until it matches
// or the timeout expires. This is the canonical way to await asynchronous server
// responses that update labels (price tickers, order status, live scores).

describe('Real-time data: live sports score updates', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    // Launch with a WireMock server that serves pre-seeded scores via SSE
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      launchArgs: {
        API_BASE_URL: 'http://10.0.2.2:8080', // Android emulator → host
        SCORES_SSE_URL: 'http://10.0.2.2:8080/scores/live',
      },
    });
    await element(by.id('nav-scores')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('live-scores-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('updates the home team score label within 5 seconds of the SSE event', async () => {
    // WireMock is pre-configured to emit a "goal" SSE event 2 seconds after connect
    // The app's SSE handler updates the score label asynchronously
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-score-label')))
      .toHaveText('2')
      .withTimeout(8000); // 2s SSE delay + 5s buffer for slow CI runners
  });

  it('shows the "FULL TIME" badge after the final-whistle SSE event', async () => {
    // WireMock emits the final-whistle event at T+6s from the test-suite start
    await waitFor(element(by.id('match-status-badge')))
      .toHaveText('FULL TIME')
      .withTimeout(12000);

    // Score should be frozen at final tally
    await expect(element(by.id('home-score-label'))).toHaveText('2');
    await expect(element(by.id('away-score-label'))).toHaveText('1');
  });

  it('shows an error toast when the SSE connection drops', async () => {
    // Hot-swap the WireMock mapping to return 503 on the SSE endpoint
    const fetch = require('node-fetch');
    await fetch('http://localhost:8080/__admin/mappings/reset', { method: 'POST' });
    await fetch('http://localhost:8080/__admin/mappings', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({
        request: { method: 'GET', urlPattern: '/scores/live.*' },
        response: { status: 503 },
      }),
    });

    await waitFor(element(by.id('sse-error-toast')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(10000);
    await expect(element(by.id('sse-error-toast'))).toHaveText('Live updates unavailable');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Long `withTimeout()` values (8–12 s) inflate total suite duration on CI and can mask regressions where the UI never updates — always pair `waitFor().toHaveText()` with a second assertion that validates the final settled state and, where possible, assert intermediate transitions (e.g., a loading spinner that appears and then disappears) to ensure the app is actually responding to the data rather than rendering a static default value.

**Pattern 569** — `by.traits()` for iOS Accessibility Trait–Based Matching When `testID` Cannot Be Added to Third-Party Views
```typescript
// accessibility-traits.e2e.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

// by.traits() matches iOS UIAccessibilityTraits on native and React Native views.
// Useful for testing accessibility of third-party SDK components (e.g., a MapKit
// annotation, an in-app browser toolbar, a native ad container) that don't expose
// a testID prop or accessibilityIdentifier.

describe('Accessibility trait–based interaction on SDK views', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('nav-browser')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('in-app-browser'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('taps the back button in the in-app browser toolbar using button trait', async () => {
    // The browser toolbar is rendered by a third-party SDK without testIDs
    // by.traits(['button']) matches any view with UIAccessibilityTraitButton
    // by.label() further narrows to the "Back" button specifically
    const backBtn = element(by.traits(['button']).and(by.label('Back')));
    await waitFor(backBtn).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await backBtn.tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('confirms the activity indicator has the "updatesFrequently" trait during loading', async () => {
    await element(by.id('nav-feed')).tap();
    await element(by.id('refresh-btn')).tap();

    // The loading spinner from a third-party pull-to-refresh library
    // must expose "updatesFrequently" trait for VoiceOver to announce progress
    const spinner = element(by.traits(['updatesFrequently']));
    await waitFor(spinner).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    // Spinner disappears once the feed loads
    await waitFor(spinner).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(10000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `by.traits()` is iOS only — Android does not expose `UIAccessibilityTraits` and Detox will throw a descriptive error if `by.traits()` is called during an Android test run; gate every `by.traits()` usage with `if (device.getPlatform() === 'ios')` and provide an Android alternative (e.g., `by.label()` combined with `by.type('android.widget.ImageButton')`) so that the same spec file can run on both platforms without platform-specific test files.

**Pattern 570** — `element.getAttributes()` `text` and `placeholder` Properties for Form Validation State Assertions
```typescript
// form-validation.e2e.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor, expect } from 'detox';

// getAttributes() exposes the current text, placeholder, value, and enabled state
// of any view. For form fields this enables precise validation state assertions
// that would otherwise require checking sibling error-label testIDs.

type FieldAttrs = { text?: string; placeholder?: string; enabled?: boolean; value?: string };

async function getFieldState(testID: string): Promise<FieldAttrs> {
  const attrs = await element(by.id(testID)).getAttributes();
  return attrs as FieldAttrs;
}

describe('Registration form validation', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('nav-register')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('register-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('shows placeholder text in all empty fields on fresh load', async () => {
    const emailAttrs = await getFieldState('email-input');
    expect(emailAttrs.placeholder).toBe('Email address');

    const passwordAttrs = await getFieldState('password-input');
    expect(passwordAttrs.placeholder).toBe('Password (8+ characters)');
  });

  it('shows the inline error label when an invalid email is submitted', async () => {
    await element(by.id('email-input')).typeText('not-an-email');
    await element(by.id('submit-btn')).tap();

    // The error label appears as a sibling element with a dynamic testID
    await waitFor(element(by.id('email-error-label')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);
    await expect(element(by.id('email-error-label'))).toHaveText('Please enter a valid email address');

    // The field border should turn red — verify via accessibilityHint carrying the state
    const emailAttrs = await getFieldState('email-input');
    // The app sets an accessibilityHint of "invalid" on error state for screen readers
    expect((emailAttrs as any).hint).toBe('invalid');
  });

  it('disables the submit button when the required fields are empty', async () => {
    // Clear the pre-filled invalid email so both required fields are blank
    await element(by.id('email-input')).clearText();
    const submitAttrs = await element(by.id('submit-btn')).getAttributes();
    expect((submitAttrs as any).enabled).toBe(false);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `getAttributes()` returns different key sets on iOS vs Android — iOS exposes `text`, `placeholder`, `value`, `enabled`, `hintLabel`, and `frame`; Android exposes `text`, `enabled`, `contentDescription`, and `frame` but does not reliably expose `placeholder` text as a separate key (placeholder text is merged into the `text` field when the input is empty on some Android versions); write a cross-platform helper that normalises these differences and falls back to `toHaveText()` assertions on the placeholder text as a `text` value match on Android.

**Pattern 571** — Detox `testRunner.jest.verbose` + `--forceExit` Configuration for Hanging-Test Detection in CI
```typescript
// detox.config.ts  — Jest runner configuration for reliable CI teardown
import type { Detox } from 'detox';

const config: Detox.DetoxConfig = {
  testRunner: {
    args: {
      $0: 'jest',
      config: 'e2e/jest.config.js',
      // Prevent Jest from hanging if a test leaves an unresolved Promise or open handle
      forceExit: true,
      // Emit verbose test names to the CI log — easier to correlate with flake reports
      verbose: true,
      // Explicitly set the runner timeout to 90 s per test to detect network-dependent hangs
      testTimeout: 90000,
    },
    jest: {
      setupTimeout: 180000, // extra time for device boot in beforeAll
    },
  },

  configurations: {
    'ios.sim.debug': {
      device: { type: 'ios.simulator', device: { type: 'iPhone 15' } },
      app: { type: 'ios.app', binaryPath: 'ios/build/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app' },
    },
    'android.emu.debug': {
      device: { type: 'android.emulator', device: { avdName: 'Pixel_7_API_34' } },
      app: { type: 'android.apk', binaryPath: 'android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk' },
    },
  },

  artifacts: {
    rootDir: '.artifacts',
    plugins: {
      screenshot: { shouldTakeAutomaticScreenshots: true, keepOnlyFailedTestsArtifacts: true },
      log: { enabled: true },
      video: { enabled: false }, // enable only for local debugging; too slow for CI
    },
  },
};

export default config;
```
Tradeoff: `forceExit: true` terminates the Jest worker pool after all tests complete regardless of open handles — this masks legitimate resource leaks (unclosed WireMock server, un-unregistered `DeviceEventEmitter` subscription) that would otherwise be surfaced as a "Jest did not exit" warning; use `--detectOpenHandles` locally to identify leaks before enabling `forceExit` in CI, and add a `globalTeardown` script that explicitly calls `.close()` on any HTTP servers started in `globalSetup`.

**Pattern 572** — `device.captureViewHierarchy()` Diff Between States for Regression-Detecting Layout Invariant Tests
```typescript
// hierarchy-diff.e2e.ts
import { device, element, by, waitFor } from 'detox';
import * as fs from 'fs';

// device.captureViewHierarchy() writes a .viewhierarchy file (iOS) or a dump XML
// (Android) to the artifacts directory. This pattern uses the text content of the
// dump to assert structural invariants — that certain accessibility identifiers
// still exist in the hierarchy after a navigation, without asserting exact positions.

async function captureHierarchyText(name: string): Promise<string> {
  const filePath = await device.captureViewHierarchy(name);
  return fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8');
}

describe('Navigation hierarchy invariants', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  });

  it('home screen hierarchy contains the bottom tab bar after launch', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    const hierarchy = await captureHierarchyText('home-after-launch');

    // Assert the tab bar elements are in the hierarchy regardless of exact position
    expect(hierarchy).toContain('bottom-tab-bar');
    expect(hierarchy).toContain('tab-home');
    expect(hierarchy).toContain('tab-search');
    expect(hierarchy).toContain('tab-profile');
  });

  it('modal presentation does not remove the bottom tab bar from the hierarchy', async () => {
    // Bug regression: an earlier version of the sheet modal unmounted the tab bar
    await element(by.id('open-modal-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('modal-sheet'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    const hierarchy = await captureHierarchyText('with-modal-open');

    // The tab bar must still be present in the view hierarchy even if covered by the modal
    expect(hierarchy).toContain('bottom-tab-bar');

    await element(by.id('modal-close-btn')).tap();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: On iOS, `device.captureViewHierarchy()` produces a binary `.viewhierarchy` file readable by Xcode's View Hierarchy Debugger — the file is NOT plain text and cannot be `readFileSync`'d for string matching; instead, use the Android XML dump path (where the artifact is a plain-text XML) or build a custom helper that calls `element.getAttributes()` recursively via a Detox `launchArgs`-gated endpoint in the app to expose the hierarchy as JSON; the pattern above works only for Android in production and requires an adapter for iOS.

**Pattern 573** — Parallelised Multi-Worker Detox Run with `--shard` for Per-Suite Device Allocation in Large Test Suites
```typescript
// CI orchestration: GitHub Actions matrix strategy with Detox sharding
// .github/workflows/e2e.yml (excerpt shown as TypeScript detox.config.ts equivalent)

// detox.config.ts — shard-aware configuration
import type { Detox } from 'detox';

// DETOX_SHARD_INDEX and DETOX_SHARD_COUNT are injected by the CI matrix
const shardIndex = parseInt(process.env.DETOX_SHARD_INDEX ?? '0', 10);
const shardCount = parseInt(process.env.DETOX_SHARD_COUNT ?? '1', 10);

const config: Detox.DetoxConfig = {
  testRunner: {
    args: {
      $0: 'jest',
      config: 'e2e/jest.config.js',
      // Jest --shard=<index>/<count> splits the test file list evenly across workers
      shard: `${shardIndex + 1}/${shardCount}`,
      forceExit: true,
      testTimeout: 90000,
    },
  },

  configurations: {
    'ios.sim.ci': {
      device: {
        type: 'ios.simulator',
        // Each CI runner boots a uniquely-named simulator to prevent port conflicts
        device: { type: 'iPhone 15', name: `E2E-Shard-${shardIndex}` },
      },
      app: {
        type: 'ios.app',
        binaryPath: 'ios/build/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app',
      },
      // Each shard writes artifacts to a shard-specific subdirectory
      artifacts: {
        rootDir: `.artifacts/shard-${shardIndex}`,
        plugins: {
          screenshot: { keepOnlyFailedTestsArtifacts: true },
          log: { enabled: true },
        },
      },
    },
  },
};

export default config;

// e2e/jest.config.js — referenced above
module.exports = {
  preset: 'jest-circus/runner',
  testEnvironment: './environment',
  testMatch: ['<rootDir>/specs/**/*.e2e.ts'],
  // Jest handles the --shard flag natively; no extra plugin needed
  globalSetup: './setup/globalSetup.ts',
  globalTeardown: './setup/globalTeardown.ts',
};
```
Tradeoff: Jest's `--shard=N/M` splits the test *file* list alphabetically, not by test *count* or *duration* — if some spec files contain 2 long tests and others contain 20 short tests, the wall-clock time across shards will be uneven; mitigate by splitting large spec files into smaller ones (aim for ~3–5 tests per file) and by using `--randomize` to shuffle file order across shard runs so long-test-heavy shards rotate across CI workers rather than always falling on the same shard index.

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha G330: `element.typeText()` inserts text at the cursor position rather than at the end of the field — pre-filled inputs end up with new text inserted before existing content when the cursor defaults to position 0 after `tap()`**
On iOS Simulator, tapping a `TextInput` that already contains text places the cursor at position 0 (the very beginning of the field) if the tap hits the left half of the text. When `typeText()` is called immediately after, the new characters are prepended rather than appended. Teams that write `await element(by.id('email')).tap(); await element(by.id('email')).typeText('@domain.com')` to complete a partial email end up with `@domain.comjane@` instead of `jane@@domain.com`. On Android the cursor defaults to the end of the text, so the same test behaves differently across platforms, making the bug intermittent in cross-platform CI.
Why this matters: Form-fill tests that build a value incrementally (e.g., first `typeText` the username, then `typeText` the domain) produce incorrect final values on iOS when the field has been pre-populated by autofill or a previous test step, causing the `toHaveText` assertion to fail with a value that is a scrambled permutation of the intended string.
Fix: Always call `element.clearText()` before `typeText()` on a field that may contain pre-existing content, or use `element.replaceText(fullValue)` which bypasses cursor position entirely by replacing all current content atomically. If partial editing is genuinely required, call `element.tapAtPoint({ x: fieldWidth, y: fieldHeight / 2 })` using the field's frame width to place the cursor at the end before typing.

---

**Gotcha G331: `device.launchApp({ permissions: { notifications: 'YES' } })` grants the permission in the app's sandbox but does NOT dismiss a system alert if one is already visible — the system alert remains on screen and blocks subsequent element interactions**
`launchApp({ permissions })` writes the permission decision to the simulator's TCC database before the app process starts. If the app code calls `UNUserNotificationCenter.requestAuthorization()` early in the `AppDelegate` lifecycle (before the JS bundle loads), the system prompt can appear on-screen before Detox's automation layer is ready to intercept it. The `permissions` pre-grant means the TCC database already has `YES`, so the system will not show a new prompt — but if a prompt from a prior run was not dismissed (e.g., the previous test crashed mid-alert), the stale alert is still visible and `tap()` on any element beneath it will fail with "element is not hittable".
Why this matters: CI machines that run tests in sequence across multiple configurations can accumulate undismissed system alerts from crashes in earlier jobs. The second job's `launchApp({ permissions })` does not clear the stale alert from the first job, so every element interaction in the second job fails immediately with a misleading "not hittable" error that has nothing to do with the test's own logic.
Fix: Add a `beforeAll` hook that checks for and dismisses any visible system alert before the first test action: `await element(by.label('OK')).atIndex(0).tap().catch(() => {})` wrapped in a try/catch so it is a no-op when no alert is present. For a more robust solution, register a Detox `system-alert-handler` in `detox.config.js` that auto-dismisses all system alerts during the test run so no alert can block element interactions.

---

**Gotcha G332: `element.scroll()` on a `SectionList` stops at the section header boundaries on Android — passing a large pixel value does not scroll past a sticky section header because the header intercepts the touch event and anchors the scroll position**
`SectionList` with `stickySectionHeadersEnabled={true}` (the default on Android) renders sticky headers using a native `RecyclerView` decorator. When Detox's `element.scroll(distance, 'down')` generates a fling gesture, the Android `RecyclerView` scrolls until the next sticky header is about to snap into place, then pauses to allow the header to settle. For `SectionList` components with many sections close together, a single `scroll(800, 'down')` may only advance 2–3 sections instead of the expected 6–8, because each section header boundary terminates the scroll momentum.
Why this matters: Tests that try to reach an item in a later section by scrolling a fixed pixel distance are non-deterministic — the number of scroll repetitions required to reach a target item varies with the dynamic heights of content cells above it, making the test fragile on devices with different screen densities or when content items have variable text lengths.
Fix: Instead of scrolling by fixed pixel distances, use `waitFor(element(by.id('target-item'))).toBeVisible().whileElement(by.id('section-list')).scroll(200, 'down')` — the `whileElement().scroll()` idiom repeats the scroll action in increments until the target element becomes visible, which is robust to variable section heights and sticky header interruptions.

---

**Gotcha G333: `device.reloadReactNative()` triggers the `AppState` `change` event with value `'active'` on both iOS and Android — background-session and push-notification tests that call `reloadReactNative()` to reset state accidentally activate any code guarded by `AppState.addEventListener('change', handler)` before the test's own setup steps run**
`device.reloadReactNative()` reloads the JS bundle while keeping the native app process alive. As part of the reload sequence, React Native's `AppState` module fires a `change` event with `nextAppState = 'active'` because the bridge re-attaches to a foregrounded process. If the app subscribes to this event to resume background tasks (e.g., refresh auth tokens, replay queued API calls, reconnect WebSockets), those side effects execute during the reload — before the test's `beforeEach` hook has had a chance to stub the network or set the desired initial state.
Why this matters: Tests for the "session expired" flow that call `reloadReactNative()` after faking an expired token find that the app has already attempted a silent token refresh (triggered by the `AppState` change event during reload) and re-authenticated before the first test step runs, so the sign-in screen never appears and the test fails with "element not found" on the sign-in form.
Fix: Suppress `AppState` side-effect handlers in the E2E build target by checking a launch argument (`launchArgs: { E2E_SUPPRESS_APPSTATE_EFFECTS: '1' }`) at the top of the `AppState` handler body and returning early. Alternatively, replace `reloadReactNative()` with `device.terminateApp()` followed by `device.launchApp({ newInstance: true })` in tests that are sensitive to `AppState` events — the cold-start path does not trigger a spurious `'active'` event before the bundle has loaded.

---

**Gotcha G334: `expect(element).not.toBeVisible()` passes when the element is scrolled out of the viewport but is still mounted in the React tree — the element is invisible to the user but Detox considers it "not visible" for the wrong reason, masking layout bugs where the element should be unmounted entirely**
Detox's `toBeVisible()` checks whether the element has a non-zero frame that falls within the device's visible viewport rectangle. An element that is mounted but scrolled 200 px below the fold has a valid frame (non-zero width and height) at a Y position outside the viewport, so `not.toBeVisible()` passes. Teams that assert `expect(element(by.id('error-banner'))).not.toBeVisible()` after a successful action verify only that the banner is not currently on-screen — they do NOT verify that the banner was unmounted or that its opacity was set to 0. A regression that changes `display: 'none'` to `marginTop: -9999` still passes `not.toBeVisible()` and therefore goes undetected.
Why this matters: UI cleanup bugs where a dismissed toast or resolved error banner remains mounted (wasting memory and keeping subscriptions alive) are invisible to `not.toBeVisible()` assertions. Over time these leak accumulate — unmounted-but-present views build up in long E2E sessions and eventually cause `element(by.id('error-banner')).tap()` to hit the scrolled-off element instead of the intended on-screen one when the view is later re-shown.
Fix: Where it matters that an element is genuinely unmounted (not just off-screen), assert `await expect(element(by.id('error-banner'))).not.toExist()` instead of `not.toBeVisible()`. `not.toExist()` checks that no element with that `testID` is present anywhere in the view hierarchy, including off-screen positions. Reserve `not.toBeVisible()` for cases where the element is intentionally kept in the tree but hidden (e.g., an overlay that fades out but remains mounted for animation purposes).

## Cycle 63 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 574** — Ancestor-scoped matcher with `by.id().withAncestor()` for duplicate `testID` disambiguation
```typescript
// Multiple list rows share testID='row-action-btn'; target only the one inside the selected row
const selectedRow = element(by.id('product-row').withDescendant(by.id('selected-badge')));
const actionBtn = element(
  by.id('row-action-btn').withAncestor(
    by.id('product-row').withDescendant(by.id('selected-badge'))
  )
);

await expect(selectedRow).toBeVisible();
await actionBtn.tap();

// For iOS: chain .withAncestor() to narrow by container testID then by inner state
const confirmBtn = element(
  by.id('confirm-button').withAncestor(by.id('order-card-active'))
);
await expect(confirmBtn).toBeVisible();
await confirmBtn.tap();
await expect(element(by.id('order-status-label'))).toHaveText('Confirmed');
```
Tradeoff: `.withAncestor()` traverses the entire subtree upward from the target element on every evaluation — in flat lists with 200+ rows this adds ~15 ms per assertion on Android due to the recursive accessibility tree walk; mitigate by ensuring `testID` values encode enough state to be unique without the ancestor chain (e.g., `row-action-btn-${itemId}`) and reserve `.withAncestor()` for third-party components whose `testID`s cannot be changed.

**Pattern 575** — `by.descendant()` to match a parent container whose child satisfies a predicate
```typescript
// Tap the card that contains a "SALE" badge — useful when the card itself has no unique testID
const saleCard = element(by.id('product-card').withDescendant(by.text('SALE')));
await expect(saleCard).toBeVisible();
await saleCard.tap();

// Compose with atIndex() when multiple cards have a SALE badge — target the second one
const secondSaleCard = element(
  by.id('product-card').withDescendant(by.text('SALE'))
).atIndex(1);
await secondSaleCard.tap();

// Assert the selected card navigated to the detail view
await expect(element(by.id('detail-screen'))).toBeVisible();
await expect(element(by.id('detail-sale-badge'))).toBeVisible();
```
Tradeoff: `withDescendant(by.text(...))` matches on rendered text which is locale-sensitive — tests using `.withDescendant(by.text('SALE'))` will fail under any locale that translates the badge label; prefer `.withDescendant(by.id('sale-badge'))` and set the `testID` on the badge component to make the match locale-invariant.

**Pattern 576** — `element.swipe('down', 'fast', normalizedOffset)` with normalized swipe distance for sheet dismissal
```typescript
// Dismiss a bottom sheet modal with a downward fast swipe covering 60 % of screen height
async function dismissBottomSheet(sheetTestId: string): Promise<void> {
  await waitFor(element(by.id(sheetTestId)))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(3000);
  // normalizedOffset 0.0–1.0 maps to fraction of element's own height
  await element(by.id(sheetTestId)).swipe('down', 'fast', 0.6);
  await waitFor(element(by.id(sheetTestId)))
    .not.toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(2000);
}

// Usage in test
await openFilterSheet();
await dismissBottomSheet('filter-bottom-sheet');
await expect(element(by.id('results-list'))).toBeVisible();
```
Tradeoff: `swipe('down', 'fast', 0.6)` relies on the sheet's own dismiss velocity threshold — if the product team raises the required swipe velocity to prevent accidental dismissals, the same normalized offset at `'fast'` speed may still dismiss reliably while `'slow'` would not; always use `'fast'` for sheet dismissal and `'slow'` for intra-sheet scrolling to stay on the right side of velocity thresholds.

**Pattern 577** — `element.tapAtPoint({ x, y })` for canvas, map pin, and hit-zone precision tapping
```typescript
// Tap a specific pixel coordinate inside a custom canvas drawing element
const canvasEl = element(by.id('signature-canvas'));
await expect(canvasEl).toBeVisible();

// Start a signature stroke: tap top-left, drag center, release bottom-right
await canvasEl.tapAtPoint({ x: 40, y: 60 });
await canvasEl.tapAtPoint({ x: 120, y: 140 });
await canvasEl.tapAtPoint({ x: 220, y: 200 });

// Verify the canvas now reports a non-empty signature via accessibilityLabel
const attrs = await canvasEl.getAttributes();
// @ts-expect-error custom testAttributes set via AccessibilityLabel
expect(attrs.label).not.toBe('empty');
await element(by.id('submit-signature-btn')).tap();
await expect(element(by.id('confirmation-screen'))).toBeVisible();
```
Tradeoff: `tapAtPoint` coordinates are in points relative to the element's own origin — they do not auto-scale with screen density, so a tap at `{ x: 40, y: 60 }` on a 1× simulator and a 3× device hits the same logical point, but if the canvas scales its internal coordinate space to physical pixels the drawn strokes will appear at different positions; align your coordinate system by reading the element's `frame` from `getAttributes()` and computing tap points as fractions of `frame.width`/`frame.height`.

**Pattern 578** — `device.setLocation(lat, lng)` for geofence entry/exit and location-permission flows
```typescript
// Test geofence-triggered push notification when user enters a zone
describe('Geofence entry notification', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      permissions: { location: 'always' },
      newInstance: true,
    });
  });

  it('shows arrival notification when device enters store geofence', async () => {
    // Start outside the geofence boundary (store center: 37.7749, -122.4194, radius 200 m)
    await device.setLocation(37.7730, -122.4210);
    await element(by.id('map-screen')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('geofence-status-label'))).toHaveText('Outside zone');

    // Move inside the geofence boundary
    await device.setLocation(37.7749, -122.4194);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('geofence-status-label')))
      .toHaveText('Inside zone')
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.setLocation()` is iOS-Simulator-only and requires the `--allow-device-restart` Xcode flag to be absent from the sim configuration — on Android the equivalent is a mocked `LocationManager`; if the app uses `CLRegionMonitoring` the OS may batch geofence events and delay firing them up to 30 s after `setLocation()` is called, so `withTimeout(5000)` may need to be raised to `withTimeout(35000)` for real region-monitoring tests.

**Pattern 579** — `by.type('RCTTextInput')` fallback matcher for React Native core components without `testID`
```typescript
// Target a TextInput rendered by a third-party library that does not accept testID
// RCTTextInput is the underlying native type for React Native's TextInput on iOS
const isAndroid = device.getPlatform() === 'android';

// On Android the native type is 'android.widget.EditText'
const inputMatcher = isAndroid
  ? by.type('android.widget.EditText')
  : by.type('RCTTextInput');

const searchField = element(inputMatcher).atIndex(0);
await searchField.tap();
await searchField.clearText();
await searchField.typeText('shoes');

await element(by.id('search-submit-btn')).tap();
await expect(element(by.id('results-list'))).toBeVisible();
await expect(element(by.id('results-count'))).not.toHaveText('0 results');
```
Tradeoff: Native type names like `RCTTextInput` are implementation details of the React Native renderer — they change across RN versions (e.g., `RCTTextInput` → `RCTSinglelineTextInputView` in some RN 0.73 builds) and are absent in the New Architecture's JSI-based renderer, making `by.type()` a fragile last resort; always lobby the library maintainer to expose a `testID` prop before falling back to type-based matching.

**Pattern 580** — `element.scroll(distance, direction, startNormalizedX, startNormalizedY)` for scroll-start offset control
```typescript
// Scroll a horizontal carousel from its center to avoid edge dead zones on iOS
async function scrollCarouselRight(carouselId: string, times: number): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < times; i++) {
    // startNormalizedX=0.5 starts the drag from horizontal center
    // startNormalizedY=0.5 starts the drag from vertical center
    await element(by.id(carouselId)).scroll(280, 'right', 0.5, 0.5);
    // Brief settle wait — carousels often have deceleration animations
    await waitFor(element(by.id(`carousel-indicator-${i + 1}`)))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(1500);
  }
}

await scrollCarouselRight('featured-carousel', 3);
await expect(element(by.id('carousel-slide-4'))).toBeVisible();
```
Tradeoff: Using `startNormalizedX=0.1` (near the left edge) on a horizontal carousel often triggers the OS's back-gesture recognizer on iOS, consuming the swipe gesture before the scroll view sees it — always use `0.4`–`0.6` for horizontal scrolls on iOS to stay clear of the interactive back gesture zone that spans the leftmost 20 % of the screen.

**Pattern 581** — `element.pinch(scale, speed, angle)` for map zoom and pinch-to-zoom gesture testing
```typescript
// Test that pinch-zoom in on a MapView updates the zoom level label
describe('Map zoom gestures', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('map-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('map-view')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('zooms in when user pinches out with scale > 1', async () => {
    const mapEl = element(by.id('map-view'));
    const attrsBefore = await mapEl.getAttributes();
    // scale > 1 = zoom in (spread fingers); scale < 1 = zoom out (pinch fingers)
    await mapEl.pinch(2.0, 'fast', 0);
    const attrsAfter = await mapEl.getAttributes();
    // Zoom level stored in accessibilityValue.now (maps to aria-valuenow)
    expect(Number(attrsAfter.value)).toBeGreaterThan(Number(attrsBefore.value));
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `element.pinch()` is iOS-only — Detox does not synthesise a multi-touch pinch gesture on Android; for Android map-zoom tests you must either call a custom JavaScript bridge method that invokes `animateCamera({ zoom })` directly, or use `adb shell input` two-pointer gesture injection which is unreliable across API levels and not integrated into Detox's synchronisation lifecycle.

**Pattern 582** — `element.getAttributes()` with `frame` field for dynamic coordinate arithmetic
```typescript
// Compute the exact center of an element at runtime and tap its right-third hit zone
async function tapRightThird(testId: string): Promise<void> {
  const el = element(by.id(testId));
  await expect(el).toBeVisible();
  const attrs = await el.getAttributes();
  // frame is { x, y, width, height } in points relative to screen origin
  const rightThirdX = Math.round(attrs.frame.width * 0.83);
  const centerY = Math.round(attrs.frame.height / 2);
  await el.tapAtPoint({ x: rightThirdX, y: centerY });
}

// Usage: tap the ">" disclosure chevron in a list row without giving it a testID
await tapRightThird('settings-notification-row');
await expect(element(by.id('notification-settings-screen'))).toBeVisible();
```
Tradeoff: `getAttributes()` makes a synchronous accessibility-tree query which adds one full Detox IPC round trip (~20–50 ms on a local simulator, ~80–150 ms over a real-device USB bridge) before every `tapAtPoint` that uses it; avoid this pattern inside loops over large lists — instead, add a `testID` to the specific tap target so a direct `element.tap()` suffices.

**Pattern 583** — `waitFor(element).toHaveValue(value).withTimeout()` for async picker and slider state assertions
```typescript
// Assert that a Slider reaches a target accessibility value after automated adjustment
describe('Volume slider', () => {
  it('reflects the adjusted value in accessibility state', async () => {
    const slider = element(by.id('volume-slider'));
    await expect(slider).toBeVisible();

    // adjustSliderToPosition sets the slider to a 0.0–1.0 normalised position
    await slider.adjustSliderToPosition(0.75);

    // toHaveValue checks the accessibilityValue.now field (maps to aria-valuenow)
    await waitFor(slider)
      .toHaveValue('75')
      .withTimeout(2000);

    // Verify UI label also reflects the change
    await expect(element(by.id('volume-display-label'))).toHaveText('75%');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `toHaveValue()` reads `accessibilityValue.now` which React Native maps from the slider's `value` prop — if the component uses a debounced `onValueChange` to update the label (e.g., only fires after the user lifts their finger), `toHaveValue` may resolve before the label updates, causing a race between the slider value assertion passing and the label assertion failing; add an explicit `waitFor(...label...).toHaveText('75%').withTimeout(1000)` after `adjustSliderToPosition` rather than relying on sequential execution.

**Pattern 584** — `device.sendUserNotification(payload)` for foreground push-notification UI testing
```typescript
// Test that a foreground push renders a notification banner and navigates on tap
const pushPayload = {
  trigger: { type: 'push' } as const,
  title: 'Order Shipped',
  body: 'Your order #1042 is on its way',
  badge: 1,
  payload: { orderId: '1042', screen: 'OrderDetail' },
};

it('shows in-app notification banner for foreground push and navigates on tap', async () => {
  // App must be foregrounded for sendUserNotification to show an in-app banner
  await device.sendUserNotification(pushPayload);

  await waitFor(element(by.id('in-app-notification-banner')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(3000);
  await expect(element(by.id('notification-title'))).toHaveText('Order Shipped');

  await element(by.id('in-app-notification-banner')).tap();
  await expect(element(by.id('order-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible();
  await expect(element(by.id('order-id-label'))).toHaveText('#1042');
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.sendUserNotification()` is iOS-only and delivers the notification through the simulator's UNUserNotificationCenter — it cannot simulate background-delivered APNs payloads that wake a suspended app; for Android foreground push testing use a mock FCM server integrated via `launchArgs` to avoid platform-specific test code paths.

**Pattern 585** — `element.scrollTo('top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right')` for edge-reach assertions
```typescript
// Assert a T&C list shows an accept button only after scrolling to the bottom
async function scrollToBottomAndAccept(listId: string): Promise<void> {
  const list = element(by.id(listId));
  await expect(list).toBeVisible();

  // Scroll to the bottom edge — no pixel-distance guessing required
  await list.scrollTo('bottom');

  // Accept button should now be enabled at the bottom of the list
  await waitFor(element(by.id('accept-terms-btn')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(2000);
  await expect(element(by.id('accept-terms-btn'))).not.toHaveToggleValue(false);
  await element(by.id('accept-terms-btn')).tap();
}

await scrollToBottomAndAccept('terms-scroll-view');
await expect(element(by.id('account-created-screen'))).toBeVisible();
```
Tradeoff: `scrollTo('bottom')` performs an instant jump to the bottom content edge rather than a velocity-driven scroll, so any scroll-progress-based `enabled` logic in the component (e.g., a JS `onScroll` handler that enables the button when `scrollPosition >= contentHeight - viewportHeight`) may not fire if the component throttles `onScroll` events and the jump skips intermediate positions; verify the component uses `onContentSizeChange` or an `onMomentumScrollEnd`-based check rather than a frame-by-frame `onScroll` check to be compatible with `scrollTo`.

**Pattern 586** — `by.label()` matcher for iOS VoiceOver accessibility label assertions
```typescript
// Verify VoiceOver reads the correct label for a custom icon button with no visible text
describe('Accessibility label correctness', () => {
  it('cart icon announces item count to VoiceOver', async () => {
    // Add two items to cart
    await element(by.id('add-to-cart-btn')).atIndex(0).tap();
    await element(by.id('add-to-cart-btn')).atIndex(1).tap();

    // by.label matches against the accessibilityLabel prop (iOS) or contentDescription (Android)
    const cartBtn = element(by.label('Shopping cart, 2 items'));
    await expect(cartBtn).toBeVisible();
    await cartBtn.tap();

    await expect(element(by.id('cart-screen'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('cart-item-count'))).toHaveText('2');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `by.label()` performs an exact string match against `accessibilityLabel` — any change to the label format (e.g., `'Shopping cart, 2 items'` → `'Cart (2)'`) breaks the matcher silently if the label is generated dynamically and the test is not updated; use `by.label()` together with a snapshot or contract test on the accessibility label generation function to catch format regressions before they reach E2E.

**Pattern 587** — `element.longPressAndDrag()` for drag-and-drop list reordering on iOS
```typescript
// Reorder a draggable list: drag the first item to the third position
async function dragListItemToPosition(
  sourceIndex: number,
  targetIndex: number,
  listItemTestIdPrefix: string
): Promise<void> {
  const sourceEl = element(by.id(`${listItemTestIdPrefix}-${sourceIndex}`));
  const targetEl = element(by.id(`${listItemTestIdPrefix}-${targetIndex}`));

  // duration: ms to hold before drag starts (500 ms triggers drag mode in most RN lists)
  // normalized positions: 0.5, 0.5 = center of each element
  await sourceEl.longPressAndDrag(
    500,    // holdDuration before drag activates
    0.5,    // startNormalizedX
    0.5,    // startNormalizedY
    targetEl,
    0.5,    // targetNormalizedX
    0.9,    // targetNormalizedY — drop slightly below center to insert after target
    'slow',
    100     // holdDuration at drop point before release
  );
}

await dragListItemToPosition(0, 2, 'playlist-track');
await expect(element(by.id('playlist-track-0'))).toHaveText('Track C');
```
Tradeoff: `longPressAndDrag` is iOS-only and its eight-parameter signature is easy to mis-order — transposing `startNormalizedY` and `targetNormalizedX` produces a drag that moves horizontally off-screen rather than vertically down the list; write a thin wrapper function with named parameters (as shown) to make call sites readable and reduce mis-ordering bugs.

**Pattern 588** — `device.disableSynchronization()` + manual `waitFor` gates for video-player and animation-heavy screens
```typescript
// Disable Detox's automatic idle-waiting while a looping video plays to prevent test hang
describe('Video player controls', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('media-library-tab')).tap();
    await element(by.id('video-item-0')).tap();
    // Video playback keeps the JS run-loop busy — disable auto-sync to prevent infinite wait
    await device.disableSynchronization();
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await device.enableSynchronization();
  });

  it('pauses video on single tap and resumes on second tap', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('video-player'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    await element(by.id('video-player')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('pause-icon'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await element(by.id('video-player')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('play-icon'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.disableSynchronization()` turns off Detox's automatic waiting for the JS queue, native animations, and network requests — any `element.tap()` or `element.typeText()` called while synchronization is disabled will execute immediately without waiting for pending renders to settle, so you must add explicit `waitFor` gates before every interaction; forgetting even one `waitFor` causes flaky tests that pass on fast simulators but fail on slow CI machines where renders take longer.

### Community Gotchas

**G335** — `element.atIndex(n)` uses accessibility tree order, not visual top-to-bottom order on iOS
Why this matters: On iOS, UIKit accessibility elements are enumerated in the order the views were added to the parent view hierarchy, not in the order they appear on screen after Auto Layout. If a list row is reused by a `UITableView` in reverse-insertion order (prepend pattern), `element(by.id('message-bubble')).atIndex(0)` returns the oldest message (first inserted), not the topmost visible one (which is the newest). Tests asserting "the first visible message is from the current user" pass locally (where only 1–2 messages exist) but fail in CI after loading a fixture with 50 messages, because `atIndex(0)` resolves to a message deep in the history.
Fix: Instead of relying on `atIndex(0)` for the topmost visible item, give the most-recent item a dedicated `testID` (e.g., `latest-message`) so the matcher is always unambiguous regardless of list position. Alternatively, use `waitFor(element(by.id('message-bubble'))).toBeVisible().whileElement(by.id('messages-list')).scroll(50, 'up')` to scroll to the bottom of the list first and then assert against the visually last item.

---

**G336** — `device.reloadReactNative()` does not reset `AsyncStorage` — data written in one test persists into the next
Why this matters: `device.reloadReactNative()` keeps the native process alive and reloads the JS bundle, but does not wipe the simulator's sandboxed storage. `AsyncStorage`, MMKV, SQLite databases, and `NSUserDefaults` values written during an earlier test are still present when the next test runs. Teams that store auth tokens in `AsyncStorage` and call `reloadReactNative()` in `beforeEach` instead of `device.launchApp({ newInstance: true })` find that later tests start in the authenticated state even though the test's intent is to test the sign-in flow, making tests order-dependent.
Fix: Use `device.launchApp({ newInstance: true })` for tests that require a fully clean storage state. For tests that only need to reset JS state (not storage), `reloadReactNative()` is fine. As a belt-and-suspenders measure, expose a `__E2E_RESET_STORAGE__` launch argument that clears all `AsyncStorage` keys in the app's `useEffect` during test runs so a controlled reset is possible without a full process restart.

---

**G337** — `toBeVisible()` returns `true` for an element with `opacity: 0` on Android — opacity is not included in Detox's Android visibility check
Why this matters: Detox's Android visibility check uses the `ViewCompat.isVisibleToUser()` API which checks `View.VISIBLE` (not `View.INVISIBLE` or `View.GONE`), `isAttachedToWindow()`, and whether the view's frame intersects the screen rectangle. It does NOT check the view's computed `alpha` value. An element animated out with `Animated.timing(opacity, { toValue: 0 })` is still considered visible by Detox on Android because its `View.VISIBLE` flag is set and its frame is on-screen. On iOS, UIKit's accessibility visibility check does account for alpha, so the same assertion behaves differently: `expect(element).toBeVisible()` fails on iOS but passes on Android for a zero-opacity element.
Fix: For opacity-based show/hide patterns on Android, also assert `toHaveValue('0')` (if you expose opacity through `accessibilityValue`) or, better, unmount the element rather than fading it to zero opacity. Alternatively, wrap the fade in a callback that sets `display: 'none'` after the animation completes so both platforms agree on visibility.

---

**G338** — `element.typeText()` on a field inside a `Modal` fails on Android when the keyboard is in `adjustResize` mode and shifts the element's frame out of the pre-tap position
Why this matters: When `android:windowSoftInputMode="adjustResize"` is set in `AndroidManifest.xml`, the entire activity window shrinks when the software keyboard appears. If Detox taps the field at its frame position before the keyboard appears, then the keyboard opens and the activity resizes, the element may shift upward. Subsequent `typeText()` calls still succeed (they use the focused element, not coordinates), but assertions that check elements directly above the keyboard (e.g., a validation label just above the field) fail because those elements are now partially obscured by the keyboard overlay.
Fix: After calling `element.tap()` on a field inside a Modal, add `await waitFor(element(by.id('keyboard-avoiding-container'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(1500)` (targeting the `KeyboardAvoidingView` wrapper) to confirm the layout has settled after keyboard appearance before asserting any positions. Alternatively, switch to `adjustPan` for E2E test builds via a `<meta-data>` tag in the debug manifest to prevent the activity from resizing.

---

**G339** — `waitFor(element).toBeVisible().whileElement().scroll()` does not work when the scrollable container is inside a `Modal` on iOS
Why this matters: The `whileElement(by.id('modal-scroll'))` argument is supposed to restrict the scroll to a specific scroll view. On iOS, when the modal is presented using React Native's `<Modal>` component, the modal's content is rendered in a separate UIWindow layer above the main app window. Detox's `whileElement().scroll()` resolves scroll view elements by searching the main UIWindow's accessibility tree; the modal's scroll view lives in the overlay UIWindow and may not appear in the main window's tree, so the scroll action falls back to the closest scrollable element in the main window — typically the root scroll view behind the modal.
Fix: Give the modal's scroll view a `testID` and replace the `whileElement().scroll()` pattern with a direct `element(by.id('modal-scroll')).scroll(200, 'down')` call inside a `waitFor` polling loop. The direct `element.scroll()` call resolves the element by accessibility ID across all UIWindow layers, avoiding the main-window-only limitation of the `whileElement` resolver.

## Cycle 64 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 589** — `element.tapBackspaceKey()` and `element.tapReturnKey()` for keyboard control without relying on native keyboard coordinates
```typescript
// Use semantic keyboard action helpers instead of coordinate-based taps
// to reliably interact with the soft keyboard across device sizes and OS versions
describe('Search field keyboard interactions', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('search-bar')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('search-input'))).toBeFocused().withTimeout(2000);
  });

  it('clears last character with backspace and submits with return key', async () => {
    await element(by.id('search-input')).typeText('react natve'); // intentional typo
    await element(by.id('search-input')).tapBackspaceKey();      // remove 'e'
    await element(by.id('search-input')).tapBackspaceKey();      // remove 'v'
    await element(by.id('search-input')).tapBackspaceKey();      // remove 't'
    await element(by.id('search-input')).typeText('ive');        // re-type correct suffix
    await element(by.id('search-input')).tapReturnKey();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('search-results-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    await expect(element(by.id('search-results-count'))).toHaveText('12 results');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `tapBackspaceKey()` and `tapReturnKey()` fire the hardware-keyboard delete and return events rather than tapping pixel coordinates on the soft keyboard, so they work identically on all simulator sizes and physical devices; however, they only operate on the currently focused element — if focus has shifted due to an auto-advance behavior (e.g., a PIN entry field that moves focus to the next digit box after one character), each `tapBackspaceKey()` call deletes from whichever field is currently focused, not necessarily the one you targeted, requiring explicit re-focus taps between backspace sequences.

**Pattern 590** — `element.clearText()` followed by `element.typeText()` for idempotent field replacement across pre-populated form fields
```typescript
// Pre-populated edit forms retain old values — clearText() + typeText() ensures
// the field contains exactly what the test needs, regardless of existing content
describe('Edit profile form', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: false });
    // Navigate to the profile edit screen where fields are pre-populated from the server
    await element(by.id('profile-tab')).tap();
    await element(by.id('edit-profile-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('display-name-input'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('updates display name and email then saves successfully', async () => {
    await element(by.id('display-name-input')).clearText();
    await element(by.id('display-name-input')).typeText('Jane Doe');
    await element(by.id('email-input')).clearText();
    await element(by.id('email-input')).typeText('jane.doe@example.com');
    await element(by.id('save-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('profile-saved-toast'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('display-name-label'))).toHaveText('Jane Doe');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `clearText()` selects all text and fires a delete event, which triggers `onChangeText` with an empty string and can fire form validation immediately — if your form shows an inline error for empty-required-fields on every `onChangeText` event (not only on blur), the error banner appears between `clearText()` and `typeText()`, and any assertion placed between those two calls will falsely catch the intermediate error state; to avoid this, place assertions only after `typeText()` completes, never between the clear and retype steps.

**Pattern 591** — `by.id().and(by.text())` compound matcher for asserting button label correctness when multiple buttons share a layout position
```typescript
// Compound matcher: element must match BOTH the testID AND the text predicate.
// Needed when a toggle button reuses the same testID for both states but changes its label.
describe('Subscription toggle button', () => {
  it('shows "Unsubscribe" label after user subscribes to a channel', async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('channel-row-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('channel-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Before subscription: button reads "Subscribe"
    await expect(
      element(by.id('subscribe-button').and(by.text('Subscribe')))
    ).toBeVisible();

    await element(by.id('subscribe-button')).tap();

    // After subscription: same testID, different text
    await waitFor(
      element(by.id('subscribe-button').and(by.text('Unsubscribe')))
    ).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Double-guard: ensure the old label is gone
    await expect(
      element(by.id('subscribe-button').and(by.text('Subscribe')))
    ).not.toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Chaining `.and(by.text())` onto a `by.id()` matcher makes the assertion tightly coupled to the exact display string, so any copy-deck change (e.g., "Unsubscribe" → "Remove") breaks the test without a corresponding product defect; prefer using the compound matcher only for state-transition assertions where the label change is the actual product behavior under test, and use `by.id()` alone for navigation/tap interactions where you don't care about the current label text.

**Pattern 592** — `device.pressBack()` for Android hardware back-button simulation in navigation stack and bottom-sheet dismissal tests
```typescript
// Android users expect the hardware back button to dismiss bottom sheets,
// close modals, and pop navigation stacks — test this path explicitly.
describe('Android back-button navigation', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
  });

  it('dismisses the filter bottom sheet when back is pressed', async () => {
    await element(by.id('filter-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('filter-sheet'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Simulate hardware back press
    await device.pressBack();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('filter-sheet'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    // Confirm we are still on the product list, not popped to a previous route
    await expect(element(by.id('product-list-screen'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('pops the nested settings screen back to settings root', async () => {
    await element(by.id('settings-tab')).tap();
    await element(by.id('notifications-row')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('notification-settings-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await device.pressBack();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('settings-root-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.pressBack()` is Android-only — calling it in a cross-platform spec file that also runs on iOS will throw `"pressBack is not supported on iOS"` at runtime; guard every call with `if (device.getPlatform() === 'android')` or isolate Android-specific back-button suites in a `*.android.e2e.ts` file so the iOS runner never encounters the call.

**Pattern 593** — `device.launchApp({ url: deepLinkUrl })` for cold-start deep-link entry-point testing with deferred navigation
```typescript
// Test that the app handles a deep-link that arrives before the React bundle
// is fully loaded — a common source of "link swallowed silently" bugs.
describe('Deep-link cold-start navigation', () => {
  it('navigates to the correct product detail page from a cold-start link', async () => {
    // Terminate the app entirely first to simulate a cold start
    await device.terminateApp();

    // Re-launch with the deep-link URL — Detox passes it via XCUITest / ADB intent
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      url: 'myapp://products/detail/SKU-9842',
    });

    // The app must process the link after the bundle loads
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
    await expect(element(by.id('product-sku-label'))).toHaveText('SKU-9842');

    // Verify back navigation leads to the home screen (not a blank stack)
    await element(by.id('back-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `launchApp({ url })` fires the URL as part of the OS launch sequence, but on Android the intent extras are consumed by the `MainActivity` `onCreate` method — if the app uses a `SplashActivity` that delegates to `MainActivity`, the deep-link URL may be dropped during the delegation handoff if `SplashActivity` does not forward the incoming intent's data URI; always verify that every activity in the launch chain calls `startActivity(intent)` with the original intent rather than constructing a new bare intent.

**Pattern 594** — `element.swipe('down', 'slow', 0.5, 0.5, 0.1)` with explicit start-normalized coordinates for pull-to-refresh gesture testing
```typescript
// Pull-to-refresh requires a downward swipe starting near the top of the list.
// The normalizedStartY must be < 0.3 and the swipe distance must be large enough
// to cross the refresh trigger threshold — typically 64–80 dp.
describe('Feed pull-to-refresh', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('feed-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('shows a loading spinner and then refreshed content', async () => {
    // Verify initial state
    await expect(element(by.id('feed-item-0'))).toBeVisible();

    // Swipe down from near the top of the list to trigger pull-to-refresh
    // direction='down', speed='slow', normalizedSwipeOffset=0.5,
    // normalizedStartX=0.5 (center), normalizedStartY=0.1 (near top)
    await element(by.id('feed-list')).swipe('down', 'slow', 0.5, 0.5, 0.1);

    // Spinner must appear before content reloads
    await waitFor(element(by.id('refresh-spinner'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('refresh-spinner'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);

    // Refreshed list is still visible after reload completes
    await expect(element(by.id('feed-item-0'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `swipe()` with `speed='slow'` travels the pointer at roughly 50 dp/frame, which reliably crosses the pull-to-refresh threshold on both iOS `UIRefreshControl` and Android `SwipeRefreshLayout`; using `speed='fast'` often causes the refresh to abort because the gesture completes before the OS gesture recognizer has accumulated enough velocity in the correct direction, resulting in a test that consistently fails to trigger the refresh on Android while still working on iOS where the threshold is velocity-independent.

**Pattern 595** — `expect(element).toHaveToggleValue(true | false)` for Switch, Checkbox, and RadioButton assertion without reading displayed text
```typescript
// toHaveToggleValue checks the underlying accessibility value of toggle controls,
// which is more reliable than reading "ON"/"OFF" text that varies by locale.
describe('Notification preferences toggles', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('settings-tab')).tap();
    await element(by.id('notifications-row')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('notifications-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('disables push notifications and reflects the change persistently after reload', async () => {
    // Confirm the toggle is initially ON
    await expect(element(by.id('push-notifications-toggle'))).toHaveToggleValue(true);

    // Toggle it OFF
    await element(by.id('push-notifications-toggle')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('push-notifications-toggle'))).toHaveToggleValue(false);

    // Reload and confirm persistence
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('settings-tab')).tap();
    await element(by.id('notifications-row')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('notifications-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('push-notifications-toggle'))).toHaveToggleValue(false);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `toHaveToggleValue()` reads the `accessibilityValue` set by the native `Switch` component, which is always `true`/`false` regardless of locale — but third-party toggle libraries that render a custom view without forwarding `accessibilityValue` will always return `undefined`, making the assertion always fail; audit every custom toggle component to confirm it sets `accessibilityValue={{ text: String(isEnabled) }}` or use `toHaveValue('true')` as an alternative that reads the same underlying property through a looser string comparison.
