**Pattern 596** — `system.element(by.system.label())` for iOS system dialog (permission alert) acceptance using the Detox system API
```typescript
// iOS permission dialogs are rendered by SpringBoard in a separate process —
// they are NOT part of the app's accessibility tree and require the system API.
describe('Camera permission flow', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    // Launch fresh so the permission dialog appears on first use
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true, permissions: { camera: 'unset' } });
  });

  it('grants camera permission through the system dialog and opens the scanner', async () => {
    await element(by.id('scan-qr-button')).tap();

    // The system permission dialog appears in SpringBoard — use system matchers
    await waitFor(system.element(by.system.label('OK'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    await system.element(by.system.label('OK')).tap();

    // After granting, the camera preview screen should appear
    await waitFor(element(by.id('camera-preview'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('qr-scan-overlay'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('denies camera permission and shows the permission-required banner', async () => {
    await element(by.id('scan-qr-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(system.element(by.system.label("Don't Allow"))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    await system.element(by.system.label("Don't Allow")).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('camera-permission-banner'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `system` API with `by.system.label()` is the only supported way to interact with iOS system dialogs in Detox — the older `device.disableSynchronization()` + raw `tapAtPoint` workaround coordinates were fragile across iPhone screen sizes; however, `system.element` resolution depends on the dialog appearing within the `withTimeout` window, which varies by iOS version (iOS 16 shows dialogs ~200 ms after the permission-requesting API call, iOS 17+ can delay up to 1 s), so always use a timeout of at least 4000 ms to avoid intermittent failures on slower CI simulators.

**Pattern 597** — `device.setStatusBar()` for controlling status-bar clock, battery, and network indicators in screenshot-based visual tests
```typescript
// Stabilise status-bar content before taking deterministic screenshots.
// A real-time clock or changing Wi-Fi signal in the status bar makes pixel
// snapshots non-deterministic and causes spurious visual-diff failures.
describe('Onboarding screen visual regression', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    // Freeze status-bar state for reproducible screenshots
    await device.setStatusBar({
      time: '9:41',       // Apple's iconic demo time
      batteryLevel: 1.0,  // Full battery — no charging icon
      batteryState: 'charged',
      dataNetwork: 'wifi',
      wifiMode: 'active',
      wifiBars: 3,
    });
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    await device.resetStatusBar(); // restore live status bar
  });

  it('matches the onboarding welcome screen snapshot', async () => {
    await waitFor(element(by.id('onboarding-welcome-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    const screenshot = await device.takeScreenshot('onboarding-welcome');
    expect(screenshot).toMatchImageSnapshot({ threshold: 0.01 });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.setStatusBar()` is iOS Simulator–only — Android's `adb shell am broadcast` approach for status-bar overrides is not exposed through Detox's cross-platform `device` API, so any test file that calls `device.setStatusBar()` must be guarded with `if (device.getPlatform() === 'ios')` or restricted to an iOS-only test suite; on Android, consider relying on `@jest/image-snapshot` ignore-region masks to exclude the status bar from diff comparisons instead.

**Pattern 598** — `element.getAttributes()` `elements` array for asserting partial visibility of off-screen list items
```typescript
// getAttributes() on a matcher that resolves multiple elements returns { elements: [...] }.
// Use the array to assert that early items are fully visible while the last
// item is only partially clipped — confirming the list is scrollable.
describe('Product grid scrollability hint', () => {
  it('shows first 3 items fully visible and the 4th item partially clipped', async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-grid'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);

    // Get attributes for all product-card elements currently in the accessibility tree
    const attrs = await element(by.id('product-card')).getAttributes();

    // When multiple elements match, Detox returns { elements: [...] }
    const items = (attrs as { elements: Detox.ElementAttributes[] }).elements;

    // First three cards should be fully visible
    expect(items[0].visible).toBe(true);
    expect(items[1].visible).toBe(true);
    expect(items[2].visible).toBe(true);

    // Fourth card should be only partially visible (peek to hint scrollability)
    expect(items[3].visible).toBe(false); // frame extends below the viewport
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `getAttributes()` returns `{ elements: [...] }` only when the matcher resolves more than one element — if a layout change reduces the matched count to one, the return type silently switches to a flat `ElementAttributes` object without the `elements` key, causing `(attrs as { elements: [...] }).elements` to be `undefined` and `.length` to throw; always add a defensive `if ('elements' in attrs)` guard before destructuring to handle single-match regressions after UI changes shrink the list.

**Pattern 599** — `waitFor(element).toBeVisible().whileElement(by.id()).scroll()` for nested `FlatList` inside a horizontal parent `ScrollView`
```typescript
// Nested scroll: the horizontal ScrollView paginates between tabs,
// while each tab contains a vertical FlatList. Use chained waitFor+whileElement
// to scroll within the correct nested container.
describe('Horizontal tab pager with nested vertical lists', () => {
  it('scrolls to the last item in the "Trending" tab vertical list', async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('tab-pager'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);

    // Swipe horizontally to the "Trending" tab (index 2)
    await element(by.id('tab-pager')).swipe('left', 'fast', 1.0);
    await element(by.id('tab-pager')).swipe('left', 'fast', 1.0);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('trending-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Scroll within the vertical FlatList inside the Trending tab
    await waitFor(element(by.id('trending-item-last')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .whileElement(by.id('trending-list'))
      .scroll(250, 'down');

    await expect(element(by.id('trending-item-last'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('end-of-list-label'))).toHaveText("You're all caught up");
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `whileElement().scroll()` resolves the scroll container by accessibility ID and restricts scrolling to that container's bounds, preventing accidentally paging the outer horizontal `ScrollView` instead of the inner vertical `FlatList`; but the scroll step size (250 px per iteration) must not exceed the container's visible height — if the target item is 100 px below the fold and you scroll 250 px, the item briefly appears then exits above the top of the viewport, so `toBeVisible()` remains unsatisfied; use a step size of roughly 80% of the container's visible height for reliable convergence.

**Pattern 600** — `device.launchApp({ userActivity })` for Spotlight and Handoff `NSUserActivity` entry-point testing on iOS
```typescript
// NSUserActivity is the mechanism behind Spotlight search results, Handoff,
// and Universal Links on iOS. Test that the app resumes correctly when the OS
// delivers a userActivity rather than a plain URL.
describe('Spotlight search Handoff entry', () => {
  it('opens the correct recipe detail when resumed from a Spotlight result', async () => {
    await device.terminateApp();

    // Simulate the OS delivering a NSUserActivity to the app at launch
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      userActivity: {
        activityType: 'com.myapp.recipe',
        userInfo: { recipeId: 'RECIPE-1042' },
        webpageURL: 'https://myapp.com/recipes/RECIPE-1042',
      },
    });

    // App must handle the userActivity in application(_:continue:restorationHandler:)
    await waitFor(element(by.id('recipe-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
    await expect(element(by.id('recipe-title'))).not.toHaveText('');
    await expect(element(by.id('recipe-id-label'))).toHaveText('RECIPE-1042');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.launchApp({ userActivity })` passes the activity dictionary through XCUITest's `launchEnvironment`, and the simulator delivers it synchronously at app launch — the timing is therefore more deterministic than a real Handoff resume where the OS may buffer the activity for several seconds; this means tests can pass in Detox while real Handoff resumes fail in production if the app reads `userActivity.userInfo` before `viewDidAppear` (when the view hierarchy is ready), so complement Detox tests with a manual Handoff smoke test on a real device pair before each release.

**Pattern 601** — `element.replaceText()` for atomic field content replacement without triggering intermediate `onChangeText` validation events
```typescript
// replaceText() atomically replaces the field's entire content in one operation,
// bypassing character-by-character onChange events that can trigger premature validation.
describe('Password reset form', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('forgot-password-link')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('reset-password-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('accepts a valid password and shows the strength indicator', async () => {
    // replaceText avoids triggering "password too short" errors on each keystroke
    await element(by.id('new-password-input')).replaceText('Str0ng!Pass#2024');
    await element(by.id('confirm-password-input')).replaceText('Str0ng!Pass#2024');

    // Strength indicator should reflect the full password, not an intermediate state
    await expect(element(by.id('password-strength-label'))).toHaveText('Strong');
    await expect(element(by.id('passwords-match-indicator'))).toBeVisible();

    await element(by.id('reset-submit-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('reset-success-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `replaceText()` sets the field's text value directly through the accessibility API without simulating individual key events, so it bypasses any `onKeyPress` handlers and `TextInputState` listeners used for real-time masking (e.g., credit card number formatting, phone number hyphenation) — the displayed value will be unformatted raw text even if the app's `onChangeText` handler would normally format it; use `typeText()` instead of `replaceText()` when the test specifically needs to verify that real-time formatting or input masking works correctly.

**Pattern 602** — `device.captureViewHierarchy('label')` for post-failure diagnostics in CI with automatic hierarchy file archiving
```typescript
// Call captureViewHierarchy in afterEach to capture a .viewhierarchy file
// whenever a test fails — lets engineers inspect the full element tree
// in Xcode's View Hierarchy debugger without needing to reproduce locally.
describe('Checkout flow', () => {
  afterEach(async () => {
    // Capture on failure using Jest's assertion state
    const state = (expect as unknown as { getState: () => Record<string, unknown> }).getState() as {
      currentTestName: string;
      assertionCalls: number;
      assertionErrors?: number;
    };
    const failed = (state.assertionErrors ?? 0) > 0;
    if (failed) {
      const label = state.currentTestName.replace(/\s+/g, '-').toLowerCase();
      await device.captureViewHierarchy(label);
      // Detox writes to <artifacts-dir>/<test-name>/<label>.viewhierarchy
    }
  });

  it('displays the order summary before placing the order', async () => {
    await element(by.id('add-to-cart-button')).tap();
    await element(by.id('cart-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('checkout-button'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await element(by.id('checkout-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('order-summary-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('item-count-label'))).not.toHaveText('0');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.captureViewHierarchy()` is iOS-only and generates a `.viewhierarchy` binary that requires Xcode 12+ to open — on Android CI you must rely on `device.takeScreenshot()` for equivalent post-failure diagnostics; the viewhierarchy file can be large (5–20 MB for complex screens), so capturing it in `afterEach` for every test (not just failures) will significantly inflate CI artifact storage and slow down test teardown.

**Pattern 603** — `by.type('UIPickerView')` for native date picker and system-owned component targeting when `testID` cannot be applied
```typescript
// On iOS, the native UIDatePicker and share sheet are UIKit components
// that React Native wraps without exposing a testID hook.
// Use by.type() to target the underlying native class directly.
describe('Appointment booking date picker', () => {
  it('selects a date from the native UIDatePicker and confirms the selection', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('book-appointment-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('date-picker-container'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // The native date picker spinner uses UIPickerView internally
    // Use setColumnToValue for wheel-picker style date selection
    await element(by.type('UIPickerView')).setColumnToValue(0, 'June');   // month column
    await element(by.type('UIPickerView')).setColumnToValue(1, '15');     // day column
    await element(by.type('UIPickerView')).setColumnToValue(2, '2026');   // year column

    await element(by.id('confirm-date-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('selected-date-label'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await expect(element(by.id('selected-date-label'))).toHaveText('June 15, 2026');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Matching by `by.type('UIPickerView')` couples the test to UIKit's internal class hierarchy — Apple can rename or restructure the underlying view class in a future iOS version, instantly breaking all `by.type('UIPickerView')` matchers; encapsulate all native-type matchers in a `datePickerHelper.ts` utility so a single-file update repairs every test that uses the picker, and add an iOS-version guard that logs a warning when running on iOS 18+ until the class name has been re-verified.

### Community Gotchas

**G340** — `element.replaceText()` does not fire `onSubmitEditing` or `onEndEditing` — forms that validate only on blur silently skip validation
Why this matters: `replaceText()` uses the accessibility API to set the field value atomically. It does not simulate the user pressing Return, moving focus away, or tapping outside the field. Forms that attach validation logic to `onSubmitEditing`, `onEndEditing`, or a blur handler (common in Formik and React Hook Form when `validateOn='blur'`) will not run validation after `replaceText()`. The test sees no error messages (because validation never ran), taps the submit button, and the app shows an error in production that the test never caught — giving a false green.
Fix: After `replaceText()`, explicitly simulate a blur by tapping a neutral element outside the field (e.g., `await element(by.id('form-scroll-view')).tap()`) or by calling `element.tapReturnKey()`. This triggers `onEndEditing` and `onSubmitEditing`, causing validation to fire before the test proceeds to the submit assertion.

---

**G341** — `device.launchApp({ permissions: { notifications: 'YES' } })` pre-grants permission but does not prevent the system banner from appearing on the first `requestAuthorization()` call on iOS 17+
Why this matters: On iOS 16 and earlier, the `permissions` key in `launchApp()` writes a TCC override before the app starts, suppressing the system dialog entirely. Starting with iOS 17, Apple added an ephemeral permission state where even a pre-granted TCC entry can trigger a reduced "Your app wants to send you notifications" banner the first time `UNUserNotificationCenter.requestAuthorization()` is called. Tests that assert `system.element(by.system.label('Allow'))` does not appear after pre-granting will fail intermittently on iOS 17+ simulators.
Fix: Also pass `newInstance: true` alongside `permissions` so the app is freshly installed with the TCC override already in place. Wrap the `waitFor` assertion in a `try/catch` — if the dialog appears unexpectedly, tap "Allow" and log a warning rather than failing the entire suite, since this is an OS-level behavior change, not an app defect.

---

**G342** — `element.swipe('down', ...)` on a `ScrollView` with `bounces={false}` on iOS does not trigger pull-to-refresh
Why this matters: React Native's `<ScrollView refreshControl={<RefreshControl>}>` only registers the pull-to-refresh gesture when `bounces` is `true` (the default). When `bounces={false}` is set (common in modals to prevent the rubber-band effect), iOS's `UIScrollView` disables the `UIRefreshControl`'s gesture recognizer because it relies on the over-scroll event that only fires when bounce is enabled. Detox's `swipe('down')` gesture physically scrolls the view but the `UIRefreshControl` never activates, so `waitFor(element(by.id('refresh-spinner'))).toBeVisible()` times out even though the gesture succeeded.
Fix: Remove `bounces={false}` from any `ScrollView` that hosts a `RefreshControl` — this is already a React Native documentation recommendation. If the bounce effect must be suppressed for aesthetic reasons, use `bounces={true}` with `alwaysBounceVertical={false}`, which allows the refresh gesture while suppressing bounce on upward over-scroll.

---

**G343** — `waitFor(element).toBeVisible().withTimeout(N)` counts from the moment the `waitFor` line executes, not from the moment the preceding action completes — low timeouts cause flaky failures on slow emulators
Why this matters: When Detox executes `await element(by.id('submit-button')).tap()` followed by `await waitFor(element(by.id('success-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000)`, the `withTimeout(5000)` clock starts from the moment the JS event loop reaches the `waitFor` line. The preceding `tap()` consumes its own separate internal timeout — those milliseconds are NOT deducted from the `waitFor(5000)`. However, if a network request triggered by the tap takes 3 seconds to resolve, the `waitFor` window starts counting from after the tap resolves at the JS level, giving the full 5 seconds from a quiet baseline. Teams that set very low `withTimeout` values (500–1000 ms) expecting "the tap already waited" get flaky failures on slow Android emulators.
Fix: Set `withTimeout` values based on the expected duration of the server operation or animation triggered by the preceding action: at minimum `(P99 server latency + 2 × animation duration + 1000 ms buffer)`. Never assume a preceding action's own settling time reduces the effective window available to the next `waitFor`.

---

**G344** — `testID` is silently stripped from non-touchable `<View>` components in Android release builds when `accessible` is not explicitly set
Why this matters: React Native's Android renderer only propagates `testID` to the underlying `View.setTag()` method when the component's `accessible` prop is `true` OR the component is a touchable (`TouchableOpacity`, `Pressable`, `TouchableHighlight`). For purely presentational `<View testID="banner-container">` wrappers where `accessible` is not explicitly set, the `testID` is present in debug builds (where `__DEV__` enables broader accessibility tagging) but is stripped in release builds. E2E tests run against a release APK will fail to find `banner-container` while the same tests pass against a debug APK, creating a dangerous false-positive gap.
Fix: Add `accessible={true}` explicitly to every `<View>` that carries a `testID` intended for Detox selectors, regardless of whether the view needs to be tappable. Alternatively, run E2E tests against a dedicated `releaseTest` build variant that enables `testID` propagation via a `ReactFeatureFlags` override, keeping the production release APK clean.

## Cycle 65 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 604** — `element.pinch(scale, speed, angle)` with platform-conditional scale values for zoom gesture testing
```typescript
// Detox pinch() uses a two-finger spread gesture. The scale parameter
// behaves differently per platform: iOS interprets scale as a multiplier
// relative to the element's current zoom level, while Android interprets
// it as an absolute scale factor applied to the touch spread distance.
// Use platform guards and encapsulate in a helper to keep tests portable.
async function pinchElement(
  matcher: Detox.NativeMatcher,
  direction: 'in' | 'out',
  platform = device.getPlatform()
): Promise<void> {
  const iosScale = direction === 'out' ? 2.5 : 0.5;
  const androidScale = direction === 'out' ? 2.0 : 0.4;
  const scale = platform === 'ios' ? iosScale : androidScale;
  await element(matcher).pinch(scale, 'slow', 0);
}

describe('Map zoom gestures', () => {
  it('zooms in and out on the map view', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('map-view'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);

    await pinchElement(by.id('map-view'), 'out');   // zoom in (spread)
    await expect(element(by.id('zoom-level-badge'))).toHaveText('Zoom: 14');

    await pinchElement(by.id('map-view'), 'in');    // zoom out (pinch)
    await expect(element(by.id('zoom-level-badge'))).toHaveText('Zoom: 12');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Wrapping `pinch()` in a platform-conditional helper prevents cross-platform scale inversion bugs, but the helper adds an abstraction layer that hides the raw Detox API from test readers — document the actual scale values in JSDoc comments so reviewers can reason about expected gesture magnitude without tracing into the helper.

**Pattern 605** — `element.adjustSliderToPosition(normalizedPosition)` for range input and seek-bar testing
```typescript
// adjustSliderToPosition() accepts a 0.0–1.0 normalized value where 0.0 is
// the leftmost (minimum) position and 1.0 is the rightmost (maximum).
// On iOS it controls UISlider; on Android it controls SeekBar.
// Combine with getAttributes() to read back the slider's .value for assertion.
describe('Audio seek bar', () => {
  it('seeks to 75% of the track duration', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('play-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('seek-bar'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Position 0.75 = 75% through the track
    await element(by.id('seek-bar')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.75);

    // Read back the value attribute that React Native SliderIOS exposes
    const attrs = await element(by.id('seek-bar')).getAttributes();
    if (!('elements' in attrs)) {
      // normalizedValue is 0–1 on iOS; value is raw int on Android
      const rawValue = Number(attrs.value);
      expect(rawValue).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }

    await expect(element(by.id('current-time-label'))).not.toHaveText('0:00');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `adjustSliderToPosition(0.75)` sets the physical thumb position rather than a semantic value — if the slider's minimum and maximum change at runtime (e.g., a variable-length podcast), 0.75 maps to a different absolute value each test run, making deterministic assertions on the label text impossible without first reading the track's total duration from another element.

**Pattern 606** — `device.sendUserNotification(params)` for simulating foreground push notifications on iOS Simulator
```typescript
// device.sendUserNotification() delivers a local notification payload to the
// running iOS Simulator app, exercising UNUserNotificationCenter handlers
// without a real APNs server. The app must be running in the foreground.
// Android does not support this API — use device.launchApp({ userNotification })
// for a cold-start notification test on Android.
const pushPayload = {
  trigger: { type: 'push' },
  title: 'New message from Alex',
  body: 'Hey, are you free this afternoon?',
  badge: 1,
  userInfo: { messageId: 'msg-999', senderId: 'user-alex' },
};

describe('Foreground push notification handling', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      permissions: { notifications: 'YES' },
    });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('inbox-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('shows the in-app banner and increments the unread badge', async () => {
    await device.sendUserNotification(pushPayload);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('in-app-banner'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('in-app-banner-body'))).toHaveText(
      'Hey, are you free this afternoon?'
    );
    await expect(element(by.id('unread-count-badge'))).toHaveText('1');
    await element(by.id('in-app-banner')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('message-thread-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await expect(element(by.id('thread-sender-name'))).toHaveText('Alex');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `sendUserNotification()` tests the in-app notification handler (`UNUserNotificationCenterDelegate.userNotificationCenter(_:willPresent:withCompletionHandler:)`) but cannot test the system notification tap path (when the app is backgrounded and the user taps the OS banner) — for that code path use `device.launchApp({ userNotification: payload })` with `newInstance: false` after moving the app to background with `device.sendToHome()`.

**Pattern 607** — `by.label()` for accessibility label matching when `testID` is absent on third-party components
```typescript
// Third-party UI libraries (e.g., react-native-maps, react-native-camera)
// render native views that do not forward the testID prop. These views
// expose accessibility labels set via accessibilityLabel or the native
// UIAccessibility API. by.label() matches against those labels.
// Combine with by.type() to narrow when labels are shared across components.
describe('Third-party map marker interaction', () => {
  it('taps a map annotation marker by its accessibility label', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('map-container'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

    // The native MKAnnotationView sets accessibilityLabel from the annotation title
    await element(by.label('Coffee Shop — 4.7 stars')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('place-detail-sheet'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await expect(element(by.id('place-name-heading'))).toHaveText('Coffee Shop');
    await expect(element(by.id('place-rating'))).toHaveText('4.7');

    // Dismiss the sheet
    await element(by.id('place-detail-sheet')).swipe('down', 'fast');
    await waitFor(element(by.id('place-detail-sheet')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(1500);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `by.label()` matches the full accessibility label string — any copy change in the annotation title (including the star count if it updates dynamically from an API) breaks the matcher immediately, since there is no wildcard or regex variant; mitigate by seeding the map with fixture data served from a mock server so that annotation labels are deterministic across every test run.

**Pattern 608** — `element.longPress(duration)` for context menu and drag-handle activation
```typescript
// longPress(duration) holds a finger on an element for `duration` milliseconds
// before lifting. The default duration is 1000 ms. iOS UIKit and Android
// LongClickListener respond to hold gestures differently — iOS typically
// activates context menus at 500–800 ms while Android uses 400–600 ms.
// Use the duration override to stay within the platform's activation window
// without waiting the full 1000 ms default.
describe('Message long-press context menu', () => {
  const MESSAGE_PRESS_DURATION_IOS = 700;
  const MESSAGE_PRESS_DURATION_ANDROID = 500;

  it('opens the context menu on long press and selects "Copy"', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('message-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);

    const duration =
      device.getPlatform() === 'ios'
        ? MESSAGE_PRESS_DURATION_IOS
        : MESSAGE_PRESS_DURATION_ANDROID;

    await element(by.id('message-bubble-0')).longPress(duration);

    // iOS shows UIMenuController; Android shows a custom BottomSheet menu
    await waitFor(element(by.id('context-menu-copy-button')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(1500);
    await element(by.id('context-menu-copy-button')).tap();

    // Verify that the clipboard received the message text
    await expect(element(by.id('toast-message'))).toHaveText('Copied to clipboard');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: A hardcoded `duration` value in milliseconds is tightly coupled to each platform's activation threshold — if a React Native upgrade changes the gesture responder timing or a device manufacturer shortens the long-press window in their OS skin, the test will either fail to open the menu (duration too short) or trigger unwanted drag behavior (duration too long); expose the duration constants as environment variables or `detox.config` custom params so CI can tune them per device farm.

**Pattern 609** — `device.setURLBlacklist(patterns)` for blocking specific network requests during tests
```typescript
// setURLBlacklist() tells Detox's synchronization layer to ignore pending
// network requests matching the provided URL patterns when deciding whether
// the app is idle. Use it for long-polling endpoints, SSE streams, or
// analytics beacons that keep the app perpetually "busy", causing
// waitFor() assertions to time out waiting for a synchronization idle state.
const ANALYTICS_URLS = [
  '.*\\.segment\\.io/.*',
  '.*\\.amplitude\\.com/.*',
  '.*\\.firebase\\.com/.*',
  '.*\\/api\\/heartbeat',
];

describe('Dashboard load time assertion', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    // Blacklist long-poll and analytics endpoints so synchronization
    // doesn't wait for them before declaring the UI idle.
    await device.setURLBlacklist(ANALYTICS_URLS);
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  });

  afterAll(async () => {
    // Reset the blacklist so other suites are not affected
    await device.setURLBlacklist([]);
  });

  it('renders the dashboard within 3 seconds of login', async () => {
    await element(by.id('email-input')).replaceText('test@example.com');
    await element(by.id('password-input')).replaceText('test-password');
    await element(by.id('login-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('dashboard-header'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `setURLBlacklist()` prevents Detox from waiting for blacklisted requests to settle, which speeds up tests but also means the test cannot assert anything that depends on those blocked responses — analytics events, feature flag evaluations served from a blocked domain, and heartbeat-driven session renewal will all be silently dropped, masking integration bugs in those flows that only appear in production.

---

**Pattern 610** — `device.disableSynchronization()` / `device.enableSynchronization()` for controlled async boundary testing
```typescript
// Synchronization auto-waits for JS timers, animations, and network requests.
// Disabling it gives precise control over timing-sensitive test steps —
// useful when you need to assert intermediate states during an animation,
// verify a loading spinner is shown before data arrives, or test
// race condition edge cases.
describe('Upload progress indicator', () => {
  it('shows the progress bar during upload and hides it on completion', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('upload-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Disable synchronization BEFORE triggering the upload so Detox
    // does not wait for the upload to finish before returning control.
    await device.disableSynchronization();
    try {
      await element(by.id('upload-button')).tap();

      // Assert the progress bar is visible while upload is in progress
      await waitFor(element(by.id('upload-progress-bar')))
        .toBeVisible()
        .withTimeout(500);
      await expect(element(by.id('upload-cancel-button'))).toBeVisible();
    } finally {
      // ALWAYS re-enable in a finally block — failure to do so leaves
      // all subsequent tests in the file running without synchronization.
      await device.enableSynchronization();
    }

    // Re-enabled synchronization: now wait for upload to finish naturally
    await waitFor(element(by.id('upload-success-toast')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(10000);
    await expect(element(by.id('upload-progress-bar'))).not.toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Wrapping `disableSynchronization()` in a `try/finally` block is essential — if the assertion inside throws before `enableSynchronization()` is called, every downstream test in the worker process will run without synchronization, producing cascading false positives that are extremely difficult to debug because no individual test shows a clear error.

---

**Pattern 611** — `by.traits(['button'])` for iOS accessibility trait-based filtering of unlabeled interactive elements
```typescript
// by.traits() matches elements by their UIAccessibilityTraits bitmask.
// Available traits: 'button', 'link', 'header', 'search', 'image',
// 'selected', 'plays', 'key', 'text', 'summary', 'disabled',
// 'frequentUpdates', 'startsMedia', 'adjustable', 'allowsDirectInteraction',
// 'pageTurn'. Use when a third-party component does not expose testID
// but does set its accessibility traits correctly.
// NOTE: by.traits() is iOS-only — add a platform guard for cross-platform suites.
describe('Toolbar action buttons (iOS accessibility traits)', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    jestExpect(device.getPlatform()).toBe('ios');
  });

  it('finds all toolbar buttons by trait and taps the first enabled one', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('editor-toolbar'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Match any button inside the toolbar that is NOT disabled
    const buttonMatcher = by.traits(['button']).and(by.ancestor(by.id('editor-toolbar')));

    // getAttributes() with multiple matches returns { elements: ElementAttributes[] }
    const attrs = await element(buttonMatcher).getAttributes();
    if ('elements' in attrs) {
      // Filter to first non-disabled button by checking its .enabled property
      const firstEnabled = attrs.elements.find((el) => el.enabled !== false);
      jestExpect(firstEnabled).toBeDefined();
    }

    // Tap the bold button by combining traits with label for precision
    await element(by.traits(['button']).and(by.label('Bold'))).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('bold-indicator-active'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `by.traits()` is iOS-only and silently fails to match anything on Android, so mixing trait-based matchers with testID-based matchers inside the same test block requires careful platform-conditional branching — using a shared test utility that returns the correct matcher per platform (`getToolbarButtonMatcher(platform, label)`) keeps the test body readable but adds one more abstraction to the project's helper layer.

**Pattern 612** — `element.scroll(offset, direction, startNormalizedX, startNormalizedY)` for precisely anchored scroll gestures in nested layouts
```typescript
// element.scroll() scrolls by a fixed pixel offset in a given direction.
// The startNormalizedX/Y parameters (0.0–1.0) control where the gesture
// finger begins relative to the element — critical when a ScrollView is
// nested inside a drag-dismissable BottomSheet, where starting the gesture
// near the top of the sheet triggers the dismiss instead of the scroll.
describe('Product details bottom sheet scrolling', () => {
  it('scrolls the product description to the bottom without dismissing the sheet', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('product-card-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-sheet'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Start the scroll gesture from the lower 40% of the scroll view (Y=0.7)
    // to avoid the drag-dismiss zone at the top of the BottomSheet handle area.
    // Scroll 600 pixels downward in three increments to reach the review section.
    const SCROLL_OFFSET = 600;
    const SAFE_START_Y = 0.7;

    for (let pass = 0; pass < 3; pass++) {
      await element(by.id('product-description-scroll')).scroll(
        SCROLL_OFFSET,
        'down',
        NaN, // startNormalizedX: NaN means horizontally centered
        SAFE_START_Y
      );
    }

    await waitFor(element(by.id('customer-reviews-section')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);
    await expect(element(by.id('review-count-label'))).not.toHaveText('');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using a fixed pixel `offset` per scroll call makes the test dependent on the device's screen density — a 600-pixel scroll on an iPhone SE (375pt wide) covers proportionally more content than on an iPad Pro (1024pt wide); replace the fixed offset with a viewport-fraction calculation (`(await device.getWindowSize()).height * 0.5`) to keep the number of scroll passes consistent across screen sizes.

**Pattern 613** — `device.shake()` for triggering undo gesture and error-reporting dialogs on iOS Simulator
```typescript
// device.shake() simulates the iOS shake-to-undo and shake-to-report gestures.
// On physical devices these map to accelerometer data; on Simulator, Detox
// sends the equivalent UIEvent. Guard against the system Undo alert appearing
// by first tapping a neutral element, which clears any active undo stack.
describe('Shake-to-report feedback flow', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    if (device.getPlatform() !== 'ios') {
      pending('device.shake() is iOS Simulator only');
      return;
    }
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    // Dismiss any undo state by tapping a safe area before shaking
    await element(by.id('home-screen')).tap();
  });

  it('opens the feedback dialog on shake', async () => {
    await device.shake();

    // The app-level shake handler shows a custom ReportBugModal
    await waitFor(element(by.id('report-bug-modal')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);
    await element(by.id('feedback-text-input')).typeText('Test shake feedback');
    await element(by.id('submit-feedback-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('report-bug-modal')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(1500);
    await expect(element(by.id('feedback-confirmation-toast'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.shake()` on iOS Simulator can race with the OS-level "Undo Typing" alert if any text field was focused immediately before the shake — the system Undo alert is a `UIAlertController` that intercepts touch events and blocks all Detox element interactions until it is explicitly dismissed via `system.element(by.system.label('Undo'))`, so always clear text-field focus before shaking.

**Pattern 614** — `waitFor(element).toBeVisible().whileElement(by.id(...)).scroll()` for revealing off-screen list items
```typescript
// The whileElement().scroll() idiom scrolls a parent container while polling
// for visibility of a target element — Detox automatically stops scrolling
// and resolves the waitFor once the element becomes visible.
// This replaces fragile "scroll N times then assert" patterns.
describe('Contacts list — scroll to specific contact', () => {
  it('finds and taps "Zhao Wei" deep in a 500-item contacts list', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('contacts-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);

    // Poll every 200px scroll increment; limit total scroll to avoid infinite loop
    await waitFor(element(by.id('contact-zhao-wei')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .whileElement(by.id('contacts-flat-list'))
      .scroll(200, 'down', NaN, 0.5);

    await element(by.id('contact-zhao-wei')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('contact-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await expect(element(by.id('contact-name-heading'))).toHaveText('Zhao Wei');
  });

  it('scrolls up to find a contact near the top after navigating down', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('contacts-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    // First scroll far down, then search upward
    await element(by.id('contacts-flat-list')).scroll(3000, 'down', NaN, 0.5);

    await waitFor(element(by.id('contact-adam-ali')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .whileElement(by.id('contacts-flat-list'))
      .scroll(200, 'up', NaN, 0.5);
    await element(by.id('contact-adam-ali')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('contact-name-heading'))).toHaveText('Adam Ali');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `whileElement().scroll()` has no built-in scroll limit — if the target element never becomes visible (e.g., due to a filter applied to the list that hides the item), Detox will scroll indefinitely until the global test timeout fires, making the failure mode a timeout error rather than a clear "element not found" message; always pair it with a `withTimeout()` on the outer `waitFor` to get a bounded failure window.

---

**Pattern 615** — `element.longPressAndDrag()` for reordering list items with drag handles on iOS
```typescript
// longPressAndDrag(duration, normalizedPositionX, normalizedPositionY,
//   targetElement, normalizedTargetPositionX, normalizedTargetPositionY,
//   speed, holdDuration) performs a press-hold-drag-drop sequence.
// Only available on iOS; Android drag-and-drop requires a custom gesture chain.
async function dragListItemToPosition(
  sourceId: string,
  targetId: string,
  speed: Detox.Speed = 'slow'
): Promise<void> {
  await element(by.id(sourceId)).longPressAndDrag(
    500,   // hold 500ms before drag starts
    0.9,   // drag from right side where the handle icon lives (X=90%)
    NaN,   // vertically centered (Y = middle of element)
    element(by.id(targetId)),
    0.9,   // drop on the right side of the target
    NaN,
    speed,
    500    // hold at destination 500ms before releasing
  );
}

describe('Task list reordering', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    if (device.getPlatform() !== 'ios') {
      pending('longPressAndDrag is iOS-only');
      return;
    }
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('task-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('moves "Buy groceries" above "Call dentist"', async () => {
    await dragListItemToPosition('task-item-buy-groceries', 'task-item-call-dentist');
    // After reorder, "Buy groceries" should appear above "Call dentist"
    // Verify via order-dependent testIDs or positional attribute comparison
    const listAttrs = await element(by.id('task-list')).getAttributes();
    if ('elements' in listAttrs) {
      const ids = listAttrs.elements.map((el) => el.identifier);
      expect(ids.indexOf('task-item-buy-groceries')).toBeLessThan(
        ids.indexOf('task-item-call-dentist')
      );
    }
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `longPressAndDrag()` requires the drag handle to be a distinct tappable region (hence X=0.9 for a right-side handle icon) — if the drag trigger zone changes as part of a UI refresh (e.g., the handle moves from right to left, or is hidden behind an edit-mode toggle), the normalized X coordinate becomes silently wrong and the drag gesture fires but moves the wrong element, giving a false positive when the list order happens to be unchanged.

**Pattern 616** — `device.openURL({ url, sourceApp })` for universal link and custom URL scheme navigation testing
```typescript
// device.openURL() opens a URL in the running app as if tapped from another
// app or the Safari address bar. Use it to test universal link routing,
// OAuth redirect URIs, and custom scheme deep links without needing a real
// source app to trigger the link.
const DEEP_LINKS = {
  productDetail: 'myapp://products/42',
  orderConfirmation: 'myapp://orders/confirm?orderId=ORD-9981',
  universalBlogPost: 'https://www.myapp.com/blog/detox-testing-guide',
};

describe('Deep link routing', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('routes the product detail deep link to the ProductDetailScreen', async () => {
    await device.openURL({ url: DEEP_LINKS.productDetail });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('product-id-label'))).toHaveText('42');
  });

  it('routes the universal link blog post to the in-app WebView', async () => {
    await device.openURL({ url: DEEP_LINKS.universalBlogPost });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('in-app-webview'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('webview-title-bar'))).toHaveText('Detox Testing Guide');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.openURL()` only works when the app is already in the foreground or background — calling it immediately after `launchApp()` before the app is fully initialized can cause the URL to be received before the navigation stack is ready, resulting in a silently swallowed deep link; always `waitFor` the home screen to be visible before calling `openURL()`, and add a `waitFor` on the target screen with a generous timeout to absorb the navigation latency.

**Pattern 617** — `element(by.focused()).typeText()` for keyboard-driven multi-field form navigation
```typescript
// element(by.focused()) matches whichever element currently holds keyboard focus
// on iOS (based on UIResponder.isFirstResponder). Use it to type into whatever
// field is focused without re-identifying the element by testID — this matches
// how a real user fills a form using the "Next" keyboard button to advance fields.
async function fillFormByKeyboard(fields: string[]): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < fields.length; i++) {
    await element(by.focused()).typeText(fields[i]);
    if (i < fields.length - 1) {
      // Advance to the next field using the Return/Next key
      await element(by.focused()).tapReturnKey();
      // Allow the focus transfer animation to settle
      await waitFor(element(by.focused())).toExist().withTimeout(500);
    }
  }
}

describe('Registration form keyboard navigation', () => {
  it('fills all fields using keyboard "Next" progression and submits', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('first-name-input')).tap(); // focus the first field

    await fillFormByKeyboard([
      'Jane',
      'Doe',
      'jane.doe@example.com',
      'SecurePass123!',
      'SecurePass123!', // confirm password
    ]);

    // After the last field the keyboard shows "Done" — tap Submit button
    await element(by.id('submit-registration-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('registration-success-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `element(by.focused())` works reliably on iOS but is not consistently supported on Android in Detox — on Android the focused matcher may match the entire screen or a parent container rather than the active text field; use `by.id()` explicit matchers for each field in Android tests and only use `by.focused()` in iOS-gated describe blocks or behind a `device.getPlatform() === 'ios'` guard.

**Pattern 618** — `by.id().withDescendant()` combined with `by.ancestor()` for complex list cell assertions
```typescript
// toHaveText() requires an exact full-string match. For cells whose text
// includes dynamic substrings (timestamps, IDs), use withDescendant()
// to match the cell by a stable child element, then assert the child
// directly rather than the full cell text.
describe('Notification center — complex cell assertion', () => {
  it('verifies the notification title and sender without asserting the timestamp', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('notification-list'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);

    // Find the cell that contains a child with testID='notif-sender-alex'
    // This avoids matching the entire cell text including the dynamic timestamp.
    const cellMatcher = by.id('notification-cell').withDescendant(
      by.id('notif-sender-alex')
    );

    // Assert that the specific cell exists and is visible
    await expect(element(cellMatcher)).toBeVisible();

    // Assert individual child elements within the matched cell
    await expect(
      element(by.id('notif-title').and(by.ancestor(cellMatcher)))
    ).toHaveText('New message from Alex');

    await expect(
      element(by.id('notif-preview').and(by.ancestor(cellMatcher)))
    ).toHaveText('Hey, are you free this afternoon?');

    // Tap the cell to open the message thread
    await element(cellMatcher).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('message-thread-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Chaining `withDescendant()` with `by.ancestor()` creates deeply nested matcher expressions that are difficult to read and debug when they fail — Detox's error message for a compound matcher failure does not indicate which sub-expression failed; extract the matcher chain into a named constant (e.g., `const alexNotifCell = by.id('notification-cell').withDescendant(by.id('notif-sender-alex'))`) and log it in `beforeEach` so CI logs clearly show which cell was being targeted.

### Community Gotchas

**G345** — `element.longPressAndDrag()` silently succeeds on Android without performing any drag — it is an iOS-only API
Why this matters: `longPressAndDrag()` is documented as iOS-only but does not throw an error when called on Android — it completes immediately and returns without performing any gesture. Tests that call it without a platform guard appear to pass (the assertion after the drag may pass coincidentally if the list is already in the expected order or the assertion is insufficiently specific), masking the fact that the drag-and-drop feature was never exercised on Android at all. This creates a silent gap in Android coverage.
Fix: Add `if (device.getPlatform() !== 'ios') { pending('longPressAndDrag is iOS-only'); return; }` at the top of any test that uses `longPressAndDrag()`. For Android drag-and-drop, implement a multi-step gesture: `longPress()` on the drag handle, then chain `element.swipe()` or use `device.pressBack()` patterns specific to the Android RecyclerView's `ItemTouchHelper` drag mode.

---

**G346** — `device.setURLBlacklist()` affects synchronization globally for the entire worker process — calling it inside `beforeEach` without a matching reset causes blacklist accumulation across suites
Why this matters: Each call to `device.setURLBlacklist(patterns)` replaces the current blacklist entirely — it does not append to it. However, if a test suite sets the blacklist in `beforeEach` but does not call `device.setURLBlacklist([])` in `afterEach` or `afterAll`, the blacklist persists for all subsequent suites executed on the same Detox worker process. When Detox runs multiple spec files on the same worker (common in parallel configurations with fewer workers than spec files), suites that never call `setURLBlacklist()` will inherit the blacklist set by an earlier suite, silently skipping synchronization on URLs they expect to block.
Fix: Always pair every `setURLBlacklist(patterns)` call with a corresponding `device.setURLBlacklist([])` in `afterAll` (not `afterEach`, to avoid redundant resets). Centralise blacklist management in a shared `setupNetworkBlacklist()` / `teardownNetworkBlacklist()` helper imported from a test utility file, so the pattern is not forgotten when new suites are added.

---

**G347** — `element(by.focused())` returns the screen root on Android API 34+ when no soft keyboard is visible — causes `typeText()` to fail with "element not found" or inject text into the wrong element
Why this matters: On Android, the `focused()` semantics depend on the IME (input method editor) being actively shown. When the soft keyboard is dismissed (e.g., after `tapReturnKey()` closes the keyboard before focus moves to the next field), the accessibility focus model on API 34+ reverts to the window root, and `element(by.focused())` matches the root `ViewGroup` rather than the next text field. A subsequent `typeText()` call on the root element either throws "Element is not an input field" or inserts text into an unexpected element without error.
Fix: After calling `tapReturnKey()`, tap the next field explicitly by `testID` before using `element(by.focused()).typeText()`. On Android, treat `by.focused()` as unreliable for form navigation and always use explicit `by.id()` matchers per field. Alternatively, check `(await element(by.focused()).getAttributes()).identifier` at runtime to assert focus landed on the expected field before typing.

---

**G348** — `device.sendUserNotification()` throws `"Cannot deliver notification: app is not in foreground"` when called while a modal or bottom sheet is presented
Why this matters: Detox's `sendUserNotification()` requires the app's `UIApplicationDelegate` to be in the `UIApplicationStateActive` state. When a modal (`presentViewController`) or a full-screen bottom sheet is presented, iOS briefly transitions the presenting view controller to `inactive` state during the presentation animation. If `sendUserNotification()` is called while that transition animation is in-flight (even after `waitFor(modal).toBeVisible()` resolves, which only checks rendering, not UIApplicationState), the notification delivery fails with an undocumented internal error.
Fix: After presenting a modal, add a `waitFor(element(by.id('modal-close-button'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(1000)` assertion that implicitly waits for the modal's appear animation to complete (not just initial visibility) before calling `sendUserNotification()`. Alternatively, send the notification before presenting the modal and test the foreground-intercept behavior from the base view controller state.

---

**G349** — `by.label()` matches are case-sensitive and locale-sensitive — `accessibilityLabel` values from `I18n.t()` change with device locale, breaking tests run on non-English CI runners
Why this matters: `by.label('Add to Cart')` matches the `accessibilityLabel` prop exactly, including capitalisation and punctuation. When `accessibilityLabel` is populated from a localisation call (`accessibilityLabel={I18n.t('addToCart')}`), the matched string changes per device locale. CI runners configured with a non-English locale (common on Android emulators where the default locale follows the system image language, not an explicit test config) will silently fail to find `'Add to Cart'` and instead match nothing, causing `waitFor` to time out rather than surfacing a clear "wrong locale" error.
Fix: Always set the device locale explicitly in `detox.config.js` via the `device.bootArgs` parameter for simulators (`-AppleLanguages '(en)'` for iOS, `--locale en_US` for Android ADB) or in the `beforeAll` hook via `device.launchApp({ languageAndLocale: { language: 'en', locale: 'en_US' } })`. This ensures `accessibilityLabel` values are always in English regardless of the host machine's system locale.

## Cycle 66 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

---

**Pattern 619** — `device.appLaunchArgs.modify()` for per-test feature-flag injection without cold-restart overhead
```typescript
// Use device.appLaunchArgs.modify() to patch only specific arguments
// instead of re-calling launchApp() which forces a full cold restart.
// This is especially useful for toggling feature flags mid-suite.
describe('Feature flag: new checkout flow', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  });

  it('shows legacy checkout when flag is off', async () => {
    device.appLaunchArgs.modify({ FEATURE_NEW_CHECKOUT: '0' });
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('checkout-button')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('legacy-checkout-screen'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('shows new checkout when flag is on', async () => {
    device.appLaunchArgs.modify({ FEATURE_NEW_CHECKOUT: '1' });
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('checkout-button')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('new-checkout-screen'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.appLaunchArgs.modify()` followed by `device.reloadReactNative()` is significantly faster than `launchApp({ newInstance: true })`, but `reloadReactNative()` does NOT reset in-memory Redux/Context state or clear AsyncStorage — tests that depend on a clean store between flag variants must still call `launchApp({ newInstance: true })` or explicitly reset state via a test helper, otherwise the residual store from the previous variant can cause false passes on conditional rendering driven by cached state rather than the flag value.

---

**Pattern 620** — `element.typeText()` with Unicode emoji and non-ASCII characters for internationalisation input validation
```typescript
// element.typeText() delegates to the accessibility keyboard simulator.
// On iOS this fully supports Unicode including emoji; on Android it uses
// InputMethodManager and requires the software keyboard to accept the codepoint.
describe('Profile bio unicode input', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('profile-edit-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('bio-text-input'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('accepts and displays emoji characters in the bio field', async () => {
    await element(by.id('bio-text-input')).clearText();
    await element(by.id('bio-text-input')).typeText('Hello World');
    await expect(element(by.id('bio-text-input'))).toHaveText('Hello World');
  });

  it('accepts right-to-left Arabic text without character reversal', async () => {
    await element(by.id('bio-text-input')).clearText();
    await element(by.id('bio-text-input')).typeText('Marhaba');
    await expect(element(by.id('bio-text-input'))).toHaveText('Marhaba');
  });

  it('saves non-ASCII content and round-trips through the API correctly', async () => {
    await element(by.id('save-profile-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('profile-bio-display'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('profile-bio-display'))).toHaveText('Marhaba');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: On Android, `typeText()` with characters outside the ASCII range can fail silently on API 24–26 emulators when predictive text is enabled, because `InputMethodManager.commitText()` may drop or transpose the injected characters without throwing an error — the text field then shows an empty or garbled string, producing a false pass if the assertion checks for an empty string rather than the intended content; always pair `typeText()` with `toHaveText()` that asserts the non-trivial expected value, never rely on a `not.toHaveText('')` guard alone.

---

**Pattern 621** — `device.setLocation(lat, lng)` for location-gated feature and map centring tests
```typescript
// device.setLocation() simulates CoreLocation / LocationManager updates.
// On iOS simulator it uses the simctl location command internally.
// On Android it uses the mock location provider via ADB.
describe('Store locator — location-gated content', () => {
  const LONDON_LAT = 51.5074;
  const LONDON_LNG = -0.1278;
  const NEW_YORK_LAT = 40.7128;
  const NEW_YORK_LNG = -74.006;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      permissions: { location: 'always' },
    });
    await element(by.id('store-locator-tab')).tap();
  });

  it('centres the map on London when location is set to London', async () => {
    await device.setLocation(LONDON_LAT, LONDON_LNG);
    await element(by.id('use-my-location-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('nearest-store-label')))
      .toHaveText('Oxford Street Store')
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('switches nearest store when location changes to New York', async () => {
    await device.setLocation(NEW_YORK_LAT, NEW_YORK_LNG);
    await element(by.id('use-my-location-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('nearest-store-label')))
      .toHaveText('5th Avenue Store')
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.setLocation()` only changes the GPS coordinate reported by the OS location API — it does not simulate the `accuracy`, `altitude`, `heading`, or `speed` fields; apps that gate navigation mode behind `CLLocation.horizontalAccuracy < 20` will silently ignore `setLocation()` because simulated coordinates default to `accuracy = 0` on some iOS simulators, causing navigation assertions to time out even though the coordinate value is correct.

---

**Pattern 622** — `expect(element).toHaveValue()` for asserting `TextInput` and `Slider` value without relying on visible label text
```typescript
// toHaveValue() reads the accessibility value (not the visible text) of a control.
// For TextInput: matches the current content string.
// For Slider: matches the accessibility value string announced to VoiceOver/TalkBack.
describe('Search filter — price range inputs', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('search-tab')).tap();
    await element(by.id('filter-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('filter-sheet'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('reflects correct value after programmatic field population', async () => {
    await element(by.id('min-price-input')).replaceText('10');
    await element(by.id('max-price-input')).replaceText('500');
    await expect(element(by.id('min-price-input'))).toHaveValue('10');
    await expect(element(by.id('max-price-input'))).toHaveValue('500');
  });

  it('slider accessibility value matches the formatted price label', async () => {
    await element(by.id('price-range-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.5);
    // accessibilityValue.now is exposed as the value for Slider controls
    await expect(element(by.id('price-range-slider'))).toHaveValue('$250');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `toHaveValue()` reads `accessibilityValue` on iOS and `ContentDescription` on Android — custom `Slider` wrappers that do not explicitly set `accessibilityValue` (common in third-party libraries such as `@miblanchard/react-native-slider`) expose an empty string, causing `toHaveValue('$250')` to fail with `expected: $250 / received: (empty)` even when the visual position is correct; verify the accessibility tree with `element.getAttributes()` during initial test authoring before committing `toHaveValue()` assertions on custom slider components.

---

**Pattern 623** — `by.id().withAncestor(by.id())` scoped matcher for duplicate `testID` values inside list cells
```typescript
// When a FlatList renders many cells each containing a 'delete-button' testID,
// element(by.id('delete-button')) matches ALL of them. Use withAncestor()
// to scope the query to the specific parent cell's testID.
describe('Shopping cart — per-item delete', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('cart-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('cart-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('deletes only the second cart item without affecting the first', async () => {
    // Verify both items exist before deletion
    await expect(element(by.id('cart-item-name').withAncestor(by.id('cart-row-0')))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('cart-item-name').withAncestor(by.id('cart-row-1')))).toBeVisible();

    // Delete only the second item using scoped ancestor matcher
    await element(by.id('delete-button').withAncestor(by.id('cart-row-1'))).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('cart-row-1'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);

    // Verify the first item is unaffected
    await expect(element(by.id('cart-item-name').withAncestor(by.id('cart-row-0')))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `withAncestor()` traverses the accessibility tree upward looking for a matching ancestor — this works reliably in React Native's Paper renderer, but after migrating to the Fabric renderer, intermediate wrapper views inserted by Fabric's view flattening can change the tree depth at which `testID` is attached; audit `withAncestor()` and `withDescendant()` chains using `device.captureViewHierarchy()` after any Fabric migration to verify tree depth matches the matcher expectations.

---

**Pattern 624** — `element.adjustSliderToPosition(normalizedPosition)` with step-snap compensation for discrete range inputs
```typescript
// adjustSliderToPosition() sets an absolute normalised 0.0–1.0 position.
// Sliders with discrete steps (step={10} on a 0–100 range) snap to the
// nearest step — pre-compute the expected snapped position before asserting.
describe('Settings — notification frequency slider', () => {
  // Slider: min=0, max=10, step=1 — normalized 0.0 to 1.0 in 0.1 increments
  const STEP = 0.1;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('settings-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('notifications-settings-section'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('sets frequency to 3 per day by sliding to 0.3 position', async () => {
    await element(by.id('notif-frequency-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.3);
    // Compute expected snapped position: round(0.3 / 0.1) * 0.1 = 0.3
    const expected = Math.round(0.3 / STEP) * STEP;
    const attrs = await element(by.id('notif-frequency-slider')).getAttributes();
    expect(Math.abs((attrs as { normalizedSliderPosition: number }).normalizedSliderPosition - expected)).toBeLessThan(0.05);
    await expect(element(by.id('notif-frequency-label'))).toHaveText('3 per day');
  });

  it('silences notifications at position 0.0', async () => {
    await element(by.id('notif-frequency-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.0);
    await expect(element(by.id('notif-frequency-label'))).toHaveText('Off');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `Math.abs(actual - expected) < 0.05` instead of strict `toBeCloseTo` gives tolerance for floating-point rounding in `normalizedSliderPosition`, but hides precision regressions where the slider lands two steps away from the target; for safety-critical settings sliders (e.g., alarm volume, medication reminder frequency), tighten the tolerance to `< STEP / 2` so off-by-one step errors produce explicit test failures rather than passing within the tolerance band.

**Pattern 625** — `device.shake()` for accelerometer-triggered undo dialogs (iOS-only with explicit platform guard)
```typescript
// device.shake() fires a synthetic accelerometer shake event on iOS simulators.
// Android emulators do not support device.shake() — guard with getPlatform().
describe('Canvas editor shake-to-undo', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('canvas-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('canvas-view'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('shows undo confirmation dialog on iOS after shake gesture', async () => {
    if (device.getPlatform() !== 'ios') {
      return pending('device.shake() is iOS-simulator-only');
    }
    await element(by.id('canvas-view')).swipe('right', 'slow', 0.3);
    await device.shake();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('undo-dialog')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);
    await expect(element(by.id('undo-dialog-title'))).toHaveText('Undo last stroke?');
    await element(by.id('undo-confirm-button')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('empty-canvas-hint'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('dismisses undo dialog without reverting when Cancel is tapped', async () => {
    if (device.getPlatform() !== 'ios') {
      return pending('device.shake() is iOS-simulator-only');
    }
    await element(by.id('canvas-view')).swipe('left', 'slow', 0.3);
    await device.shake();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('undo-dialog'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
    await element(by.id('undo-cancel-button')).tap();
    await expect(element(by.id('empty-canvas-hint'))).not.toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `pending()` skip inside the test body means Jest reports the test as passing rather than skipped on Android — this inflates the green test count without exercising the feature; use `test.skip()` combined with a top-level `if (device.getPlatform() === 'android')` condition, or move platform-specific tests to an iOS-only spec file configured in Jest's `testPathIgnorePatterns` for Android runs, which produces an accurate skipped/failed distinction in CI reports.

**Pattern 626** — `device.takeScreenshot()` with `beforeEach`/`afterEach` hooks for visual regression audit trails
```typescript
// Capture a screenshot before and after each test for a visual diff pipeline.
// Detox stores PNG artifacts to the path configured in detox.config.js artifacts.
describe('Onboarding flow visual regression', () => {
  let testIndex = 0;

  beforeEach(async () => {
    testIndex++;
    await device.takeScreenshot(`onboarding-before-${testIndex}`);
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await device.takeScreenshot(`onboarding-after-${testIndex}`);
  });

  it('renders the welcome screen with correct hero image', async () => {
    await expect(element(by.id('welcome-hero-image'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('get-started-button'))).toHaveText('Get Started');
  });

  it('navigates to permissions screen after CTA tap', async () => {
    await element(by.id('get-started-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('permissions-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('allow-notifications-cta'))).toBeVisible();
  });

  it('completes onboarding and reaches home screen', async () => {
    await element(by.id('allow-notifications-cta')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('home-feed-title'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.takeScreenshot()` writes to Detox's artifact pipeline asynchronously on Android — the PNG may be a zero-byte file if the test runner moves to the next test before the I/O thread flushes the buffer; never assert on screenshot file existence within the test itself, and always validate artifact integrity in a post-suite CI step using `find artifacts/ -name "*.png" -empty` to surface zero-byte files as a separate failure.

**Pattern 627** — `element.scroll(offset, direction, startNormalizedX, startNormalizedY)` with explicit start-point for WebView and swipeable tab avoidance
```typescript
// Default scroll() starts at the element center (0.5, 0.5).
// Supply a custom startNormalizedX to avoid iOS 16+ swipe-back zones (left ~15%)
// and edge-swipe-forward zones (right ~85%) when scrolling full-width WebViews.
describe('Help center in-app WebView', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('help-button')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('help-webview'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
  });

  it('scrolls the help article down without triggering swipe-back navigation', async () => {
    // Start at 60% from left — safely away from the iOS 15% swipe-back zone
    await element(by.id('help-webview')).scroll(300, 'down', 0.6, 0.5);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('help-section-2'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('scrolls back to article top without triggering swipe-forward zone', async () => {
    await element(by.id('help-webview')).scroll(600, 'up', 0.6, 0.7);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('help-article-header'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('scrolls horizontally through an image carousel embedded in the article', async () => {
    // Horizontal scroll within a child carousel — use startNormalizedY = 0.5
    await element(by.id('help-image-carousel')).scroll(250, 'right', 0.3, 0.5);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('carousel-image-2'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Setting `startNormalizedX = 0.6` avoids the iOS swipe-back zone but shifts the scroll origin to the right half of a WebView — if the WebView uses a two-column CSS layout where the right column is a fixed table-of-contents sidebar, the scroll gesture lands on the non-scrollable sidebar and the main article does not scroll; always test `startNormalizedX` values against the actual rendered layout in the target viewport dimensions before settling on a fixed value across all device sizes.

**Pattern 628** — `detox test --testNamePattern` with `--testPathPattern` for targeted single-test CI re-runs on flaky tests
```bash
# Combine --testNamePattern and --testPathPattern for precise targeting.
# --testNamePattern: Jest RegExp against the full "describe > it" name.
# --testPathPattern: restricts Jest to files matching the path pattern.
# Without --testPathPattern, multiple files with the same describe name
# will both be exercised, inflating re-run scope.

# Re-run a single flaky test in a specific file:
npx detox test \
  --configuration ios.sim.release \
  --testPathPattern "e2e/tests/checkout.test.ts" \
  --testNamePattern "completes payment with Apple Pay" \
  --loglevel verbose \
  --record-logs all

# Re-run all tests in a describe block across a targeted file:
npx detox test \
  --configuration android.emu.release \
  --testPathPattern "e2e/tests/cart" \
  --testNamePattern "Shopping cart" \
  --record-videos failing

# CI re-run with JUnit XML for dashboard reporting:
npx detox test \
  --configuration ios.sim.release \
  --testPathPattern "e2e/tests/auth.test.ts" \
  --testNamePattern "biometric login"
```
Tradeoff: `--testNamePattern` is a JavaScript `RegExp` evaluated against the concatenated `describe` + `it` string — a pattern like `"login"` matches every test whose name includes the substring `login`, including unrelated tests named `"Facebook login"` or `"login error handling"`; always use `^` and `$` anchors or a full describe+it path string (e.g., `"^Authentication > login with valid credentials$"`) in CI re-run scripts to guarantee exactly one test is targeted.

**Pattern 629** — `jestExpect` combined with Detox `expect` for numeric and structural assertions on `getAttributes()` output
```typescript
// Detox's expect() handles accessibility-layer assertions.
// Use jestExpect for numeric range, array, and object assertions
// on the output of getAttributes() without name collision.
import { expect as jestExpect } from 'expect';

describe('Media player seek bar performance', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await element(by.id('player-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('now-playing-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('seek-bar normalizedSliderPosition is within 5% of the 75% target', async () => {
    await element(by.id('seek-bar')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.75);
    const attrs = await element(by.id('seek-bar')).getAttributes() as {
      normalizedSliderPosition: number;
    };
    jestExpect(attrs.normalizedSliderPosition).toBeGreaterThan(0.70);
    jestExpect(attrs.normalizedSliderPosition).toBeLessThan(0.80);
  });

  it('tap-to-seek animation completes within 300ms performance budget', async () => {
    const t0 = Date.now();
    await element(by.id('seek-bar')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.5);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('playback-time-label')))
      .toHaveText('1:30')
      .withTimeout(1500);
    jestExpect(Date.now() - t0).toBeLessThan(300);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Mixing `jestExpect` numeric assertions with Detox accessibility assertions in the same test file means failures from the two libraries surface in different log sections — Detox failures include the element hierarchy path and native state, while `jestExpect` failures show only a value diff with no native context; add a `device.captureViewHierarchy()` call in the `afterEach` hook so CI always has a hierarchy snapshot available to correlate with `jestExpect` failures that lack element context.

**Pattern 630** — `device.launchApp({ languageAndLocale })` for locale-specific date format and right-to-left layout testing
```typescript
// Pass languageAndLocale to launchApp() to force a specific locale
// without changing the simulator's system language.
// This is the correct way to test locale-sensitive UI rendering.
describe('Date display — locale-specific formatting', () => {
  it('formats dates as DD/MM/YYYY in en_GB locale', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      languageAndLocale: { language: 'en', locale: 'en_GB' },
    });
    await element(by.id('event-date-label')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('formatted-date'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('formatted-date'))).toHaveText('14/05/2026');
  });

  it('formats dates as MM/DD/YYYY in en_US locale', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      languageAndLocale: { language: 'en', locale: 'en_US' },
    });
    await element(by.id('event-date-label')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('formatted-date'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
    await expect(element(by.id('formatted-date'))).toHaveText('05/14/2026');
  });

  it('renders RTL layout in Arabic locale without text overlap', async () => {
    await device.launchApp({
      newInstance: true,
      languageAndLocale: { language: 'ar', locale: 'ar_SA' },
    });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('nav-back-button'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `languageAndLocale` in `launchApp()` applies only to the app process (via `NSUserDefaults` on iOS and `intent.putExtra(LocaleConfig)` on Android) — the OS-level system locale remains unchanged, so system-provided UI components (date pickers, permission dialogs, IME keyboards) continue to render in the host simulator's system locale regardless of the app locale setting; tests that assert on system-owned strings (e.g., the "Allow" button on a permission dialog) must set the locale in the simulator boot args in `detox.config.js`, not just in `launchApp()`.
