**Pattern 665** — `element(by.id('toast-message')).waitFor().toBeVisible()` + `.not.toBeVisible()` for testing auto-dismissing toast notifications with exact timing assertions
```typescript
describe('Save confirmation toast', () => {
  it('appears after saving and auto-dismisses within 3 seconds', async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('edit-profile-btn')).tap();
    await element(by.id('display-name-input')).clearText();
    await element(by.id('display-name-input')).typeText('New Name');
    await element(by.id('save-profile-btn')).tap();

    // Toast must appear within 1 second of the save action
    await waitFor(element(by.id('save-toast')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(1000);

    await expect(element(by.id('save-toast'))).toHaveText('Profile saved successfully');

    // Toast must auto-dismiss within 3 seconds of appearing
    await waitFor(element(by.id('save-toast')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);

    // Underlying screen must still be intact after toast disappears
    await expect(element(by.id('profile-edit-screen'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `withTimeout(3000)` on `.not.toBeVisible()` is calibrated to the toast's configured `duration` prop — if the toast uses the platform's default `Toast.LENGTH_SHORT` (2 s on Android) vs. a custom React Native timer (3 s), the timeout must be at least 500 ms greater than the configured duration to account for bridge latency; hardcode the expected duration in a shared constant imported by both the component and the test to keep them in sync.

**Pattern 666** — `element.longPress(800)` + `expect(element(by.id('haptic-feedback-indicator'))).toBeVisible()` for testing haptic feedback UI mirrors in accessibility builds
```typescript
describe('Haptic feedback on long press', () => {
  it('triggers haptic feedback and its UI mirror indicator during long press on bookmark', async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('article-item-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('article-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Long press the bookmark icon to trigger haptic feedback
    await element(by.id('bookmark-btn')).longPress(800);

    // The article should be bookmarked and a visual indicator should appear
    await waitFor(element(by.id('bookmark-active-icon'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(1000);

    // Accessibility build exposes a testID-tagged view that becomes visible
    // when UIImpactFeedbackGenerator fires — testable in simulator without haptic hardware
    await expect(element(by.id('haptic-fired-indicator'))).toBeVisible();

    // Confirm the bookmark persists after the indicator disappears
    await waitFor(element(by.id('haptic-fired-indicator')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(500);

    await expect(element(by.id('bookmark-active-icon'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Haptic feedback itself cannot be asserted by Detox — the simulator does not have a vibration motor and the `UIImpactFeedbackGenerator` fires silently; testing haptics requires your app to expose a companion `View` with a sentinel `testID` that becomes visible for ~200 ms when the feedback generator fires (rendered only in `__DEV__` or `__E2E__` builds); this adds test-only instrumentation to the production component tree, which must be stripped by the release build configuration to avoid shipping the sentinel view.

---

**Pattern 667** — `device.reverseTCP(8081, 8081)` + custom `fetch()` in `beforeAll` for verifying that test-mode API mocks are reachable before the suite runs
```typescript
// globalSetup.ts — runs before all test files
import { execSync } from 'child_process';

module.exports = async () => {
  if (process.env.E2E_PLATFORM === 'android') {
    // Ensure the mock server on the host is reachable from the Android emulator
    try {
      execSync('adb reverse tcp:8081 tcp:8081', { stdio: 'ignore' });
      execSync('adb reverse tcp:3000 tcp:3000', { stdio: 'ignore' });
      console.log('[globalSetup] ADB port forwarding configured');
    } catch (err) {
      console.warn('[globalSetup] ADB reverse failed — mock server may not be reachable:', err);
    }
  }
};

// In a test file — verify mock server connectivity before exercising the UI:
describe('Mock API server connectivity check', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

    // The app should show a "Connected to test server" banner in E2E mode
    await waitFor(element(by.id('mock-server-connected-badge')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('renders data from the mock server in the product list', async () => {
    await element(by.id('products-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-item-0'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    await expect(element(by.id('product-name-0'))).toHaveText('Mock Product Alpha');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `adb reverse` only works when the emulator has a valid ADB connection — on cloud-based device farms (AWS Device Farm, Sauce Labs) that use remote ADB over WebSocket, `adb reverse` is either unsupported or requires the farm's proprietary TCP tunnelling mechanism; for cloud test execution, configure the mock server URL via `device.appLaunchArgs.modify({ mockServerUrl: 'https://mockserver.ci.internal' })` instead of relying on localhost port forwarding.

**Pattern 668** — `element(by.id('animated-number')).waitFor().toHaveText()` with polling-based assertion for animated counter and score increment UI
```typescript
describe('Score counter animation', () => {
  it('animates the score from 0 to 1000 and lands on the correct final value', async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('start-game-btn')).tap();

    // Assert the counter starts at zero
    await waitFor(element(by.id('score-counter')))
      .toHaveText('0')
      .withTimeout(1000);

    // Trigger a scoring event that starts the animated increment
    await element(by.id('answer-btn-correct')).tap();

    // The score animates from 0 to 1000 over 800 ms
    // Poll until the counter shows the expected final value
    await waitFor(element(by.id('score-counter')))
      .toHaveText('1000')
      .withTimeout(3000); // 3x animation duration to absorb CI slowness

    // Verify the score badge also updated in sync
    await expect(element(by.id('score-badge'))).toHaveText('1,000 pts');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `waitFor().toHaveText()` polls the accessibility label or text value at Detox's internal check interval (default 100 ms) — for counters that animate through many intermediate values (e.g., 0, 50, 100, ..., 1000), each poll checks whether the current displayed value equals the target; this works correctly but any intermediate value that matches the target string by coincidence (e.g., if the target were '100' and the counter passes through '100' en route to '1000') would cause a false pass; always assert the definitive final value, not an intermediate milestone.

**Pattern 669** — `element(by.id('pdf-viewer')).swipe('left')` for testing multi-page PDF navigation in embedded document viewers
```typescript
describe('Embedded PDF viewer pagination', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('documents-tab')).tap();
    await element(by.id('doc-item-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('pdf-viewer'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(6000);
  });

  it('navigates to page 2 by swiping left on the PDF viewer', async () => {
    await expect(element(by.id('pdf-page-indicator'))).toHaveText('Page 1 of 5');

    await element(by.id('pdf-viewer')).swipe('left', 'slow', 0.7);

    await waitFor(element(by.id('pdf-page-indicator')))
      .toHaveText('Page 2 of 5')
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('navigates back to page 1 by swiping right from page 2', async () => {
    await element(by.id('pdf-viewer')).swipe('left', 'slow', 0.7);
    await waitFor(element(by.id('pdf-page-indicator'))).toHaveText('Page 2 of 5').withTimeout(3000);

    await element(by.id('pdf-viewer')).swipe('right', 'slow', 0.7);

    await waitFor(element(by.id('pdf-page-indicator')))
      .toHaveText('Page 1 of 5')
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: PDF viewers built on `react-native-pdf` or WKWebView-embedded PDFs receive swipe gestures through the native gesture responder system — if the PDF viewer uses a built-in `UIScrollView` pan gesture that takes priority over Detox's synthetic swipe, the gesture may scroll within the page rather than advancing to the next page; validate that the `pdf-viewer` element's `testID` is applied to the outermost page-swipe container (not the inner content scroll), and set `pagingEnabled={true}` on that container to ensure the swipe snaps to page boundaries.

**Pattern 670** — `element(by.id('segmented-control')).tapAtPoint({ x })` for selecting a specific segment when each segment lacks an individual `testID`
```typescript
describe('Segmented control selection', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('analytics-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('time-range-segmented-control'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('selects the "Monthly" segment (third of four) via proportional tap point', async () => {
    // Fetch the frame to compute a proportional tap position
    const segAttrs = await element(by.id('time-range-segmented-control')).getAttributes();
    if (!('frame' in segAttrs) || !segAttrs.frame) {
      throw new Error('Could not read segmented control frame');
    }

    const { width } = segAttrs.frame;
    // Segment positions: [0%–25%, 25%–50%, 50%–75%, 75%–100%]
    // Tap at 62.5% of width to hit the centre of the third segment ("Monthly")
    const tapX = Math.round(width * 0.625);
    const tapY = Math.round(segAttrs.frame.height / 2);

    await element(by.id('time-range-segmented-control')).tapAtPoint({ x: tapX, y: tapY });

    await waitFor(element(by.id('analytics-chart')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);

    await expect(element(by.id('chart-period-label'))).toHaveText('Monthly');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Computing segment positions by dividing the total width equally assumes all segments have equal width — a segmented control with variable-width segments (e.g., "Day" vs. "Last 12 Months") will have non-uniform tap zones; derive the actual tap centre by reading `getAttributes()` on each individual segment element if they have `testID` props, or ask the app team to add per-segment `testID` values to eliminate the frame-arithmetic dependency.

**Pattern 671** — `expect(element(by.id('error-boundary-fallback'))).toBeVisible()` for testing React Error Boundary rendering after simulated component errors
```typescript
describe('Error boundary fallback UI', () => {
  it('shows the error boundary fallback screen when a child component throws', async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();

    // Navigate to the screen that wraps the crash-prone component
    await element(by.id('experimental-features-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('experimental-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Tap a button that triggers a known error in the test build
    // (the button is only visible when __E2E__ flag is set)
    await element(by.id('trigger-crash-btn')).tap();

    // The Error Boundary should catch the error and render its fallback UI
    await waitFor(element(by.id('error-boundary-fallback')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);

    await expect(element(by.id('error-boundary-message')))
      .toHaveText('Something went wrong. Please try again.');

    // The "Try Again" button should reload the component tree
    await element(by.id('error-boundary-retry-btn')).tap();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('experimental-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);

    await expect(element(by.id('error-boundary-fallback'))).not.toExist();
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Triggering errors in production code via a test-only button creates a dependency between the test suite and debug-mode component instrumentation — the `trigger-crash-btn` must be gated behind `__E2E__` or `__DEV__` flags and stripped by the release build; if the release build accidentally ships the crash trigger, it becomes an in-app attack surface; use Metro bundler's `transform.visitor` to strip test-only elements from release builds and add a CI check that the release APK/IPA does not contain the `trigger-crash-btn` testID.

**Pattern 672** — `element(by.id('chart')).scroll(200, 'right')` for asserting time-series chart pan interaction and data window updates
```typescript
describe('Revenue chart time-window pan', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('dashboard-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('revenue-chart'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('panning the chart right shows older data and updates the date-range header', async () => {
    const initialHeader = await element(by.id('chart-date-range-header')).getAttributes();
    const initialText = 'text' in initialHeader ? initialHeader.text : '';

    // Pan right (scroll right = show older data = move window backward in time)
    await element(by.id('revenue-chart')).scroll(200, 'right');

    await waitFor(element(by.id('chart-date-range-header')))
      .not.toHaveText(initialText)
      .withTimeout(2000);

    // The date range should shift backward (older dates)
    const newHeader = await element(by.id('chart-date-range-header')).getAttributes();
    const newText = 'text' in newHeader ? newHeader.text : '';

    // Simple sanity check: the new date range label should differ from the initial
    expect(newText).not.toBe(initialText);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Chart pan interactions often rely on `PanResponder` or `react-native-gesture-handler`'s `Pan` gesture — Detox's `scroll()` action on a non-`ScrollView` element sends a swipe gesture that may not be recognized by `PanResponder` if the component uses `onStartShouldSetPanResponder: () => true` with a minimum pan distance threshold; if `scroll()` has no effect, use `swipe()` with explicit `startNormalizedX` and `normalizedSwipeOffset` instead, which more closely mimics the continuous-press-and-drag gesture that `PanResponder` expects.

**Pattern 673** — `element(by.id('video-player')).tap()` + `waitFor(by.id('play-controls')).toBeVisible()` for testing video player control bar reveal on tap
```typescript
describe('Video player control bar', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('media-tab')).tap();
    await element(by.id('video-item-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('video-player-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
    // Wait for the video to start playing (control bar auto-hides after 3 s)
    await waitFor(element(by.id('video-control-bar')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('reveals the control bar on tap and it auto-hides after 3 seconds', async () => {
    // Tap the player to reveal the control bar
    await element(by.id('video-player')).tap();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('video-control-bar')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(1000);

    await expect(element(by.id('play-pause-btn'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('seek-bar'))).toBeVisible();

    // Control bar should auto-hide after 3 seconds of no interaction
    await waitFor(element(by.id('video-control-bar')))
      .not.toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('pauses the video when the pause button is tapped', async () => {
    await element(by.id('video-player')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('play-pause-btn'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(1000);

    await element(by.id('play-pause-btn')).tap();

    // After pausing, the control bar should remain visible (does not auto-hide while paused)
    await expect(element(by.id('video-control-bar'))).toBeVisible();
    await expect(element(by.id('play-pause-btn'))).toHaveLabel('Play');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Video auto-hide timers use `setTimeout` internally, which Detox's synchronisation mechanism tracks and waits for — this means `waitFor(controlBar).not.toBeVisible()` in the auto-hide test will resolve only after Detox's idle detector sees the timer fire and the animation complete, adding the full auto-hide delay (~3 s) to the test's execution time; if the test suite has many video player tests, consider using `device.disableSynchronization()` + an explicit `waitFor` with the expected hide timeout to avoid double-waiting.

**Pattern 674** — `element(by.id('text-area')).scroll(300, 'down')` for asserting multi-line `TextInput` scroll behaviour and line count
```typescript
describe('Multi-line text area', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('compose-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('compose-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('scrolls within a multi-line TextInput when content exceeds the visible area', async () => {
    await element(by.id('compose-text-area')).tap();

    // Type a long text that will cause the TextInput to scroll internally
    const longText = Array(20).fill('This is a test line of text.').join('\n');
    await element(by.id('compose-text-area')).typeText(longText);

    // The last line should initially be at the cursor position (bottom)
    const initialAttrs = await element(by.id('compose-text-area')).getAttributes();

    // Scroll up within the text area to verify the first line is reachable
    await element(by.id('compose-text-area')).scroll(300, 'up');

    // The character count label should reflect all typed content
    await expect(element(by.id('char-count-label'))).not.toHaveText('0 / 500');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Scrolling inside a `TextInput` with `multiline={true}` uses the native `UITextView` (iOS) or `EditText` (Android) internal scroll mechanism — Detox's `element.scroll()` action sends a native scroll gesture to the text view, but the gesture may be intercepted by a parent `ScrollView` if the `TextInput` does not set `scrollEnabled={true}` explicitly; always verify `scrollEnabled` is true on multi-line `TextInput` components before writing scroll-within-text-area tests.

**Pattern 675** — `element(by.id('date-picker')).setDatePickerDate(dateStr, formatStr)` with ISO 8601 format for calendar picker selection in booking flows
```typescript
describe('Flight booking date selection', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('book-flight-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('booking-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('selects a departure date 7 days from today using the date picker', async () => {
    // Compute a date 7 days in the future in the format expected by setDatePickerDate
    const departureDate = new Date();
    departureDate.setDate(departureDate.getDate() + 7);
    const dateString = departureDate.toISOString().slice(0, 10); // 'YYYY-MM-DD'

    await element(by.id('departure-date-field')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('date-picker-modal'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);

    await element(by.id('departure-date-picker')).setDatePickerDate(dateString, 'YYYY-MM-DD');

    await element(by.id('date-picker-confirm-btn')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('date-picker-modal'))).not.toBeVisible().withTimeout(1500);

    // The departure field should display the selected date in the app's display format
    const displayDate = departureDate.toLocaleDateString('en-US', {
      month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric',
    });
    await expect(element(by.id('departure-date-field'))).toHaveText(displayDate);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `setDatePickerDate` with `'YYYY-MM-DD'` format works reliably for iOS `UIDatePicker` in `.date` mode — on Android the format string is passed to `java.text.SimpleDateFormat` which uses `'yyyy-MM-dd'` (lowercase `y` and `d`); passing an iOS-style `'YYYY-MM-DD'` format string to Android causes a parsing error or silently selects the wrong year because uppercase `Y` means "week year" in Java's date formatting; always use `'yyyy-MM-dd'` for Android and gate the format string behind `device.getPlatform()`.

**Pattern 676** — `element(by.id('search-bar')).focus()` + `waitFor(by.id('search-suggestions')).toBeVisible()` for testing search-as-you-type suggestion panels
```typescript
describe('Product search suggestions', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('search-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('search-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('shows trending search suggestions immediately when the search bar is focused', async () => {
    await element(by.id('search-input')).tap();

    // Suggestions should appear as soon as the field gains focus (empty query)
    await waitFor(element(by.id('trending-suggestions-list')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);

    const attrsResult = await element(by.id('trending-suggestion-item')).getAttributes();
    expect('elements' in attrsResult && attrsResult.elements.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  it('filters suggestions as the user types and selects the first result', async () => {
    await element(by.id('search-input')).tap();
    await element(by.id('search-input')).typeText('wireless');

    await waitFor(element(by.id('search-suggestions-list')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);

    await waitFor(element(by.id('suggestion-item-0')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(2000);

    await element(by.id('suggestion-item-0')).tap();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('search-results-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Search-as-you-type tests depend on debounce timers in the search component — `typeText('wireless')` sends all characters in rapid succession, which may fire the debounced API call before all characters are delivered if the debounce is shorter than the total `typeText` execution time (~50 ms for 8 characters); add a `waitFor(element(by.id('search-loading-indicator'))).not.toBeVisible()` after `typeText` to confirm the API call has completed and results are stable before asserting on `suggestion-item-0`.

**Pattern 677** — `device.terminateApp()` + `device.launchApp({ newInstance: false })` for simulating app resume-from-background without losing native state
```typescript
describe('App backgrounding and foreground resume', () => {
  it('resumes to the same screen after being backgrounded and brought back', async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('orders-tab')).tap();
    await element(by.id('order-item-0')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('order-detail-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Send the app to background (equivalent to pressing the home button)
    await device.sendToHome();

    // Wait briefly to simulate a real background period
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));

    // Bring the app back to foreground without creating a new process
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: false });

    // The app should resume on the same order detail screen
    await waitFor(element(by.id('order-detail-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(3000);

    // Verify the order data is still displayed (not cleared on resume)
    await expect(element(by.id('order-status-label'))).not.toHaveText('');
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `device.launchApp({ newInstance: false })` brings the app to foreground if it is backgrounded, or launches it if it is terminated — it cannot distinguish between a fresh launch and a resume in the test assertion; if your test needs to verify that the resume path specifically (not the cold-start path) is taken, instrument the app with a `AppState` listener that sets a `testID`-tagged flag (`just-resumed-indicator`) visible only after `change` events of `'active'` following `'background'`, and assert on that flag.

**Pattern 678** — `element(by.id('carousel')).swipe('left', 'fast', 0.9)` with repeat loop for multi-step carousel auto-advance verification
```typescript
describe('Onboarding carousel complete walk-through', () => {
  it('steps through all 5 carousel pages and reaches the Get Started screen', async () => {
    await device.terminateApp();
    await device.uninstallApp();
    await device.installApp();
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });

    await waitFor(element(by.id('onboarding-carousel'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);

    const TOTAL_PAGES = 5;

    for (let page = 1; page < TOTAL_PAGES; page++) {
      // Verify current page indicator before advancing
      await expect(element(by.id(`page-dot-${page - 1}-active`))).toBeVisible();

      // Swipe left to advance to the next page
      await element(by.id('onboarding-carousel')).swipe('left', 'fast', 0.9);

      // Wait for the next page's content to become visible
      await waitFor(element(by.id(`onboarding-page-${page}`)))
        .toBeVisible()
        .withTimeout(2000);
    }

    // Final page should show the Get Started CTA
    await expect(element(by.id('get-started-btn'))).toBeVisible();
    await element(by.id('get-started-btn')).tap();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(4000);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: A `for` loop of swipe gestures adds latency proportional to the page count — each `swipe()` + `waitFor()` takes ~500–700 ms, so a 10-page carousel takes ~7 s for the swipe loop alone; for very long carousels where you only care about the final CTA, use `element(by.id('onboarding-carousel')).scrollTo('right')` to jump to the last page in one gesture, reserving the loop pattern for tests that must assert intermediate page content.

### Community Gotchas

**G365** — `element.typeText()` on a `TextInput` inside a `KeyboardAwareScrollView` fires the keyboard-avoidance layout shift mid-type, causing characters to be dropped on Android
Why this matters: `react-native-keyboard-aware-scroll-view` listens for the `keyboardDidShow` event and adjusts the scroll view's content offset when the keyboard appears. On Android, the keyboard show event fires after the first character is typed (not before focus), so the layout shift happens while Detox is still injecting characters. The `InputMethodManager.commitText()` call that Detox uses to type characters is interrupted by the layout change, dropping the characters that were queued during the animation frame in which the scroll adjustment occurred. This produces truncated text values (e.g., `'passw'` instead of `'password'`) that appear to be timing issues.
Fix: Tap the target field first to establish focus and trigger the keyboard appear event, then wait for the `KeyboardAwareScrollView` to finish its adjustment (assert that the scroll view's `contentOffset` has stabilised by waiting for a sentinel element to move to its final position), and only then call `typeText()`. Alternatively, replace `KeyboardAwareScrollView` with React Native's built-in `KeyboardAvoidingView` in the test build, which adjusts synchronously and does not drop characters.

---

**G366** — `waitFor(element).toBeVisible().withTimeout(N)` resolves on stub/skeleton elements that share the same `testID` as the real content — the test interacts with the skeleton before data loads
Why this matters: A common pattern in React Native apps is to render a `ContentLoader` skeleton with the same `testID` as the real content element, toggling between them via a `loading` boolean prop. When `loading` is true, a `<View testID="product-card-0">` skeleton is rendered; when false, the real `<TouchableOpacity testID="product-card-0">` replaces it. `waitFor(element(by.id('product-card-0'))).toBeVisible()` resolves on the skeleton as soon as it mounts — the subsequent `tap()` lands on the non-interactive skeleton, does nothing, and the test fails on the next `waitFor` with a confusing "home screen not found" error.
Fix: Assign distinct `testID` values to skeleton and content elements (e.g., `product-card-skeleton-0` vs. `product-card-0`). After `waitFor(element(by.id('product-card-0'))).toBeVisible()`, add `await expect(element(by.id('product-card-skeleton-0'))).not.toExist()` to confirm the skeleton has been replaced before proceeding. Alternatively, assert a content-specific attribute (`toHaveText('Product Name')`) on the card before tapping.

---

**G367** — `device.launchApp({ permissions: { microphone: 'YES' } })` does not prevent the microphone permission dialog from appearing on Android 13+ due to the new `RECORD_AUDIO` runtime permission model
Why this matters: On Android 13 (API 33) and above, `RECORD_AUDIO` became a runtime permission that must be granted interactively even if the app declares it in the manifest. Detox's `permissions: { microphone: 'YES' }` sets the permission via `adb shell pm grant com.example.app android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO`, which works on Android 12 and below. However, on Android 13+, the ADB grant command alone is insufficient — the permission requires a `PackageManager.PERMISSION_GRANTED` check that considers additional `AppOpsManager` flags that ADB does not set. Tests that start voice recording features on Android 13 emulators encounter the permission dialog despite the launch-time grant, causing the dialog-dependent flow to time out.
Fix: After `device.launchApp()`, add a `system.element(by.system.label('Allow'))` conditional tap that handles the permission dialog if it appears: `const allowBtn = system.element(by.system.label('Allow')); if (await allowBtn.getAttributes().catch(() => null)) { await allowBtn.tap(); }`. Alternatively, set the `AppOpsManager` permission via a pre-launch ADB command: `adb shell appops set com.example.app RECORD_AUDIO allow`.

---

**G368** — `element(by.id('modal')).swipe('down')` on iOS 17+ sheet presentations dismisses the modal into a detached state — the element remains in the accessibility tree with a non-zero frame
Why this matters: iOS 17 introduced `UISheetPresentationController` detents that allow modals to be dragged partially down without dismissing. When Detox's `swipe('down')` gesture covers less than the sheet's minimum dismiss distance, the sheet enters a "rubber band" intermediate state — it animates back upward but leaves a brief window where the accessibility frame is at a non-standard position. On iOS 17+, this intermediate frame is sometimes reported to the accessibility system as a valid visible frame even after the sheet has visually returned to its full presentation, causing `waitFor(modal).not.toBeVisible()` to time out because the stale frame is still non-zero. Tests that assume `swipe('down')` always fully dismisses the sheet become intermittently flaky on iOS 17.
Fix: Use `swipe('down', 'fast', 0.9)` with a large normalized offset to ensure the gesture crosses the full dismiss threshold. After the swipe, assert `not.toExist()` rather than `not.toBeVisible()` — `not.toExist()` checks for complete removal from the accessibility tree, which is more reliable than the frame-based visibility check when intermediate animation states are involved.

---

**G369** — `element.replaceText(longString)` on Android silently truncates text to 255 characters when the `TextInput` uses `android:maxLength` in the underlying native view
Why this matters: Android's `EditText` has a hard limit on content set via the accessibility `setText()` action — the `android:maxLength` attribute enforced at the native level applies to both user-typed input and programmatically set values. When Detox calls `replaceText()` on a `TextInput` that has `maxLength={300}` in React Native props, the value is first set by the React Native bridge (which respects `maxLength`) and then re-read via the accessibility API (which may apply Android's own native limit if the `inputFilter` is configured separately). For fields with very long expected values in tests, `replaceText()` may silently stop at the native limit, not the React Native prop limit, producing a value shorter than expected without throwing an error.
Fix: For fields where you need to assert exact long string content, always verify post-`replaceText()` with `toHaveValue(expected)` to confirm the full string was accepted. If the value is shorter than expected, check whether the `TextInput` component has both `maxLength` (React Native) and `android:maxLength` (native XML attribute, possibly from a third-party library's style) set to different values, and reconcile them to the same limit.

### Pattern 679 — `element.adjustSliderToPosition()` for deterministic slider testing

React Native `Slider` components (both the built-in and `@react-native-community/slider`) expose a normalized 0.0–1.0 position API in Detox. Use `adjustSliderToPosition()` instead of gesture-based drag — gestures depend on the slider's rendered pixel width and break on different device sizes.

```typescript
describe('Volume slider', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('settings-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('volume-settings-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('sets volume to 50% via the slider', async () => {
    await element(by.id('volume-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.5);

    // Verify the displayed value label updates
    await expect(element(by.id('volume-value-label'))).toHaveText('50%');
  });

  it('sets volume to maximum and confirms accessibility value', async () => {
    await element(by.id('volume-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(1.0);

    const attrs = await element(by.id('volume-slider')).getAttributes();
    // iOS: value property reflects the slider's normalizedValue mapped to min–max
    // Android: value property reflects the raw progress integer
    if (device.getPlatform() === 'ios') {
      expect(Number(attrs.value)).toBeCloseTo(1.0, 1);
    } else {
      // Android Slider max defaults to 1 unless overridden — check label instead
      await expect(element(by.id('volume-value-label'))).toHaveText('100%');
    }
  });

  it('disables audio when slider is set to 0', async () => {
    await element(by.id('volume-slider')).adjustSliderToPosition(0.0);
    await expect(element(by.id('muted-icon'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

Tradeoff: `adjustSliderToPosition()` maps to `UIAccessibility.setValue()` on iOS and `AccessibilityNodeInfo.ACTION_SET_PROGRESS` on Android. On iOS `UISlider` with `isContinuous = false` (discrete steps), the slider snaps to the nearest allowed value — passing `0.5` when there are only 4 steps (0, 0.33, 0.66, 1.0) will land on `0.33` or `0.66` depending on rounding. Always verify the final value via `getAttributes()` or a label assertion rather than assuming the position argument is the exact result (see Gotcha 370).

---

### Pattern 680 — `by.ancestor()` + `by.descendant()` compound matchers for disambiguating duplicate testIDs in list rows

When a FlatList renders the same component template for each row, multiple elements share identical testIDs (e.g., `action-button` in every row). Use `by.ancestor()` or `by.descendant()` to scope the selector to a specific row without relying on `atIndex(N)` (which is positional and breaks if rows reorder).

```typescript
// Component example — each row has the same internal testIDs
// <View testID={`cart-item-${item.id}`}>           ← unique row anchor
//   <Text testID="item-name">{item.name}</Text>    ← duplicated
//   <TouchableOpacity testID="remove-btn">         ← duplicated
//   <Text testID="item-price">{item.price}</Text>  ← duplicated
// </View>

describe('Cart item interactions', () => {
  it('removes a specific item by name-scoped selector', async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
    await element(by.id('cart-tab')).tap();
    await waitFor(element(by.id('cart-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);

    // Scope "remove-btn" to the row whose ancestor has a known unique testID
    const removeButtonForItem42 = element(
      by.id('remove-btn').and(by.ancestor(by.id('cart-item-42')))
    );

    await expect(removeButtonForItem42).toBeVisible();
    await removeButtonForItem42.tap();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('cart-item-42'))).not.toExist().withTimeout(3000);
  });

  it('asserts price label within a specific cart row using by.descendant()', async () => {
    // by.descendant scopes the parent to rows that CONTAIN the child matcher
    const row = element(
      by.id('cart-item-42').and(by.descendant(by.id('item-price')))
    );
    await expect(row).toBeVisible();

    // Now target the price label inside the confirmed row
    const priceLabel = element(
      by.id('item-price').and(by.ancestor(by.id('cart-item-42')))
    );
    await expect(priceLabel).toHaveText('$29.99');
  });
});
```

Tradeoff: `by.ancestor()` / `by.descendant()` compound matchers are evaluated on the full accessibility tree traversal, which is O(N) in the number of nodes. For very large lists (500+ rows), prefer `scrollToIndex({ index })` to bring the target row into view, then assert with `atIndex(0)` on the now-visible slice. The compound matcher approach is optimal when the list is short (< 100 rows) and row reordering is a real concern.

---

### Pattern 681 — `device.appLaunchArgs.modify()` and `.reset()` for per-test launch-arg management

`device.appLaunchArgs` provides a mutable interface to the arguments passed to the app at launch. Unlike `device.launchApp({ launchArgs })` which requires a full restart, `appLaunchArgs.modify()` updates the args for the *next* launch — combine with `device.reloadReactNative()` for a fast per-test arg change without a full process restart.

```typescript
// In detoxrc.js, define a base set of launchArgs for the configuration:
// apps: { 'ios.release': { launchArgs: { MOCK_API: '1', FEATURE_FLAGS: 'onboarding_v2' } } }

describe('Feature flag gating', () => {
  afterEach(async () => {
    // CRITICAL: always reset to the baseline after each test
    device.appLaunchArgs.reset();
    await device.reloadReactNative();
  });

  it('shows the legacy onboarding with FEATURE_FLAGS=onboarding_v1', async () => {
    device.appLaunchArgs.modify({ FEATURE_FLAGS: 'onboarding_v1' });
    await device.reloadReactNative();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('legacy-onboarding-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('shows the new onboarding with FEATURE_FLAGS=onboarding_v2', async () => {
    // No modification needed — baseline config already sets onboarding_v2
    await device.reloadReactNative();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('new-onboarding-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(4000);
  });

  it('enables maintenance mode banner via IS_MAINTENANCE launch arg', async () => {
    device.appLaunchArgs.modify({ IS_MAINTENANCE: '1' });
    await device.reloadReactNative();

    await expect(element(by.id('maintenance-banner'))).toBeVisible();
  });
});

// Helper for reading launch args inside the app (React Native side):
// import { NativeModules } from 'react-native';
// const args = NativeModules.DetoxLaunchArgs?.get() ?? {};
// const featureFlags = args.FEATURE_FLAGS ?? 'default';
```

Tradeoff: `appLaunchArgs.modify()` changes are staged in memory on the Detox server side and applied at the next `launchApp()` or `reloadReactNative()` call. They do **not** take effect immediately for a running app. If you forget `device.reloadReactNative()` after calling `modify()`, the test runs with the previous args and produces a confusing false pass. Always pair `modify()` + reload. Also see Gotcha 372 — args persist across specs if `reset()` is not called in `afterEach`.

---

### Pattern 682 — Multi-configuration `.detoxrc.js` for phone / tablet / TV CI matrix

Large React Native apps that target multiple form factors (phone, tablet, TV) need separate Detox configurations that share the test runner setup but differ in device type, app binary, and environment variables. Centralize shared config in a `shared` object and spread it into each named configuration.

```js
// .detoxrc.js
const shared = {
  testRunner: {
    args: {
      config: 'e2e/jest.config.js',
      maxWorkers: 2,
    },
    jest: { setupTimeout: 120000 },
    retries: 1,
  },
};

/** @type {import('@wix/detox/src/types/config').DetoxConfig} */
module.exports = {
  ...shared,
  apps: {
    'ios.phone.release': {
      type: 'ios.app',
      binaryPath: 'ios/build/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app',
      build: 'xcodebuild -workspace ios/MyApp.xcworkspace -scheme MyApp-Release ...',
    },
    'ios.tablet.release': {
      type: 'ios.app',
      binaryPath: 'ios/build/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app',
      build: 'xcodebuild -workspace ios/MyApp.xcworkspace -scheme MyApp-Tablet-Release ...',
    },
    'android.phone.release': {
      type: 'android.apk',
      binaryPath: 'android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk',
      build: './gradlew assembleRelease assembleAndroidTest',
    },
  },
  devices: {
    'iphone-15': {
      type: 'ios.simulator',
      device: { type: 'iPhone 15', os: 'iOS 18.4' },
    },
    'ipad-air': {
      type: 'ios.simulator',
      device: { type: 'iPad Air 13-inch (M2)', os: 'iOS 18.4' },
    },
    'pixel-9': {
      type: 'android.emulator',
      device: { avdName: 'Pixel_9_API_35' },
    },
  },
  configurations: {
    'ios.phone': {
      device: 'iphone-15',
      app: 'ios.phone.release',
    },
    'ios.tablet': {
      device: 'ipad-air',
      app: 'ios.tablet.release',
      testRunner: {
        ...shared.testRunner,
        args: {
          ...shared.testRunner.args,
          // tablet-only test suite
          testPathPattern: 'e2e/tablet',
        },
      },
    },
    'android.phone': {
      device: 'pixel-9',
      app: 'android.phone.release',
    },
  },
};
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions matrix — runs all configurations in parallel
jobs:
  e2e:
    strategy:
      matrix:
        config: [ios.phone, ios.tablet, android.phone]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.config == 'android.phone' && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'macos-15' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npx detox build --configuration ${{ matrix.config }}
      - run: npx detox test --configuration ${{ matrix.config }} --headless
```

Tradeoff: Spreading `shared` at the top level and again inside individual `configurations[x].testRunner` is required because `configurations` entries override rather than merge the top-level `testRunner`. If the per-config override is partial (only changing `testPathPattern`), always spread the parent `testRunner.args` to preserve `maxWorkers`, `setupTimeout`, and `retries`. Forgetting the spread silently drops retry/worker settings for that configuration.

---

### Pattern 683 — `testRunner.retries` idempotency guard for legitimate flake mitigation

Detox `testRunner.retries` re-runs a failed test up to N times within the same worker process. This is useful for genuine platform flakiness (animation timing, emulator hiccups) but dangerous if the test is not idempotent — a non-idempotent test retried after a partial run can corrupt shared state. The `runOnce()` guard ensures setup steps that must only happen once per test execution (seeding data, launching with specific permissions) are skipped on retries.

```typescript
// helpers/runOnce.ts
let _setupDone = false;

/**
 * Executes `fn` only on the first call within a test.
 * On Detox retries, the test body re-runs but the module-level flag persists
 * within the same worker process — `fn` is skipped on retry #2+.
 *
 * Use for: API seed calls, device.launchApp({ delete: true }), permission grants.
 * Reset by calling runOnce.reset() in globalTeardown or afterAll.
 */
export function runOnce(key: string, fn: () => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
  const store: Record<string, boolean> = (global as any).__runOnceStore ?? {};
  (global as any).__runOnceStore = store;
  if (store[key]) return Promise.resolve();
  store[key] = true;
  return fn();
}

// e2e/purchase-flow.test.ts
describe('Purchase flow', () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    // Seed test data only on the first run — skip on Detox retries
    await runOnce('purchase-flow:seed', async () => {
      await fetch(`${TEST_API_BASE}/seed/purchase-flow`);
    });
    await device.reloadReactNative();
  });

  it('completes checkout and shows order confirmation', async () => {
    await element(by.id('product-item-0')).tap();
    await element(by.id('add-to-cart-btn')).tap();
    await element(by.id('cart-tab')).tap();
    await element(by.id('checkout-btn')).tap();
    await element(by.id('confirm-order-btn')).tap();

    await waitFor(element(by.id('order-confirmation-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(8000);
  });
});
```

```js
// .detoxrc.js — enable retries globally
module.exports = {
  testRunner: {
    retries: 1,           // re-run each failed test once
    args: { config: 'e2e/jest.config.js' },
  },
  // ...
};
```

Tradeoff: `testRunner.retries` interacts with `jest --bail`: bail counts each retry as a separate failure, so with `retries: 2` and `bail: 3`, a single flaky test burns 2 bail tokens on retries before consuming the final token on a real failure. Set `bail` conservatively (10+) when retries are enabled, or omit it entirely for e2e suites where a single test failure should not abort the run (see Gotcha 374).

---

### Pattern 684 — Istanbul/NYC JS coverage collection from Detox runs

To collect JavaScript coverage from Detox end-to-end tests, instrument the Metro bundle with Istanbul via Babel and then merge coverage reports in `globalTeardown`. This gives you real user-path coverage data that unit tests cannot capture.

```js
// babel.config.js — conditional Istanbul instrumentation
module.exports = (api) => {
  const isTest = api.env('test') || api.env('coverage');
  return {
    presets: ['module:@react-native/babel-preset'],
    plugins: isTest && process.env.BABEL_ENV === 'coverage'
      ? ['istanbul']
      : [],
  };
};
```

```js
// .detoxrc.js — coverage configuration
module.exports = {
  apps: {
    'ios.debug.coverage': {
      type: 'ios.app',
      binaryPath: 'ios/build/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app',
      build: 'BABEL_ENV=coverage npx react-native bundle --dev true ...',
      launchArgs: { COVERAGE_ENABLED: '1' },
    },
  },
  configurations: {
    'ios.coverage': {
      device: 'iphone-15',
      app: 'ios.debug.coverage',
    },
  },
};
```

```js
// e2e/setup/globalTeardown.js — merge per-test coverage files and generate report
const { execSync } = require('child_process');
const path = require('path');
const fs = require('fs');

module.exports = async () => {
  const coverageDir = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../.nyc_output');
  if (!fs.existsSync(coverageDir)) return;

  // Merge coverage from all workers and generate lcov + text summary
  execSync('npx nyc merge .nyc_output .nyc_output/merged-coverage.json', {
    cwd: path.resolve(__dirname, '../..'),
    stdio: 'inherit',
  });
  execSync('npx nyc report --reporter=lcov --reporter=text-summary', {
    cwd: path.resolve(__dirname, '../..'),
    stdio: 'inherit',
  });

  console.log('[Coverage] Report written to coverage/lcov.info');
};
```

```js
// e2e/jest.config.js — wire up teardown
module.exports = {
  rootDir: '../..',
  testEnvironment: 'detox/runners/jest/testEnvironment',
  testTimeout: 120000,
  globalTeardown: './e2e/setup/globalTeardown.js',
  reporters: ['default'],
};
```

```tsx
// App.tsx — flush coverage data before app teardown (required for accurate coverage)
import { NativeModules, AppState } from 'react-native';

if (__DEV__ && process.env.COVERAGE_ENABLED) {
  AppState.addEventListener('change', (nextState) => {
    if (nextState === 'background' || nextState === 'inactive') {
      // Flush Istanbul coverage to the file system via a native bridge
      NativeModules.CoverageCollector?.flush?.();
    }
  });
}
```

Tradeoff: Istanbul instrumentation adds ~30–60% to Metro bundle time and ~15% to runtime performance. Never enable `BABEL_ENV=coverage` in standard smoke or regression CI jobs — create a dedicated `coverage` configuration that runs only the critical user-path tests. Coverage from e2e tests is complementary to unit coverage; do not aim for 80% e2e coverage targets, as that incentivises duplicating unit-test scenarios as slow integration tests (see Gotcha 375).

---

### Pattern 685 — `clearText()` vs `tapBackspaceKey()` vs `replaceText('')` disambiguation guide

Three Detox APIs can clear a text input, but they behave differently across platforms, input types, and app state. Use this guide to choose the right one:

| Method | iOS | Android | Masked inputs | Triggers onChange |
|--------|-----|---------|---------------|-------------------|
| `clearText()` | Uses `UITextField.text = ''` via accessibility | Uses `setText('')` via `AccessibilityNodeInfo` | Yes | No on Android |
| `tapBackspaceKey()` | Sends keyboard backspace events | Sends `KeyEvent.KEYCODE_DEL` events | Yes | Yes |
| `replaceText('')` | Sets value + fires JS onChange | Sets value + fires JS onChange | Yes (clears) | Yes |

```typescript
// clearText() — fast, no onChange side-effects on Android
// Best for: wiping a pre-filled field before re-filling, no validation needed
it('clears the search field and resets results', async () => {
  await element(by.id('search-input')).clearText();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('empty-search-state'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(2000);
});

// replaceText('') — fires onChange, triggers validation/state updates
// Best for: controlled inputs with validation logic that must re-evaluate on clear
it('clears the amount field and shows required-field error', async () => {
  await element(by.id('amount-input')).replaceText('');
  await expect(element(by.id('amount-required-error'))).toBeVisible();
});

// tapBackspaceKey() — simulates real user deletion, character by character
// Best for: OTP / PIN inputs that respond to individual keystrokes
it('deletes last digit of OTP and expects re-entry prompt', async () => {
  // OTP already filled from a previous step — delete the last digit
  await element(by.id('otp-input-5')).tapBackspaceKey();
  await expect(element(by.id('otp-input-5'))).toHaveValue('');
  await expect(element(by.id('otp-input-5'))).toBeFocused();
});

// Cross-platform safe clear-and-refill helper
async function clearAndFill(testId: string, value: string): Promise<void> {
  // replaceText handles clear + fill atomically and fires onChange
  await element(by.id(testId)).replaceText(value);
}
```

Tradeoff: On Android, `clearText()` does not fire the React Native `onChangeText` callback because it uses the low-level `setText('')` accessibility action, which bypasses the TextWatcher. If your test requires validation logic to run (e.g., "required field" error to appear), use `replaceText('')` instead. On iOS, both `clearText()` and `replaceText('')` fire `onChange`. If you need the exact behaviour across platforms, `replaceText('')` is the safest universal choice, with the caveat that it is slower on Android because it goes through the full JS bridge round-trip.

---

### Pattern 686 — `device.captureViewHierarchy()` + Jest inline snapshot for zero-regression view-tree CI gate

Use `captureViewHierarchy()` to take a structural snapshot of the accessibility tree at a key screen state and compare it against a stored baseline in CI. This catches unexpected layout changes, missing `testID` regressions, and accessibility structure drift without a visual screenshot comparison.

```typescript
import { stripVolatileAttributes } from '../helpers/hierarchyUtils';

describe('Home screen hierarchy regression', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
  });

  it('home screen hierarchy matches the approved baseline', async () => {
    // Capture the hierarchy — saved to <artifacts-path>/home-hierarchy.viewhierarchy (iOS)
    // or home-hierarchy.uihierarchy (Android)
    const hierarchyPath = await device.captureViewHierarchy('home-hierarchy');

    // Parse and strip volatile attributes (frame coords, timestamps, dynamic text)
    const hierarchy = await readHierarchyFile(hierarchyPath);
    const stable = stripVolatileAttributes(hierarchy);

    // Store the first snapshot and lock it — subsequent runs diff against it
    expect(stable).toMatchSnapshot('home-screen-hierarchy');
  });
});

// e2e/helpers/hierarchyUtils.ts
import fs from 'fs';
import path from 'path';

/** Read and parse the .viewhierarchy/.uihierarchy XML file */
export async function readHierarchyFile(filePath: string): Promise<string> {
  return fs.readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8');
}

/**
 * Strip attributes that change between runs but carry no structural signal:
 * - frame/bounds coordinates (layout shifts with device frame)
 * - visible-to-user boolean (can flip during animation capture)
 * - Android display-cutout attribute (varies by emulator skin — Gotcha 376)
 */
export function stripVolatileAttributes(xml: string): string {
  return xml
    .replace(/\s*frame="\{[^}]+\}"/g, '')        // iOS frame coords
    .replace(/\s*bounds="\[[^\]]+\]"/g, '')       // Android bounds
    .replace(/\s*visible-to-user="[^"]*"/g, '')   // Android visibility flag
    .replace(/\s*display-cutout="[^"]*"/g, '')    // Android API 36 attribute (Gotcha 376)
    .replace(/\s*timestamp="[^"]*"/g, '');        // Any timestamp attributes
}
```

```bash
# Update baseline snapshots when intentional changes are made
UPDATE_HIERARCHY_BASELINES=true npx detox test --configuration ios.phone -t "hierarchy regression"
# In test: if (process.env.UPDATE_HIERARCHY_BASELINES) { expect.anything(); return; }
```

Tradeoff: View hierarchy snapshots are XML strings that can be several hundred kilobytes on complex screens. Jest's inline `toMatchSnapshot()` stores the full XML in the `__snapshots__` directory — commit this file to source control. On screens with dynamic content (live counters, user names), `stripVolatileAttributes()` must also strip the dynamic text nodes, otherwise every test run will generate a diff. Prefer hierarchy snapshots for structural regression (missing elements, wrong nesting) and leave dynamic content assertions to regular `toHaveText()` / `toHaveLabel()` matchers.

---

### Community Gotchas (continued)

**G370** — `element.adjustSliderToPosition(0.5)` lands on the wrong value when the iOS `UISlider` has discrete steps configured
Why this matters: `UISlider` does not natively support discrete steps in iOS — the `step` prop in `@react-native-community/slider` is implemented in the React Native bridge by rounding the value on `onValueChange`. When Detox calls `UIAccessibility.setValue('0.5')`, iOS sets the raw float value on the underlying `UISlider` before the RN bridge applies the step rounding. The accessibility tree then reports the *raw* float value (0.5) rather than the rounded step value (e.g., 0.4 or 0.6), causing a `toHaveValue('0.5')` assertion to pass even though the visible displayed value is '40%'. Tests that assert on `getAttributes().value` after `adjustSliderToPosition()` without verifying the displayed label are silently asserting the wrong thing.
Fix: After `adjustSliderToPosition()`, always assert the rendered label (`toHaveText('50%')`) or the step-rounded accessibility value rather than the raw float. On Android, `setProgress()` via `ACTION_SET_PROGRESS` respects the step rounding at the native level, so Android assertions on `getAttributes().value` are reliable — only iOS requires the label cross-check.

---

**G371** — `by.ancestor(by.id('container'))` silently matches nothing on Android API 34+ when the ancestor `ViewGroup` has `importantForAccessibility='no-hide-descendants'`
Why this matters: Android's accessibility system uses `importantForAccessibility` to control which views are exposed to accessibility services (and by extension, to Detox's matcher). When a `ViewGroup` has `importantForAccessibility='no-hide-descendants'`, all its descendant views are hidden from the accessibility tree. Detox's `by.ancestor()` matcher resolves ancestors by walking the accessibility tree — it cannot find an ancestor that is marked as hiding its descendants, so the entire compound matcher silently returns 0 matches. This is particularly common in list-row `ViewGroup`s that wrap native performance optimisations and set `importantForAccessibility` to reduce accessibility overhead.
Fix: Set `accessible={true}` and do not set `importantForAccessibility='no-hide-descendants'` on any `ViewGroup` that you intend to use as a `by.ancestor()` anchor in Detox tests. Use the `by.id()` suffix anchor on the innermost element plus `atIndex()` as a fallback when the ancestor approach fails.

---

**G372** — `device.appLaunchArgs.modify()` mutations persist across test specs in the same Detox worker unless explicitly reset
Why this matters: Detox workers are long-lived Node.js processes that run multiple test files sequentially. The `appLaunchArgs` object is shared state on the Detox client within the worker process. When a test calls `device.appLaunchArgs.modify({ FLAG: '1' })` in `beforeEach` without a corresponding `device.appLaunchArgs.reset()` in `afterEach`, the modified argument remains in effect for all subsequent test files assigned to that worker. This causes false passes (later tests run with an unexpected flag enabled) or false failures (tests that expect baseline args fail because a previous file's flag is still set). The bug is intermittent because it depends on the order in which the test runner assigns files to workers.
Fix: Always call `device.appLaunchArgs.reset()` in `afterEach` (not `afterAll`) when using `modify()`. For test suites that rely on a specific non-default arg throughout, set it in `beforeAll` with a `device.appLaunchArgs.reset()` + `device.appLaunchArgs.modify()` sequence, and reset in `afterAll`.

---

**G373** — Multi-config `.detoxrc.js` with `device.type: 'android.emulator'` and `device.type: 'android.genycloud'` cannot safely share a single named `device` entry — separate them
Why this matters: Detox `devices` entries are typed — a `type: 'android.emulator'` entry uses AVD name resolution while `type: 'android.genycloud'` uses Genycloud recipe resolution. If two `configurations` entries reference the same `devices` entry but one target expects AVD and the other expects Genycloud, Detox uses the `device.type` from the `devices` entry (not the `configurations` entry), so the wrong launcher is invoked. The error messages are misleading ("AVD not found" when you intended Genycloud) and reproduce only when running both configurations in the same CI job.
Fix: Define separate `devices` entries for each `device.type`: `android-avd` and `android-genycloud` with explicit `type` fields, and reference them from their respective `configurations`.

---

**G374** — `testRunner.retries > 0` combined with Jest `--bail` causes bail to count each retry as a separate failure
Why this matters: Jest's `--bail N` stops the test run after N failures. When Detox retries are enabled (`testRunner.retries: 1`), a single flaky test that fails twice (first run + one retry) consumes 2 bail tokens — making `--bail 2` effectively equivalent to `--bail 1` for flaky tests. In a suite of 80 tests with 3 occasional flakers and `retries: 1`, a run where all 3 flake and recover uses 6 bail tokens before any test permanently fails. If `--bail 6` was set expecting it to stop after 6 unique broken tests, it now stops after 3 flakers that actually recovered.
Fix: When `testRunner.retries > 0` is set, either omit `--bail` entirely for e2e suites (prefer a CI job timeout), or set `--bail` to `(acceptable_failures * (retries + 1) + buffer)` to account for retry tokens. Never set `--bail 1` in a suite with retries enabled.

---

**G375** — `BABEL_ENV=coverage` Metro bundle instrumentation increases cold-start time by 30–60% and causes Detox watchdog timeouts
Why this matters: Istanbul's instrumentation adds a counter increment call at every statement in every source file. For a React Native app with 500+ source files, this means several thousand extra function calls during the module evaluation phase — the synchronous JS execution that happens between `require('App')` and the first rendered frame. Detox's watchdog timer defaults to 120 seconds for app launch, but some complex apps with heavy import trees can exceed this threshold when instrumented, producing a "App appears to be busy" timeout with no other indication that coverage was the cause.
Fix: Create a dedicated `e2e/jest.coverage.config.js` with `testTimeout: 240000` and a Detox configuration with `testRunner.jest.setupTimeout: 240000` for coverage runs. Only run the 20–30 most important user-path tests in coverage mode — do not run the full 300-test suite instrumented. Gate coverage CI jobs to run only on PR merges to `main`, not on every push.

---

**G376** — `device.captureViewHierarchy()` on Android API 36 produces `.uihierarchy` XML with a `display-cutout` attribute not present in earlier Android APIs — naive snapshot diffs always fail
Why this matters: Android 16 (API 36) adds cutout inset information to every view's accessibility record, serialised as `display-cutout="{top:xx, bottom:xx, left:xx, right:xx}"`. When a hierarchy snapshot is captured on an API 36 emulator and compared against a baseline captured on API 35, every element that is a descendant of the root window will have an additional `display-cutout` attribute — the snapshot diff reports thousands of lines changed even though no structural change occurred. This makes the hierarchy regression gate permanently red after upgrading the CI emulator to API 36.
Fix: Strip the `display-cutout` attribute in `stripVolatileAttributes()` (shown in Pattern 686). Alternatively, pin the hierarchy regression CI job to a specific API level emulator (API 35) and add a separate API 36 smoke job that does not compare hierarchies. When intentionally updating baselines for API 36, regenerate all snapshots together with `UPDATE_HIERARCHY_BASELINES=true`.

### Pattern 687 — `element.scroll()` `visiblePercent` threshold and the Detox 20.48 scroll-gate change

Detox 20.48 raised the internal `visiblePercent` threshold required before an element is considered "visible enough to scroll into" from 50% to 75%. This broke suites that scrolled a list until a partially-visible item satisfied `toBeVisible()`. The canonical fix is to either tighten the test to scroll until the element is truly visible, or to pass an explicit `visiblePercent` option where the API allows it.

```typescript
// e2e/helpers/scrollUntilVisible.ts

/**
 * Scroll a container until the target element is at least `visiblePercent`
 * visible (default 75% to match Detox 20.48+ internal threshold).
 *
 * Use this instead of bare waitFor().whileElement().scroll() when the list
 * contains items that are partially clipped at the edge of the screen.
 */
export async function scrollUntilVisible(
  targetId: string,
  containerId: string,
  direction: 'down' | 'up' | 'left' | 'right' = 'down',
  pixelStep = 200,
  maxScrolls = 20,
): Promise<void> {
  for (let i = 0; i < maxScrolls; i++) {
    try {
      // toBeVisible() uses the 75% threshold internally in Detox 20.48+
      await expect(element(by.id(targetId))).toBeVisible();
      return; // element is sufficiently visible — done
    } catch {
      // Not yet visible — scroll one step and retry
      await element(by.id(containerId)).scroll(pixelStep, direction);
    }
  }
  // Final check: throw the real Detox assertion error if still not visible
  await expect(element(by.id(targetId))).toBeVisible();
}
```

```typescript
// e2e/product-list.test.ts
it('scrolls to the last recommended product and taps it', async () => {
  await scrollUntilVisible('product-item-recommended-last', 'product-scroll-view');
  await element(by.id('product-item-recommended-last')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('product-detail-screen')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(5000);
});
```

**`.detoxrc.js` workaround — `scrollToEdge` as a fallback for known-bottom items:**

```js
// When the target is always near the bottom of the list, scrollTo('bottom') is cheaper
// than a manual loop. Use only when the list length is bounded and always fully loaded.
it('taps the Save button at the bottom of the settings form', async () => {
  await element(by.id('settings-form-scroll')).scrollTo('bottom');
  await element(by.id('save-settings-btn')).tap();
  await waitFor(element(by.id('save-success-toast'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
});
```

Tradeoff: The `scrollUntilVisible` helper adds O(N) Detox round-trips where N is the number of scroll steps needed. For lists where you know the item's index, prefer `scrollToIndex` via a custom `FlatList` `ref` callback exposed through a test-only launchArg, or use stable unique testIDs with `waitFor().whileElement().scroll()`. The bare `waitFor().whileElement().scroll()` API does not accept a `visiblePercent` parameter — the 75% threshold is implicit.

### Pattern 688 — `device.openURL()` for Universal Link and App Clip cold-start testing

`device.openURL()` dispatches a URL to the running app without going through the home screen. Use it to test Universal Links (iOS) and App Links (Android) that bypass the browser and open the app directly. The critical constraint is that the app must already be running when `openURL` is called — dispatching a URL before the app's `AppDelegate`/`Activity` is ready silently drops the intent.

```typescript
// e2e/universal-links.test.ts
describe('Universal Links', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    // Must launch the app FIRST, then open the URL — NOT device.launchApp({ url })
    // device.launchApp({ url }) is correct for deep links; device.openURL() is for
    // Universal Links dispatched to an already-running app (warm-start simulation).
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await device.reloadReactNative();
  });

  it('opens the product page from a Universal Link (warm start)', async () => {
    // App is already running — openURL dispatches through the OS URL handler
    await device.openURL({ url: 'https://www.myapp.com/products/42' });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('product-screen-42')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
    await expect(element(by.id('product-title'))).toHaveText('Awesome Product');
  });

  it('handles an invalid Universal Link path gracefully (warm start)', async () => {
    await device.openURL({ url: 'https://www.myapp.com/products/INVALID_ID' });
    await waitFor(element(by.id('not-found-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(5000);
  });
});
```

**Cold-start Universal Link test (iOS) — launch + URL simultaneously:**

```typescript
// For cold-start: pass url to launchApp directly
it('opens product screen from Universal Link on cold start', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({
    newInstance: true,
    url: 'https://www.myapp.com/products/42',
    permissions: { notifications: 'YES' },
  });
  // Cold-start Universal Link routing takes longer than warm-start
  await waitFor(element(by.id('product-screen-42')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(8000);
});
```

**Android App Link pattern (intent dispatch via ADB):**

```typescript
// Android: device.openURL dispatches as an implicit intent with ACTION_VIEW
// The intent resolves to the app only if the Android App Link is verified
it('opens the article screen from an Android App Link', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);

  await device.openURL({ url: 'https://www.myapp.com/articles/99' });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('article-screen-99')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(6000);
});
```

**App Clip testing (iOS 16+) — requires a separate App Clip binary:**

```js
// .detoxrc.js — App Clip as a separate app entry
apps: {
  'ios.appclip': {
    type: 'ios.app',
    binaryPath: 'ios/build/AppClip.app',
    bundleId: 'com.myapp.Clip',
    build: 'xcodebuild -target MyAppClip -configuration Release ...',
  },
},
configurations: {
  'ios.appclip.release': {
    device: 'iphone-15',
    app: 'ios.appclip',
  },
},
```

```typescript
// e2e/app-clip.test.ts (run with --configuration ios.appclip.release)
it('App Clip launches to the correct offer screen', async () => {
  await device.launchApp({
    newInstance: true,
    url: 'https://www.myapp.com/clip/offer/PROMO50',
  });
  await waitFor(element(by.id('clip-offer-screen-PROMO50')))
    .toBeVisible()
    .withTimeout(10000);
});
```

Tradeoff: `device.openURL()` on iOS goes through the OS URL dispatcher and may trigger a system confirmation dialog ("Open in MyApp?") the first time a Universal Link is dispatched in a fresh simulator session. Pre-grant URL association trust by adding the associated domains entitlement to the test build and verifying the app's `apple-app-site-association` file is served from a mock server on CI.

### Pattern 689 — `by.semanticType()` practical selection guide

`by.semanticType()` (Detox 20.47+, PR #4793) provides cross-platform semantic matching that maps to native element types without requiring `testID` props. It is the preferred fallback when a third-party component library does not expose `testID` and `by.type()` requires different strings on iOS vs Android.

```typescript
// Semantic type reference
// by.semanticType('touchable')  → iOS: UIButton / RCTButton / Pressable
//                                → Android: View with clickable=true
// by.semanticType('textInput')  → iOS: UITextField / UITextView
//                                → Android: EditText / AppCompatEditText
// by.semanticType('scrollView') → iOS: UIScrollView
//                                → Android: ScrollView / RecyclerView
// by.semanticType('text')       → iOS: UILabel / RCTText
//                                → Android: TextView
// by.semanticType('image')      → iOS: UIImageView
//                                → Android: ImageView

// Decision tree:
// 1. Has testID?           → by.id()                    (always first choice)
// 2. Has accessibilityLabel? → by.label()               (second choice)
// 3. Is a standard RN component? → by.semanticType()    (cross-platform)
// 4. Is iOS-specific?      → by.traits()                (iOS only)
// 5. Is Android-specific?  → by.type('android.widget.X') (Android only)
// 6. Visible text only?    → by.text()                  (fragile, last resort)
```

```typescript
// e2e/settings-no-testids.test.ts
// Scenario: third-party settings library does not expose testID props

it('changes notification toggle state', async () => {
  // Narrow to the settings section by ancestor, then match the first touchable
  await element(
    by.semanticType('touchable')
      .withAncestor(by.id('notifications-section'))
  ).atIndex(0).tap();

  // Verify the toggle changed by asserting a unique label update
  await waitFor(
    element(by.label('Notifications enabled'))
  ).toBeVisible().withTimeout(3000);
});

it('finds the search text input without testID', async () => {
  // atIndex(0) because the screen might have a filter input and a search input
  await element(by.semanticType('textInput')).atIndex(0).tap();
  await element(by.semanticType('textInput')).atIndex(0).typeText('react native');
  await waitFor(element(by.id('search-results'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
});

it('scrolls the first scrollable container to the bottom', async () => {
  await element(by.semanticType('scrollView')).atIndex(0).scrollTo('bottom');
  await expect(element(by.id('footer-element'))).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Bridgeless Mode (RN 0.74+) note:** `by.semanticType()` works correctly in both Bridge and Bridgeless modes as it queries the native accessibility tree rather than the JS bridge. However, components that override `accessibilityRole` to a non-semantic value (`'none'` or `'adjustable'`) will not be found by the expected semantic type — use `by.id()` for those.

**Fallback when `by.semanticType()` returns 0 matches:**

```typescript
// Generic fallback helper
async function tapFirstSemanticOrId(
  semanticType: string,
  fallbackId: string,
): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await element(by.semanticType(semanticType)).atIndex(0).tap();
  } catch {
    // Semantic type unavailable (RNGH Pressable, custom native component, etc.)
    await element(by.id(fallbackId)).tap();
  }
}
```

Tradeoff: `by.semanticType('touchable')` does not match `react-native-gesture-handler` Pressable components that use `useAnimatedStyle` internally — RNGH Pressable renders as a `View` with a `GestureHandlerRootView` overlay rather than a native button type, so Detox's semantic mapping finds no touchable trait. Always add `testID` props to RNGH Pressable components used in testable flows (see Gotcha 379).

### Pattern 690 — WebView `web(element())` interaction patterns for hybrid app flows

Detox's `web(element(by.id('webview-id')))` API bridges from the native test context into the WebView's DOM. Use it for hybrid apps that embed a WebView for payment flows, onboarding web pages, or embedded dashboards that cannot be driven via native selectors.

```typescript
// e2e/payment-webview.test.ts
// The app has a native checkout screen that embeds a <WebView testID="payment-webview">
// for the actual payment form.

describe('Payment WebView flow', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
    await loginAs('user'); // use the auth helper from Pattern 17
  });

  beforeEach(async () => {
    await element(by.id('checkout-btn')).tap();
    // Wait for the native screen that contains the WebView to appear
    await waitFor(element(by.id('payment-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(5000);
    // Wait for the WebView to fully load — the DOM must be ready before web() calls
    await waitFor(element(by.id('payment-webview'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(10000);
  });

  it('fills in card details and submits payment', async () => {
    const webCtx = web(element(by.id('payment-webview')));

    // by.web.id() — matches DOM element.id
    await webCtx.element(by.web.id('card-number-input')).tap();
    await webCtx.element(by.web.id('card-number-input')).typeText('4111111111111111');

    // by.web.cssSelector() — full CSS selector support
    await webCtx.element(by.web.cssSelector('#expiry-input')).tap();
    await webCtx.element(by.web.cssSelector('#expiry-input')).typeText('12/28');

    await webCtx.element(by.web.id('cvv-input')).tap();
    await webCtx.element(by.web.id('cvv-input')).typeText('123');

    // Tap the submit button identified by its text content
    await webCtx.element(by.web.cssSelector('button[type="submit"]')).tap();

    // Wait for the native confirmation screen (returned from WebView via postMessage)
    await waitFor(element(by.id('payment-success-screen')))
      .toBeVisible()
      .withTimeout(10000);
  });

  it('shows validation error for an expired card', async () => {
    const webCtx = web(element(by.id('payment-webview')));

    await webCtx.element(by.web.id('card-number-input')).typeText('4000000000000002');
    await webCtx.element(by.web.cssSelector('#expiry-input')).typeText('01/20'); // expired
    await webCtx.element(by.web.id('cvv-input')).typeText('123');
    await webCtx.element(by.web.cssSelector('button[type="submit"]')).tap();

    // Assert the in-WebView error message using by.web.cssSelector()
    await waitFor(webCtx.element(by.web.cssSelector('.payment-error-banner')))
      .toExist()
      .withTimeout(5000);

    // Verify its text using getAttributes() — returns the DOM element's innerText
    const errorAttrs = await webCtx.element(by.web.cssSelector('.payment-error-banner')).getAttributes();
    expect(errorAttrs.label).toContain('expired');
  });
});
```

**Multi-frame WebView disambiguation:**

```typescript
// When the WebView contains multiple iframes, scope to the correct one
// using by.web.xpath() to select the iframe context node first.
it('interacts with an embedded iframe form', async () => {
  const webCtx = web(element(by.id('dashboard-webview')));

  // xpath selector for an input inside a known iframe
  await webCtx.element(by.web.xpath('//iframe[@id="report-frame"]//input[@name="dateFrom"]'))
    .tap();
  await webCtx.element(by.web.xpath('//iframe[@id="report-frame"]//input[@name="dateFrom"]'))
    .typeText('2026-01-01');

  await webCtx.element(by.web.xpath('//iframe[@id="report-frame"]//button[@type="submit"]'))
    .tap();
});
```

**Running JS inside the WebView context:**

```typescript
// element.runScript() — execute arbitrary JS in the WebView context
// Useful for programmatic form submission or reading DOM state
it('reads the session token set by the WebView', async () => {
  const webCtx = web(element(by.id('auth-webview')));

  const token = await webCtx.element(by.web.cssSelector('body')).runScript(
    'return window.sessionStorage.getItem("auth_token");'
  );
  expect(token).toBeTruthy();
});
```

**IPC latency budget:**

Each `web(element(...))` call crosses the native/WebView boundary via IPC and takes 300–800 ms. Budget accordingly: a form with 5 fields + 1 submit tap will take 1.8–4.8 s just for the IPC overhead, before any DOM rendering or network time. Set `withTimeout` to at least 3x the expected IPC + DOM time. Never use WebView interactions inside a `waitFor` polling loop — the IPC cost multiplies with every poll iteration.

Tradeoff: `by.web.id()` is the most reliable WebView selector (stable across DOM changes), followed by `by.web.cssSelector()` (powerful but breaks if the CSS class name changes). Avoid `by.web.xpath()` except for iframe scoping — XPath selectors are slow and brittle in dynamic single-page apps. For assertion-only scenarios, `runScript()` is faster than DOM queries because it skips the hit-test and accessibility round-trip.
