### Community Gotchas (continued)

**G377** — `element.scroll()` `visiblePercent` default raised from 50% to 75% in Detox 20.48 — borderline-visible scroll targets silently break
Why this matters: Before Detox 20.48, `waitFor().toBeVisible()` resolved when at least 50% of the element was within the visible area. Detox 20.48 (PR #4843) raised this threshold to 75% to reduce false-positive "visible" assertions on elements clipped by a bottom safe-area inset. Tests that used `whileElement(scrollContainer).scroll(100, 'down')` + `toBeVisible()` in tight loops now require more scroll steps before the assertion resolves — suites that previously needed 2–3 scroll iterations may need 4–6. The test appears to time out at the `withTimeout` boundary with no diagnostic message about the threshold change.
Fix: Increase the scroll step size from 100 px to 200–300 px in `whileElement` loops, or switch to the `scrollUntilVisible()` helper (Pattern 687) which uses `toBeVisible()` as the termination condition after each scroll step. Do not decrease `withTimeout` as a workaround.

---

**G378** — `device.openURL()` on Android cold-start races the Activity intent dispatch — "activity not found" crash
Why this matters: `device.openURL()` dispatches an `ACTION_VIEW` implicit intent to Android. If the app's main `Activity` has not yet registered its intent filter in `ActivityManager` (which happens during the `onCreate` phase), the intent dispatch window closes before the app catches it — the OS logs "activity not found" and the URL is dropped silently. This race window is approximately 400–600 ms after `launchApp()` returns on a cold-start. Tests that call `device.openURL()` immediately after `device.launchApp({ newInstance: true })` are inside this race window on slow CI emulators.
Fix: Always wait for a known screen element to be visible before calling `device.openURL()` on a fresh app instance. The waitFor ensures `ActivityThread` has progressed past `onCreate` before the intent is dispatched:

```typescript
await device.launchApp({ newInstance: true });
await waitFor(element(by.id('home-screen'))).toBeVisible().withTimeout(8000);
// Activity is now registered — intent dispatch is safe
await device.openURL({ url: 'https://www.myapp.com/articles/99' });
```

---

**G379** — `by.semanticType('touchable')` does not match `react-native-gesture-handler` Pressable using `useAnimatedStyle` — requires `by.id()` fallback
Why this matters: `by.semanticType('touchable')` works by querying the native accessibility type. React Native core `TouchableOpacity`, `TouchableHighlight`, and the built-in `Pressable` (without RNGH) render as native button types (`UIButton` on iOS, `View` with `clickable=true` on Android), which Detox maps to `touchable`. RNGH `Pressable` built with `useAnimatedStyle` renders differently: on iOS it becomes a `UIView` with a `GestureRecognizer` attached (not a `UIButton`), and on Android it becomes a `View` with a Gesture Handler root overlay — neither matches the native "button" type. `by.semanticType('touchable')` silently returns 0 matches for these components.
Fix: Always add `testID` to RNGH Pressable components used in testable user flows. If a third-party library uses RNGH Pressable internally and does not forward `testID`, wrap it in a `<View testID="wrapper-pressable">` and tap the wrapper. As a fallback detector: `by.traits(['button'])` on iOS will also fail to match RNGH Pressable — if both `by.semanticType('touchable')` and `by.traits(['button'])` return no elements, the component is almost certainly RNGH-based.

---

**G380** — `web(element(by.id(...)))` IPC round-trip adds 300–800 ms per call — avoid inside `waitFor` polling loops
Why this matters: Each call to a WebView element via `web(element(...))` crosses the native/WebView bridge via IPC. The round-trip cost is 300–800 ms depending on WebView load and device/emulator speed. `waitFor` polls every ~100 ms, so a `waitFor(webCtx.element(by.web.id('success-banner'))).toExist().withTimeout(5000)` loop can make 6–16 IPC calls — spending 2–12 s in IPC overhead alone before the timeout fires, even when the element already exists at poll #2. The test appears to hang on a "visible WebView element" as if the timeout is too short, while the real bottleneck is IPC cost per poll.
Fix: Instead of polling with `waitFor` on a WebView element, either (a) wait for a native element that the WebView posts via `window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage()` when ready, or (b) use a single `runScript()` call to check DOM readiness and then interact: `await webCtx.element(by.web.cssSelector('body')).runScript('return document.getElementById("success-banner") !== null')` — and gate the subsequent interaction on that boolean. For animations inside the WebView, disable them via JS injection: `webCtx.element(by.web.cssSelector('body')).runScript('document.body.style.setProperty("--animation-duration", "0ms", "important")')`.
